## usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py
- Canonical three-layer overlay paths (lowest precedence first). Every element is
- overridable so a caller (or a test/CI on a non-FHS host) can retarget without
- editing this file. VENDOR is repo-relative when MIOS_TOML_ROOT is set.
- The ONE canonical palette-default map -- mirrors mios.toml [colors] verbatim so
- no tool re-declares the 12 semantic hexes (+ ansi slots). resolve = SSOT over these.
- UNIFIED PORTS (operator directive: every port floats from SSOT, one scheme):
- each [ports].<x> emits BOTH canonical alias forms -- MIOS_PORT_<x> AND
- ever hardcodes a port number; the value is operator-defined in mios.toml [ports].
- A few keys carry a historical service-canonical name that differs from the raw key.

## usr/lib/mios/paths.sh
- /usr/lib/mios/paths.sh -- runtime FHS path constants for MiOS.
- Shipped in the image; sourced by /usr/libexec/mios/* and /usr/bin/mios*.
- Idempotent. Override any constant from the environment before sourcing.
- Mirror of automation/lib/paths.sh (which is build-time only and not shipped).
- Keep these two files aligned when adding constants.
- /usr/* -- read-only composefs surface
- /etc/* -- admin-override surface (3-way merged on bootc upgrade)
- /var/* -- runtime mutable (declared via tmpfiles.d, never written at build)

## usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh
- tools/lib/userenv.sh -- read the unified 'MiOS' user config and export
- entry-point script, and any tool that needs the user-overridden values.
- THERE IS ONE CANONICAL FILE PATH PER LAYER. Higher layers shadow lower
- layers field-by-field; the user-edit copy lives in mios-bootstrap and is
- staged into /etc/mios/mios.toml at install time.
- 1. /usr/share/mios/mios.toml   (vendor defaults; baked into image)        lowest
- 2. /etc/mios/mios.toml         (host-local; bootstrap-staged)
- 3. ~/.config/mios/mios.toml    (per-user; XDG)                            highest
- Schema is the same in all three layers (TOML 1.0; section names below).
- Resolution mode: deep merge by section.field. The Python helper below
- reads each layer in order and writes one consolidated set of MIOS_*
- exports back to the calling shell.
- Section -> MIOS_* env mapping (typed slots; non-typed fields can still
- be reached via the [env] table for free-form injection):
- [identity]    .username/.fullname/.hostname/.shell/.groups
- -> MIOS_USER, MIOS_USER_FULLNAME, MIOS_HOSTNAME,
- MIOS_USER_SHELL, MIOS_USER_GROUPS (CSV)
- [locale]      .timezone/.keyboard_layout/.language
- -> MIOS_TIMEZONE, MIOS_KEYBOARD, MIOS_LOCALE
- [auth]        .ssh_key_action/.password_policy
- -> MIOS_SSH_KEY_ACTION, MIOS_PASSWORD_POLICY
- [network]     .firewalld_default_zone
- -> MIOS_FIREWALLD_ZONE
- [ai]          .endpoint/.model/.embed_model/.api_key/.system_prompt_file/.mcp_registry
- -> MIOS_AI_ENDPOINT, MIOS_AI_MODEL, MIOS_AI_EMBED_MODEL,
- MIOS_AI_KEY, MIOS_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FILE, MIOS_MCP_REGISTRY
- [desktop]     .session/.color_scheme/.flatpaks
- -> MIOS_DESKTOP_SESSION, MIOS_COLOR_SCHEME,
- MIOS_FLATPAKS (CSV; consumed by Containerfile build arg)
- [image]       .ref/.branch/.base/.bib/.name/.tag/.local_tag
- -> MIOS_IMAGE_REF, MIOS_BRANCH, MIOS_BASE_IMAGE,
- MIOS_BIB_IMAGE, MIOS_IMAGE_NAME, MIOS_IMAGE_TAG,
- MIOS_LOCAL_TAG
- [bootstrap]   .mode/.mios_repo/.bootstrap_repo
- -> MIOS_BOOTSTRAP_MODE, MIOS_REPO_URL, MIOS_BOOTSTRAP_REPO_URL
- [profile]     .role/.features
- -> MIOS_PROFILE_ROLE, MIOS_PROFILE_FEATURES (CSV)
- [colors]      .bg/.fg/.accent/.cursor/.success/.warning/.error/.info/
- .muted/.subtle/.earth/.silver/.ansi_*
- -> MIOS_COLOR_BG, MIOS_COLOR_FG, MIOS_COLOR_ACCENT, ...
- MIOS_ANSI_0_BLACK, MIOS_ANSI_1_RED, ...
- (consumed by /etc/profile.d/mios-colors.sh, the
- oh-my-posh theme, the configurator HTML's :root,
- and globals.{sh,ps1} as default overrides)
- [env]         arbitrary KEY = "VALUE" pairs                exported verbatim
- Backwards compat:
- - The legacy lightweight schema ([user]/[build]/[flatpaks].install) is
- still understood as a fallback when [identity]/[image]/[desktop] are
- absent. 'just init-user-space' migrates the legacy split files.
- - The legacy split files (env.toml, images.toml, build.toml,
- flatpaks.list, the bare 'env' file) are still read when no
- mios.toml is present in any layer.
- Usage: source ./tools/lib/userenv.sh
- Note: must be sourced (not executed) to affect the calling shell.
- 1. TOML overlay (vendor -> host -> per-user). Use python tomllib (3.11+
- stdlib; tomli fallback for older). The Python block prints shell-safe
- 'export' lines that the surrounding shell evals.
- Drop-in discovery (R1): each tier = monolith + its mios.d/*.toml fragments.
- Vendor fragments live in /usr/lib/mios/mios.d (Law 1 USR-OVER-ETC); admin/
- user fragments sit in a mios.d/ beside their monolith. Tier-major precedence
- (vendor < host < user); the Python block globs + orders them exactly like the
- peer resolver usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py. No-op until the first fragment exists.
- LOG-HYGIENE: the resolved SSOT is thousands of MIOS_* exports. Under a caller's `set -x`
- (e.g. the OCI bake's `set -ex`) the `exports=` capture traces as ONE multi-KB line and the
- eval below traces thousands of `+ export MIOS_...` lines -- flooding the build log to where
- it is unreadable/un-pasteable past this point. Suppress xtrace for the resolution + eval,
- then restore the caller's xtrace state (set -e safe: if-form, never a failing last cmd).
- `if`-form so set -e treats the test as a conditional, not a fatal.
- WS-0 pgvector bind hardening (Wave 0): derive the concrete listener bind
- address the quadlet renders from the [pgvector].listen_loopback boolean.
- true (default) -> 127.0.0.1 (loopback-only; the confined agent-pipe reaches
- it over loopback, nothing off-box can). false -> 0.0.0.0 (off-box exposure;
- deliberately federated deployments only). Degrade-open: if the key is unset
- we default to the safe loopback bind. The slot map can only copy a value
- verbatim, so this boolean->address transform lives here as a post-load step.
- 2. Backwards-compat: legacy split files (per-user only). Read only when
- none of the three TOML layers contain a [identity] or [user] section --
- i.e., the user is on a pre-unified-schema deployment. Each is shallow
- KEY="VALUE", grep-friendly.
- `[[ ... ]] && cmd` returns 1 when the test is false; under set -e
- in callers like mios-build-driver, that's fatal even though
- "key not present in legacy file" is the expected case for fresh
- installs. Use `[[ -z ... ]] || cmd` form so set -e treats the
- whole expression as a guard, not a hard fail.
- shellcheck disable=SC1091
- Whitelist of dynamically mapped ports/keys for static analysis (97-ssot-lint.sh)

## usr/lib/os-release
- MiOS is a bootc-based OCI bootable OS built on top of
- ghcr.io/ublue-os/ucore-hci:stable-nvidia (Universal Blue's HCI variant
- of Fedora CoreOS), with a sibling minimal target on
- quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc:latest available as Containerfile.minimal.
- The ID_LIKE chain "fedora coreos" preserves CoreOS ancestry for tools
- (zincati, rpm-ostree, bootc) that branch on it; the ID=mios is the new
- canonical identity that fastfetch / motd / postcheck see.
- The seven version-bearing fields (VERSION, VERSION_ID, PRETTY_NAME,
- CPE_NAME, BUILD_ID, IMAGE_VERSION, OSTREE_VERSION) are NOT authored here:
- they are PROJECTED at build time from the single SSOT
- mios.toml [meta].mios_version (via /ctx/VERSION -> MIOS_VERSION in
- automation/88-finalize.sh), and drift-check (42) fails the build if the
- committed values above ever diverge from that SSOT. Edit the version in
- mios.toml [meta].mios_version ONLY.

## usr/lib/profile.d/mios-wsl2.sh
- WSLg display environment for login shells in WSL2.
- WSLg supplies a Wayland socket via /mnt/wslg/. GTK apps refuse to start
- without XDG_SESSION_TYPE set ("Unsupported or missing session type ''").
- pam_systemd would set this for a proper logind session; under WSLg there
- is no PAM session, so set it here as a fallback.
- logind creates /run/user/<uid> and pam_systemd exports XDG_RUNTIME_DIR.
- WSL bypasses PAM at login, so populate the var if logind made the dir
- but the env var is unset.

## usr/lib/sudoers.d/wheel-nopasswd
- MiOS: Podman-machine-style passwordless sudo for wheel members

## usr/libexec/mios-boot-diag
- /usr/libexec/mios-boot-diag -- MiOS boot-time diagnostic.
- Wired in via /usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-boot-diag.service which
- runs once per boot, after basic.target, before graphical.target.
- Output goes to journal+console so a degraded boot still surfaces
- the diagnostic on the console without requiring an interactive
- login.
- Read-only by design: enumerates known signals (failed units,
- greenboot result, bootc state, NVIDIA CDI freshness, ostree HEAD,
- fs-verity status, /run/mios/* status files) and prints a concise
- summary. Never modifies state -- safe on every deploy shape.

## usr/libexec/mios-flatpak-install
- /usr/libexec/mios-flatpak-install -- first-boot Flatpak deployer.
- Wired in via /usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-flatpak-install.service:
- Type=oneshot, ConditionVirtualization=!container,
- After=network-online.target, Before=display-manager.service.
- Reads the operator's selected Flatpaks from the layered TOML
- resolver and installs them system-wide via the host Flatpak.
- Idempotent: already-installed apps short-circuit; a sentinel
- /var/lib/mios/.flatpaks-installed records the merged set so a
- subsequent boot reinstalls only what's NEW.
- Source order (highest precedence first):
- 1. ~/.config/mios/mios.toml      (per-user, only meaningful on
- single-user systems)
- 2. /etc/mios/mios.toml            (host override)
- 3. /usr/share/mios/mios.toml      (vendor default)
- The TOML key consulted is `[desktop].flatpaks` -- a list of
- flathub IDs. A line-delimited fallback at /usr/share/mios/flatpak-list
- is supported for build-time injections (40-flatpak-bake.sh).
- Ensure flathub is configured (system-wide).
- Resolve the flatpak list. The toml resolver lives in /usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh
- and exports MIOS_DESKTOP_FLATPAKS as a comma-separated list.
- shellcheck disable=SC1091
- Build-time bake fallback (40-flatpak-bake.sh writes this file).
- Normalize: split on comma, trim whitespace, drop empties + comments.
- Skip those already installed system-wide. mios.toml entries may be
- prefixed with `<remote>:<appid>`; split on the first colon. Bare
- app ids fall back to flathub.
- shellcheck disable=SC2207
- shellcheck disable=SC2207
- Refresh appstream for the target remote so search sees current metadata.
- Ambiguous-branch fallback: under --noninteractive, an id that publishes
- several runtime branches (e.g. org.freedesktop.Platform.VulkanLayer.*)
- errors "Multiple refs match ... must specify one" instead of prompting.
- Retry once with a default //<branch> appended (unless already branched).

## usr/libexec/mios-grd-setup
- MiOS -- mios-grd-setup: GNOME Remote Desktop firstboot setup.
- Triggered by mios-grd-setup.service (oneshot, guarded by SENTINEL).
- Generates a self-signed EC TLS keypair, wires it into grdctl, optionally
- applies a default credential when MIOS_PASSWORD is exported, and opens the
- RDP port via firewalld.
- shellcheck source=/usr/lib/mios/paths.sh
- Security: never bake mios:mios as a default. Caller may export MIOS_PASSWORD,
- or admins may write ${MIOS_ETC_DIR}/grd/credentials post-install.

## usr/libexec/mios-hyperv-enhanced
- /usr/libexec/mios-hyperv-enhanced -- Hyper-V Enhanced Session bring-up.
- Wired in via /usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-hyperv-enhanced.service:
- ConditionVirtualization=microsoft, oneshot, after gdm.service.
- Configures the guest side of Hyper-V Enhanced Session so the
- Windows host can connect via the integrated VMConnect viewer
- (clipboard sync, dynamic resolution, audio, USB redirection)
- instead of the bare framebuffer console.
- Steps:
- 1. Confirm we're a Hyper-V guest (ConditionVirtualization is the
- first gate; we re-check at runtime so manual invocation is safe).
- 2. Ensure hv_* kernel modules are loaded (hv_sock, hv_utils,
- hv_balloon, hv_storvsc, hv_netvsc).
- 3. Enable systemd units required by Enhanced Session: hv-kvp-daemon,
- hv-vss-daemon, hv-fcopy-daemon (best-effort -- naming varies
- slightly by Fedora release).
- 4. Configure xrdp to listen on the Hyper-V vsock transport
- (hvsock://2:5d2a17ed-... vendored by hyperv-daemons / xrdp).
- 5. Symlink the colord polkit "color manager" rule that suppresses
- the GNOME color popup that breaks Enhanced Session login.
- 6. Set GDM to remember the last login (avoids the picker hang
- that some Hyper-V displays trigger).
- Idempotent: every step probes for the desired final state first
- and skips if already there. /var/lib/mios/.hyperv-enhanced-applied
- acts as a coarse sentinel for log output filtering.
- 1. Defensive virt check (the systemd unit gates on this too, but
- manual `bash mios-hyperv-enhanced` from a non-HV host is a no-op).
- 2. Hyper-V kernel modules. Most Fedora kernels load these via udev
- automatically; explicitly loading is harmless.
- 3. Hyper-V daemons.
- 4. xrdp on the Hyper-V vsock transport. Hyper-V Enhanced Session
- uses HV_SOCK CIDs (instead of TCP) -- xrdp supports this via
- `port=vsock://-1:3389` on Fedora 39+. We patch xrdp.ini idempotently.
- Backup once.
- 5. Suppress the color-manager auth popup that hangs Enhanced
- Session logins on first display attach. Polkit drops the prompt
- entirely for users in the wheel group.
- 6. GDM "remember last login" -- skips the picker that hangs on
- some Hyper-V framebuffer rotations.

## usr/libexec/mios-verify
- /usr/libexec/mios-verify -- post-install architectural-purity check.
- Wired in via /usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-verify.service (initrd
- context) and also runnable from the command line for ad-hoc audits.
- Exit non-zero on architectural-law violations so a `mios-verify`
- in CI / smoke pipelines fails loudly.
- Checks performed (each gated on the relevant filesystem being
- present, so this script works in initrd, full boot, dev VM, and
- WSL contexts):
- 1. ostree HEAD reachable and matches a known commit.
- 2. composefs root has fs-verity enabled (when running from initrd).
- 3. /usr is read-only at runtime (immutable contract).
- 4. /var has been realized by systemd-tmpfiles (no build-time
- writes leaked through; LAW 2: NO /VAR WRITES AT BUILD).
- 5. /etc/mios layered config resolves cleanly via userenv.sh.
- 6. /usr/share/mios overlay present (vendor defaults landed).
- 7. mios.toml SSOT exists at /usr/share/mios/mios.toml.
- 8. Critical systemd units load (no-mask, no-fail-on-load).
- 9. fapolicyd is in enforcing mode (when present).
- 10. SELinux is enforcing (when present).
- 11. /usr/bin/mios CLI exists and responds to --version.
- Detect context. The same script runs in initrd (limited tools),
- full system boot, dev-VM, and WSL distro -- branch behavior on
- what's actually mounted.
- 1. ostree HEAD.
- 2. composefs + fs-verity.
- 3. /usr read-only at runtime (LAW 1: USR-OVER-ETC immutable).
- 4. /var realization (LAW 2: NO /VAR WRITES AT BUILD).
- Sample tmpfiles.d-managed dirs; if they exist with the expected
- owner the realizer ran. If /var holds files older than the
- tmpfiles entries they'd be build-time leaks.
- 5. mios.toml SSOT layered resolver.
- 6. /usr/share/mios overlay. PACKAGES.md moved to /usr/share/doc/mios/reference/
- in v0.2.4 (mios.toml [packages.<section>].pkgs is the only runtime SSOT).
- 7. /etc/mios.
- 8. Critical systemd units load (no Reload errors).
- 9. fapolicyd enforcing.
- 10. SELinux enforcing.
- 11. mios CLI.

## usr/libexec/mios/test_mios_daemon_launchclaim.py
- The CLI is a Linux daemon that loads libc.so.6 via ctypes at import time;
- on a non-Linux build host that load fails. Shim CDLL so the module body
- (the launch-claim detector under test) can be exercised cross-platform.
- The keyword/English-phrase regex list + the Steam|Epic|... app-name
- allowlist MUST be gone -- the detection is model-driven now.
- Force the model mode regardless of the host's mios.toml.
- (1) MODEL says it's a launch claim -> target taken from the model, generic.
- (1b) A non-English / non-listed target still resolves (no app-name list).
- (2) MODEL says NOT a claim -> empty dict (no claim recorded).
- (3a) Lane unreachable (empty llm_chat) -> DEGRADE-OPEN None (skip, no fabricate).
- (3b) Unparseable model output -> degrade-open None.
- (4) Detector mode != model -> None (verification disabled), and the
- classifier never even calls the model.
- (5) Oversized/empty model target is structurally rejected, not back-filled.

## usr/libexec/mios/test_mios_daemon_postcheck.py
- The CLI loads libc.so.6 via ctypes at import; shim CDLL so the module
- body under test imports cross-platform on a non-Linux build host.
- The verb->check mapping must NOT be a baked dispatch map -- the source
- no longer hard-codes which verb gets which check.
- (1) The map is READ from the SSOT [daemon.post_check] table. Point the
- reader at the repo's real vendor mios.toml and assert the shipped
- defaults are what drives coverage (values are NOT compiled in).
- (2) Behavior follows SSOT: a NON-DEFAULT layer that maps a brand-new
- verb to file_exists makes the daemon check THAT verb, while a verb
- dropped from the table degrades-open (checked=False). Proves the
- mapping is data, not baked code.
- open_app is absent from this layer -> no post-check (degrade-open).
- The newly-mapped verb dispatches the file_exists IMPLEMENTATION.
- (3) Signal dispatch wires the right implementation: file_nonempty
- fails an empty file but passes a non-empty one (distinct from
- file_exists, which would pass the empty file).
- (4) Unknown signal in the SSOT map -> degrade-open (no impl, no crash).
- (5) Empty/unreadable map -> every verb degrades-open.

## usr/libexec/mios/test_mios_daemon_refusal.py
- The CLI loads libc.so.6 via ctypes at import time; on a non-Linux build
- host that fails. Shim CDLL so the module body (the refusal judge under
- test) can be exercised cross-platform.
- The English-regex PRE-FILTER that GATED whether to even check MUST be gone
- -- detection is the model's job now.
- The READ PATH must be gone: no env-var pointing at the file, no
- .read_text of it. (A timeless prose comment may still name the deleted
- file -- we ban the mechanism, not the word.)
- Force the model mode regardless of the host's mios.toml.
- (1) The judge is consulted on EVERY candidate -- a response that contains
- NO refusal-keyword text at all is still judged; a YES verdict records it.
- (Under the old regex pre-filter this benign-looking line would never have
- reached the LLM; now there is no gate.)
- (1b) A non-English response is judged too (no ascii/keyword gate).
- (2) MODEL says NO -> not a refusal (False, nothing recorded).
- (3a) Lane unreachable (empty llm_chat) -> DEGRADE-OPEN None (skip).
- (3b) Unparseable verdict -> degrade-open None.
- (3c) Empty input -> None without consulting the model.
- (4) Mode != model -> None (detection disabled), model never consulted.

## usr/libexec/mios/test_mios_find_ranker.py
- scoring SSOT (tier ordering, category-priority weights, fuzzy bounds) from
- mios.toml -- defaults preserve historical behaviour, a non-default config
- flips the winner. Pure in-process exec of the script's embedded ranker; no
- bash, no mios-apps subprocess.
- mios-find invokes the ranker heredoc as `python3 - "<.../lib/mios>" "$QUERY"`,
- so argv[1] is the shared-resolver lib dir and argv[2] is the query. Mirror that
- 3-arg contract here (was the old 2-arg [prog, query] -> ModuleNotFoundError /
- IndexError -> the libexec test gate die'd the whole OCI build).
- mios-find's ranker reads the shared mios_toml resolver, which layers
- VENDOR<HOST<USER from MIOS_VENDOR_TOML/MIOS_HOST_TOML/MIOS_USER_TOML (NOT
- the old MIOS_TOML). Point the vendor layer at the fixture and isolate
- host/user at nonexistent paths so ONLY the fixture is merged.
- The ranker resolves config via mios_toml.load_merged(), which memoizes a
- PROCESS-GLOBAL cache for layers=None. These tests exec() the ranker
- repeatedly in ONE process, each pointing MIOS_VENDOR_TOML at a different
- fixture; without invalidating that cache every test after the first reuses
- the FIRST fixture's merged config and the override assertions fail. Clear
- it so each fixture is re-read (mios_toml lives on the _LIB dir).
- Config snippets ---------------------------------------------------------
- A toml with NO ranker sections -> loader degrades to the baked defaults.
- Two entries tie at the strongest tier (name_exact); the category-priority
- weight is the only tiebreaker, so flipping it in config flips the winner.
- Historical default: windows-app (1) outranks mios-shim (6) -> APP.
- Invert the weights via SSOT -> the shim now wins. If the weights were
- baked in code this override would be ignored and APP would still win.
- "foobar" matches query "foo" at name_prefix; "a foo b" matches at
- name_word. Default ordering ranks name_prefix above name_word.
- Reorder so name_word outranks name_prefix -> WORD wins.
- Query "discrod" is a 2-edit typo of "discord" (token length 7).
- Require tokens >= 10 chars -> the 7-char query token is ineligible,
- so the typo no longer matches -> no match (exit 1).
- Tighten to <=1 edit -> the 2-edit typo no longer matches.
- "foreg fake" contains two tokens >=4 chars: "foreg" and "fake".
- "foreg" matches "forge" (edit dist 1), but "fake" matches nothing.
- It must NOT match because not all query tokens have a match.
- "wallpapr engine" contains "wallpapr" (matches "wallpaper" dist 1) and
- "engine" (matches "engine" dist 0). Both match, so it must succeed.

## usr/libexec/mios/test_mios_window_region.py
- (mios_window_region.region_rect / rect_from_layout). Asserts the named regions
- derive their rectangles from the LIVE work-area W/H with no pixel constants,

## usr/share/mios/agents/Containerfile
- mios-agents (A2O super-container) — ONE image containing:
- * code-server  : browser IDE (the "glass wall")
- * tmux         : the A2O war room
- * Claude Code  : Linux-native architect/operator engine
- * agy          : Antigravity CLI = Gemini 3.x operator engine
- * mios-a2o     : the Architect->Operator muxer harness
- Credentials are MOUNTED/entered at runtime (podman -v / secrets), NEVER baked.
- Base = code-server so the same container serves the IDE AND hosts the war room,
- sharing one filesystem + one tmux socket (native glass wall).
- IMPORTANT: agy + mios-a2o live in /usr/local/bin (a SYSTEM path), NOT in
- /home/coder/.local/bin -- mios-agents.service bind-mounts a persistent
- /var/lib/mios/agents over /home/coder (to keep agy/claude logins across
- restarts), which would otherwise SHADOW binaries placed under /home/coder.
- Claude Code CLI (architect + Linux-native operator engine) -> /usr/local/bin/claude
- agy -- Antigravity CLI (Gemini operator), native Linux build. Installed as coder
- (its installer targets ~/.local/bin), then copied to /usr/local/bin so the
- persistent /home/coder mount does not shadow it.
- the A2O muxer harness (engine-aware: agy|claude|gemini) + the mios-frontier
- launcher -- system path, mount-safe.
- Baked fallback for the orchestrator doctrine (mios-a2o also finds the LIVE copy
- under /mnt/mios-root via the PATH self-heal, so edits to the brief take effect
- without a rebuild).
- Self-heal PATH from the LIVE deployed root. /mnt/mios-root (the whole MiOS root)
- is bind-mounted RW into this container, so prefer the live mios / mios-a2o /
- mios-frontier + the mios-* toolset from there -- always CURRENT, never a
- baked-stale copy (operator-flagged: mios-frontier "command not found" inside a
- stale image). The baked /usr/local/bin copies remain the fallback when the root
- is not mounted. Applied to login (/etc/profile.d) AND interactive non-login
- (/etc/bash.bashrc) shells so the code-server terminal always resolves them.
- Default git identity + safe.directory so the war-room can commit the native
- workspace out-of-box (the operator overrides in-container if they want).
- code-server's default entrypoint keeps serving the browser IDE; the tmux war
- room is created on-demand by `mios-a2o` from the IDE terminal.

## usr/share/mios/agents/mios-a2o
- mios-a2o — Architect->Operator terminal-muxer harness for MiOS.
- A persistent tmux "war room" (inside the MiOS host / agents container) into which
- an ORCHESTRATOR (Claude Sonnet 5, main panel) dispatches build/debug tasks to two
- operator sub-agents — LANE A = Claude Opus 4.8 (framework + ~80%), LANE B = Gemini
- Flash 3.5 (finalize, last ~20%) — each in its own tmux window, tee'd to a log,
- with status tracking. Humans watch/steer via `tmux attach` or the code-server
- browser terminal attached to the same socket.
- ── FRONTIER ROLES ── main panel = ORCHESTRATOR; two sub-agent lanes A/B. Each role
- = engine + model + reasoning effort. These defaults are the single documented
- baseline (operator spec); the SSOT that overrides them is mios.toml
- [frontier], bridged to MIOS_A2O_* env via install.env -- NO-HARDCODE.
- Lane B degrade-open FALLBACK. When agy's Gemini account is quota-blocked (429) its
- generation returns empty and finalize work stalls; PREFER_FALLBACK routes Lane B to
- a Claude engine instead so the last ~20% still ships. Baselines EQUAL mios.toml
- [frontier].lane_b_fallback_* (SSOT, bridged via install.env) -- NO-HARDCODE. Empty
- engine/model degrade-open (see cmd_lane): unknown fallback => behave as agy today.
- Per-engine reasoning-effort flag TEMPLATE ({e} -> effort). EMPTY = omit the flag
- (degrade-open: never break an engine whose effort flag is unverified). Set the real
- flag for your installed CLI once confirmed in-container, e.g.
- MIOS_A2O_CLAUDE_EFFORT_FLAG='--reasoning-effort {e}'
- Orchestrator doctrine the Sonnet-5 main panel is seeded with (SSOT file; operator-
- editable). Resolved from the harness dir / the live root / the vendor path.
- True when the Lane-B prefer-fallback switch is set truthy (1/true/yes/on, any case).
- Render the reasoning-effort flag for an engine (empty template or effort -> none).
- Build the runtime exec line for an engine. $PROMPT is a RUNTIME variable (kept
- literal here). model/effort override the per-engine defaults (frontier roles pass
- them; plain dispatch leaves them empty -> legacy per-engine model, no effort).
- F-023: agy --print ALWAYS exits 0 and prints NOTHING to stdout on failure;
- its trace (incl. quota/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED lines) goes only to --log-file.
- Route it to a per-task debug log so the runner can detect silent failures.
- F-023: per-task agy debug/trace sink (agy exits 0 even on hard failure and hides
- its errors here). Lives under RUND, NOT LOGS, so it never matches the "$LOGS"/*.log
- glob that status/capture/follow scan (else it would show as a phantom task).
- Cleared alongside the task log so a re-dispatch can't match a stale error line.
- F-011 "everything streams": resolve the reasoning-stream flag + sink ONCE here
- (the parent holds the SSOT-bridged env; a tmux server snapshots its env at
- first-start, so a child runner can't rely on inheriting it) and BAKE the
- resolved values into the runner. Off by default -> _stream_on=0 -> the emit
- function is a no-op and the runner is byte-identical to before.
- F-023 anti-fabrication (AGY ONLY): agy --print returns 0 and empty stdout even on
- hard failure, so PIPESTATUS is a lie for agy. Bake a post-run detector that turns
- "empty response" OR a known error in the debug log into a real non-zero rc and
- surfaces a concise reason. For claude/gemini this variable is EMPTY, so the
- runner line below is byte-identical to before (the ${_agy_post} prefix vanishes).
- Run fallback
- !/usr/bin/env bash
- tail, which the agent-pipe folds into the mios_status reasoning channel it
- already publishes (OWUI/CLI/Discord subscribe to it). EVERY failure is
- swallowed: streaming must never break a dispatch (degrade-open).
- The war room runs inside the mios-agents container with host / mounted at
- \$A2O_MOUNT_ROOT; re-anchor the host-absolute sink under that mount when its
- raw parent dir is absent (running directly on the host uses the path as-is).
- name/engine are slug-constrained ([A-Za-z0-9._-] / a fixed engine set) and the
- transition text is digits+letters+space+'=', so the detail carries no JSON
- metacharacters -- safe to interpolate without escaping. TODO(finalize): to
- stream arbitrary LOG LINES (not just start/finish transitions) this needs a
- real JSON string-escape; transitions are the safe MVP the mandate asks for.
- Race-tolerant bound on the append-only sink. A lost trim just trims on a later
- append (the consumer reads only the tail + filters by ts, so a transient
- over-length file is harmless).
- Dispatch to a configured sub-agent role lane (engine+model+effort). Prompt on stdin.
- agy quota workaround: when prefer_fallback is on AND a fallback engine is
- actually set, route Lane B to the Claude fallback instead of agy so finalize
- work never stalls on a 429. Degrade-open: empty fallback engine => agy as
- today. Lane A and plain `dispatch` are untouched.
- !/usr/bin/env bash
- ── frontier-layout assertion (ENGINE-FREE) ── prove `frontier` lays out exactly
- 4 titled panes with the resolved role model ids. Launched headless into a
- throwaway session (MIOS_A2O_NOATTACH=1 so it never attaches). Degrade-open: a
- missing/unauthed engine still yields 4 panes — the orchestrator pane falls back
- to a shell, it does NOT vanish — so this passes with no claude/agy auth.
- Orchestrator launcher script (avoids tmux send-keys quoting hell). Sonnet-5
- interactive, model+effort pinned, seeded with the A2O doctrine via
- --append-system-prompt; degrade to a shell+help if the engine is missing.
- !/usr/bin/env bash
- pane0 = ORCHESTRATOR (left). Right column = LANE A / LANE B / MONITOR.

## usr/share/mios/agents/mios-agents-dev.sh
- Build + run the mios-agents DEV war-room from THIS repo and bring mios-frontier
- online on :8801 in the target composition (Sonnet-5 orchestrator + Opus-4.8 /
- Gemini-Flash-3.5 lanes). YOU run this.
- WSL fact this encodes: a /mnt/c (drvfs/9p) bind-mount is NOT writable from inside
- a podman container (rootless OR rootful) -- the agents could read but never EDIT
- the repo. So the war-room works on a NATIVE ext4 replica (writable) synced to
- GitHub (origin). Seed once from the repo (captures uncommitted edits), then it is
- git-managed -- re-runs rebuild+restart WITHOUT clobbering the workspace.
- The container's coder maps to a uid != the workspace owner (WSL userns quirk);
- make the native workspace writable by any container uid (dev workspace).
- Serve the IDE via ROOTFUL --network=host (rootless -p forwarding is unreliable
- under WSL, and --network=host conflicts with --userns=keep-id). Root also writes
- the native workspace cleanly. Stop the stale systemd service so it frees the port.

## usr/share/mios/agents/mios-forge-mirror.sh
- Create/refresh a Forgejo PULL-MIRROR of the GitHub MiOS repo. GitHub stays the
- canonical origin; Forgejo holds an auto-syncing local mirror (offline-first).
- NO-HARDCODE: owner + forge port are resolved from SSOT at runtime — never a
- literal. Resolution order (all runtime): $FORGE_OWNER override -> install.env
- identity (MIOS_FORGE_ADMIN_USER/MIOS_LINUX_USER/MIOS_USER) -> the SSOT-
- provisioned Forgejo admin account (queried live). Port from MIOS_PORT_FORGE_HTTP.
- The token is minted via the in-container admin CLI and piped straight into the
- API call — never printed. Idempotent (409 -> mirror-sync).
- Resolve owner from SSOT (never a literal).
- Mint a scoped token for OWNER, straight into the API call (never printed).

## usr/share/mios/base/Containerfile
- FROM, so containers/storage + composefs deduplicate the base layer ONCE across the whole offline
- bound-image store instead of pulling ~14 upstream sidecars with ~14 different bases (~60GB). Built
- from fedora-minimal (microdnf, ~100MB) + the common runtime every MiOS service needs; per-service
- images add only their small diff on top. This is the keystone of the container-consolidation refactor
- (WS-CONSOLIDATE): it makes the fat MIOS_BAKE_BOUND_IMAGES=1 store fit a normal builder AND stay
- offline-complete. NON-HARDCODE: version floats latest (SBOM-not-hardcode, ADR-0003).
- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Sized from research (wjoekgit0): fedora-minimal ~100MB on-disk / ~32MB compressed (microdnf, no
- systemd/python by default); UBI-micro distroless is ~2.6x smaller than standard but has NO in-image
- package manager -- MiOS service builds need microdnf/dnf at build time, so fedora-minimal is the pick.
- Common runtime shared by MiOS service containers (kept DELIBERATELY minimal -- per-service deps go
- in the derived image, not here). weak-deps off + nodocs + purge docs/man/locale so the shared layer
- stays as small as possible; every byte here is paid ONCE across all derived services (that is the
- whole point). tini gives derived multi-service images a proper PID1 reaper; shadow-utils lets each
- service run under its own non-root uid (Law 6 UNPRIVILEGED).
- Non-root by default; derived images create their own service users and may override.
- Shared, hardened defaults every MiOS service inherits.
- Derived MiOS service images (mios-web, mios-data, mios-observ, ...) start FROM localhost/mios-base
- and add ONLY their service binaries/venvs -- so the store = mios-base (once) + N small diffs.

## usr/share/mios/crawl4ai/Containerfile
- MiOS slim crawl4ai image -- NO bundled Chromium.
- Why this exists: the dev VM host is Python 3.14, which has no prebuilt
- wheels for crawl4ai's deps (lxml et al), so a host venv can't build. This
- image pins Python 3.12 (full wheel coverage) JUST for the crawl engine.
- Engines (operator directive 2026-05-24):
- PRIMARY  : crawl4ai attaches to the EXISTING host Chrome over CDP
- (ws://127.0.0.1:9222, the ChromeDev flatpak). The quadlet runs
- this image with Network=host so 127.0.0.1:9222 IS the host's
- Chrome. NO Chromium is bundled or downloaded here.
- FAIL-RETRY: camoufox (stealth Firefox) -- the ONLY browser that lives in
- this image (~150MB), the anti-detect fallback. Its Firefox
- runtime libs come from `playwright install-deps firefox`.
- MiOS build host = WSL2, whose NAT has no working IPv6. Make glibc's resolver
- prefer IPv4 (covers pip/PyPI, camoufox fetch, playwright, git) and force apt
- to IPv4 -- without this, apt-get update and pip stall on the IPv6 addresses
- deb.debian.org / pypi.org return (operator 2026-06-12).
- crawl4ai CORE (CDP attach -- we never run crawl4ai-setup, so no Chromium)
- + camoufox (stealth Firefox) + the slim FastAPI service stack. playwright
- is pulled in for its Firefox dep-installer below.
- Firefox runtime system libraries for headless camoufox (gtk/x11/alsa/...).
- playwright ships the canonical dependency installer for the firefox set.
- Bake camoufox's patched stealth Firefox (~150MB) into the image so the
- fail-retry path is ready offline at runtime.
- The service module is MOUNTED at runtime (quadlet Volume) so it can be
- iterated without an image rebuild.

## usr/share/mios/cuda/Containerfile
- --- Llama-swap source (the light-LLM-lane binaries -- ghcr, small) ---
- The vLLM + SGLang "source" stages were REMOVED. They pulled the ~47GB
- docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai + docker.io/lmsysorg/sglang whale images ONLY to
- COPY /usr/local -> /opt/{vllm,sglang}-venv, but NOTHING consumed those venvs:
- the heavy LLM lanes run the vLLM/SGLang CONTAINER images directly via their
- Quadlets (mios-llm-heavy / -alt, firstboot-pulled -- see mios.toml
- [build.bake].firstboot_tokens). Baking them re-pulled the whales at BUILD time
- -> disk overrun + Docker Hub rate limit on CI runners, and bloated mios-cuda
- with dead venvs. Removed to keep the whales strictly firstboot-tier.
- --- Final/Main CUDA Base Image Stage ---
- Install CUDA packages and runtime dependencies
- Upstream ghcr.io/mostlygeek/llama-swap:cuda now ships llama-server + llama-swap TOGETHER with their
- shared libraries (libggml*/libllama*.so) under /app. llama-server is a thin (~17KB) binary that
- dynamically loads those /app .so's at runtime -- so copying ONLY the binary (the old
- `COPY --from=.../usr/bin/llama-server`) both fails now (path moved off /usr/bin, 2026-07) AND would
- ship a binary that can't find its libs. Copy the WHOLE /app tree, register it on the dynamic-loader
- path, and expose the two binaries on PATH via symlinks. Verified against the live image (paths located,
- not hardcoded-guessed): /app/llama-server, /app/llama-swap + libggml*/libllama* .so siblings.

## usr/share/mios/owui/pipes/mios_agent_pipe.py
- ─── Qwen-style XML function-call markup the model sometimes leaks ────
- ─── Narration line classifier (kept IN SYNC with mios_antimeta_filter) ──
- Anchored to start-of-line; matches the meta-speak the operator wants
- collapsed into <think>...</think> rather than showing in the answer.
- ─── hermes-tail bridge polling ──────────────────────────────────────
- ── Retired database best-effort writer ─────────────────────────────────────
- Migration note: the legacy DB is retired. Cross-agent state is now managed by
- PostgreSQL/pgvector via agent-pipe. The writes in this class are retired.
- Resilience: writes are FIRE-AND-FORGET via asyncio.create_task so the
- streaming response is never delayed. A 30s "DB down" backoff prevents
- hammering a downed endpoint on every chat turn.
- Absent-value sentinels (mirror server.py _ENV_SENTINELS) -- case-insensitive so
- OWUI's 'Unknown'/'undefined'/'n/a' geo never overrides a real value nor slips
- through. Shared by _collect_env_vars across all env channels (operator
- the prior ad-hoc {None,'','None','Unknown'} checks were case-
- sensitive and disagreed with the server).
- ── In-pipe CPU refinement (operator-architecture) ──
- MiOS-Agent IS the CPU refiner -- it sits in front of hermes,
- takes the user's raw prompt, calls a small CPU model on
- local inference lanes, and forwards a refined / contextualized prompt to
- the heavy orchestrator. Sub-second target. Operator:
- "OWUI's MIOS_AGENT OPERATES ON THE CPU MODEL ... QUICKLY
- REFINING THE USERS PROMPTS WITH MORE CONTEXT AND CLEARER
- DIRECTIONS FOR HERMES AGENTS/DELEGATED SUB-AGENTS".
- ── Output refinement (operator-architecture) ──
- The downstream agent dispatch (hermes-agent today; later
- opencode / MCP / delegated subagents the same way) emits a
- mix of narration, tool I/O, and final result. MiOS-Agent
- wraps the WHOLE raw stream as <details type="reasoning">
- collapsed thinking, then runs a CPU polish pass to produce
- the operator-facing answer.
- Operator quote: "ALL MiOS-Agent(OWUI)'s dispatches
- (MiOS-Hermes, MiOS-OpenCode, etc) are always capturing their
- outputs as thinking and providing an appropriate final
- answer normally in OWUI chats".
- ── Phase-2 Critic loop (see docs/multi-agent-architecture.md)
- The Critic Agent reviews the compose draft against the
- structured tool history. If the draft claims success on a
- tool that failed, claims a step ran when no tool_call for
- it exists, or otherwise mismatches the structured truth,
- critic returns issues; compose revises once. Bounded loop.
- Router (layer-1 classifier): dispatch | chat | agent.
- Operator directive "prompt refining should be tool
- aware to be able to hint". The refine system prompt has a
- {tool_table} placeholder filled at init from the YAML manifest
- at /usr/share/mios/owui/tool-hints.yaml. Adding a new shim =
- one YAML entry, no prompt rewrite.
- Build the tool table once at init; pipe restart picks up
- YAML edits.
- 1. Frontend-captured variables (browser locale/timezone/geo). Keys
- arrive as the full "{{TOKEN}}" literal.
- 1b. body['variables'] -- OWUI's pipe contract ALSO carries the frontend
- variables dict here (the same dict the server's _client_env reads);
- the pipe previously read ONLY __metadata__['variables'].
- 1.5 LIVE-GEO RECOVERY. OWUI's BACKEND substitutes
- {{USER_LOCATION}} into the SYSTEM-PROMPT TEXT (the SSOT template
- carries "location is {{USER_LOCATION}}."), NOT into the structured
- variables the Pipe sees -- so the iPhone's live geo reaches the model
- but was invisible to the orchestrator's grounding / refine / web-
- search. Recover it from the resolved system message so it flows to
- :8640 as a structured fact. Anchored on the SSOT wording; requires an
- alphanumeric value (so a stripped "location is ." can't match) and
- no leftover "{{"; best-effort -- degrades to prior behaviour on miss.
- Match the prose form ("...location is <v>.") AND the labelled
- env-block form ("User location: <v>" / "location = <v>").
- 2. Host clock -- fills CURRENT_* the frontend/OWUI may have left.
- 3. __user__ fields (name/email/persisted-profile location).
- Strip any token we could not resolve so no literal {{...}}
- reaches the model (the template wording treats a missing fact
- as "not provided").
- Inject a noop placeholder so .format() doesn't KeyError.
- Compact markdown table: name | intent | example. Three
- columns keeps each row scannable; the model uses the
- 'intent' column to match the user's ask.
- Optional intent_patterns block -- per-pattern hints for
- composite asks the verb table alone doesn't cover.
- OWUI dropdown shows `<function.name><pipe.name>` with no
- separator. The function row's name is already "MiOS-Agent",
- so we leave the pipe.name EMPTY -- otherwise the dropdown
- reads "MiOS-AgentMiOS-Agent" (operator-flagged).
- ─── CPU REFINEMENT (in-pipe, sub-second target) ─────────────
- Architecture: MiOS-Agent (this pipe) IS the prompt enhancer.
- Operator: "OWUI's MIOS_AGENT OPERATES ON THE CPU MODEL ...
- IS QUICKLY REFINING THE USERS PROMPTS WITH MORE CONTEXT AND
- CLEARER DIRECTIONS FOR HERMES AGENTS/DELEGATED SUB-AGENTS".
- The pipe owns this step end-to-end:
- 1. Receive raw user text
- 2. Call a small CPU model (default qwen3.5:4b)
- with a tight system prompt -- num_predict capped low,
- keep_alive=-1, num_gpu=0, native /api/chat endpoint
- 3. Return the refined text -- forwarded as the user message
- to the prefilter -> hermes chain
- The refiner runs INLINE in the pipe so the operator sees it
- as a discrete OWUI status emit ("🧠 refining via qwen3.5:4b
- on CPU...") rather than as an invisible sidecar pre-step.
- Curly-quote (U+2019) tolerant. Operator-flagged
- "How's it going?" (with smart-quote apostrophe) fell through the
- gate -> triggered the dashboard rule and the agent dumped
- mios-system-status as the answer to a greeting. Both ' (U+0027)
- and ' (U+2019) now match the optional apostrophe slot.
- Operator directive GLOBAL SWEEP to remove hardcoded
- English. The conversational gate now matches greetings/acks/
- farewells across the languages the operator's chats commonly
- use. New languages can be added without code review by editing
- the alternation. The bare-name list (hi, hola, etc.) covers
- standalone tokens; the phrase list covers multi-word openers.
- English / generic. The "X there"/"X y'all"/"X everyone"
- forms (Hey there!, Hi y'all, Hello everyone) are bundled
- in the leading-word alternation so they also short-circuit
- to skip-refine. Operator-flagged "Hey there!"
- was inflating from 10c to 111c via refine because the
- 1-word gate failed to match.
- Spanish / Portuguese
- French
- Italian
- German / Dutch / Nordics
- Slavic (Latin transliteration tolerated; native scripts below)
- Asian (Latin)
- Other / multilingual
- Native-script openers (single-line)
- Refine system prompt — standard schema-driven refinement prompt.
- Tool-aware: the {tool_table} placeholder is filled at runtime
- from /usr/share/mios/owui/tool-hints.yaml.
- ── Output polish system prompt ──
- The output-refinement pass runs AFTER the agent dispatch (hermes
- today; opencode / MCP / delegate children the same way) has
- streamed its raw output. The raw output is preserved verbatim
- inside a collapsed <details type="reasoning"> block; this polish
- pass produces the operator-facing answer.
- Hard constraints (these are the failure modes from operator
- chats we're closing):
- * RAW OUTPUT is ground truth. NEVER invent paths, IDs, numbers,
- statuses, app names, registry coords, port numbers, etc.
- * Strip narration. "Let me", "I'll", "First I...", "Now I'll"
- are agent thinking; the operator sees the polished answer
- only -- they don't need to read the agent's stream of
- consciousness.
- * If the agent failed, say what failed in ONE sentence + surface
- the verbatim error.
- * NO "would you like me to..." trailing questions unless the
- agent's raw output already proposed exactly that.
- * NO suggestions to "try X if Y" unless the agent surfaced X.
- Cheap heuristic: if there's no narration marker AND the output
- is short, skip the polish call entirely (saves 30-180s of CPU
- for a result that's already clean).
- "Looks like structured markdown" -- a heading line OR a markdown
- table separator (`|---|`). When raw output starts with one of
- these, hermes is already shaping the answer; polish has nothing
- to add and a non-trivial chance of mangling it.
- Known agent-error signatures: if the raw output contains these,
- ALWAYS polish (so the "KNOWN AGENT ERRORS" rewrites in the polish
- prompt have a chance to clean them up).
- WSLg gaslighting (operator-flagged after agent ran 6 calls
- then claimed all three of these to refuse opening gnome-control-center)
- Native multi-agent compose -- structured handoff from Hermes
- session JSON (operator directive "HOW WOULD THIS
- MULTI_AGENTIC_REASONING WORK NATIVELY!??? RESEARCH!" + "make
- sure this is ALL ALSO OpenAI API COMPLIANT and COMPLETELY
- FUnctional on a Bootc Bootable OCI MiOS image").
- Architecture (see /usr/share/mios/docs/multi-agent-architecture.md
- for the full research + migration plan):
- Phase 1 (this code): Compose reads Hermes session JSON for
- the OpenAI-format tool_calls + tool_result message history,
- reasons over STRUCTURE instead of text-mangled stream.
- Phase 2 (future):    Add explicit Critic Agent loop on
- iGPU micro-LLM (qwen3:1.7b).
- Phase 3 (future):    Refine emits JSON {intent, plan} rather
- than INTENT/TOOLS/DELEGATE/PLAN labels.
- Phase 4 (future):    Drop regex post-processors (think /
- details strip, KNOWN_AGENT_ERROR_RE, etc.).
- OpenAI compliance: the tool_call + tool_result shape is the
- standard OpenAI Chat Completions message format. Hermes
- records exactly this in session JSON; we surface it untouched
- to the compose model. Any OpenAI-API-compatible model
- (Claude, GPT-*, local engines) can consume the structured
- input identically.
- Older than the dispatch -- not this turn's session.
- Keep only the operator-relevant slice: the LAST
- user-message and every message after it.
- Build call-id -> result-content index
- Trim noisy content for the compose prompt.
- ── Router classifier system prompt + dispatch ─────────────────
- Micro-LLM gets a terse tool list + the user's prompt; emits
- JSON {action, tool?, args?, reply?}. JSON Mode (inference
- /v1/chat/completions response_format) constrains the output --
- no parsing tax.
- Best-effort event: layer-1 router verdict.
- Map verb name -> shell command. Keep this in lockstep with
- mios_verbs.Tools method bodies.
- Use mios-launch, NOT mios-find: mios-launch scans the
- live environment in the operator-expected priority order
- (internal-service alias -> URL -> Windows GUI builtin ->
- browser CDP -> Windows games-cache -> MiOS shim -> Linux
- GUI -> plain CLI). mios-find's "best match" scoring puts
- MiOS shims ahead of real apps which caused "launch steam"
- to resolve to mios-steamcmd (a CLI shim) instead of the
- actual operator-installed Steam client. mios-launch is
- the environment-generative path: games-cache is populated
- by mios-apps at runtime, not from a baked priority list.
- No 2>/dev/null filter -- the broker's CAPTURE_JSON
- protocol (used below) now returns stdout / stderr / exit
- SEPARATELY, so English narrative on stderr lands in
- tool_result.stderr (labeled-as-stderr in the envelope)
- instead of polluting tool_result.output.
- Operator directive "all focused/re-focused apps
- that are opened/focused are resized and launch as per default
- params". A bare focus that leaves the window at whatever
- geometry it last had violates this -- re-focused windows
- must also re-apply the default golden+16:10-centered
- placement unless the operator named another position OR
- explicitly opted out via position="as-is".
- mios-window <pos> implies a raise -- but chain focus
- explicitly so the geometry change happens AFTER the
- window is foregrounded (some WMs ignore size requests
- on hidden/minimized windows). MIOS_LAUNCH_POSITION
- is exported so the place_block reads the same enum
- mios-windows launch consumes.
- Linux-side filesystem search -- the agentic peer to
- everything_search (which is Windows-only via Voidtools).
- Operator directive "MiOS-Agent(s) can navigate,
- search, exec--all the same in the Linux Environments as well".
- systemctl is-active + status snapshot for a Linux service.
- Read-only. Picks system bus by default; passes through
- whatever the operator named.
- systemctl restart <name>. WRITE verb -- visible side
- effect on the operator's system. Returns the post-restart
- is-active line so the agent can confirm.
- ps snapshot sorted by RSS (default) or CPU. limit caps lines.
- filter is a case-insensitive substring on the command name.
- podman ps -a snapshot (all containers, including stopped).
- No filter = all; filter = case-insensitive substring on name.
- podman restart <name>. WRITE verb. Confirms by showing the
- post-restart status line.
- Broker dispatch (same socket Tools.* uses).
- Capture call start for tool_call.latency_ms.
- CAPTURE_JSON: protocol -- broker returns a single
- JSON line with {stdout, stderr, exit_code} so we can
- bucket English narrative on stderr into its own
- envelope field (instead of mixing with structured
- tool_result.output). Backward-compat CAPTURE: stays
- available on the broker for older callers.
- Best-effort retired write: tool_call row. Carries session id
- if pipe() opened one this turn (self._session_id). Output is
- truncated to keep the row compact.
- session is a record link; assign as a raw expression
- (record-id literals aren't JSON-quoted).
- Short + clean -> skip (original case)
- Long but structured markdown -> skip (new case)
- Even on skip-polish, strip reasoning leaks ("Thought\n\n",
- <think>...</think>, <details>...</details>) from the
- raw text. Hermes uses reasoning-mode models that emit
- these prefixes; the operator should never see them.
- Operator-flagged "Hey there!" returned
- "Thought\n\nHello! How can I assist you today?" because
- polish skipped and the leading "Thought" passed through.
- Try to load the structured tool history from Hermes session
- JSON (OpenAI-format messages with tool_calls + tool_result).
- When available, compose reasons over STRUCTURE; when not,
- falls back to the legacy text-blob path. Operator directive
- to keep this OpenAI-API-compliant + Day-0-bootc.
- Append the structured tool history at the bottom of the
- system prompt when available. The model sees the legacy
- text-blob raw_output AND the structured tool_history; the
- structured part is authoritative for success/fail reasoning.
- Sanity check: if polish is suspiciously short vs raw, suspect
- truncation; pass raw through with a one-line summary header.
- Strip the outer ```markdown ... ``` wrapper if the model
- ignored the no-fence rule. The system prompt explicitly
- forbids this but qwen2.5-coder:7b sometimes does it anyway,
- and OWUI then renders the WHOLE answer as a code block
- (operator-flagged every polished response was
- showing as raw markdown source instead of rendered markup).
- Strip <think>...</think> + leading "Thought" leaks.
- ── Phase-2 Critic reflexion loop ──────────────────────────
- Only runs when we HAVE structured tool history to reason
- over (the critic's whole value-add is checking the draft
- against ground truth); skipped on the text-blob fallback
- path. Bounded by CRITIC_MAX_ITERATIONS.
- Re-compose with the critic's issues fed back.
- Strip code fences a chatty model might add.
- Best-effort event: critic verdict.
- Match a leading ```markdown / ``` fence. The closing ``` is
- OPTIONAL because polish sometimes truncates mid-output (token
- cap hit on a long table) -- in that case there's an open fence
- with no close, and OWUI renders the WHOLE answer as a code
- block. We strip the open fence either way; if a close exists
- at end-of-text we also drop that. Operator-flagged
- MiOS System Dashboard table came back wrapped in ```markdown
- because polish ran out of tokens before closing the fence.
- Reasoning leakage in polish output (operator-flagged
- "<think>I need to use the Windows tool instead..." rendered as
- part of the final answer). Strip <think>...</think>, <reasoning>
- ...</reasoning>, and bare "Thought\n\n<text>" pattern leaks.
- Polish sometimes emits an additional <details type="reasoning">
- block in its output, on top of the agent-thinking <details> the
- pipe already wrapped. Operator-flagged chat showed
- two stacked <details> blocks. The polished answer must NEVER
- contain a <details>; that wrapper is the pipe's job, not the
- polish model's.
- Only unwrap if the inner content itself doesn't START with
- a fence (preserves answers that genuinely lead with a code
- block as their first element).
- Sanitized emit (no model name); see polish emit comment above.
- qwen3.5-family thinking-mode -- final answer empty,
- thinking field has the trace. Use it but mark.
- Route to the CPU refine/polish model, not to Hermes.
- Strip any sampling overrides that would slow the small model
- down on trivial gen tasks.
- Cap token budget on task-gen so a runaway generation doesn't
- eat a full polish-sized output for a title.
- mios-llm-light exposes /v1/chat/completions as an OpenAI-compatible
- endpoint -- same request + streaming shape as the BACKEND_URL
- OWUI was hitting before. No client-side transform needed.
- Task-gen calls are short -- bound the timeout tighter than user chats.
- Only process up to the last newline; anything after stays buffered.
- head already excludes the trailing newline; restore it for splitlines.
- 1) ACTION proposal -> confirmation dialog -> run on OK.
- 2) CLARIFICATION question -> input dialog -> continue with the typed answer.
- __event_call__ (OWUI >= v0.3.8) BLOCKS + returns the user's choice from a
- native dialog -- used to render the ask-to-run PROPOSAL as a real
- confirmation popup ("OWUI... handle asking with prompts").
- ── Task-generation bypass (OWUI internal calls) ─────────────
- OWUI calls the same model for title / tags / follow-up /
- autocomplete / query / image-prompt generation. These calls
- come WITH __task__ set + expect raw JSON or short labels back
- (NOT refined, NOT wrapped in <details>, NOT polished into
- markdown). Running them through refinement+polish strips the
- JSON the followup template asks for -- which is why
- ENABLE_FOLLOW_UP_GENERATION=True yields no followups in OWUI
- (operator-flagged). Detect + passthrough.
- Some OWUI versions stash task in metadata.task instead of __task__
- Sanitized: no model name in the emit; task_kind is the
- OWUI-defined identifier (title_generation, etc.) and
- stays cross-locale.
- Resolve / strip OWUI template tokens on every system message
- FIRST: backfill any {{...}} OWUI left unresolved ({{USER_LANGUAGE}}
- / {{CURRENT_TIMEZONE}} are frontend-only and leak when the browser
- didn't send them; direct-API callers get no substitution at all)
- and strip the rest so no literal token reaches the model
- (- the leaked/locale-pinned language tokens
- were behind the wrong-language + dual-language replies).
- Per-user PERSONA (UserValves) -- inject AFTER OWUI's already-
- substituted vendor system prompt (with {{USER_NAME}}/locale vars)
- and BEFORE the user turn, so the operator's fields augment the
- environment-grounded base. Empty persona -> no-op.
- Status emits use short symbol+term form, no English narrative
- (operator directive GLOBAL SWEEP -- "remove any
- hardcoded english (other than generic technically accurate
- terminologies)"). Tool/model names stay since they're
- cross-locale identifiers; verbs like "receiving" -> emoji.
- (No hardcoded status pill here. The live thinking stream + the
- tail-derived generative status carry the activity. Operator
- "nothing hardcoded -- pure streamed + generative".)
- ── Retired database session open ──────────────────────────────────
- Open a session row for this OWUI turn; subsequent tool_call /
- event writes link back via SET session = <record_id>. Fire-
- and-forget so the DB write never delays streaming. Per-turn
- session (not per-chat) -- aligns with OWUI's pipe lifecycle
- where each turn is a fresh pipe() invocation.
- The retired database returned record-id as "table:hashid"
- already in unquoted form.
- Collect + forward chat identity as the OpenAI-standard `metadata`
- object (string values, <=16 pairs) so :8640 keys its per-chat agent
- scratchpad off a stable conversation id..
- Forward the resolved OWUI ENVIRONMENT (location / timezone / locale /
- datetime / weekday / name) to :8640 as metadata.variables -- OWUI's
- own braced-key shape. The agent-pipe orchestrator reads it (server.py
- _client_env) to resolve 'near me' to the real location, set temporal
- grounding to the USER's timezone, and answer in the user's locale.
- Before this the env only reached a {{...}} system-prompt placeholder,
- so refine/swarm/web-search never saw the location -> 'near me' became
- an unfillable '[user location]' placeholder (
- 'didnt use detected environments details ... OWUI provides entire
- environment details ... USE them in the pipeline'). Values are length-
- capped; absent-value sentinels already dropped in _collect_env_vars.
- Tag the invocation SURFACE so the orchestrator knows WHERE the turn
- came from ("OWUI should know where it's being
- spoken to from ... aware of all env details for all chat surfaces").
- The agent-pipe (_client_env) reads metadata.variables.surface.
- Extract the last user message text (used by router + refine).
- ── Layer-1 ROUTER -- DELEGATED to mios-agent-pipe service ──
- The router + dispatch + chat-fast-path + database writes
- are owned by the standalone agent-pipe service at :8640 now
- (operator directive "discord chats not going
- through MiOS-Agent paths" -- extracted the chain into a
- gateway-agnostic service so Hermes Discord + future
- Slack/Telegram get the same tool surface). The OWUI pipe
- POSTs to agent-pipe (BACKEND_URL = :8640) which runs the
- router and either returns a tool_calls envelope (dispatch),
- a short reply (chat), or streams hermes content (agent path).
- OWUI-specific behaviors RETAINED in this shim:
- - task-gen bypass (above)
- - tail_watcher (Hermes-internal tool_call emits via the
- /var/lib/mios/hermes-tail/latest.json sideband)
- - mios_status SSE field translation (below) -- agent-pipe
- emits {emoji, label, done} markers on each phase; the
- translator below calls _emit() so the OWUI status pill
- stays lit during dispatch/chat/agent paths
- - CPU REFINE / CRITIC / POLISH (kept below; these add
- OWUI-specific quality but aren't ported to agent-pipe
- yet -- Step 2b if Discord needs them too)
- ── CPU REFINEMENT (in-pipe) ─────────────────────────────────
- Extract the last user message, refine via the small CPU model,
- replace the user message in-place with the refined text. The
- downstream chain (prefilter -> hermes) sees the enriched
- prompt, not the raw input.
- OpenAI multi-part content shape: pick the first text segment
- Write back as a plain string (downstream tolerates both)
- Forward the STABLE OWUI conversation id to the agent-pipe so its conv-scoped
- state is stable ACROSS TURNS of this chat -- specifically the ask-to-run pending
- proposals ("ask user to run things"). OWUI hands the chat_id
- in __metadata__, not the body, so without this the agent-pipe falls back to a
- per-request id and the next-turn "yes" can't find the proposal. Degrade-open.
- Humanistic "got it" emission while we hand the prompt
- over to agent-pipe. agent-pipe will emit its own casual
- phase strip (📡 listening / ✨ thinking / 🧭 picking the
- right helper / 🤖 working on it) once it picks up the
- request -- this pipe just acknowledges receipt so the
- operator sees activity during the handoff latency.
- (No hardcoded "got it" pill -- generative status comes from the
- live hermes-tail work stream below..)
- Mark the dispatch moment so compose (after hermes finishes
- streaming) can find the matching Hermes session JSON by
- mtime > _dispatch_ts. Shared mutable scratch location:
- /var/lib/mios/hermes/sessions/ (operator directive
- "shared global scratpad(s) in mutable locations").
- Unbounded sock_read (LLM stream can idle 10s+ between chunks on
- CPU); only sock_connect bounded so we don't hang if the backend
- is down. TIMEOUT_S=0 => unbounded total.
- ── ALL agent dispatch output is captured + wrapped as
- collapsible <details type="reasoning">. After the stream
- ends, the polish pass emits the operator-facing answer.
- Operator architecture "ALL MiOS-Agent(OWUI)'s
- dispatches (MiOS-Hermes, MiOS-OpenCode, etc) are always
- capturing their outputs as thinking and providing an
- appropriate final answer normally in OWUI chats".
- Operator-flagged open `<details>` was being
- yielded EAGERLY before hermes responded -- if hermes was
- cold-loading a model (30-90s) the operator saw the open tag
- alone, and if hermes returned empty, the close was missed
- and OWUI rendered the rest of the message as
- collapsed-reasoning. Fix: lazy-open. We only emit the open
- tag the first time a real chunk arrives. _details_opened
- tracks state so the close path knows whether to emit a
- matching close.
- `done="true"` tells OWUI to render the block as a
- complete (collapsed-by-default) reasoning dropdown the
- operator can click to expand. Without it OWUI keeps the
- block open + spinning forever -- operator-flagged
- "Thinking doesn't collapse(or stream/emit!)".
- Live, GENERATIVE thinking: poll the hermes-tail (the AI's actual
- tool/reasoning events) and stream them INTO the reasoning dropdown
- as they happen; close it when the answer begins. The latest work
- line doubles as the status chip -- no hardcoded label map.
- "pure streamed + generative from the AI
- pipeline(s)". last-seen ts starts at dispatch so we never replay
- the historical buffer.
- BUFFER reasoning deltas and emit ONE complete <details type="reasoning">
- block when the answer starts, instead of streaming an OPEN <details>
- that OWUI shows INLINE in the chat for the whole (1-2 min) research
- phase and only collapses once the answer closes it (
- "thinking leaks into chat field before moving to think"). Live progress
- still streams via the transient mios_status pills (separate channel).
- LIVE thinking: stream the orchestrator's reasoning_content deltas as
- <think>...</think> tags in the CONTENT channel. This is OWUI's
- canonical, default-on reasoning path (DEFAULT_REASONING_TAGS in
- backend utils/middleware.py): OWUI extracts the tag-interior text
- into the native Thinking dropdown LIVE, token by token, WITHOUT
- leaking it into the chat field, and collapses it when </think>
- arrives. Replaces the old buffer-and-dump of a literal
- <details type="reasoning"> block -- that is OWUI's STORAGE form, not
- an input: emitting it raw bypassed the live-stream state machine and
- risked removeAllDetails() stripping, so the dropdown never populated
- live ("thinking doesnt show up still!"; research:
- OWUI PR #9241 / issue #23923 / docs reasoning-models). ONE think
- block per turn: opened on the first reasoning delta, closed when the
- answer begins (or at stream end / timeout / error).
- Nothing to close yet -- we never opened.
- The agent-pipe now STREAMS Hermes's inline output
- as self-contained <details type="reasoning">
- blocks directly in the content channel (operator
- "stream all of Hermes's inline output
- into checkpointed reasoning blocks"). The pipe no
- longer polls the hermes-tail to build its own
- dropdown -- that duplicated the streamed blocks.
- It just forwards content + the agent-pipe's
- mios_status pills below.
- agent-pipe injects mios_status on content-empty
- chunks for the dispatch FAST PATH + orchestration
- phases (no hermes-tail there). Forward it as the
- status pill so those keep feedback; the agent
- path's live THINKING comes from the tail above.
- Agent-pipe now streams the live thinking on the
- STANDARD delta.reasoning_content channel (
- keystone refactor). Re-wrap it as OWUI's
- <details type="reasoning"> dropdown so OWUI shows a
- live Thinking block, while strict clients hitting the
- agent-pipe directly (Firefox Smart Window) ignore
- reasoning_content and get only the clean answer.
- Stream reasoning LIVE inside a <think> block.
- Open it on the first fragment; OWUI routes the
- interior to the Thinking dropdown as it arrives.
- First answer content -> CLOSE the live think block so
- OWUI collapses it, then stream the clean answer.
- Empty/early-exit turn: close the live think block if the answer
- never arrived, so OWUI doesn't render an orphaned open <think>.
- If polish is OFF, the legacy flow already emitted text
- via yield above; nothing more to do.
- ASK-TO-RUN native prompt: render any proposed
- action as a native confirmation dialog + run it on approval.
- Polish: CPU pass to clean narration + surface concrete
- results. Falls back to raw on any error.
- ASK-TO-RUN native prompt ("OWUI... handle asking with
- prompts"): if the agent proposed an action, show a NATIVE confirmation dialog
- + run it on approval. raw_text (not polished) carries the proposal block.
- Close the live <think> block ONLY if it actually opened, so we
- never orphan a tag on empty-stream / cold-load timeouts.

## usr/share/mios/owui/pipes/mios_antimeta_filter.py
- Lines that match any of these REGEXEN are wrapped in <think>...</think>
- instead of being passed through verbatim. Each is intentionally
- anchored to the START of a stripped line (text.strip()) so we only
- catch lines whose lead phrase is meta-narration -- prose that
- happens to contain "let me check" mid-sentence is left alone.
- splitlines drops trailing newline; preserve it if original had one

## usr/share/mios/owui/pipes/mios_sidecar_filter.py
- ─── Where each sibling agent writes its state ────────────────────────
- Two writers feed this filter:
- * mios-hermes-tail        -> hermes-tail/latest.json (in-flight tools)
- * mios-delegation-prefilter -> delegation-prefilter/latest.json (refiner)
- * mios-daemon (consolidated micro-LLM) -> daemon/state.json with
- three sub-objects (classify/refusal/cron) that mirror the old
- per-service files. ONE poll -> three categories of events.
- The unified mios-daemon state file replaces the three predecessor
- files (nudger / log-watcher / cron-director) -- the daemon writes
- them under a single roof. Old per-service paths are kept in the
- fallback table below ONLY for compatibility with hosts that haven't
- rebooted into the consolidated daemon yet; they'll be removed in a
- future commit once the migration window closes.
- NEW unified daemon
- Legacy fallbacks (pre-mios-daemon hosts -- deprecated)
- ─── Per-chat last-seen-mtime cache ──────────────────────────────
- ─── Per-agent formatters: each returns a short status string ────
- Expected shape: {"ts", "events": [...], "active_session_count",
- "inflight_subagents"}. Surfaces the MOST RECENT
- event with priority weighting -- chronic failure modes
- (invalid_tool, max_retries) are highlighted; routine tool
- calls only emit if no failure is in the recent window.
- Priority sort: failures first, then synthesis/spawn, then routine.
- Expected shape: {"trigger": "<phrase>", "model": "...", "ts": ...}
- Expected: {"tag": "...", "count": N, "ts": ...} or {"events": [...]}
- Expected: {"last_fire": {"rule": "...", "ts": ...}}
- ─── Formatters for the unified mios-daemon state file ─────────
- Sub-objects under daemon/state.json: {classify, refusal, cron}.
- Each formatter reads its OWN sub-key from the same blob; the
- three SIBLING_AGENTS entries for "daemon-*" all point at the
- same file but render different categories.
- Expected: {"original": "...", "refined": "...", "ts": ...}
- ─── Walk every sibling file, emit only NEW activity ─────────────
- Skip if older than staleness window
- Skip if we already emitted this mtime for this chat
- ─── OWUI Filter contract ────────────────────────────────────────
- Brief settle delay so nudger/log-watcher have a chance to react
- to THIS turn's response before we read their state.

## usr/share/mios/owui/tools/mios_verbs.py
- Phase-3 migration (operator directive "What's ALL NATIVE
- to OpenAI API and industry standards"): typed Literal[...] enums
- replace SOUL.md prose rules. OWUI's introspector emits these as
- JSONSchema `enum: [...]` constraints; strict-mode function calling
- enforces them client-side -- the model CANNOT emit an invalid
- position value, so the schema teaches the surface instead of a
- 700-line rule book.
- Position enum: "default" is the MiOS global launch geometry
- (operator directive) -- a 16:10 window sized at
- screen_width / phi (golden ratio ~0.618) and centered on the
- primary monitor's WorkingArea. Concretely on 1920x1080:
- W = 1920 / 1.618 ~= 1186
- H = W * 10/16    ~= 741
- centered at      (367, 169)
- Use "as-is" to OPT OUT (leave wherever the OS placed it).
- "center" = native-size centered (no resize).
- CAPTURE_JSON: returns a single JSON line {stdout, stderr, exit_code}
- so we get clean per-stream output for the agent envelope (English
- narratives from downstream tools land in stderr, structured data
- in stdout). Fire-and-forget calls (capture=False) keep the legacy
- plain-text protocol ("OK" / "ERROR: ...").
- Parse the JSON line. If parsing fails (e.g. broker pre-dates
- CAPTURE_JSON support and replied with raw bytes), fall back to
- treating the whole reply as stdout.
- Pre-CAPTURE_JSON fallback path: raw text reply.
- Fire-and-forget: "OK\n" or "ERROR: ..."
- ─── launch_app ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
- mios-launch prints "mios-launch: <DisplayName> -> <cmd>" on
- successful resolve; extract for visibility.
- ─── everything_search ──────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── fs_search ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Linux-side peer to everything_search. Operator directive
- "MiOS-Agent(s) can navigate, search, exec--all the same in the Linux
- Environments as well". everything_search covers Windows NTFS via
- Voidtools; fs_search covers the Linux FHS (the OS this agent runs
- ON) via plocate -> locate -> find. Both verbs exposed so the agent
- picks based on intent (Windows .exe / install -> everything_search;
- Linux config / shim / log -> fs_search).
- ─── web_search ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
- The MISSING capability behind the fabrication failure:
- the agent invented a weather/event report (wrong city, °F for a
- Canadian user, made-up details) because the OWUI tool surface had
- ONLY filesystem search -- no web tool. SearXNG was already up and
- advertised as the web_search backend; this exposes it so OWUI's
- tool-calling can GROUND current-world answers on real fetched data.
- mios-web-search prints a single JSON line; pass it through so the
- model sees structured, citable hits. Fall back to raw on a miss.
- ─── mios_apps ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── mios_find ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── knowledge_search ──────────────────────────────────────────
- The shim already returns JSON on stdout; surface it
- verbatim so the model sees the typed hits array.
- ─── directory_lookup ──────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── os_recipe ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── system_status ──────────────────────────────────────────────
- mios-system-status is a self-contained JSON-emitting helper.
- Broker dispatch so we hit it from the operator-side context
- (nvidia-smi + model list + systemctl all behave the same in
- the broker context, but going through the broker keeps the
- tool stateless and consistent with the other verbs).
- If the helper emitted JSON, pass it through; else surface the
- error so the model knows it can't trust the answer.
- ─── PHASE-3 typed window/launch surface (operator directive
- native OpenAI strict function-calling with enum
- positions; replaces SOUL.md prose rules + env-var preludes
- like `MIOS_LAUNCH_POSITION=top-right mios-find ... | bash`). ──
- Build the broker invocation: MIOS_LAUNCH_POSITION env +
- extra args after the name.
- mios-find returns a shell-line for the named app; pipe to
- bash so it executes. Extra args concat after the resolved
- command would need a different path -- for now, when args
- are present, dispatch via mios-windows launch directly.
- mios-window has subcommands matching the enum names.
- ─── service_status ─────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── service_restart ────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── process_list ───────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── container_status ───────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── container_restart ──────────────────────────────────────────

## usr/share/mios/sys/Containerfile
- --- Go compiler builder stage for Firecrawl's Go HTML-to-markdown library ---
- Float latest (SBOM-not-hardcode / ADR-0003): NOTHING is version-pinned. golang floats latest;
- Firecrawl's newest release tag is resolved at BUILD via the releases/latest redirect (no API,
- no rate limit) so a Day-N+ rebuild always re-resolves to the newest upstream.
- --- Main/Final Image Stage ---
- Install core runtime packages (including chromium for headless crawling, and guacd for remote desktop).
- NOTE: no chromium-sandbox -- it is not a separate package on Fedora 44 (dnf: "No match for
- argument: chromium-sandbox"), and headless chromium runs --no-sandbox in this container anyway.
- Download static Go/Rust/C++ binaries (Wave 1 & Wave 2)
- 1. AdGuard Home
- Every release below FLOATS LATEST: resolve the newest release tag at build via the
- releases/latest redirect (no GitHub API -> no rate limit), then download that version.
- --wildcards keeps tar extraction version-agnostic. A Day-N+ rebuild re-resolves to newest.
- 2. Matchbox
- 3. Forgejo
- 4. Forgejo Runner
- 5. Jaeger
- 6. CrowdSec -- the release ships one version-agnostic crowdsec-release.tgz whose prebuilt
- binaries live under crowdsec-<tag>/cmd/ ; --wildcards + strip 3 lands them in /usr/bin.
- 7. K3s -- the +k3sN build-metadata suffix must be URL-encoded to %2B in the download path.
- 8. code-server
- Setup virtualenvs and install interpreted runtime stacks (Wave 2)
- /opt is a symlink to /var/opt on the ucore/bootc base image; inside the nested sys
- build /var/opt does not exist yet, so `git clone` / `python -m venv` into /opt/* dies
- with "could not create leading directories of '/opt/...': No such file or directory".
- Materialize the symlink target up front so ALL the /opt stacks below (searxng,
- open-webui, crawl4ai, firecrawl) resolve.
- 9. SearXNG
- --no-build-isolation makes the editable build use the venv, so SearXNG's setup.py sees
- msgspec (a runtime dep it imports at build time). But that ALSO means the build backend
- (setuptools.build_meta) must already live IN the venv -- and a Python 3.12+ venv ships pip
- ONLY, no setuptools/wheel -> "BackendUnavailable: Cannot import 'setuptools.build_meta'".
- So install setuptools+wheel into the venv up front (before the editable install).
- 10. Open WebUI -- floats latest, but MUST run on python3.12: every open-webui release caps
- requires_python <3.13, so a default (Fedora 44 = Python 3.14) venv resolves ZERO candidates
- ("Could not find a version that satisfies open-webui"). python3.12 is the NEWEST interpreter
- the floating package supports -- a compatibility constraint, not a version pin.
- 11. Crawl4AI
- Skip puppeteer's Chromium auto-download during pnpm install -- firecrawl uses the system
- chromium via PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH; a bake-time browser download is slow + failure-prone.
- 12. Firecrawl -- float latest release tag + latest pnpm (same tag the go-builder resolved).
- Firecrawl v2 relocated the Go html-to-markdown lib to apps/api/sharedLibs/go-html-to-md/
- (was apps/api/src/lib/go-html-to-md/); mirror the .so there so the runtime client finds it.

## usr/share/mios/vendored/k3s/k3s-install.sh
- Usage:
- curl ... | ENV_VAR=... sh -
- or
- ENV_VAR=... ./install.sh
- Example:
- Installing a server without traefik:
- curl ... | INSTALL_K3S_EXEC="--disable=traefik" sh -
- Installing an agent to point at a server:
- curl ... | K3S_TOKEN=xxx K3S_URL=https://server-url:6443 sh -
- Environment variables:
- - K3S_*
- Environment variables which begin with K3S_ will be preserved for the
- systemd service to use. Setting K3S_URL without explicitly setting
- a systemd exec command will default the command to "agent", and we
- enforce that K3S_TOKEN is also set.
- - INSTALL_K3S_SKIP_DOWNLOAD
- If set to true will not download k3s hash or binary.
- - INSTALL_K3S_FORCE_RESTART
- If set to true will always restart the K3s service
- - INSTALL_K3S_SYMLINK
- If set to 'skip' will not create symlinks, 'force' will overwrite,
- default will symlink if command does not exist in path.
- - INSTALL_K3S_SKIP_ENABLE
- If set to true will not enable or start k3s service.
- - INSTALL_K3S_SKIP_START
- If set to true will not start k3s service.
- - INSTALL_K3S_VERSION
- Version of k3s to download from github. Will attempt to download from the
- stable channel if not specified.
- - INSTALL_K3S_COMMIT
- Commit of k3s to download from temporary cloud storage.
- * (for developer & QA use)
- - INSTALL_K3S_PR
- PR build of k3s to download from Github Artifacts.
- * (for developer & QA use)
- - INSTALL_K3S_BIN_DIR
- Directory to install k3s binary, links, and uninstall script to, or use
- /usr/local/bin as the default
- - INSTALL_K3S_BIN_DIR_READ_ONLY
- If set to true will not write files to INSTALL_K3S_BIN_DIR, forces
- setting INSTALL_K3S_SKIP_DOWNLOAD=true
- - INSTALL_K3S_SYSTEMD_DIR
- Directory to install systemd service and environment files to, or use
- /etc/systemd/system as the default
- - INSTALL_K3S_EXEC or script arguments
- Command with flags to use for launching k3s in the systemd service, if
- the command is not specified will default to "agent" if K3S_URL is set
- or "server" if not. The final systemd command resolves to a combination
- of EXEC and script args ($@).
- The following commands result in the same behavior:
- curl ... | INSTALL_K3S_EXEC="--disable=traefik" sh -s -
- curl ... | INSTALL_K3S_EXEC="server --disable=traefik" sh -s -
- curl ... | INSTALL_K3S_EXEC="server" sh -s - --disable=traefik
- curl ... | sh -s - server --disable=traefik
- curl ... | sh -s - --disable=traefik
- - INSTALL_K3S_NAME
- Name of systemd service to create, will default from the k3s exec command
- if not specified. If specified the name will be prefixed with 'k3s-'.
- - INSTALL_K3S_TYPE
