## usr/libexec/mios/copy-build-log.sh
- 'MiOS' Build Log Copy Service
- Preserves build-time logs for post-deployment diagnostics.
- shellcheck source=/usr/lib/mios/paths.sh
- Find the latest build log in the immutable store. Use a glob
- expansion + nullglob so a no-match returns zero entries instead
- of failing the pipeline under 'set -euo pipefail' -- the previous
- 'ls ... | head' form aborted the entire service whenever the log
- was absent (the common case on a fresh deploy, which is when
- this oneshot fires).

## usr/libexec/mios/cpu-isolate
- 'MiOS' CPU core isolation engine -- runtime helper.
- Reads `isolcpus=` from /proc/cmdline (set by usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/), then
- moves every existing user-space process onto the non-isolated host cores
- via `taskset -cp`. Kernel threads are left alone (taskset can't move them
- and the scheduler routes them by other means).
- Service unit: mios-cpu-isolate.service (Type=oneshot, RemainAfterExit=yes,
- ConditionVirtualization=no). Skipped on virtualization where isolcpus has
- no effect.
- When `isolcpus=` is absent, this is a no-op (logs "no isolation kargs").
- When set, the service activates at multi-user.target and the host range
- becomes the complement (e.g. isolcpus=4-7 on 8-core box -> host range 0-3).
- shellcheck source=/usr/lib/mios/paths.sh
- Parse isolcpus= from /proc/cmdline (handles "isolcpus=4-7" and
- "isolcpus=managed_irq,4-7" variants -- pulls the trailing CPU list).
- Strip leading flag terms (managed_irq, domain, ...) keeping last comma-sep field
- Compute host range = full CPU set minus isolated set
- Skip kernel threads (kthreadd is pid 2; its children are kthreads)

## usr/libexec/mios/enumerate-mios-desktops.sh
- Enumerate every visible .desktop entry inside the WSL distro --
- flatpak apps + every /usr/share/applications/ entry that isn't
- explicitly hidden -- so Windows Start Menu shows the full Linux
- app surface. Operator-flagged "I want all the Linux
- apps icons visible in windows".
- Filter: only NoDisplay=true entries are skipped (those are explicitly
- hidden per the freedesktop spec -- internal MIME handlers, portal
- helpers, OAuth providers, GNOME Settings sub-panels). Terminal=true
- entries (btop++, nvtop, etc.) ARE included since wslg.exe can launch
- them in a Linux terminal that surfaces on the Windows side.
- Operator-flagged "not seeing ALL apps in windows sise".
- Everything else is emitted as one pipe-delimited record:
- Name|Exec|Icon|NoDisplay|Terminal|Categories|file
- De-dup by basename: prefer the flatpak version when an rpm + flatpak
- ship the same app (e.g. Fedora's nautilus vs flatpak Nautilus.Devel).

## usr/libexec/mios/flatpak-launch
- /usr/libexec/mios/flatpak-launch <flatpak-app-id> [args...]
- Robust GUI flatpak launcher. Re-derives the WSLg / Wayland / X11 / PulseAudio
- / D-Bus environment whenever the calling shell stripped it (su -, nsenter -m,
- sudo without -E, systemd-run, cron), then exec's `flatpak run --system <id>`.
- WHY THIS EXISTS
- ───────────────
- The per-app shims under /usr/local/bin/ (nautilus, epiphany, ptyxis, codium,
- gnome-software, flatseal) get launched from every imaginable context. Login
- shells under WSL get DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY via /etc/profile.d/mios-wslg.sh,
- but the moment the operator goes through `su - mios`, `sudo nsenter -m -p`,
- `sudo -i`, or any systemd unit, those vars vanish and the flatpak fails with
- one of:
- Cannot autolaunch D-Bus without X11 $DISPLAY
- Gtk-WARNING **: cannot open display:
- ** WARNING **: Failed to create XdpPortal instance:
- Cannot autolaunch D-Bus without X11 $DISPLAY
- The /etc/profile.d/mios-wslg.sh helper would fix all of those, but only
- login shells source profile.d/. Flatpak shims invoked from a non-login
- shell (e.g. `bash -c 'nautilus'` from a script, or interactive bash from
- `su -l mios` whose PAM stack didn't run because we entered via nsenter)
- bypass it entirely.
- This script is the inner-shell complement: it runs every time a GUI
- flatpak is launched, and only sets variables that are unset, so it never
- overrides a working bare-metal GNOME or Wayland session that already
- arranged its own environment.
- DESIGN
- ──────
- 1. WSL detection via /proc/version (namespace-stable; survives nsenter -m
- because /proc is bind-mounted into every namespace).
- 2. XDG_RUNTIME_DIR: prefer /run/user/$UID (real tmpfs that supports the
- sticky-bit chmods rootless podman performs); fall back to WSLg's 9p
- runtime-dir when the per-uid tmpfs is absent.
- 3. DISPLAY / WAYLAND_DISPLAY: WSLg defaults (:0 / wayland-0).
- 4. PULSE_SERVER: prefer $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pulse/native, fall back to
- /mnt/wslg/PulseServer.
- 5. DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS: derived from $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus when the
- user@$UID.service socket is up. This is the single var that breaks
- epiphany the loudest -- "Cannot autolaunch D-Bus without X11 $DISPLAY"
- is libportal's complaint when DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS is empty AND
- DISPLAY is empty (it tries X11 cookie autolaunch as last resort).
- Inert on bare-metal Linux desktops (where the session manager already
- set everything) and on macOS hosts running MiOS in a VM (no /proc/version
- Microsoft signal, no /mnt/wslg). On those substrates the exec falls
- straight through to `flatpak run` with the caller's environment intact.
- ─── Auto-center on launch (operator: "all apps launch CENTERED ALWAYS!") ──
- WSLg/flatpak windows ignore Win32 launch placement, so we center them
- post-hoc via the Windows OS-control executor: snapshot the visible-window
- hwnds NOW (before the launch fires), then hand that set to mios-autocenter
- which polls for the NEW window and centers it by hwnd. Centering by hwnd
- (not title) works for apps whose title omits the app-id (Nautilus="Files",
- Epiphany="GNOME Web", ...). No-op when no executor endpoint is configured
- (bare-metal Linux desktop -- the WM/compositor handles placement there).
- Step 0 ── Service-user re-exec (operator-confirmed regression 2026-05-15:
- "launching epiphany from Hermes CLI WORKS, just not from Open WebUI").
- Hermes-Agent's gateway service runs as `mios-hermes` (uid 820). When OWUI
- asks the agent to launch a GUI flatpak, the agent's `terminal` tool forks
- under that service user. mios-hermes is deliberately locked down:
- * HOME=/var/empty (root-owned, NOT writable -- flatpak needs a real
- home to write app state under ~/.var/app/<id>/, and dies with a
- bare "error: Permission denied" without it)
- * no `user@820.service` socket -> no DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS -> the
- entire portal stack (Open File, Notifications, Secrets) refuses to
- start, GTK then aborts the window
- * no XDG seat / login session -> can't acquire the screen
- The Hermes CLI works fine because the operator runs `hermes` from their
- own login shell as the `mios` user (uid 992) -- their session has DISPLAY,
- WAYLAND_DISPLAY, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS, a real HOME, all already set.
- Fix: when this script is invoked as a service user (uid < 1000 OR HOME
- unwritable), re-exec via `sudo` to the operator. The mios-hermes sudoers
- grant (/etc/sudoers.d/10-mios-hermes -> NOPASSWD: ALL) lets this happen
- without prompting; the operator's session has all the GUI plumbing the
- flatpak needs. _MIOS_FLATPAK_REEXEC=1 guards against an infinite loop if
- the sudo escalation ever lands back in a service user (it shouldn't, but
- belt and suspenders).
- Resolve the operator UID from mios.toml [identity].username.
- Used to decide whether to re-exec through the operator-side
- launcher path. If we're ALREADY the operator (or any uid >= 1000),
- no re-exec is needed -- the calling shell already has the right
- WSLg env and can launch flatpak directly.
- Bug fix 2026-05-15: previous test was `id -u < 1000` which mis-
- triggered for the operator (uid 992 on MiOS-DEV; in the system-
- user range despite being a real interactive user). Operator
- typed `nautilus` in their own terminal and got "[mios-as-operator]
- broker rejected: -- falling back to wsl.exe path" because the
- launch chain ran the re-exec path it shouldn't have entered.
- Need re-exec ONLY if we're a system service user (NOT the operator,
- AND uid < operator's uid -- catches mios-hermes 820 + similar).
- WSLg path: when on WSL2 + service user, prefer mios-as-operator
- (which prefers the broker socket → falls back to wsl.exe --user).
- CRITICAL (operator 2026-05-29 OS-control train: gedit window OPENED but
- launch_app "timed out after 45s, exit -1"): a GUI flatpak is LONG-RUNNING
- (the operator keeps the window open for minutes). The old `exec mios-as-
- operator flatpak run ...` ran the app in the FOREGROUND, so this call
- BLOCKED until the app exited -- which means the agent-pipe broker that
- dispatched `mios-launch <app>` sat blocked until its 45s capture timeout
- fired and returned exit -1, marking a SUCCESSFUL launch as failed. The
- detached systemd-run path below carries the same "do NOT --wait" lesson.
- So DETACH here too: fire the launch in the background (setsid, own session)
- so flatpak-launch returns ~instantly; the agent-pipe's own before/after
- window-diff is the authoritative success check, not this call blocking.
- "dispatched" not "fired/opened": this is a DETACHED hand-off, NOT a
- confirmation a window surfaced. The caller (mios-gui) does the
- authoritative bounded new-window poll; over RDP a WSLg window may not paint.
- Resolve operator UID/name from mios.toml's identity.username (default
- 'mios'); fall back to whatever uid 1000 exists if username lookup fails
- (single-tenant dev VM contract).
- KEY POINT: `sudo -u <op>` alone is NOT enough. It changes uid+gid
- but INHERITS the parent's mount namespace -- and the parent here
- is hermes-agent.service, which has ProtectSystem=strict. That
- namespace makes /var/home read-only, so the flatpak's first
- `mkdir(/var/home/<op>/.var/app/<id>)` dies with "Read-only file
- system" (operator-confirmed 2026-05-15 journal: nautilus failed
- 0.24s into the agent's terminal call with that exact errno).
- Same fix as mios-build-driver's namespace escape: route through
- `systemd-run --pipe --wait` so PID 1 forks the unit FRESH outside
- the agent's namespace, with PID 1's default mount view (the host's
- writable /var/home). --uid=<op> sets the unit user; --setenv
- carries DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY/etc. inside the new namespace.
- If systemd-run is unavailable (atypical install), fall back to
- plain sudo -- works on bare-metal where ProtectSystem isn't a
- factor, breaks honestly inside the agent.
- CRITICAL: do NOT pass --wait/--pipe here. GUI flatpaks are long-
- running (the user keeps the window open for minutes/hours);
- --wait would block this exec until the GUI exits, which means
- the agent's terminal call never returns, OWUI times out the
- chat, and the operator sees "couldn't open epiphany" even
- though the window IS up (operator-confirmed regression
- 2026-05-15: bwrap epiphany running as mios while the agent's
- call sat blocked on systemd-run --wait).
- Without --wait, systemd-run registers the transient unit, lets
- PID 1 take ownership of it, and returns ~instantly with the
- unit name. The GUI then runs DETACHED in the operator's
- session, outliving this script and the agent's tool call.
- --collect cleans up the transient unit when the GUI exits.
- If we get here the operator user doesn't exist (atypical install) --
- fall through and let flatpak fail with whatever its own error is.
- Step 1 ── WSL detection. /proc/version is namespace-stable.
- Step 2 ── XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. Prefer /run/user/$UID; on WSL fall back to
- /mnt/wslg/runtime-dir if the per-uid tmpfs hasn't been created yet
- (early-boot interactive shells before mios-wsl-runtime-dir.service runs).
- Step 3 ── Wayland / X11 / Pulse defaults. Only on WSL: a bare-metal GNOME
- session that's missing DISPLAY is in a broken state we can't paper over,
- but on WSL we know the defaults are stable across every distro that has
- guiApplications=true in /etc/wsl.conf.
- Step 3b ── WSL_INTEROP + WSL2_GUI_APPS_ENABLED best-effort recovery.
- systemd-spawned contexts running as the operator (mios-launcher.service,
- hermes-agent.service) don't inherit these. NOTE (operator trace
- 2026-05-30): setting WSL_INTEROP to a borrowed/foreign socket is NOT
- sufficient on its own -- the flatpak portal credential handshake
- requires the process to actually BELONG to the session that owns the
- interop, else it dies with "--env-fd: Not an open file descriptor: 13"
- + "failed to receive credentials". The real fix is the wsl.exe login-
- session re-launch in Step 6 below. This recovery is kept only as
- belt-and-suspenders for callers that ARE already in a usable session
- but had the var stripped. Harmless on bare-metal (no /run/WSL).
- Step 4 ── D-Bus session bus. The libportal autolaunch-error path triggers
- when this is empty -- portals (Open File, Save File, Notification) refuse
- to function without it, and nautilus/epiphany then crash on first dialog.
- Step 4b ── Pre-launch portal heal. WSLg consistently lets
- flatpak-portal idle out (10-18min observed); when an agent or
- operator launches a flatpak after the idle, the sandbox-credential
- bootstrap fails ("Connection: failed to receive credentials") and
- the app dies at startup. mios-wsl-flatpak-heal idempotently
- re-starts the user-side portal stack + pings flatpak-portal to
- confirm responsiveness. Cheap (~200ms when portals already up;
- ~1s on cold heal) -- run it BEFORE every flatpak launch so the
- operator never sees the idle-out failure mode.
- Operator binding 2026-05-19: "fix epiphany and ALL Flatpaks
- anching issues -- FIX GTK GLOBALLY NOW".
- Step 5 ── per-app extra flags (read from a static file so MiOS source
- can ship app-specific launch defaults without having to regenerate
- the bootstrap shim layer). Lookup order:
- 1. /etc/mios/flatpak-flags/<app-id>.flags         (operator override)
- 2. /usr/share/mios/flatpak-flags/<app-id>.flags   (vendor default)
- Each file is plain text, one flag per line (or all on one line, shell-
- tokenised). Lines starting with `#` are comments. Operator file wins.
- This is how Chrome gets its CDP port + dark-mode + Wayland decorations
- without the bootstrap shim having to special-case com.google.ChromeDev
- (operator-confirmed 2026-05-15: putting the flags in the bootstrap
- shim heredoc is fragile to re-overlay, and inline-shim flag arrays
- are unreadable; static .flags file = tracked in git, easy to extend).
- Strip comment lines + blank lines, fold to one space-separated string
- Step 5b ── WSLg GTK render env is set via `flatpak override --env=GSK_RENDERER=...`
- (a flatpak app-config mechanism), NOT injected here: `flatpak run` OPTIONS like
- --env MUST precede the APP_ID, but EXTRA_FLAGS/the args below are appended AFTER
- it -- a 2026-06-15 attempt to add --env to EXTRA_FLAGS made flatpak pass it to the
- APP, which rejected it ("Unknown option --env=...") and exited with NO window.
- The override (set by mios-wsl-flatpak-heal / firstboot) persists per-app, so no
- launch-command surgery is needed. Tunable via MIOS_GSK_RENDERER.
- Step 6 ── exec the flatpak. `flatpak run --system` resolves the app
- from the system installation (/var/lib/flatpak); --user installs are
- not used by MiOS because the dev VM is single-tenant.
- Stderr is filtered to drop flatpak 1.17.x debug noise:
- "F: Not replacing /usr/share/* with tmpfs: Path /usr is reserved"
- These are informational warnings hardcoded into flatpak 1.17 -- not
- silenceable via FLATPAK_LOG_LEVEL or G_MESSAGES_DEBUG. They print on
- EVERY app launch and the operator flagged the noise 2026-05-16:
- ptyxis launch transcript "F: Not replacing /usr/share/icons ...".
- /usr/share/{themes,icons,fonts} are already negated in the global
- override (mios-flatpak-overrides-apply); flatpak still tries the
- mount internally and logs the rejection. Drop those lines, keep
- everything else.
- Arm auto-center (snapshot windows now, center the new one once it maps).
- ─── THE WSLg launch fix (operator trace 2026-05-30: every flatpak GUI
- "nothing launched at all"). On WSL a flatpak GUI app needs a REAL
- wsl.exe login session for its xdg-portal / D-Bus credential handshake.
- A broker- or systemd-spawned context -- EVEN running as the operator
- (uid 992, _NEED_REEXEC=0, so the re-exec paths A/B above were skipped) --
- is SESSIONLESS, and the app dies at startup with:
- error: --env-fd: Not an open file descriptor: 13
- ERROR: Connection: failed to receive credentials: ... read zero bytes
- Pointing WSL_INTEROP at a borrowed/foreign live socket does NOT fix it
- (Step 3b) -- the process must BELONG to the session that owns the interop.
- So re-launch through a FRESH `wsl.exe -d <distro> --user <op>` session
- (which the operator-uid broker context CAN exec even without WSL_INTEROP),
- kept alive a few seconds for the flatpak to finish its portal bootstrap.
- The app SURVIVES the session's death afterward (verified 2026-05-30), so
- the keepalive only needs to cover startup. The whole re-launch is DETACHED
- (setsid &) so the broker dispatch / agent tool-call returns ~instantly --
- the agent-pipe before/after window-diff is the authoritative success check.
- _MIOS_FLATPAK_INSESSION guards against re-wrapping once we're inside the
- fresh session. Bare-metal Linux (no wsl.exe) falls through to direct launch.
- Only re-exec via wsl.exe when the broker is SESSIONLESS (no live WSLg env).
- A broker running in the operator's user@ session already has WAYLAND_DISPLAY +
- the live socket, so it launches DIRECTLY (the setsid path below) -- which
- persists and renders. The fresh wsl.exe session was observed to DIE after the
- WSL 2.8.x upgrade (open_url -> "epiphany summary=no-window", process gone),
- so reserve it for the sessionless fallback only. Operator-hit 2026-06-06.
- Resolve the WSL distro for re-entry: env -> /etc pin -> wsl.exe -l.
- Safely single-quote each token for transit through `bash -lc`.
- EXTRA_FLAGS are flatpak-run OPTIONS (--env/--filesystem/--socket/...) and MUST
- precede the APP_ID; a 2026-06-15 bug placed them AFTER -> flatpak passed them to
- the app, which exited "Unknown option --env=..." with no window. App args ($@)
- still follow the APP_ID.
- Background the GUI inside the session, then keep the session alive
- $_boot seconds so the portal handshake completes before it exits.
- "dispatched" not "fired/opened": detached hand-off into a fresh wsl.exe
- session, NOT proof a window mapped. Caller (mios-gui) confirms via the
- bounded new-window poll; over RDP a WSLg window may not surface at all.
- Non-WSL (bare-metal Linux desktop) OR already inside a usable session:
- direct detached launch. GUI flatpaks are fire-and-forget -- launch in
- their own session and return ~instantly (the old foreground `exec flatpak
- run` blocked the caller until the GUI exited, tripping the agent-pipe 45s
- capture timeout and marking a successful launch as failed). >/dev/null 2>&1
- also drops the flatpak 1.17 "F: Not replacing /usr/*" noise.
- shellcheck disable=SC2086 -- intentional word-splitting on EXTRA_FLAGS
- operator 2026-06-15: CAPTURE the launch stderr instead of discarding it to
- /dev/null. Ground truth this session: epiphany's binary runs fine (--version
- OK, no coredump) but the DETACHED GUI process dies without surfacing a window
- and the reason was being thrown away (cf. the WSL 2.8.x detach-reaping note
- above). Per-app log (last run wins) so the failure is diagnosable without
- launching the GUI by hand. Tunable off via MIOS_FLATPAK_LOG=/dev/null.
- "dispatched" not "fired/opened": the launch is detached + fire-and-forget;
- this line is NOT a confirmation that a window surfaced. The caller (mios-gui)
- runs the authoritative bounded new-window poll and reports honestly. Bare-metal
- Linux paints reliably; over a separate RDP session WSLg windows may not.

## usr/libexec/mios/flatpaks-manage.sh
- mios-flatpaks -- thin wrapper over `flatpak` for the MiOS-shipped
- system-wide Flatpak surface. Operator-friendly verbs that don't
- require remembering the long flatpak invocations.
- mios-flatpaks list             list all installed system Flatpaks
- mios-flatpaks add    <ref>     install <ref> from flathub system-wide
- mios-flatpaks remove <ref>     uninstall <ref> system-wide
- mios-flatpaks update           update all installed Flatpaks
- mios-flatpaks search <term>    search flathub for <term>
- mios-flatpaks bake-state       show the build-time bake state
- (/usr/lib/mios/state/flatpak-bake.env)
- To make a Flatpak persist across `bootc switch` (the self-replication
- loop), edit the canonical mios.toml [desktop].flatpaks array via the
- configurator HTML at /usr/share/mios/configurator/mios.html, then
- `mios-rebuild` to push and trigger a runner-side rebuild.

## usr/libexec/mios/flight-control.sh
- 'MiOS' flight-control -- shows active build variable mappings

## usr/libexec/mios/forge-firstboot.sh
- /usr/libexec/mios/forge-firstboot.sh
- First-boot admin-bootstrap for the mios-forge Quadlet (Forgejo).
- Runs once via mios-forge-firstboot.service after mios-forge.service is
- healthy. Creates the operator's admin user using values that
- mios-bootstrap install.sh wrote to /etc/mios/install.env, which were
- themselves resolved from mios-bootstrap.git/mios.toml at install time:
- MIOS_FORGE_ADMIN_USER     defaults to MIOS_LINUX_USER ([identity].username)
- MIOS_FORGE_ADMIN_EMAIL    defaults to <user>@<hostname>.local
- MIOS_FORGE_ADMIN_PASSWORD if empty, a 24-byte URL-safe random
- password is generated and written to
- /etc/mios/forge/admin-password (root-owned,
- mode 0600); operator reads it once and
- changes it via the web UI on first login.
- Idempotent: marks completion via /var/lib/mios/forge/.firstboot-done
- and short-circuits on every subsequent boot. To re-trigger (e.g. after
- wiping the SQLite DB), delete that sentinel file and restart the
- mios-forge-firstboot.service.
- Ensure host data volume has correct user ownership (UID 1000 git user)
- Source install.env if present; tolerate absence (operator may run this
- script manually with env-vars set inline).
- shellcheck source=/dev/null
- Guard set -u: a value with shell-metachars must not abort under set -u.
- Resolution: explicit MIOS_FORGE_* wins; otherwise fall back to the
- linux user identity that bootstrap captured. Final fallback to 'mios'.
- Default to the global MiOS password (mios.toml [identity].default_password).
- Operators can override per-service via MIOS_FORGE_ADMIN_PASSWORD, or set
- Wait for mios-forge to come up. Forgejo's HTTP listener is the canonical
- Generate a password if none was supplied. 24 bytes -> 32 base64 chars.
- Create the admin via the in-container forgejo CLI. Idempotency: if the
- user already exists (e.g. someone created one via the web UI before
- this service ran), 'forgejo admin user create' returns non-zero and
- we accept that as a soft success.
- --user 816 matches the in-container UID we configured via USER_UID=816
- in the Quadlet. The container's internal username is 'git' (the Forgejo
- image's convention), not 'mios-forge'; we pass the numeric UID so the
- podman exec lookup succeeds against the container's /etc/passwd.
- --must-change-password=false: TOML-first invariant. The admin
- password is resolved from mios.toml [identity] (default_password /
- credential, not a throwaway. With =true Forgejo locks every
- basic-auth API call behind a "you must change your password" 403,
- which breaks the very next steps in THIS script (repo-create,
- runner-token mint) and every downstream automation that authbenticates
- as the admin (the self-replication push loop, CI). The dashboard
- even advertises `forge mios/mios` as working credentials. Operators
- who want a forced rotation can set MIOS_FORGE_ADMIN_PASSWORD=__random__
- (handled above) -- that path still leaves the password usable, just
- unknown until read from /etc/mios/forge/admin-password.
- ── Initial repository for the deployed root ────────────────────────────────
- MiOS's defining feature: the live `/` is a git working tree, and the
- Forgejo container hosts the bare repo it tracks. For `git -C / push
- http://localhost:3000/<admin>/mios` to work on first run, the repo
- has to already exist on the forge. Create it via the admin API.
- Idempotent: 409 Conflict (already exists) is treated as success.
- ── Wire the deployed root `/` to this forge (Day-0 self-host loop) ──────────
- code-server bind-mounts `/` at /mnt/mios-root and the Forgejo Runner builds
- /Containerfile on push, so the only missing link for "dev from INSIDE
- MiOS-DEV" is making `/` a git working tree pointed at this forge. The image
- build (Containerfile) excludes ./.git, so a fresh deploy has none -- create
- it here. The root is a PROPER, deliberately-curated git working tree:
- /.gitignore is a whitelist that tracks exactly the MiOS-owned surface
- (etc/, usr/, var/lib/mios, the Quadlets, the verbs) and nothing else -- it is
- the complete, intentional manifest of what MiOS owns, by design. `git add -A`
- stages that curated tree cleanly; it is not a defensive filter against the
- kernel's runtime mounts. We wire config only -- the operator (or code-server)
- drives the first commit + push. Idempotent; never fatal to firstboot.
- Forgejo is the loop HUB: point `origin` at the local Forgejo repo so a push
- from code-server (or `git -C / push`) triggers .forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml
- on the Runner. The chain the operator wants is: .git=/ -> Forgejo -> code-server
- edits /mnt/mios-root. Password is embedded so the push is frictionless on this
- single-user self-host box; /.git/config is never committed (git ignores .git/).
- Any pre-existing non-Forgejo origin is preserved as 'local-bare'.
- ── Forgejo Runner registration token ──────────────────────────────────────
- The Runner Quadlet (mios-forgejo-runner.container) reads this file via
- EnvironmentFile= and self-registers on first start. Stored at root-only
- permissions; never tracked in git (whitelist .gitignore excludes
- /etc/mios/forge/ entirely except for files we explicitly allow).
- Try the in-container Forgejo CLI first -- most reliable across versions.
- `forgejo actions generate-runner-token` prints the token on stdout.
- Fallback: admin API. Some Forgejo versions return a wrapper object,
- others return the bare string; sed handles either shape.
- The runner registers with -- and the daemon then connects to --
- whatever network mios-forge is actually on. On bridge shapes (real
- MiOS OCI builds) forge runs on mios.network and is reachable by
- container DNS as mios-forge:<port>. On the WSL / dev-VM testbed,
- build-mios.ps1 drops BOTH forge and the runner to Network=host via
- Quadlet drop-ins -- there container DNS does not exist, and the
- host-published PublishPort=3000:3000 means localhost:<port> is the
- only address that resolves for both. mios-forge is up by now (this
- script polled its HTTP listener above), so inspect its live network
- and write the URL the runner daemon will actually be able to reach.
- Falls back to the container-DNS form if inspect yields nothing.
- Trigger the runner chain so it registers immediately rather than
- waiting for next boot. --no-block is LOAD-BEARING: this script is
- the ExecStart of mios-forge-firstboot.service, and the runner
- chain is ordered After=mios-forge-firstboot.service. A *blocking*
- `systemctl start` here would wait for a job (mios-forgejo-runner.
- service) that is itself queued behind this very unit finishing
- activation -- a hard ordering deadlock (operator-confirmed
- forge-firstboot stuck "activating", runner jobs stuck
- "waiting"). --no-block enqueues the chain and returns immediately
- so this unit can reach "active", which then unblocks the queue.
- mios-forgejo-runner.service Wants= the runner-firstboot
- registration unit, so starting it pulls the whole chain.
- One-line operator hint, dropped into the system journal.

## usr/libexec/mios/git-root-init.sh
- /usr/libexec/mios/git-root-init.sh
- Initialize the deployed root `/` as a git working tree of the local
- Forgejo `mios.git` mirror. Runs once via mios-git-root-init.service
- after mios-forge-firstboot.service has created the admin user and
- the operator's mios.git repo on the local Forgejo instance.
- Architecture invariant (mios_root_git memory): the deployed `/` IS a
- git working tree. Operators edit files at FHS paths, `git commit`,
- push to localhost:3000, the Forgejo Runner builds a new OCI image,
- and `bootc switch` swaps to it on the next boot. Without /.git
- present, the loop is broken -- the operator can't `git diff /` to
- see what diverged from the deployed image.
- What this script does:
- 1. Skip if /.git already present (idempotent; sentinel-free).
- 2. Wait for the local Forgejo to respond on http://localhost:3000/
- (up to 60s). Forgejo bootstrap can take 30-45s on first boot.
- 3. Probe whether the operator's mios.git repo exists at
- http://localhost:3000/<user>/mios.git. If absent, skip and
- log -- operator initializes via the Forgejo web UI or CLI.
- 4. `git -C / init -b main`
- 5. `git -C / remote add origin http://localhost:3000/<user>/mios.git`
- 6. `git -C / fetch origin main` -- pull the upstream tree.
- 7. `git -C / reset --soft FETCH_HEAD` -- adopt the FETCH_HEAD as
- HEAD without touching the working tree (the deployed files
- already match the image; `reset --soft` only updates the index
- so `git status` shows no changes).
- After this runs, `git status` at / works, `git diff` shows operator
- edits since deploy, and `git push` against localhost:3000 triggers
- the Forgejo Runner build.
- shellcheck source=/usr/lib/mios/paths.sh
- Idempotent: /.git is the sentinel.
- Resolve the operator's username (drives the Forgejo repo path).
- shellcheck disable=SC1091
- Guard set -u: a value with shell-metachars must not abort under set -u.
- Wait for Forgejo to be up. mios-forge.service can take 30-45s for
- the first SQLite-DB write after a fresh container start.
- Probe whether the mios.git repo exists. If not, the operator hasn't
- created it yet -- skip; they'll init via web UI / git push.
- Init / as a git tree without disturbing the deployed working tree.
- Adopt FETCH_HEAD as HEAD without rewriting the working tree.
- `reset --soft` only moves the branch pointer + index; the on-disk
- files (which already match the image build) stay put. `git status`
- then shows whatever the operator has edited since deploy.

## usr/libexec/mios/gpu-detect
- Install-robustness 2026-06-21: a VM with a REAL passed-through NVIDIA GPU
- (VFIO/SR-IOV on KVM/qemu, or the WSL2 /dev/dxg paravirt-CUDA surface) must
- NOT have nvidia blacklisted -- that kills the very GPU the AI lanes need.
- Only blacklist on a genuinely GPU-less VM (the paravirt-display-only case).
- GTK 4.16+ removed the cairo renderer. ngl via llvmpipe is the optimal VM fallback.
- Load nvidia now that blacklist is removed
- RTX 50-series (Blackwell) VFIO reset bug detection
- VRAM check for dGPU heavy lane auto-enablement (>8GB VRAM)

## usr/libexec/mios/gpu-pv-detect
- 'MiOS' Hyper-V GPU paravirt guest detection.
- Run by mios-gpu-pv-detect.service (gated ConditionVirtualization=microsoft;
- only fires inside Hyper-V/WSL2 guests). Writes a status file the rest of
- the GPU stack reads to decide whether to enable hardware-accelerated
- rendering vs llvmpipe software rendering.
- Status file: /run/mios/gpu-pv.status  (KEY=VALUE)
- gpu_pv_present=1|0     -- /dev/dxg present (DirectX kernel passthrough)
- wslg_active=1|0        -- /mnt/wslg/.X11-unix exists (WSLg display)
- nvidia_in_guest=1|0    -- nvidia-smi succeeds inside the guest
- shellcheck source=/usr/lib/mios/paths.sh

## usr/libexec/mios/hermes-worker-firstboot
- /usr/libexec/mios/hermes-worker-firstboot
- The Hermes WORKER (P1) uses a SEPARATE HERMES_HOME=/var/lib/mios/hermes-worker
- with its OWN non-thin config.yaml. mios-hermes-firstboot re-thins ONLY the
- primary :8642 config (/var/lib/mios/hermes/config.yaml) on every boot, so the
- worker config at a DISTINCT path is durable. This seeder just guarantees the
- worker config is in place (the tmpfiles `C` line is the copy-if-absent
- primary; this also re-seeds if the vendor template is NEWER, for schema heals).
- HERMES_HOME (tmpfiles also declares it; install -d is idempotent + ordered
- before this unit, but re-assert so a manual run works too).
- Seed when absent OR when the vendor template is newer (schema heal). An

## usr/libexec/mios/install-ai-clis.sh
- /usr/libexec/mios/install-ai-clis.sh
- Install MiOS-default AI assistant CLIs (Claude Code + Gemini CLI) as
- global npm packages. Both are Node.js CLIs distributed via npm, so
- they don't fit RPM packaging. This script is invoked once by the
- build-mios.ps1 overlay phase and is also operator-re-runnable any
- time (idempotent: `npm install -g <pkg>` upgrades or installs as
- needed).
- Reads the npm_globals list from mios.toml [packages.ai] -- operator
- can extend by editing the list before `mios update`.
- Operator override: MIOS_SKIP_AI_CLIS=1 skips entirely.
- set -e covered by set -euo pipefail at top
- Pull npm_globals from layered mios.toml (~/.config > /etc/mios > /usr/share/mios).
- Vendor fallback if the toml lookup fails: the two operator-canonical
- AI CLIs.
- Extract npm_globals = [ "...", "..." ] from [packages.ai] section.
- Capture into a var so we can check if any content was produced.
- Previous form `awk | grep | tr && return 0` always returned 0
- because tr (last cmd in the pipe) exits 0 on empty input -- the
- function short-circuited before reaching the vendor fallback,
- leaving the install loop with zero packages to install.
- Vendor fallback -- claude-code + gemini-cli are the operator-canonical
- AI CLIs (defaults ON per mios.toml [packages.ai].npm_globals).
- Ensure npm prefix is a system path that's on $PATH for all users.
- Default `npm -g` prefix on Fedora is /usr/local; install bins land
- at /usr/local/bin/ which IS on PATH (in /etc/login.defs's PATH +
- /etc/profile + /etc/skel default shells).
- Force npm prefix explicitly so installed binstubs ALWAYS land in
- /usr/local/bin (some NodeSource RPMs ship a per-user default of
- ~/.npm-global which would put the binaries outside the operator's
- default PATH).
- NOT --silent so operator sees download progress / failure detail.
- Capture exit via process-subst-friendly form.

## usr/libexec/mios/install-nvidia-wsl-userland.sh
- /usr/libexec/mios/install-nvidia-wsl-userland.sh
- Install NVIDIA's Vulkan ICD + GLX/EGL userspace libs for WSLg
- dev-VM hosts. Called by build-mios.ps1's Quadlet/overlay phase
- AND idempotent-callable from `mios install-gpu` for live re-runs.
- What this gets you:
- * /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.x86_64.json
- * /usr/lib64/libGLX_nvidia.so + libEGL_nvidia.so + libGLESv2_nvidia
- * libnvidia-ml + libnvidia-gpucomp (already provided by WSL drop,
- installing the RPM versions is harmless and adds versioned symlinks)
- * egl-wayland + egl-gbm + egl-x11 (EGL platform implementations)
- What this does NOT do:
- * NO kernel-module install (kmod-nvidia / akmod-nvidia) -- the
- kernel module isn't applicable on WSL2; /dev/dxg is the kernel-
- mode bridge and it's already there.
- * NOT a full CUDA toolkit install -- libnvidia-ml is enough for
- `nvidia-smi` and PyTorch's CUDA detection. Operators wanting
- the full toolchain run `dnf install cuda-toolkit-X-Y` separately.
- Caveat: this installs NVIDIA's NATIVE Vulkan ICD which expects
- /dev/nvidia* device nodes. WSL2 doesn't have those -- it has
- /dev/dxg (WDDM) instead. So the NVIDIA Vulkan ICD doesn't enumerate
- any GPU under WSL; Vulkan workloads still go through Microsoft's
- `dzn` ICD (Direct3D12 translation). Why install NVIDIA libs anyway?
- 1. Compute / CUDA workloads work via libcuda + libnvidia-ml
- (Microsoft's WSL drop) regardless of NVIDIA Vulkan availability.
- 2. nvidia-smi becomes available so the operator can verify GPU
- health from inside the dev VM.
- 3. Flatpak apps that bundle libGLX_nvidia detection get a real
- (if non-functional under WSL) vendor lib to point at, avoiding
- "no NVIDIA driver detected" warnings on launch.
- 4. Forward-compatible: when WSL2 eventually exposes /dev/nvidia*
- (or NVIDIA ships a WSL-aware Vulkan ICD that targets /dev/dxg),
- this stack is already in place.
- Idempotent + safe to re-run: dnf install of already-present pkgs
- is a no-op; repo add with --overwrite refreshes the .repo file.
- Operator override: set MIOS_SKIP_NVIDIA_INSTALL=1 to skip entirely.
- set -e covered by set -euo pipefail at top
- Gate on WSLg presence -- this script is for WSLg dev VMs only.
- Detect upstream Fedora version. MiOS-branded os-release sets
- VERSION_ID to the MiOS version; PLATFORM_ID preserves the Fedora
- upstream as "platform:fXX".
- Probe NVIDIA CUDA repo URLs. Try the detected fedora version first,
- fall back to nearby versions if 404 (NVIDIA publishes per-Fedora-
- version repos on a release-by-release basis).
- Install userland-only. Excludes are defensive against weak-deps
- pulling in a kernel-module package; --setopt=install_weak_deps=False
- is also belt-and-suspenders.
- Verify install landed.

## usr/libexec/mios/libvirtd-firstboot
- 'MiOS' libvirtd first-boot wiring.
- Run by mios-libvirtd-setup.service once per deploy (sentinel:
- /var/lib/mios/libvirtd-setup.done, written by ExecStartPost in the
- unit). After=libvirtd.service so the daemon is up.
- What it does:
- * Defines the default 'mios' libvirt network if missing
- * Defines the default 'images' storage pool at /var/lib/libvirt/images
- * Autostarts both
- * Joins the mios user to the libvirt group (idempotent)
- All steps are idempotent: skipping when already-defined, autostart-
- already-on, member-already-of-group.
- shellcheck source=/usr/lib/mios/paths.sh
- Wait briefly for libvirtd socket
- Default network 'mios'
- Default storage pool 'images'
- Join the mios user to libvirt group (sysusers.d already does this, but
- be defensive for distros that didn't pick up the m-line)

## usr/libexec/mios/mcp-init.sh
- 'MiOS' MCP server pre-flight (ExecStartPre for mios-mcp.service).
- Verifies the MCP server's runtime directories + sqlite vault paths exist
- before the long-running mcp-server-runner is launched. Fast (<100 ms),
- idempotent, no network.
- Lays down:
- /var/lib/mios/mcp/             owner mios-ai:mios-ai mode 0750
- /var/lib/mios/mcp/state.db     touched if missing (sqlite WAL friendly)
- /var/log/mios/mcp/             owner mios-ai:mios-ai mode 0750
- /srv/ai/mcp/                   read-only mount target for server config
- shellcheck source=/usr/lib/mios/paths.sh
- Target the service's OWN user (mios-ai after the agent-user consolidation).
- This runs as the service User= via ExecStartPre, so `id -u`/`id -g` are that
- user -- avoiding the old hardcoded `mios`, which EPERM-crashed once the
- service moved to mios-ai and could no longer chown/chmod mios-owned dirs
- (the dirs are now pre-created with the right owner by tmpfiles.d/mios.conf).
- Writable runtime dirs only. /srv/ai/mcp is the read-only config mount
- target -- it's pre-created by usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/mios.conf at boot,
- and on bootc/composefs deployments where /srv resolves into the
- read-only image surface, `install -d` fails on the chmod step. The
- mcp server reads config from there but never writes, so verification
- is enough; no mutation.

## usr/libexec/mios/mcp-server-runner
- 'MiOS' MCP server runtime wrapper (ExecStart for mios-mcp.service).
- Discovers and runs the MCP server entrypoint under /srv/ai/mcp/. Three
- entrypoint forms are supported (first match wins):
- 1. /srv/ai/mcp/server.py         -- Python 3 module, run via `python3 -m`
- 2. /srv/ai/mcp/server.sh         -- shell script, exec'd directly
- 3. /srv/ai/mcp/server            -- bare executable
- When none is present, the runner sleeps as a placeholder so the unit
- stays "active" without thrashing through restarts. The MCP image / config
- is expected to drop one of those entry points at /srv/ai/mcp/.
- Env passed through:
- MIOS_AI_ENDPOINT  (default http://localhost:8642/v1)
- MIOS_MCP_PORT     (default 8765)
- MIOS_MCP_LOG_DIR  (default /var/log/mios/mcp)
- T-032: When invoked with arguments (by the agent-pipe MCP client), acts as a
- GATEKEEPER that validates tool arguments and optionally sandboxes execution:
- mcp-server-runner <command> [args...]
- Security checks:
- 1. Directory traversal blocking (../ , /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow)
- 2. MIOS_WRITE_ALLOWED_PATHS enforcement for write operations
- 3. Optional rootless podman sandbox wrapping
- shellcheck source=/usr/lib/mios/paths.sh
- ── T-032: Security validation helpers ────────────────────────────────────────
- Block directory traversal patterns in any argument. Returns 1 if blocked.
- Block explicit traversal sequences
- Block direct access to sensitive system files
- Validate that a write target path is within MIOS_WRITE_ALLOWED_PATHS.
- Returns 0 if allowed, 1 if blocked.
- Execute a command inside a rootless podman sandbox.
- Falls back to direct exec if podman is unavailable.
- ── T-032: Gatekeeper mode (invoked with arguments by agent-pipe MCP client) ─
- Security check 1: directory traversal
- Security check 2: if sandbox mode is enabled, route through sandbox
- ── Service mode (ExecStart for mios-mcp.service, no arguments) ──────────────
- No custom /srv/ai/mcp entrypoint -> serve the BUILT-IN MiOS verb relay
- (mios-mcp-server) over Streamable-HTTP on 127.0.0.1:$MIOS_MCP_PORT. This
- replaces the old placeholder-sleep so MiOS actually SERVES its [verbs.*]
- catalog as MCP tools. 127.0.0.1-only by design: tools/call dispatches
- verbs, so no unauthenticated tailnet exposure until an auth gate ships.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-a2a-discover
- The agent-pipe port comes from the SSOT ([ports].agent_pipe), never a literal:
- resolved per run in main() (env MIOS_A2A_PORT / MIOS_PORT_AGENT_PIPE override).
- The mDNS browse helper is a sibling file with a hyphenated (extensionless) name,
- loaded by path below.
- bound the sweep so a /16 typo can't scan 65k hosts
- mDNS-discovered candidates (FED-G5): browse the LAN for the A2A service type
- when [a2a].mdns_discovery is on. Each is card-probed below before being
- trusted, so this only ever ADDS verified peers (degrade-open when off/absent).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-a2a-mdns
- Output (rendered) avahi service file + the source template. Law 1: the static
- template ships read-only under /usr/lib; the rendered copy is admin/runtime
- state under /etc. Both overridable for tests / non-standard layouts.
- Browse-result cache backing the [a2a].mdns_refresh_sec throttle FLOOR: a browse
- within the window reuses this instead of re-hitting avahi, so discovery never
- loses peers between live scans. /run/mios is the tmpfiles-declared volatile
- runtime dir (cleared each boot). Overridable for tests / non-standard layouts.
- Withdraw: remove the rendered file so avahi de-registers. Absent
- already = success (idempotent).
- Substitute ONLY the two SSOT-driven placeholders; everything else in
- the template is an A2A protocol constant.
- Primary: documented positions.
- Fallback: first parseable IP, first valid port at/after it (version-drift
- robust; purely structural).
- -p parse-friendly, -r resolve, -t terminate (one-shot). Bounded so a
- wedged daemon can't hang the refresh timer.
- advertise + browse (print candidates) + reload -- the all-in-one an
- operator or a timer can call directly.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-a2a-test

- Confirm via tasks/get that the task is durably retrievable by id.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-adguard-firstboot
- Split-DNS: keep the MagicDNS suffix on Tailscale's resolver so *.ts.net
- pretty URLs resolve, with ad-blocking on everything else.

- which a YAML parser would read as an inline sequence. Quoting keeps each
- entry a plain string for AdGuard to parse.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-agents-firstboot.sh
- (code-server IDE + tmux war room + Claude CLI + agy/Gemini + the mios-a2o muxer).
- Runs as ExecStartPre of mios-agents.service; idempotent no-op when the image exists.

- The mios-a2o / mios-frontier SCRIPTS do NOT force a rebuild -- they are read LIVE
- from the bind-mounted /mnt/mios-root via the image's profile.d PATH self-heal, so

- build netns otherwise attempts unroutable IPv6 on some substrates (WSL testbed).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-clear
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-clear [--dry-run] [--yes]
- DAY-0 GLOBAL CLEAN SLATE for the MiOS AI stack. Wipes ALL accumulated
- runtime state and rebuilds the databases to Day-0 values:
- * Hermes scheduled jobs (cron/jobs.json + output)  <- stops Discord spam
- * Hermes state: sessions, kanban, response_store, memories, logs
- * OWUI: chat / message / memory / feedback / tags  (via mios-ai-reset)
- * Observability: log-watcher + cron-director batches
- * Browser sidecar profile, opencode subagent caches
- * pgvector agent state: events, sessions, tool_call, metrics, skill
- index, directory cache, AND the doc RAG (mios_rag) -- re-ingested
- * agent-env inventory caches (windows-apps, suggestions)
- PRESERVED (identity / config / models -- NOT regenerable):
- * OWUI: user, auth, group, model, function, tool, api_key
- * Hermes: config.yaml, SOUL.md, .env, skills/, bin/, hooks/
- * pgvector: agent_keypair, agent, person  (crypto identity + registry)
- * models, /etc/mios/* configs, vendor /usr/share/mios/*
- Operator directive 2026-05-20: "clear ... EVERYTHING to Day-0 ... constant
- discord reports daily and want a completely clean slate". Root cause of the
- Discord spam: scheduled posters in Hermes cron/jobs.json (AMD stock +
- trending-topic posts every 15 min) -- this clears them.
- Run as `mios ai clear` from any MiOS shell, or `mios-ai-clear` directly.
- --dry-run shows what would be cleared. --yes skips the confirm prompt.
- Root (re-exec via non-interactive sudo if available).
- WS-9: agent state lives in PostgreSQL+pgvector now (the legacy BSL store
- retired). Reset via the pure-python pg wire client (loopback trust, no
- auth/psql/podman needed) -- same path mios-rag / mios-db --pg use.
- TD-1: eval-safe, input=internal hardcoded commands, not agent-controlled
- TRUNCATE the runtime/event/cache tables -- the schema-init.sql definitions
- stay so agents don't error on a missing table. RESTART IDENTITY resets the
- bigint id sequences to Day-0; CASCADE clears the natural-key edge
- (resolves_to <- app_install). IF EXISTS tolerates tables not yet created
- at runtime (e.g. mios_rag before first ingest). Each statement is wrapped
- so a missing table can't abort the batch. agent_memory (mios-remember's
- operator/agent facts) is PRESERVED as identity-adjacent, mirroring the old
- pgvector preserve of agent/person/agent_keypair.
- Delegate to the existing guardrailed clean-slate -- it re-stops (no-op),
- wipes the conversational state, and RESTARTS hermes/owui/log-watcher/
- cron-director/hermes-browser.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-firstboot
- 'MiOS' AI first-boot provisioning.
- Completes the build-time AI setup on deployments where it wasn't baked into
- the image (overlay-provisioned MiOS-DEV, WSL imports, any non-bootc-built
- host). Two pieces, both idempotent + best-effort:
- 1. the shared agent venv (hermes-agent + agent-pipe), via the canonical
- builder automation/72-hermes-agent.sh (checked out at / by the overlay);
- 2. the llama.cpp GGUFs for the mios-llm-light lane, downloaded as HF-native
- GGUFs (the tags come from /usr/share/mios/llamacpp/mios-llm-light.yaml).
- Then it (re)starts the AI services so they pick up the new prerequisites.
- The sentinel /var/lib/mios/.ai-firstboot-done is written ONLY when the venv,
- the GGUFs AND (if opted-in) the vLLM weights are all in place; until then the
- script degrades open (exit 0) and mios-ai-firstboot.timer re-fires it on a
- ~10min cadence (the .service carries ConditionPathExists=!<sentinel> so the
- timer-fired run no-ops once complete). Retry is owned by the TIMER, not a
- Restart=on-failure storm.
- NO `set -e` -- every step is guarded; a partial provision must not wedge boot.
- Guard set -u: a value with shell-metachars must not abort under set -u.
- WSL persistence link logic (preserves downloaded weights across developer env refreshes)
- ── 1. shared agent venv (hermes pins Python <3.14) ──────────────────────────
- The canonical venv builder lives in automation/ (build-time). The overlay
- checks out usr/etc/var to / but NOT automation/, so find it across the
- locations it can actually be: a runtime copy, the / git working tree
- (materialize on demand), or the mounted Windows mios.git clone on the dev VM.
- Require lib/common.sh ALONGSIDE the script: 72-hermes-agent.sh sources it
- and exits 0 (no venv) if absent -- exactly what a script-only /automation
- checkout yields. Prefer the full /mnt/m mios.git clone (has lib/).
- BROKEN-VENV CLEANUP (AGY-38): if the builder ran but left a partial/broken
- venv (dir present but no working hermes entrypoint), rm -rf it so the
- image-seed fallback below -- and any next-boot retry -- start from a clean
- slate instead of layering onto a half-built tree that merely LOOKS present.
- Degrade-open: never hard-fail boot on the cleanup (set +eu + || true).
- HARDENING (install-robustness): if the pip build failed or its builder was
- absent (air-gapped host / dev-VM overlay where automation/ isn't checked out),
- SEED the venv from the deployed OCI image. 38-hermes-agent ran WITH build-time
- egress during the OCI build, so localhost/mios:latest ALWAYS carries a working
- venv -- extracting it needs NO network. (A bare-metal bootc host already has
- the venv baked into its rootfs, so this whole block is skipped there.) Without
- this, an offline agent-venv build left mios-agent-pipe/hermes DOWN after every
- install -> the operator-reported "outages / must deploy every time".
- ── 2. llama.cpp GGUFs (llama.cpp-NATIVE -- HF download; G5/G8) ─
- GGUFs are normally BAKED at build by automation/73-model-prep.sh (the
- offline-correct path). This firstboot block is the ONLINE retry for hosts that
- didn't bake them: it fetches the SAME MIOS_LLAMACPP_BAKE_MODELS spec
- (dest.gguf=hf_repo:file, FOSS pre-quantized) directly from Hugging Face via a
- plain curl of the resolve URL -- NO legacy-backend dependency (G5) and NO
- huggingface_hub/pip dependency (G8: the runtime pip install failed on
- air-gapped/locked hosts). When air-gapped + unbaked the lane stays inert
- (operator sets [llamacpp].bake_models + rebuilds, or seeds ${MODELS} manually)
- -- it never blocks boot.
- VRAM/size tradeoffs:
- - lfm2-700m (micro/CPU lane reasoning, ~0.7GB size, ~0.7GB VRAM): Extremely lightweight and fast, but python-specific tool call formatting.
- - embeddinggemma-300m-qat-q8_0 (Google EmbeddingGemma QAT, ~0.5GB size, ~0.5GB VRAM): Tiny footprint, native 768d vector compatibility.
- - granite-4.1-8b (brain, ~5.5GB size, ~8GB VRAM with 32k KV): Full tool-use reasoning capabilities, but heavy to download/run on low-end.
- Direct HF resolve URL -- NO huggingface_hub / pip dependency
- (G8: the runtime pip install was the firstboot failure on
- air-gapped/locked hosts). curl --fail (no 200 -> non-zero),
- -L (follow the CDN redirect), -C - (resume a partial .part).
- Download to a .part then atomic-rename so a truncated file
- never trips the .ready gate.
- ── 2b. vLLM model weights (vLLM-NATIVE -- HF download; opt-in, off-by-default) ──
- ── 2c. code-run sandbox: the dry-run sandbox Quadlet (mios-coderun-sandbox@)
- is a USER unit -- it uses %t (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR) + is started via
- `systemctl --user` by mios-coderun-session. For the mios-ai SERVICE account
- (agent-pipe) to start it headless, mios-ai needs LINGER so a persistent user
- systemd manager + the podman user generator run without an interactive login.
- Without this, run_sandboxed_code fails (systemctl --user: no bus / unit not
- found) and the agent reports a sandbox permission error (operator 2026-06-12).
- (a) subuid/subgid: the sandbox Quadlet uses UserNS=keep-id, which needs a
- rootless sub-id range for mios-ai. Build-time canonical is
- automation/11-user.sh; this is the runtime retry for overlay/WSL hosts where
- mios-ai was added without a range. Allocate the next free block after
- user/mios (524288:65536) -> 589824:65536, idempotently.
- (b) linger: persistent user manager so `systemctl --user` (used by
- mios-coderun-session) works headless for the mios-ai service account.
- ── 2d. code-run sandbox IMAGE: the user-scope Quadlet starts
- localhost/mios-coderun-sandbox:latest, which must exist in mios-ai's ROOTLESS
- store (rootless has its own image store, separate from rootful). Build it from
- the shipped context if missing -- a network build (alpine + toolkit),
- best-effort, retries next boot on failure. Needs the linger+subids above.
- ── 2e. seed accounts into pgvector datastore ──────────────────────────────────
- Waits up to 90 seconds for pgvector to accept connections, then parses
- mios.toml configurations to seed database accounts.
- 1. Wait for pgvector socket
- 2. Parse layered TOML files
- 3. Add default 'user'/'user' account first (vendor default)
- 4. Extract identity account
- 5. Extract additional accounts
- 5b. Extract AI agents from [agents] section
- 6. Build statements for mios-pg-query
- Generate NTLM hash
- Execute bulk statements via mios-pg-query --exec-json
- Try multiple paths for mios-pg-query
- Seeding system configurations and verbs into database
- ── 2b. pre-stage firstboot-tier images degrade-open ─────────────────────────
- ── 3. (re)start the AI services now their prerequisites exist ────────────────
- --no-block on hermes-agent + mios-agent-pipe: firstboot must NOT wait on them
- settling. They have their own readiness deps and can deadlock against the
- firstboot ordering -- the ~23min early-boot hang (2026-06-14). mios-llm-light
- is the inference lane (no firstboot ordering dependency) so a plain restart is
- fine there.
- ── sentinel: only when fully provisioned, so failures retry next boot ────────
- DEGRADE-OPEN (R8): a partial provision must NOT crash-loop the unit or hold
- the AI plane hostage. Log a WARNING and exit 0 so the unit shows success;
- the sentinel above is deliberately NOT touched, so mios-ai-firstboot.timer
- re-fires this script (~10min cadence) until the venv+GGUFs+vLLM are all in.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-hint-coverage
- SSOT (walk + existing_hint + indexable + SKIP/EXT) to measure what fraction of
- taggable source files carry an `AI-hint:` header, and FAILS (exit 1) when the
- untagged count exceeds a ratchet ceiling ([ai_tag].max_untagged in mios.toml,
- env MIOS_AITAG_MAX_UNTAGGED, or --max-untagged). Read-only; a CI/build drift
- gate that stops AI-hint coverage from regressing. Defines NO file/keyword lists
- of its own -- taggability is whatever mios-ai-tag says it is.
- The SSOT is the tagger; without it we cannot measure. Degrade open --
- a missing tagger must not red an unrelated build.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-reset
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-reset [--dry-run]
- Clean-slate the MiOS AI stack: wipe all chat sessions, kanban state,
- scratch/memory, observability batches, browser sidecar profiles, and
- /tmp AI artifacts. PRESERVES: user accounts, configs, models, vendor
- skills, installed deps, sudoers grants.
- Use case (operator directive 2026-05-15): before a focused live test,
- nuke conversational state so the agent starts with a fresh kanban and
- no carry-over from prior runs.
- What gets wiped:
- * Hermes:  state.db, kanban.db, response_store.db, sessions/,
- logs/, memories/, channel_directory.json, gateway_state.json,
- .skills_prompt_snapshot.json (gateway + operator-side CLI)
- * OWUI:    chat / message / chatidtag / tag / feedback / file / folder
- / memory tables (preserves user, auth, config, models,
- functions, tools, prompts, groups)
- * Observ:  /var/lib/mios/log-watcher/*.json{,l},
- /var/lib/mios/cron-director/*.json
- * Browser: /var/lib/mios/hermes-browser/* (ChromeDev profile),
- /run/mios-hermes-browser/*
- * /tmp:    agent-debug recordings, hermes-* tempfiles
- * Caches:  opencode .local/share + .cache trees
- What is PRESERVED:
- * /usr/share/mios/* (vendor, read-only)
- * /etc/mios/* (operator config + overrides)
- * /var/lib/mios/hermes/{config.yaml,SOUL.md,skills/,bin/,.local/,
- .config/,.npm/,.var/,platforms/,sandboxes/} (installed deps)
- * /var/lib/mios/open-webui/webui.db user/auth/config tables
- Restarts: hermes-agent, mios-open-webui, mios-log-watcher,
- mios-cron-director, mios-hermes-browser
- Idempotent. Safe to re-run. --dry-run prints what would be wiped.
- ─── Denylist guardrail ───────────────────────────────────────────────
- Operator-confirmed incident 2026-05-15: during a clean-slate run,
- /mnt/c/MiOS (the Windows-side source checkout) was found wiped down
- to a single file. Cause never traced to this script's rm patterns,
- BUT the consequences of an accidental targeting are catastrophic
- enough that we treat it as a hard guardrail: every rm/find -delete
- below is constrained by these denylist roots. If any expansion
- would touch one, mios-ai-reset bails before doing anything.
- _check_safe <path>  -- exits 99 if path matches a deny root EXACTLY.
- Sub-paths under a deny root are fine (we DO wipe sub-paths like
- /root/.hermes/sessions/* and /var/home/mios/.hermes/sessions/*);
- the guard is on the root itself plus any /mnt traversal.
- TD-1: eval-safe, input=internal hardcoded paths and variables, not agent-controlled
- Privilege check.
- Must look like a .hermes dir -- never .hermes==/ or similar.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-ai-tag
- + AI-related files/services/verbs + AI-functions) on every MiOS-authored file
- so agents grasp each file's use, purpose, dependencies and entrypoints at a
- glance, and mios-codebase-index can harvest it. Reuses an existing AI-hint
- (no re-LLM), generates a fresh purpose line via the local teacher when absent,
- and regex-extracts related-files + functions (accurate, no hallucination).
- Idempotent, resumable (--manifest), comment/shebang/line-ending safe.
- strip ALL AI-* header lines on retag (hint/related/functions), any comment style
- ---- existing-hint reuse + extraction ---------------------------------------
- ---- regex structure extraction (accurate, grounded) ------------------------
- systemd units -- NOT '.path' (it false-matches os.path/request.path etc.);
- real .path units are rare and still caught as mios-* / quadlet names.
- ports -> labelled 'localhost:NNNN' so the hint reads as an endpoint, not a bare int
- ---- teacher (purpose line; only when no existing hint) ----------------------
- ---- safe (re)insertion -----------------------------------------------------
- A leading UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF) MUST stay at byte 0: irm|iex and `irm | iex`
- style canonical installs parse Get-MiOS.ps1 only if the BOM (when present) is
- the very first byte. Strip it off the body before we splice the AI header in,
- then re-prepend it to the FINAL bytes -- otherwise the header lands ABOVE the
- BOM and strands U+FEFF mid-file (the Get-MiOS.ps1 install break, 2026-06-14).
- ---- selection --------------------------------------------------------------

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-app-default
- Very basic TOML array-of-tables injection

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-app-type
