## usr/libexec/mios/mios-apps
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-apps [--json] [--names] [--filter <substr>] [--category <cat>]
- Inventory of EVERY launchable thing on this MiOS host. One unified
- surface across:
- linux-flatpak    flatpaks installed system-wide (flatpak list --system)
- linux-rpm-gui    host-installed GUI RPMs (.desktop files; not NoDisplay)
- windows-gui      Windows host apps reachable via WSL interop
- mios-shim        MiOS shell helpers under /usr/libexec/mios/ + /usr/local/bin/
- agent-cli        agent toolchain CLIs (hermes, opencode, ...)
- service-url      known internal-service URLs (Cockpit, OWUI, Forgejo, ...)
- Operator directive 2026-05-15: "MiOS-Agents should be aware of all
- systems; and be able to launch apps regardless of environment".
- This helper is the awareness half; mios-launch is the launch half.
- Default output is a human-readable table grouped by category. For
- agent-friendly machine reading, use --json. For piping into other
- helpers, --names prints bare launch names one per line.
- Agents repeatedly call `mios-apps <query>` positionally
- instead of `mios-apps --filter <query>` and then conclude
- the tool is broken. Substitute the operator-typed value
- into the hint so the next-turn invocation is obvious.
- ─── helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- emit <category> <name> <description> <launch-hint>
- Match name/desc OR the CATEGORY (with a trailing-'s' stem) so a
- natural-language category word resolves to the right GROUP: "games" ->
- the "windows-game" category (ALL stores -- Steam/Epic/GOG/Store -- emit
- THERE, not separate per-store cats), "browsers" -> a browser cat, etc.
- The old name+desc-only match returned just the lone entry whose NAME
- happened to contain the word (e.g. "Wreckfest (NordicGames)") and
- DROPPED the Steam/Epic titles whose names lack it -> "what games" listed
- 1 of N (operator 2026-05-29). Generic stem match, no hardcoded
- keyword->category table.
- Wine-free Steam library scan. The Windows-side PowerShell pass reaches the
- real host only through WSL-interop, which is silently hijacked when a Wine
- binfmt handler intercepts .exe (games then invisible). Steam's library is
- plain-text VDF readable straight off the drvfs /mnt mount -- parse it there,
- with ZERO .exe execution, and emit "<name>|steam://rungameid/<appid>" lines.
- The registry SteamPath is the true SSOT but is unreadable from bash; the
- default install root only BOOTSTRAPS us to libraryfolders.vdf, which then
- enumerates every real library on any drive (so non-default installs are
- still covered).
- ─── 1. linux-flatpak ────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── 2. linux-rpm-gui ────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Skip NoDisplay=true (not user-visible) and Hidden=true entries.
- Only show entries whose Exec= resolves to an actual binary.
- strip flatpak --command, %F/%U placeholders, env vars
- ─── 3. windows-gui (GENERATIVE: live Start-Menu discovery, NO hardcoded list) ─
- operator 2026-05-29: "every app is DISCOVERED + executed from its installed
- path(s), not a hardcoded apps list". The Start Menu (.lnk catalog under
- %ProgramData% + %APPDATA% Programs) is Windows' canonical registry of what is
- ACTUALLY installed; each .lnk basename IS the app name, and `mios-windows
- launch <name>` resolves its real path at launch time (App Paths registry ->
- System32/Windows -> Start Menu -> Everything). So we enumerate the live menu
- instead of baking in a fixed list -- an app the operator installs shows up
- automatically, and one that isn't installed simply isn't listed. Capped +
- de-duplicated; best-effort (empty if PowerShell isn't exec-able from this uid
- -- the launch-time fallback still discovers any named app generatively).
- ── Wine-free native enumeration (PRIMARY) ──────────────────────────
- mios-win-scan reads the REAL host off the /mnt drvfs mount directly
- (Steam/Epic/GOG/Store-UWP/Start-Menu), so the inventory is correct even when
- .exe interop is hijacked by a Wine binfmt handler -- the single failure mode
- that made every Windows game/app invisible. When it yields results, the
- Wine-dependent PowerShell scans below are SKIPPED (set -e-safe, degrade-open).
- Skip WSLg-exported loopback shortcuts to avoid self-referential loops
- `|| true`: pwsh.exe returns non-zero when interop is down / hijacked by
- ─── 3a. windows-app (every Start-menu app on the Windows host) ──────
- Operator directive 2026-05-15: "should automatically detect installed
- hardware, services and especially; applications GLOBALLY (ALL
- SYSTEMS, ex: Windows, Linux, etc)". Get-StartApps returns ~every
- user-launchable app on the Windows side -- Win32 + UWP/MSIX --
- without the slow Win32_Product WMI walk. Cached for 5 minutes
- under /tmp/mios-windows-apps.cache to avoid the ~1s round-trip cost
- on every mios-apps call.
- Cache under /var/lib/mios/agent-env (shared dir already used for
- the games cache; world-writable via tmpfiles.d). Previous path
- /tmp/<file> stuck to whichever uid wrote it first, leaving the
- other (operator vs mios-hermes) forever blocked from `mv`-ing
- the tmp file in. Operator-flagged 2026-05-19.
- Get-StartApps -> CSV-style "Name|AppID" lines, one per app.
- Strip CR + trim
- Skip Microsoft.AutoGenerated.{GUID} AppX shims: Windows auto-creates
- these for desktop apps that ALSO register App Paths + Clients\
- StartMenuInternet (notably browsers like Zen) -- redundant GUID-named
- dupes that fuzzy-match real queries ("zen browser" -> the Zen
- AutoGenerated shim) and shadow the clean windows-browser / App-Paths
- resolution. The real app stays reachable via the windows-browser
- section + `mios-windows launch <name>` (App Paths). No hardcoded app
- list -- this filters a Windows-internal auto-gen ID pattern only.
- short = first word lowercased; not unique but useful for filtering
- If win_id is a URI handler (uplay://, steam://, epic://,
- http://, etc.), pass it DIRECTLY to Start-Process -- the
- `shell:AppsFolder\` prefix only works for UWP App-User-Model-
- IDs (curly-brace GUIDs + executable path), not URI schemes.
- Operator-confirmed regression 2026-05-16: "The Crew Motorfest
- (uplay://launch/16732/0)" emitted shell:AppsFolder\uplay://...
- which Windows rejects.
- ─── 3c. windows-browser (GENERATIVE default + registered browsers) ──
- operator 2026-06-15: the OS DEFAULT browser (e.g. Zen) is a Program Files
- install + URL-protocol handler, NOT a Get-StartApps / Start-Menu entry, so it
- was INVISIBLE to the inventory -> `mios-find "zen"` missed and mis-matched a
- garbage AutoGenerated UWP, and "open a tab" fell to the wrong browser. Discover
- browsers from Windows' CANONICAL registry (HKLM/HKCU Clients\StartMenuInternet)
- + the live https UserChoice default -- NO hardcoded browser list. Each resolves
- to its real exe basename (browsers register App Paths, so `mios-windows launch
- <name>` opens it); the OS default is marked so the agent can prefer it.
- `|| true`: under `set -o pipefail` a non-zero exit from the Windows-side
- PowerShell (interop down / hijacked by Wine) would fail the whole pipe and,
- under `set -e`, abort mios-apps entirely before the games section runs.
- ─── 3b. windows-game (Steam + Epic + GOG library scan) ──────────────
- Get-StartApps misses many installed games -- Steam games typically
- don't get individual Start Menu shortcuts (Steam itself does, but
- not each title). Operator-flagged 2026-05-16: "launch beamng on my
- pc" returned no match. Steam's library has appmanifest_<APPID>.acf
- files containing the "installdir" key -- scanning those gives us
- every installed Steam game.
- Same for Epic (.item manifests under ProgramData\Epic\
- EpicGamesLauncher\Data\Manifests) and GOG (Games subdirs under
- C:\Program Files (x86)\GOG Galaxy\Games\).
- Single PowerShell pass over Steam + Epic + GOG library locations.
- Output format: "<name>|<exe-path>" one per line. 45s budget: the
- COLD pass now also runs Get-AppxPackage + per-title marker Test-Paths
- for Game Pass discovery, which exceeds the old 12s on a cold WSL-
- interop start -> the && mv chain failed -> cache wiped -> 0 games
- (operator 2026-05-27). Result is cached 10 min, so the cost is rare.
- Steam: discover EVERY library folder from Steam itself -- the registry
- SteamPath + steamapps\libraryfolders.vdf -- so games on ANY drive/path are
- found, not just 3 guessed drives (operator 2026-05-27 "all the tools and it
- found 3 games?!! no hardcodes"). libraryfolders.vdf lists each library as a
- "path" "<dir>" entry (backslashes doubled). [char]34 = a double-quote, to
- avoid nesting quotes inside this bash-single-quoted PowerShell block.
- Steam launch URL bypasses .exe discovery entirely
- Epic: .item manifests (resolve ProgramData from the env, not a hardcoded C:).
- GOG Galaxy: enumerate from the registry -- each installed game has a key
- carrying its name + install path + exe, so no hardcoded install dirs (works
- on ANY drive). Both 64- and 32-bit hives.
- Microsoft Store / Xbox / UWP / Game Pass titles. These don'\''t
- expose an .exe at a predictable filesystem path -- Get-StartApps
- returns them as Name + AppID, where AppID is the canonical
- `<PackageFamilyName>!<Entry>` format. Launching = `cmd /c start ""
- shell:appsFolder\<AppID>` (handled by mios-windows shell: branch).
- Pattern-filter to games-y entries: anything whose Name contains
- common game-store hint words OR whose PFN matches known game
- publishers. Avoids dumping every Calculator / Notepad / system
- UWP app into the games cache (those already appear via mios-apps'\''
- windows-app section from Get-StartApps).
- Detect games by the MicrosoftGame.config marker every PC Store/Game Pass
- title ships in its install dir -- NO name-list, NO publisher-list, NO
- hardcoded path (operator 2026-05-27 "no hardcodes globally"). Join
- Get-StartApps (launchable AppID) with Get-AppxPackage (install location) and
- test for the marker; launch via shell:appsFolder\<AppID>.
- Dedup: SteamPath (registry) and libraryfolders.vdf can name the SAME library
- in different letter-case, scanning it twice; collapse identical entries.
- `|| true`: the PowerShell pass exits non-zero when WSL-interop is
- unavailable or hijacked by Wine; under `set -e` that would abort the
- ENTIRE mios-apps (losing games AND every later category). Best-effort.
- Merge the Wine-free native Steam scan so Steam games are found even
- when .exe interop is broken (the PowerShell pass then yields nothing).
- Dedup by line so a game seen by both passes appears once.
- Only cache output with REAL game lines ("name|target"). A garbage/error
- pass (e.g. an interop "powershell.exe: Invalid argument" that lands on
- stdout with exit 0) has no "|" -> discard so the next call re-scans
- instead of serving poison for 10 min (operator 2026-05-30 live-drive).
- Failed/empty/garbage pass: drop the tmp AND any stale cache so a
- previous poison line is never re-served (the file persists otherwise).
- A real game line is "name|launch-target". A line with NO launch
- target (no "|" -> empty g_path) is scan GARBAGE, e.g. a
- "powershell.exe: Invalid argument" interop error that landed on
- stdout and got captured -- NOT a game. Skip it so one failed scan
- can never poison the games list and make the agent report "no games"
- / fail to launch (operator 2026-05-30 live-drive: the error line
- became a fake game and broke "launch the best").
- Full lowercased name as the lookup key so multi-word queries
- (e.g. "wallpaper engine", "microsoft flight simulator") match
- via mios-find. Previously this was awk '{print tolower($1)}'
- which only kept the first word -- "Wallpaper Engine" became
- name="wallpaper" and the agent couldn't match the operator's
- natural-language "open wallpaper engine for me" against any
- inventory entry (operator-flagged 2026-05-17: "open
- wallpaper engine for me" -> "isn'\''t installed on your
- system" loop, agent never reached mios-find -> launch).
- For Steam: launch via steam:// URI handler (cleaner than .exe path)
- For Epic: launch via com.epicgames.launcher URI handler
- For GOG: direct .exe launch
- All paths funnel through `mios-windows launch <X>` -- its URI
- branch (steam://, com.epicgames.launcher://, shell:appsFolder\)
- wraps Start-Process with a snapshot + poll-for-new-window +
- center+focus pass so the operator never gets a top-left or
- off-screen launch. The MIOS_LAUNCH_TITLE_HINT env var tells
- the centerer which new window to pick when the protocol
- handler spawns multiple (e.g. Steam: storefront AND game).
- Operator directive 2026-05-17: "launching apps should launch
- centered too!! ... should always launch centered and focused".
- ─── 4. mios-shim ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- /usr/local/bin shims that aren't already in /usr/libexec/mios
- Pull the first comment-line description (after the shebang) as the desc
- ─── 5. agent-cli ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── 6. service-url ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Ports from SSOT: install.env bridges mios.toml [ports] -> MIOS_PORT_*.
- Hardcoded literals here silently break when [ports] is renumbered (T-120/T-121).
- Guard set -u: a value with shell-metachars must not abort under set -u.
- Always succeed if we ran: this is a best-effort GENERATIVE enumerator across
- Linux + Windows sources; a non-zero from a probe (e.g. the Windows games PS on
- a host without Steam) must NOT mark the whole dispatch failed when app data WAS
- emitted. The dispatch layer reads success from this exit code.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-as-operator
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-as-operator <command> [args...]
- Re-exec a command as the operator user IN A REAL WSL LOGIN SESSION
- so launched GUI apps inherit WSLg's full env (WAYLAND_DISPLAY,
- WSL2_GUI_APPS_ENABLED=1, WSL_INTEROP=/run/WSL/<pid>_interop, the
- operator's user@1000.service bus). This is the missing piece for
- launching flatpak GUI apps from the agent's restricted service-user
- context: systemd-run --uid=mios sets the uid but doesn't establish
- a WSL login session, so WSL2_GUI_APPS_ENABLED + WSL_INTEROP stay
- unset and the flatpak portal-helper can't bootstrap (epiphany +
- similar fail with "--env-fd: Not an open file descriptor: 13" and
- "Connection: failed to receive credentials"; operator-confirmed
- regression 2026-05-15).
- Mechanism: wsl.exe is reachable from inside the WSL distro via /init
- interop. Calling `wsl.exe -d <distro> --user <op> -- <cmd>` spins up
- a fresh login shell on the operator's behalf with the full WSLg env
- bootstrapped by the WSL service. The launched command keeps running
- detached after wsl.exe returns.
- Usage:
- mios-as-operator flatpak run org.gnome.Epiphany https://...
- mios-as-operator gnome-software
- mios-as-operator <any-command-that-needs-the-operator-WSLg-session>
- Operator user is read from mios.toml [identity].username (default mios).
- ─── Path 1: operator launcher broker (preferred) ─────────────────
- Try the operator's mios-launcher.service unix socket first. If
- present and writable, we just dump the shell line into it and the
- operator-side daemon spawns the command. This bypasses the
- /mnt/c/Windows/System32/wsl.exe perm wall (mios-hermes can't
- exec wsl.exe but CAN write to a socket the operator-side daemon
- is listening on).
- Quote the command line for safe transit through bash -lc
- Strip leading space; send single line + newline; read the OK/ERROR.
- Always python -- the nc / ncat fallbacks were unreliable across
- distro nc variants (operator-debug 2026-05-15: /usr/sbin/nc on
- MiOS doesn't accept -q so the dispatch returned empty + fell
- through to the wsl.exe path which mios-hermes can't exec).
- Python is always present.
- Silent success -- the dispatched command runs
- detached; no extra noise needed for the agent's chat.
- Don't fall through on explicit error; wsl.exe path
- would hit the same upstream issue.
- Empty response = couldn't reach broker (socket gone,
- daemon not running). Silently fall through to wsl.exe.
- ─── Path 2: wsl.exe --user (fallback for operator's own shell) ─
- Resolve operator user from mios.toml [identity].username.
- Resolve WSL distro name. Priority:
- 1. $WSL_DISTRO_NAME env (set by WSL itself when present in any
- shell that came in through interop -- absent in service-user
- contexts that didn't go through wsl.exe entry)
- 2. /etc/mios/wsl-distro file (operator-managed pin)
- 3. wsl.exe -l (parsed for the running distro on this host)
- 4. fallback default for the canonical MiOS-DEV layout
- wsl.exe -l --quiet (no headers, just distro names; first line == default).
- The output is UTF-16; strip nulls + CRs to get a clean ASCII line.
- Quote the command + args for transport through wsl.exe -- bash -lc.
- Each arg gets wrapped in single quotes with embedded single quotes
- escaped. Defensive: never assume the agent passed safe arg shapes.
- Detached invocation: wsl.exe with -- nohup setsid <cmd>. The wsl
- process itself returns once the inner shell forks; the inner
- command keeps running with a real WSL session attached.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-autocenter
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-autocenter <executor-endpoint> <before-hwnds-csv>
- Honour the operator rule "all apps launch CENTERED ALWAYS!" for WSLg /
- flatpak windows, which ignore Win32 launch-time placement (the Windows
- executor only sees them AFTER the compositor maps them).
- Strategy: the CALLER snapshots the set of visible window hwnds BEFORE
- firing the launch and passes that CSV as $2. We then poll the Windows
- OS-control executor (:11437, [os_control].executor_endpoint) for a hwnd
- that was NOT in the before-set -- i.e. the freshly-mapped window -- and
- center it by HWND. Centering by hwnd (not title) is robust for apps whose
- window title doesn't carry the app-id: Nautilus="Files", Epiphany="GNOME
- Web", gnome-text-editor="Untitled Document", etc.
- Backgrounded with setsid by the caller so it outlives the launch shim.
- No-op (exit 0) when no executor endpoint, no curl, or no python3.
- Pick the LARGEST new window (max w*h) -- the MAIN app window, not a tiny
- tooltip/popup/PopupHost that a Store/Win32 app also spawns (operator
- 2026-05-29: notepad opened with 11 popup windows; centering must hit the
- real document window). Falls back gracefully when sizes are absent.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-bake-group
- mios-bake-group -- bake ONE group of the bound sidecar images into the
- additional image store at /usr/lib/containers/storage.
- WHY THIS EXISTS (commit-fit):
- The full bound-images bake is split across several calls -- one RUN per group
- in the Containerfile -- so each `buildah commit` serializes only THAT group's
- layer diff instead of the whole ~40-60GB store at once. A single monolithic
- commit overran disk-constrained CI runners: `exit 125` / "io: read/write on
- closed pipe" while storing the layer (buildah writes ~2-3x the layer's diff
- to temp during commit -- containers/podman#22342). Every image is STILL baked
- (Law 12 BAKE-NOT-FETCH / Law 3 BOUND-IMAGES); only the layer boundaries move.
- Heavy GPU-engine images (the "heavy" group) commit FIRST, while the store is
- smallest, so the largest indivisible diff lands with the most free space.
- Usage:  mios-bake-group <group-name>
- Group order + per-group substring tokens come from the SSOT
- (usr/share/mios/mios.toml [build].bake_groups / [build].bake_group.<name>).
- Each bound image is assigned to the FIRST group whose tokens substring-match
- its rendered Image= ref; anything unmatched falls into the LAST group (the
- catch-all). This call pulls only the images assigned to <group-name>.
- Env:
- MIOS_BAKE_BOUND_IMAGES=0   skip entirely (disk-constrained / PR-validation
- builds; sidecars resolve at bootc DEPLOY time).
- MIOS_TOML   SSOT path              (default /usr/share/mios/mios.toml)
- STORE       additional image store (default /usr/lib/containers/storage)
- SCRATCH     transient pull/commit scratch, kept OUT of the committed layer
- via the Containerfile --mount=type=cache (default
- /var/tmp/mios-bakescratch)
- BDIR        bound-images dir       (default /usr/lib/bootc/bound-images.d)
- Digests are SBOM data (build-time-recorded), NEVER hardcoded in the SSOT: the
- SSOT ref is :latest (newest intent); the resolved digest is captured HERE, at
- pull time, into the SBOM provenance manifest.
- Inner store config with file-level dedup: the CUDA/torch engine images (vLLM,
- SGLang, llama-swap:cuda) share GBs of byte-identical layers; hard-linking
- stores each blob once AND shrinks each group's commit diff. use_hard_links is
- REQUIRED on ext4 (the GHA build disk) -- reflink-only dedup silently no-ops
- there. convert_images makes it apply to the non-chunked upstream images.
- Docker Hub anonymous pulls of the docker.io sidecars can hit the shared-IP rate
- limit on CI runners (HTTP 429 "toomanyrequests"); 5 quick retries won't clear a
- 6-hour window. Route docker.io through mirror.gcr.io -- Google's public pull-
- through cache of Docker Hub -- for THIS bake's podman only, with automatic
- fallback to docker.io when the mirror lacks an image. Build-time-scoped via
- CONTAINERS_REGISTRIES_CONF (below); never written into the image's registries.
- --- Read which images belong to THIS group from the pre-projected plan.d lists ---
- Record the RESOLVED manifest digest to the SBOM provenance manifest --
- this is where the :latest ref's concrete identity is captured (digests
- are SBOM, not a hardcoded literal in mios.toml).
- drop transient decompress scratch so it never enters the committed layer

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-build-driver
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-build-driver
- Entry point for the inside-MiOS-DEV phase of the MiOS build pipeline.
- This script is INVOKED FROM WINDOWS (via `wt.exe new-tab wsl.exe -d
- MiOS-DEV ... bash /usr/libexec/mios/mios-build-driver`) AFTER the
- Windows-side bootstrap finishes:
- Day-0 split (per the self-replication architecture):
- * Windows side  irm | iex -> ack -> MiOS-DEV podman machine setup
- * <handoff>     Show-PostBootstrapMenu choice "Continue to build"
- spawns a fresh Windows Terminal hosting `wsl.exe
- -d MiOS-DEV` running THIS driver
- * MiOS-DEV side fetch + overlay + identity + FULL build pipeline
- for all output formats (OCI, WSL2/g, Hyper-V,
- QEMU, Live-CD/USB, USB installer, RAW)
- The Windows side does NOT stream the build dashboard back -- the
- dashboard renders on MiOS-DEV's tty inside the SSH/wsl session, and
- the Windows Terminal is the host of that tty. That keeps the
- multi-GB, multi-image build off the WSL2/Windows boundary.
- Idempotent: re-running picks up where the previous attempt left off
- (clone is shallow; build cache is podman-managed; identity is
- already-saved-to-/etc/mios/install.env on second run).
- ── MiOS dashboard (banner + fastfetch + motd stats) ─────────────────────────
- The operator's expectation per the architecture memo is that the
- Windows-Terminal-hosted SSH window shows the unified MiOS dashboard,
- not just plain build output. /etc/issue.d/ has the live banner
- rendered by mios-dashboard-issue.service; printing it once here
- anchors the operator in the MiOS context before the build noise
- starts.
- ── Logging ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- When invoked as the mios user (the canonical handoff path from
- Windows: `wsl.exe -d podman-MiOS-DEV --user mios`), /var/log/mios
- is root-owned (FHS) and the tee write fails with "Permission denied".
- Combined with `set -euo pipefail` that silently kills the driver
- before it prints anything useful, dropping the operator to an
- interactive login bash prompt -- exactly the regression operator
- flagged 2026-05-09: "[mios@CloudWS-602 ~]$ ... random invisible
- square window... NOTHING actually happening".
- Fix: fall back to $XDG_STATE_HOME (or $HOME/.local/state/mios) when
- /var/log/mios isn't writable.  Root invocations still get the
- canonical /var/log path; non-root land in $HOME and can rotate /
- tail without sudo.
- Probe write access -- if mkdir failed or the dir isn't writable,
- fall through to /tmp so the driver still emits visible output.
- ── curl fallback build-trigger ──────────────────────────────────────────────
- The PRIMARY build trigger is the local `sudo podman build` further down. When
- podman is unavailable the OCI image cannot be built here; rather than dead-end,
- TRIGGER the Forgejo CI build over HTTP with curl -- the same self-replication
- loop `git push` drives, reached through the workflow's own workflow_dispatch
- entrypoint (.forgejo/workflows/build-mios.yml). Endpoints resolve from the SSOT
- bridge install.env (MIOS_HOSTNAME + MIOS_PORT_FORGE_HTTP, sourced via
- userenv.sh) -- never a literal host:port. Gated by [build].curl_trigger_fallback:
- degrade-open (enabled when the key is ABSENT so a runtime with no podman still
- self-heals via CI); set false to keep the historical hard-fail.
- Shared layered mios.toml resolver (vendor < host < user), path injected as argv[1].
- Degrade-open: absent key -> enabled (exit 0); honor the highest layer that sets it.
- Derive <owner>/<repo> from the origin URL (http or scp-like), .git-stripped.
- URL passed as argv (NOT piped stdin): `python3 - <<HEREDOC` reads its program
- from stdin, which would shadow a pipe and leave the parse empty.
- Workflow-dispatch needs an API token; read from env or the secrets bridge.
- ── Privilege preflight ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- The build pipeline writes /etc, overlays /, sets up accounts, persists
- /etc/mios/secrets.env, and runs rootful `podman build` -- it MUST run
- as root or as a user with NON-interactive sudo. Locked-down service
- users (notably mios-hermes, uid 820 -- the user the MiOS/Hermes agent
- runs as) have neither: nologin, not in wheel, no sudoers entry.
- Without this check the driver gets several steps in -- prints a
- dashboard, clones mios-bootstrap, enters unattended mode -- then dies
- mid-stream on the first `sudo` with the cryptic "sudo: a password is
- required". Agents then invent a fake success around that partial
- output (operator-confirmed 2026-05-14). Detect the privilege gap UP
- FRONT, before any work, and fail with ONE clear, honest, actionable
- message so the caller (human or agent) knows exactly what to do.
- ── Sandbox escape (mount-namespace) ─────────────────────────────────────────
- Even with root + a sudo grant, the build still fails when invoked from
- inside a hardened service's mount namespace (e.g., the agent's
- hermes-agent.service has ProtectSystem=strict, which remounts /usr,
- /boot, and most of / read-only INSIDE the service's mount namespace).
- sudo elevates UID/GID and capabilities -- it does NOT call setns(),
- so the child inherits the parent's mount namespace and sees the same
- read-only view. The build then dies on the first write outside
- ReadWritePaths:
- "Error: open /var/lib/containers/storage/storage.lock: read-only file system"
- "error: cannot open '.git/FETCH_HEAD': Read-only file system"
- Operators (and agents) blame "WSL" or "permissions" and chase the
- wrong fix (operator-confirmed 2026-05-15).
- Fix: detect the read-only-namespace condition (root sees a known
- root-writable dir as read-only) and re-exec via `systemd-run --scope`,
- which spawns a transient unit OUTSIDE the calling service's namespace
- with a fresh, default mount view. This is the only way to escape a
- parent service's namespace short of explicit setns() with CAP_SYS_ADMIN.
- Preserves all CLI args; the re-exec inherits stdin/stdout/stderr via --pty.
- Probe BOTH cases: agent might invoke us as root (after sudo wrap), OR as
- the unprivileged service user with a passwordless sudo grant. Both are
- affected identically by the parent service's mount namespace -- read-only
- is read-only regardless of UID. Earlier the probe only ran when id==0,
- so non-root invocations slipped past the escape and died later on `sudo
- podman build` (operator-confirmed 2026-05-15: agent dropped the `sudo`
- from `sudo mios build`, ran the driver as uid 820, escape never fired,
- build hit storage.lock read-only mid-pipeline).
- KEY POINT: --service mode (the default; do NOT pass --scope) is
- what escapes the mount namespace. --scope only registers the
- existing systemd-run process in a new cgroup; the exec happens
- in systemd-run's own namespace, which is the caller's restricted
- one (verified empirically -- /.git stays read-only with --scope).
- --service mode causes PID 1 to FORK the unit fresh, so the new
- process inherits PID 1's default mount namespace -- the host
- root view, not the agent's sandbox.
- --pipe:    forward stdin/stdout/stderr via anonymous pipes
- (works without a tty; agent invocations are headless)
- --wait:    block until the unit exits, propagate exit code
- --collect: drop failed transient unit instead of keeping it
- --quiet:   no "Running as unit:" preamble in stderr
- --uid=0:   run as root explicitly (we already are, but be loud)
- --same-dir:keep CWD instead of jumping to /
- Wrap with sudo when we're NOT already root -- systemd-run needs
- CAP_SYS_ADMIN/root to register the transient unit with PID 1.
- The privilege preflight above guarantees `sudo -n true` works
- for the calling user when uid != 0 (else we'd have FATAL'd
- before reaching here).
- ── Pre-flight ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- WORKDIR follows the same root-vs-user split the LOG_DIR section above
- uses: root invocations get the canonical /var/lib/mios/build (FHS),
- non-root land under $XDG_STATE_HOME so `mkdir -p` doesn't fail with
- "Permission denied" -- which was killing the driver under `set -euo
- pipefail` before it printed anything useful (regression caught by
- operator 2026-05-09: build chained from Windows-side auto-build,
- handed off as user `mios`, died at this mkdir).
- Resolve the MiOS repo location. Three candidates in priority order:
- 1. /.git -- live working tree (canonical when running on a real
- MiOS host where `.git IS /` per the self-replication contract)
- 2. /var/lib/mios/build/mios -- the dedicated build workspace
- 3. /ctx -- the build-context bind mount inside `podman build`
- Fetch + reset --hard origin/main so the cached clone tracks the
- latest mios.git fixes. Without this, fixes pushed since the
- initial clone never reach the build (driver bugs, userenv.sh
- fixes, Containerfile updates -- all stale until manual rm).
- `|| true` so transient network errors don't kill the build --
- falling back to the cached version is better than no build.
- mios-bootstrap is needed for build helper scripts under automation/lib/.
- ── SSOT preflight drift hardening gate ──
- ── Unattended-mode detection: strictly automated when non-interactive ───────
- `mios build` MUST run end-to-end with ZERO operator prompts whenever it
- is invoked without a real terminal -- by the Hermes/MiOS agent, by CI,
- by the Forgejo runner, or by any `bash -c`. The TOML-first invariant
- already makes mios.toml the SSOT for every value; historically the
- only things that blocked were two `read` prompts -- the configurator
- "press Enter" and the password prompt -- each gated by a SEPARATE
- env var (MIOS_SKIP_CONFIGURATOR vs MIOS_NONINTERACTIVE). That split is
- the "confusion": operators/agents could not find one switch, so agents
- fabricated fake build logs and invented non-existent flags
- (`interactive_password`, `MIOS_SKIP_PROMPTS`) trying to get past it
- (operator-confirmed 2026-05-14).
- Fix: detect a non-TTY stdin -- or an explicit MIOS_NONINTERACTIVE /
- the rest of the driver takes its already-existing no-prompt paths:
- * MIOS_SKIP_CONFIGURATOR=1 -> skip the Epiphany launch + its Enter prompt
- * MIOS_NONINTERACTIVE=1    -> password resolves from /etc/mios/secrets.env
- or the mios.toml [identity].default_password,
- never `read`
- An interactive operator on a real TTY still gets the full guided flow
- unless they opt out explicitly.
- ── Always-pull-from-origin (default) ────────────────────────────────────────
- Operator standing rule: the build always pulls the latest source from
- origin before building. Stale local trees produced repeated
- "the bound-images bake never ran" / "the cd / fix isn't deployed" /
- "wrong Containerfile" surprises -- every build now starts from
- origin/HEAD by default.
- Mechanism: `git -C "$MIOS_REPO" pull --ff-only origin <branch>` over
- whatever protocol the remote is configured for (HTTPS uses libcurl
- under the hood, which is what the operator meant by "via curl").
- Retries 3 times with backoff on transient failure (network blip,
- remote unreachable). On a real TTY the operator gets a 30-second
- countdown with Ctrl+C to abort and use the local tree as-is; in
- unattended mode the pull just runs (no one to press Ctrl+C anyway).
- Skipped entirely when MIOS_NO_PULL=1 (CI / offline / dev-iter).
- If the pull fails after retries: WARN and continue with the local
- tree (a stale build is better than no build -- the warning is loud).
- CRITICAL ORDERING: Configurator FIRST (operator edits the toml in
- Epiphany), then Resolve (sources the edited toml). Don't reverse;
- resolving before the operator has edited would lock in stale values.
- ── Configurator step: Epiphany on /configurator.html ────────────────────────
- Per the self-replication-vision memo:
- "MiOS setup requires Epiphany for editing the SSOT TOML/HTML file
- that's locally present and used to overwrite overlay global defaults"
- Launch the HTML configurator in Epiphany (via WSLg if MiOS-DEV is the
- WSL distro, native Wayland if running on bare-metal MiOS) BEFORE the
- build pipeline starts. The operator edits their identity, model
- choice, package toggles, etc., saves the resulting mios.toml from the
- browser's File System Access API, then presses Enter here to proceed.
- The mios-configurator-launch helper handles the browser plumbing:
- * stages mios.toml in ~/Downloads where the FSA portal can bind it
- * stages the HTML next to it (so file:// URLs resolve relative paths)
- * tries Epiphany flatpak first (best FSA support, WSLg-native)
- * falls back to xdg-open if Epiphany isn't installed
- * last-resort prints the URL for manual copy/paste
- Skipped if MIOS_SKIP_CONFIGURATOR=1 (CI / unattended runs that already
- have a populated /etc/mios/mios.toml from a prior session).
- Defensive: only block on Enter when stdin is a real TTY. The
- unattended-mode block above already forces MIOS_SKIP_CONFIGURATOR=1
- on a non-TTY so this branch is normally unreachable when automated,
- but guard the `read` anyway so a non-TTY caller can never hang here.
- If the operator saved to ~/Downloads/mios.toml (the FSA portal's
- default landing point), promote it to BOTH:
- 1. /etc/mios/mios.toml      -- inside MiOS-DEV, where the build
- pipeline + dev-VM runtime read
- 2. /mnt/m/etc/mios/mios.toml -- the M:\ overlay, so Windows-side
- Get-MiOS.ps1 + build-mios.ps1
- Pass-2 also see the operator's
- edits the next time the bootstrap
- is re-run from WinKey+R
- Per operator "ALL Global packages SOURCE FROM THE TOML/HTML
- FILE!!!" + "now how does changing the html change the toml
- thats read by multiple scripts and components" -- this two-way
- promote closes the SSOT loop: HTML edits → ~/Downloads/mios.toml
- → /etc/mios/ (Linux side) AND /mnt/m/etc/mios/ (Windows side).
- Promote to M:\ overlay for Windows-side bootstrap consumers.
- /mnt/m is the WSL automount of the M:\ drive; if it isn't
- writable (rare, but possible on a stale automount), warn but
- don't fail -- the Linux side still has the canonical edit.
- Re-source the env layering so subsequent steps see the new values.
- shellcheck disable=SC1091
- ── Resolve all settings from the layered mios.toml chain ───────────────────
- Runs AFTER the configurator step so the operator's edits in Epiphany
- (now landed at /etc/mios/mios.toml) are sourced into env.
- CANONICAL: identity, AI choices, locale, image, network, desktop,
- packages-to-layer (every [packages.*] enable flag), hosting/dev/build/
- run profile flags -- EVERY operator-visible setting comes from the
- layered mios.toml, edited via /configurator.html. The driver does NOT
- prompt for any of these values; they're set in the toml.
- Layer chain (highest wins):
- /usr/share/mios/mios.toml      vendor defaults baked into the image
- /etc/mios/mios.toml            host overlay (configurator promotes
- ~/Downloads/mios.toml here when the
- operator clicks Save in Epiphany)
- ~/.config/mios/mios.toml       per-user XDG overlay
- tools/lib/userenv.sh resolves the chain, exports MIOS_* env vars, and
- is the single canonical reader. Source it so the entire build pipeline
- downstream (automation/build.sh, sysusers, tmpfiles, profile.d,
- Containerfile build args) inherits the resolved values without
- re-parsing toml in 12 different ways.
- shellcheck disable=SC1090
- Vendor-shipped fallbacks for any MIOS_* the toml didn't define. Never
- prompt -- the principle is "configurator is SSOT". Missing means the
- operator hasn't edited that field and the vendor default applies.
- Password handling. The toml schema says password_hash is NEVER
- tracked in a checked-in copy. Three policies:
- * interactive: prompt once if no /etc/mios/secrets.env exists --
- the ONLY operator prompt; everything else came from the toml
- * hashed     : use literal MIOS_USER_PASSWORD_HASH already in env
- (operator pasted a sha512crypt hash into the
- configurator's password field)
- * none       : skip password setup; useful for kiosk / CI
- Hash a plaintext password to sha512crypt. Python 3.13+ removed the
- `crypt` stdlib module (PEP 594), so we use mkpasswd (whois) / openssl
- / passlib instead. Per feedback_mios_dev_equals_mios.md the dev VM is
- MiOS in full parity -- so mkpasswd, openssl, AND passlib are ALL
- expected to be present. If any one is missing it means the dev VM
- was provisioned from a stripped machine-os image rather than the
- canonical MiOS-flavored machine-os; surface that as a loud failure
- so the build pipeline (or the operator) fixes the provisioning, not
- the driver.
- `source` performs parameter expansion inside double-quoted
- values, and a sha512crypt hash starts with `$6$...$...$...`
- -- under `set -euo pipefail`, $6 triggers "unbound variable"
- and kills the driver. Parse the file with grep + manual
- stripping instead of `source` so $6 stays literal.
- Strip surrounding quotes (single OR double).
- Unattended: NEVER prompt. Resolve the password from the
- TOML-first SSOT -- [identity].default_password, exported by
- userenv.sh as MIOS_DEFAULT_PASSWORD -- falling back to the
- vendor default 'mios' only if the toml didn't set one. Then
- persist the hash to /etc/mios/secrets.env exactly like the
- interactive path does, so re-runs are idempotent and the
- built image carries a deterministic credential.
- SINGLE-quote the hash so $6$ in sha512crypt format is
- treated as a literal, not as "$6 (param 6) followed by $".
- Embedded single quotes are unlikely in a sha512crypt hash
- but escape defensively just in case.
- Persist a flat install.env SEED for downstream consumers that don't grok
- layered toml directly: /etc/profile.d/mios-env.sh, automation/build.sh
- during `podman build`, sysusers/tmpfiles generators. mios-sync-env later
- regenerates the full file from mios.toml; this seed only covers the few
- keys needed before the resolver runs.
- BARE `KEY=value` only (no double quotes): install.env is read by systemd
- EnvironmentFile=, bash `.`-source (under set -u), AND podman --env-file,
- whose quoting rules are mutually incompatible -- bare is the only safe
- form. The password HASH is NOT written here: a `$6$salt$digest` value is
- unrepresentable in a bare env file and previously detonated `. install.env`
- under set -u ("$6: unbound variable"). It lives ONLY in /etc/shadow and
- /etc/mios/secrets.env (0600, written above). install-robustness.
- ── Build invocation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- automation/build.sh expects to run inside a `podman build` against the
- Containerfile. Outside that context it's a no-op driver entry. The
- canonical way to drive the build from here is:
- cd <MIOS_REPO> && podman build -t localhost/mios:latest .
- The Containerfile then RUNs automation/build.sh with /ctx bind-mounted
- at the repo root, which in turn exec's every automation/[0-9][0-9]-*.sh
- step in order, masking secrets, capturing logs, etc.
- For now this driver is a SCAFFOLD. Subsequent migration chunks will
- wire in:
- * Multi-format output via bootc-image-builder (vhdx, qcow2, iso, raw)
- * Identity-prompt migration from build-mios.ps1 Phase 6
- * Dashboard renderer matching the Windows-side ASCII-frame UI
- * WSLg/Wayland verification for Epiphany SSOT-config editing
- When MIOS_REPO=/, podman build with `.` as context fails with:
- "Error: mounting an overlay over build context directory: ...
- mount overlay:..., data: lowerdir=/,upperdir=...: invalid argument"
- Buildah's overlay storage driver cannot stack an overlay on top of /
- (the root mount itself). We materialize the tracked tree into a fresh
- tmpdir via `git archive | tar -x`, then build from there. Operates
- on native ext4 (the cache or repo workspace), avoids overlay-on-/,
- and excludes everything outside the git index (no /proc, /sys,
- /var/lib state, etc. leaking into the build context).
- Primary build trigger = local podman build (below). If podman is missing, the
- curl fallback triggers the Forgejo CI build instead (SSOT endpoints, no literal
- host:port). Only intercepts when podman is ABSENT and the fallback is enabled
- (default), so a podman-present host or an explicitly-disabled gate is unchanged.
- `sudo podman build` -- LOAD-BEARING: the image MUST land in the
- ROOTFUL container storage (/var/lib/containers/storage). The
- bootc-image-builder step below runs `sudo podman run` (rootful,
- --privileged) and mounts that rootful storage to find the image. A
- plain (rootless) `podman build` here puts the image in the invoking
- user's ~/.local/share/containers/storage instead, so BIB then fails
- every format with "localhost/mios:latest: image not known"
- (operator-confirmed 2026-05-14). The privilege preflight at the top
- already guaranteed root or non-interactive sudo, so this always works.
- --network=host -- ALSO load-bearing. The Containerfile's RUN steps do
- `dnf5 install` and need working DNS. Rootful podman build's default
- netavark/aardvark-dns bridge is not wired for name resolution on the
- WSL2 podman-machine-os, so the build dies with "Could not resolve
- hostname for mirrors.fedoraproject.org" / "[packages.sh] FATAL:
- Mandatory 'base' packages failed to install" (operator-confirmed
- 2026-05-14). The dev VM's HOST netns resolves fine (it pulls OCI
- images, model weights, etc.), so run the build's RUN steps in the
- host network namespace. This affects only build-time network access;
- nothing about --network is baked into the resulting image.
- ── Multi-format deployment artifacts ────────────────────────────────────────
- Per the self-replication architecture, the build pipeline produces
- every deployment-shape MiOS targets. We use bootc-image-builder
- (BIB) -- the upstream-canonical tool from the bootc project -- to
- render the just-built OCI image into:
- * vhdx          Hyper-V disk
- * qcow2         QEMU / virt-manager
- * iso           Live-CD / Live-USB / Anaconda installer media
- * raw           dd-able to any block device (USB stick, SD card)
- * wsl           tar.zst usable with `wsl --import` on Windows
- All artifacts go to /var/lib/mios/build/output/ inside MiOS-DEV.
- When MiOS-DEV is hosting on M:\, that path is on the dedicated
- 256 GB partition (junctioned via the mount setup in Windows entry).
- Multi-GB artifact set comfortably fits.
- BIB is invoked via `podman run --rm --privileged --pull=newer` per
- its documented invocation pattern. Each format runs separately so
- a transient failure in one (e.g. ISO bootloader signing on a
- locked-down host) doesn't kill the whole batch -- partial success
- is logged and the operator can re-run with --type=<missing> to
- fill gaps.
- Skipped if MIOS_SKIP_BIB=1 is set (useful for fast-iter dev cycles
- where the operator only cares about the OCI image -- the bootc
- switch above is the actual self-replication closure; BIB outputs
- are for distributing the image to other machines).
- Same root-vs-user split the LOG_DIR + WORKDIR sections use: when
- invoked as the mios user (the canonical handoff path from
- Windows: `wsl.exe -d podman-MiOS-DEV --user mios`),
- /var/lib/mios is root-owned (FHS) and `mkdir -p` fails with
- "Permission denied" -- killing the driver under set -euo
- pipefail BEFORE the bootc switch can run, so the dev VM stays
- on its previous deployment. Operator-flagged 2026-05-10:
- build succeeded, bootc deploy stayed un-switched, auto-chain
- correctly reported "service succeeded but bootc deployment
- is NOT localhost/mios". Honor explicit MIOS_BIB_OUT override,
- else root -> /var/lib/mios/build/output, else non-root ->
- $XDG_STATE_HOME/mios/build/output.
- Build BIB_FORMATS from [deployment].target_<key> in the layered
- mios.toml -- the configurator HTML's "Deployment targets" section
- toggles these. Operator override via $MIOS_BIB_FORMATS="vhdx qcow2"
- still wins for fast-iter dev cycles. Final fallback to the
- historical 5-format default if the toml is missing entirely.
- Fallback default -- ONLY names bootc-image-builder actually
- accepts. Verified against `bootc-image-builder build --help`
- (2026-05-14): valid --type values are ami, anaconda-iso,
- bootc-installer, gce, iso, ova, pxe-tar-xz, qcow2, raw, vhd,
- vmdk. NOTE: `vhd` (not `vhdx`) is the Hyper-V type, and
- there is NO `wsl` type -- the WSL rootfs tarball is produced
- separately, not by BIB. The per-format loop below normalizes
- a stray `vhdx`/`wsl` from the toml just in case.
- `cd /` -- LOAD-BEARING. The BIB loop below does `sudo podman run`
- for each format. conmon (podman's container monitor) does a
- double-fork and then a `getcwd()` of its own; if the inherited CWD
- is the build-context dir (which sudo'd-root may not be able to
- read in its elevated mount/namespace context), conmon fails with
- "[conmon:e]: Failed to get working directory" / "Error: conmon
- failed: exit status 1" -- and EVERY BIB format dies instantly
- before BIB itself even runs (operator-confirmed 2026-05-14).
- `/` is always present and always accessible to root.
- toml field names use underscores (target_anaconda_iso); BIB
- --type uses hyphens (anaconda-iso). Translate.
- Normalize names that are NOT in bootc-image-builder's --type
- vocabulary (verified against `bootc-image-builder build --help`):
- vhdx -> vhd  : BIB's Hyper-V disk type is `vhd`; `vhdx` is
- rejected outright ("unsupported image type").
- wsl          : not a BIB type at all -- the WSL rootfs tarball
- is produced by a separate step, never by BIB.
- Skip it here so it doesn't show as a hard fail.
- --local dropped: newer BIB makes local-storage lookup the
- default and warns "--local is now the default behavior". The
- image is found because `sudo podman build` above placed it in
- the rootful /var/lib/containers/storage that this --privileged
- `sudo podman run` mounts in below.
- Any failed deployment format makes the whole build a failure.
- Building the OCI image is necessary but NOT sufficient: an
- operator who asked for vhd/qcow2/iso/raw and got none of them had
- a failed build, and `mios build` must exit non-zero so callers
- that chain on it -- the agent, CI, the Forgejo runner, `&&`
- chains -- actually see it. The completion banner below still
- prints either way (the log stays readable); the non-zero exit is
- applied once, at end-of-script, via _BIB_EXIT.
- ── Build complete: artifacts ready for deployment to OTHER substrates ──────
- Operator 2026-05-10 (feedback_mios_dev_vm_is_builder_only.md):
- podman-MiOS-DEV is the BUILDER, not a deploy target. We do NOT
- bootc-switch the dev VM to localhost/mios:latest. The dev VM stays
- on its podman-machine-os Fedora base + MiOS overlay (Quadlets, RPM
- layer, flatpaks, branding) -- that's all the operator-facing UX
- they need to drive the build pipeline. The artifacts produced here
- are for OTHER hosts:
- * localhost/mios:latest      OCI image -> bare-metal bootc, OCI registry push
- * vhdx                       Hyper-V import
- * qcow2                      QEMU / virt-manager
- * iso                        Live-CD / Anaconda installer media
- * raw                        dd-able to USB / SD card / disk
- * wsl tarball                wsl --import on any Windows host
- All artifacts land under $BIB_OUT (defaulted to $XDG_STATE_HOME/mios/
- build/output for non-root, /var/lib/mios/build/output for root).
- Operator copies / pushes / flashes from there to the target machine.
- Exit status: non-zero if any bootc-image-builder deployment format
- failed (see the BIB summary above). Building the OCI image alone is
- not "success" -- callers that chain on `mios build` (the agent, CI,
- the Forgejo runner) must see a real failure when artifacts didn't
- build. _BIB_EXIT defaults to 0: BIB skipped (MIOS_SKIP_BIB=1) or
- every requested format succeeded.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-build-status
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-build-status [N]
- Print the state of the most recent `mios build` run: log path, age,
- size, last-line tail, exit summary if completed. Optional N = show
- the last N lines of the log (default 30).
- Designed for the agent to answer "how's the build going" without
- having to remember /var/log/mios/build-driver-*.log naming or write
- its own shell pipeline.
- Find the most recent build-driver log. There may be a tmp fallback at
- /tmp/mios-build-driver-*.log when the driver couldn't write to /var/log
- (e.g. inside a restricted namespace before the systemd-run escape fired).
- Header: which log, age, size.
- Is the driver still running for this log?
- Match any build-driver process whose log path argv resembles ours, OR
- any build-driver that's currently active at all (best-effort).
- If the log ends with FATAL/Error/Failed, call it failed; else assume
- finished (driver exited, no failure markers in the tail).
- OCI build artifacts produced this run (if any). The build context lives
- under /var/lib/mios/build/build-context; final OCI image goes into
- rootful podman storage as localhost/mios:latest.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-build-tail
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-build-tail [-f] [N]
- Stream / tail the most recent build log. With -f, follows live (tail -f).
- Without -f, prints the last N lines (default 100) and exits.
- Companion to mios-build-status (which adds metadata + state). Use this
- when you just want the raw log content.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-cache-clear
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-cache-clear [--dry-run] [--all]
- Safe cache wipe across the MiOS agent / AI / GUI stack. Designed to
- replace the ad-hoc "delete everything" scripts the agent has been
- running -- which deleted the OWUI admin user along with the chats
- (operator-confirmed regression 2026-05-15: post-wipe lockout).
- WHITELIST -- ALWAYS preserved (never delete from these tables):
- OWUI: user, auth, group, group_member, model, function, tool,
- api_key, oauth_session
- Hermes: config.yaml, SOUL.md, .env (operator API keys),
- skills/, hooks/, bin/, cron/
- System: model weights (multi-GB), service systemd units,
- Quadlets, /etc/mios/* configs, /etc/sudoers.d/10-mios-hermes
- WIPED -- conversation/cache state, regenerable on demand:
- OWUI: chat, message, message_reaction, memory,
- feedback, prompt_history, automation_run, calendar_event,
- shared_chat, pinned_note, channel_*, tag, chat_file
- OWUI selective: file rows + knowledge rows + knowledge_file links
- that are NOT MiOS-managed (meta lacks "mios-owui-apply-
- knowledge" marker). MiOS Documentation collection survives.
- OWUI: cache/, vector_db/, uploads/ directories (vector chunks
- re-built from file.data.content on next read)
- Hermes: sessions/, response_store.db, kanban.db, plans/, memories/,
- cache/, .cache, processes.json, channel_directory.json,
- context_length_cache.yaml, models_dev_cache.json,
- .skills_prompt_snapshot.json, logs/
- Build: build-context, bib-cache, all but newest build-driver-*.log
- Chrome flatpak: cache/, GPUCache/, ShaderCache/, Code Cache/
- (preserves prefs, bookmarks, history)
- /var/tmp: entries older than 1 day
- /tmp: only MiOS-stamped throwaway files
- --dry-run: print what would be deleted, don't actually delete
- --all:     also wipe Chrome history/prefs (NOT default; user data loss)
- $1=path; $2=-name pattern; remaining=extra find args
- contents of these dirs (preserve dir itself):
- specific files:
- NEVER touch: user, auth, group, group_member, model, function, tool,
- api_key, oauth_session, channel  (these are config/identity)
- Selective wipe for file/knowledge: keep MiOS-managed (sourced from
- mios-owui-apply-knowledge -- meta has 'managed_by' set), wipe only
- operator-uploaded chat attachments + non-MiOS knowledge collections.
- Operator-confirmed regression 2026-05-15: a blanket wipe of
- knowledge + knowledge_file + file blew away the MiOS Documentation
- collection on every cache-clear; the helper had to be re-run from
- firstboot to restore.
- Files: drop only those NOT marked MiOS-managed.
- Knowledge collections: drop only those NOT marked MiOS-managed.
- knowledge_file links: drop links whose knowledge or file rows were
- deleted (cascade FK already does this when ON DELETE CASCADE is
- set; explicit cleanup for safety on older OWUI schemas).
- --all also wipes history + cookies (operator-explicit data loss)

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-cdi-detect
- 'MiOS' CDI spec detection -- generate Container Device Interface
- specs for every detected GPU vendor before nvidia-cdi-refresh.service
- fires. Run by mios-cdi-detect.service (Before=nvidia-cdi-refresh.service).
- Writes specs to /run/cdi/ (declared in usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/mios-gpu.conf
- under LAW 2). All paths are best-effort -- a missing toolkit makes
- the corresponding branch a no-op rather than failing the boot.
- Vendor coverage (May 2026):
- * NVIDIA  via nvidia-ctk (NVIDIA Container Toolkit v1.19+)
- /run/cdi/nvidia.yaml or /run/cdi/nvidia-wsl.yaml
- * AMD     via amd-ctk    (AMD Container Toolkit v1.3+, Apr 2026)
- /run/cdi/amd.json -- AMD outputs JSON, not YAML
- * Intel   via intel-cdi-specs-generator
- (intel/intel-resource-drivers-for-kubernetes v0.1+)
- /run/cdi/intel.yaml -- best-effort; tooling is v0.x
- When no GPU is present (headless server, container without /dev/dxg
- or /dev/kfd or /dev/dri), this is a no-op except for the status
- snapshot at /run/mios/cdi-detect.status.
- shellcheck source=/usr/lib/mios/paths.sh
- WSL-detected flags: AMD/Intel iGPU on WSL is exposed via /dev/dxg
- (not /dev/kfd or renderD*). When set, the iGPU branch writes a
- hand-rolled wsl2-<vendor>.yaml CDI spec instead of relying on the
- Linux-side vendor toolkit.
- Intel iGPU/Arc detection: a renderD* node whose vendor reads 0x8086.
- Iterate every renderD* node so multi-GPU boxes are correctly handled
- (e.g. discrete NVIDIA + Intel iGPU coexisting).
- ── WSL2 AMD/Intel iGPU detection via Windows interop ──────────────
- Under WSL2, AMD APUs (Ryzen with Radeon Graphics) and Intel iGPUs
- do NOT surface as /dev/kfd or /dev/dri/renderD* -- they share the
- /dev/dxg paravirt interface with NVIDIA. So the Linux-side probes
- above can't tell which Windows GPU(s) are present; we have to ask
- Windows via WMI. Operator-flagged 2026-05-17: Ryzen iGPU on the
- Windows host was undetected because /dev/kfd doesn't exist in WSL,
- so the AMD branch never ran and the iGPU never reached any
- container.
- Capped 5s; never fails the boot. The first
- "Microsoft Remote Display Adapter" is the WDDM paravirt
- one; real GPUs follow.
- `|| WIN_GPU_NAMES=""` is load-bearing: under `set -euo pipefail` a bare
- `var=$(pipeline)` EXITS the shell if the pipeline returns non-zero
- (timeout -> 124, powershell error, or pipefail on any stage). That made
- this "capped 5s, never fails the boot" probe fail the ENTIRE service on
- a podman-machine-os VM where /mnt/c powershell is slow/absent
- (2026-06-05 mios-cdi-detect.service failure). The guard restores the
- documented best-effort behaviour; the `if [[ -n ... ]]` below handles "".
- ── NVIDIA ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Prefer upstream nvidia-cdi-refresh.service when its unit is installed
- (NVIDIA Container Toolkit v1.18+). It auto-regenerates on driver/device
- change, so we don't want to race with it.
- Install-robustness 2026-06-21: only defer to upstream nvidia-cdi-refresh on
- BARE METAL. On WSL2 the upstream refresh is unreliable on the paravirt
- /dev/dxg surface and may NEVER materialize a /run/cdi spec -> the GPU is
- silently lost and the AI lanes fall back to CPU. So on WSL2 always GENERATE
- the spec (--mode=wsl below) instead of deferring.
- WSL2 surfaces GPUs via /dev/dxg with the standard WDDM
- paravirt driver. nvidia-ctk's --mode=wsl emits a CDI spec
- that picks up the host's NVIDIA driver via the WSL /usr/lib/
- wsl/lib bind-mount.
- nvidia-ctk auto-detects mode (nvml/csv/management) on
- bare metal; --mode=auto is the explicit form.
- WSL2-specific fallback when nvidia-ctk isn't on the dev VM
- (podman-machine-os 6.0 doesn't ship it; the dev-VM overlay can't
- always install it cleanly). Hand-roll the CDI YAML using the
- standard WSL2 GPU surface: /dev/dxg device node + rbind of
- /usr/lib/wsl (which has libcuda.so + libcudadebugger.so + the
- nvidia-smi binary). rbind, NOT bind: /usr/lib/wsl/lib is an
- overlay sub-mount that doesn't propagate through a plain bind.
- Operator-flagged 2026-05-11: the local inference engine loaded models
- on CPU (`load_tensors: CPU model buffer size = 16676 MiB`) because no
- CDI spec was generated and the Quadlet had no AddDevice for the
- GPU. After this YAML lands + the Quadlet adds AddDevice=
- nvidia.com/gpu=all, the engine detects the GPU via libcuda.so 1.1
- and `inference compute ... library=CUDA ... description=NVIDIA
- GeForce RTX 4090` shows in the journal.
- ── AMD (ROCm) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- AMD Container Toolkit v1.3.0 (Apr 2026) ships amd-ctk which
- generates a CDI spec the same way nvidia-ctk does. Output is JSON
- by default; podman accepts both .yaml and .json under /etc/cdi or
- /run/cdi. Spec naming follows the CNCF CDI convention:
- vendor.com/class=identifier -> amd.com/gpu=all.
- Bare-metal / true-VM path: amd-ctk reads /dev/kfd + /dev/dri.
- WSL2 path: AMD iGPU is exposed via /dev/dxg + /usr/lib/wsl libs
- (DirectX paravirt). amd-ctk doesn't know how to generate this
- shape, so we hand-roll the CDI spec the same way the WSL2
- NVIDIA fallback does. Container can then use Vulkan (mesa3d)
- or DirectML against the Windows-side AMD driver.
- Operator directive 2026-05-17: "iGPU's are ONLY micro-llms" --
- this spec REGISTERS the device with podman so containers that
- explicitly request AddDevice=amd.com/gpu=all get it. The base
- the big-model NVIDIA-lane Quadlet does NOT request
- this; only micro-LLM container(s) do.
- ── Intel (iGPU / Arc) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
- Intel's CDI tooling lives in intel/intel-resource-drivers-for-kubernetes.
- The specs-generator binary is a non-Kubernetes friendly way to
- produce a /etc/cdi/intel.yaml. Best-effort: this binary is at v0.x
- upstream and lacks the polish of nvidia-ctk / amd-ctk -- failures
- here are logged but never break the boot.
- WSL2 path mirrors the AMD WSL branch above: hand-rolled CDI
- spec keyed as intel.com/gpu using the same /dev/dxg + WSL libs.
- Per operator directive 2026-05-17: "iGPU's are ONLY micro-llms"
- -- only micro-LLM Quadlets should request this device.
- ── Status snapshot for the dashboard / mios-boot-diag ───────────────
- JSON variant for tooling that reads structured output (boot-diag's
- `gpu-passthrough.status` consumer pattern).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-cdp-fetch
- wait up to ~20s for ACTUAL body text to appear -- readyState can read
- 'complete' before a big JS-rendered page (e.g. Wikipedia) populates the
- body, which gave an empty innerText. Poll the body length instead.
- Prefer the MAIN article content (skip nav/menus/footers) so the first
- chars are the actual article -- a generic selector chain that falls back
- to <body>. Keeps the useful text within a small char budget.

- Called by firstboot mount setups to minimize MDS workload under desktop GUI sessions.
- Convert to string format for INI writing
- Also load from TOML layers in case environment variable is not active

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-cephfs-provision
- Called by pam_exec.so on session init (validate subcommand) or manually by administrator/automation.
- Parse string booleans / ints / lists
- Degrade-open fallbacks
- Speaks parameterized JSON on stdin
- Check if subvolume info can be retrieved
- Check if keyring exists
- 1. Create subvolume group
- 2. Create subvolume
- 3. CephX per-user keyring creation (T-089 capability requirements)
- Set permissions
- 1. Unmount home directory if mounted
- 2. Revoke CephX auth
- 3. Remove keyring file
- 4. Remove subvolume
- 1. Load config
- 2. Parse arguments
- DEGRADE-OPEN: log all errors but exit 0 to prevent blocking logins/PAM

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-chain-verify
- Import the SSOT chain algorithm. mios_audit's web-stack import is shimmed, so the
- pure verifier loads here WITHOUT fastapi installed (confined-user safe).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-chrony-ptp-dropin
- PTP hardware clock tuning for Chrony
- Automatically generated when /dev/ptp0 is present

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-clevis-luks-gen
- Generated from mios.toml [security.luks]

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-codebase-index
- of EVERY MiOS-authored file (docs, scripts, configs, units, source) across
- all roots into one grep-able index so any agent can DISCOVER the whole
- codebase, then read_file/run the specific file on demand. Superset of
- mios-docs-index (which is .md-only). Filesystem-discoverable (no RAG drip).
- Extensions we index (text / source / config). Plus exact basenames below.
- Never descend into vendored / generated / binary trees.
- Skip obviously binary / huge-artifact suffixes even if matched above.
- 1. explicit AI-hint: marker (may wrap onto continuation comment lines)
- absorb immediate comment-continuation lines (indented under the hint)
- 2. YAML frontmatter description: (md)
- 3. python module docstring
- 4. header comment block (after optional shebang) for #/// commented files
- skip pure path/separator/marker lines
- 5. first markdown H1
- 6. first meaningful non-comment line
- Extensionless shebang scripts (mios-* libexec/bin) -- the bulk of the tree.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-coderun
- Per-call scratch workspace (the ONLY writable path in the jail).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-coderun-broker
- Write PID file
- Read request (the protocol is a single JSON object request)
- Forward to agent-pipe HTTP endpoint

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-coderun-codemode
- The pure helpers (sibling-module pattern) -- argv/result/gating decisions live
- in mios_codemode so they are unit-tested without podman. Add the agent-pipe lib
- to the path so this libexec CLI can import it regardless of CWD.
- fall through to the shared coderun workspace root ([paths]; /etc wins
- over vendor, no per-user layer -- same order as the former inline reader).
- DEFAULT-OFF gate (degrade CLOSED for code execution).
- Write the snippet into the bind-mounted /work (mapped to <ws_root>/<sid>).
- Ensure the session sandbox is UP (idempotent start). Best-effort: if the
- orchestrator or unit is missing we still try `podman exec` and surface its
- error -- but we never run the code outside the container.
- Confirm the container is actually running before exec'ing into it.
- NETWORK posture: the Quadlet pins Network=none, so `net` here is advisory --
- log the requested+effective state in the envelope. (A net-enabled sandbox
- would be a separate unit; out of scope for this scaffold.)

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-coderun-session
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-coderun-session {start|stop|snap|revert|status} <session-id>
- Per-session orchestrator for the MiOS agent sandbox per the FS+OS
- Control guide §15. Wraps:
- * systemctl --user start/stop mios-coderun-sandbox@<id>.service
- * btrfs subvolume snapshot (when project root is on btrfs)
- * git stash --keep-index fallback (when not)
- * revert from snapshot or git stash
- Sessions are identified by an opaque <session-id> (sha256 prefix,
- uuid, or whatever the agent uses for its session). The same id
- threads through the Quadlet template (%i in mios-coderun-sandbox@.container),
- the project subdir (/var/home/mios/coderuns/<id>/), and the
- snapshot path.
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: "no hardcoded anything anywhere".
- The project-root path resolves from env -> mios.toml [paths] ->
- compiled fallback, matching the rest of the MiOS helper fleet.
- Shared layered mios.toml resolver (vendor < host < user) via the mios-toml-get CLI.
- Resolve the projects root (env -> mios.toml [paths] -> default).
- Detect whether the project root is on btrfs (enables snapshot path).
- btrfs is Linux-only; early-exit on other platforms
- Start the per-session host-side broker
- Wait for the broker to create the socket
- Stop the per-session host-side broker
- Snapshot GC -- bound retention per the guide's pitfall list.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-configurator-launch
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-configurator-launch -- open the MiOS Settings
- surface (the configurator) for editing the unified user-definitions
- dotfile (/etc/mios/mios.toml).
- Target priority:
- 1. http://localhost:8640/configure -- the MiOS Portal ALREADY embeds
- this configurator as its unified Settings surface (a Settings gear
- opens GET /portal/configurator, which serves the same mios.html
- with the SSOT theme injected; GET /configure opens the shell
- straight to it). This is the PRIMARY target and is probed first.
- 2. file:// standalone (LAST-RESORT) -- only when :8640/configure is
- unreachable. The layered mios.toml is pre-staged in ~/Downloads so
- the File System Access API can bind to it (or fall back to the
- standard <input type="file">). This is the offline / USB /
- air-gapped fallback (ADR-0008); it is demoted, never removed.
- Browser selection (for whichever URL is chosen) is operator-defined via
- mios-open-url; xdg-open and a plain echo are the last resorts.
- Invoked from:
- - /usr/share/applications/mios-configurator.desktop (GNOME Dock /
- Activities on deployed hosts; Windows Start Menu via WSLg on
- MiOS-DEV)
- - Windows-side `MiOS Configurator.lnk` Start Menu / Desktop
- shortcuts (which call `wsl -d MiOS-DEV --exec
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-configurator-launch`; pre-rename
- installs may still expose the distro as `podman-MiOS-DEV`)
- ── LAST-RESORT offline staging ──────────────────────────────────────
- Only invoked when the embedded Portal Settings surface is unreachable.
- Stages a writable mios.toml seed + the standalone HTML in ~/Downloads
- so File System Access API (or the <input type="file"> fallback) can
- bind to them, then the caller opens file://. Kept fully working as the
- offline / USB / air-gapped fallback (ADR-0008).
- Flatpak's xdg-download permission bind-mounts the host's resolved
- `xdg-user-dir DOWNLOAD` into the sandbox. On a freshly created user
- without ~/.config/user-dirs.dirs, xdg-user-dir falls back to $HOME
- (NOT $HOME/Downloads), so the bind-mount covers the home root rather
- than the actual Downloads dir -- and Epiphany then sees
- file:///var/home/mios/Downloads/mios-configurator.html as a missing
- path inside its sandbox view. Resolution: seed user-dirs.dirs so the
- bind-mount targets ~/Downloads precisely. Operator-flagged 2026-05-11
- (Epiphany "Unable to display this website" on `mios config`).
- If the helper didn't exist (no xdg-user-dirs RPM on the dev VM) or
- produced nothing, hand-roll a minimal user-dirs.dirs that points
- XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR at ~/Downloads. Flatpak only needs DOWNLOAD for
- the configurator flow; the other entries match the standard
- Fedora skel.
- Stage a writable mios.toml seed (highest layer wins).
- Stage the HTML where Flatpak's home-portal exposes it.
- ── PRIMARY: probe the embedded Portal Settings surface first ────────
- A reachable :8640/configure is the authoritative unified surface; when
- it answers we open it directly and SKIP the offline Downloads-staging
- above entirely. Only an unreachable Portal drops us to the file://
- offline fallback.
- Route via mios-open-url which resolves the default browser from
- mios.toml [[desktop.apps]] role=browser default=true. No hardcoded
- Epiphany / chromedev / etc -- operator-defined.
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: "NO HARDCODED ANYTHING ANYWHERE!!!".
- Fall back to xdg-open (delegates to whatever browser is registered).
- Last resort: print the URL so the operator can copy/paste.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-cron-director
- TWO rule sources (operator 2026-05-26): the launcher broker runs as `mios`
- (uid 1000), which cannot write root-owned /etc/mios -- so the `schedule` verb's
- shim writes the USER rules file in the group-writable state dir, while /etc
- stays for root-managed SYSTEM rules. The daemon merges both. It also WATCHES
- both files' mtimes and reloads on change, so a shim edit takes effect within a
- minute WITHOUT needing a cross-user SIGHUP (the shim, as mios, can't signal the
- mios-ai daemon). SIGHUP still works as an instant nudge.
- llama.cpp OpenAI /v1 (MiOS is /v1-only). OpenAI shape.
- In-flight single-flight guard (operator 2026-06-01 autonomous-wedge fix). A
- scheduled research rule runs the FULL agent pipe (refine + research council +
- cold model loads), which can take MINUTES -- longer than a short cron interval
- (e.g. */5 or */1). _fire was fire-and-forget with ONLY a per-MINUTE dedup, so
- a slow run got RE-LAUNCHED on the next matching minute -> runs stacked ->
- pegged CPU + VRAM thrash -> VM wedged with no user chat. Track the detached
- child PID per rule and SKIP a fire while the prior run is still alive.
- Single-flight: don't stack a new run on top of a still-running one.
- Detached, fire-and-forget; output to the journal via inherited stdio.
- Sleep to ~1s past the next minute boundary so we evaluate each minute once.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-cron-schedule
- Operator-scheduled jobs live in the USER rules file inside the group-writable
- state dir -- the launcher broker runs as `mios` (uid 1000) and CANNOT write
- root-owned /etc/mios/cron-rules.toml (that stays for root-managed SYSTEM rules).
- The daemon merges both + reloads on mtime change, so no privileged SIGHUP is
- needed (operator 2026-05-26).
- Raw 5-field cron passes through.
- Best-effort instant nudge; the daemon ALSO mtime-watches the rules file, so
- the change applies within a minute even when (as `mios`) we can't signal the
- mios-ai daemon. Failures here are non-fatal.
