## usr/libexec/mios/mios-cursor-ensure
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-cursor-ensure
- Make the MiOS cursor theme the ACTUAL, GLOBAL Linux cursor.
- Operator trace 2026-05-19:
- * "Bibata NEEDS to be set in Linux too" -- not just the Windows-side
- cursor; the X11/Xwayland default cursor must resolve to Bibata.
- * "Cursor is only partially applied to MiOS-DEV -- not GLOBALLY set"
- -- a per-user ~/.local/share/icons copy only covers ONE user. When
- we can write /usr (the build, or a dev VM whose /usr tree is
- writable as root) the theme belongs in /usr/share/icons so EVERY
- user, GDM, and every app inherits it.
- Mode (by privilege):
- GLOBAL  (root + /usr/share/icons writable): install to
- /usr/share/icons/<theme> + /usr/share/icons/default/index.theme.
- Host apps + GDM resolve it directly; flatpaks resolve it via
- the global override's --filesystem=host-os (/run/host/usr/...).
- USER    (otherwise -- e.g. a sealed bootc host with RO /usr): install
- to ~/.local/share/icons (flatpak xdg-data/icons mount) + symlink
- into ~/.icons (default libXcursor path) + gsettings.
- The DEFAULT cursor pointer (.../icons/default/index.theme ->
- Inherits=<theme>) is the key piece for the x11 backend: an app that
- doesn't pin XCURSOR_THEME resolves its cursor from there.
- Idempotent + offline-safe. Theme name + size + upstream repo come from
- mios.toml [theme.cursor_linux] (SSOT).
- ── Mode + install target ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
- World-readable for GDM + every user.
- Per-user: also expose on the DEFAULT libXcursor path (~/.icons)
- for host apps that don't inherit our XCURSOR_PATH.
- ── Already present anywhere? (re)wire + exit ──────────────────────────────
- A global /usr install satisfies user mode too -- but flatpaks reach /usr
- only via host-os, so in USER mode we still want a ~/.local/share/icons
- copy. Therefore: in global mode, accept /usr; in user mode, only accept
- a copy already at DEST or ~/.icons (NOT /usr, which a flatpak can't see
- without host-os).
- ── Fetch into DEST, then wire ─────────────────────────────────────────────

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-daemon
- ── Config (env-overridable) ────────────────────────────────────────
- Operator directive 2026-05-18: "iGPU micro-llm agent is mios-daemon"
- Default model is qwen3:1.7b -- micro size, lands on the AMD/Intel
- iGPU CDI lane (wsl2-amd.yaml / wsl2-intel.yaml) when present, freeing
- the dGPU for big-model work. Override via MIOS_DAEMON_MODEL.
- mios-llm-light (:8450) is the canonical micro-LLM /v1 lane
- for the daemon. Falls back to the dGPU lane (:11434) if the
- CPU instance isn't running. Operator directive 2026-05-18: "iGPU
- micro-llm(s)/mios-daemon agent collects Linux systems logs, journals,
- relevant AI files" -- the daemon IS that micro-LLM agent; this
- default points it at the right lane. (The "iGPU" in that quote was
- aspirational -- ROCm never reached the iGPU in WSL2, so the lane has
- always been CPU; the real AMD iGPU is the Windows-native server.)
- ── W0-T2 runaway controls (config-read from mios.toml [daemon]) ─────
- The daemon is ALWAYS-ON and fires LLM calls + cron actions on cadence;
- under host pressure (the 2026-06-XX GPU-runaway root cause) those calls
- pile onto an already-saturated box and make the runaway worse. These
- four controls bound that:
- 1. _host_pressure_gate -> SKIP a tick (no LLM) when load/GPU-util high
- 2. classify fingerprint dedup -> collapse identical high-sev spam
- 3. cron concurrency cap -> never re-fire while a prior Popen is alive
- 4. quiescence backoff -> widen classify cadence when nothing notable
- ALL knobs flow from mios.toml [daemon] (env still wins) with SAFE
- defaults so behavior is UNCHANGED until the operator tunes/enables them.
- pressure_skip defaults FALSE = degrade-open (gate observes but never
- skips until enabled); dedup + cron-cap are safe to default ON.
- Only adopt SCALAR keys here -- nested tables ([daemon.index],
- [daemon.roots], ...) are owned by their own readers.
- (1) Host-pressure gate. Ceilings: 1-min loadavg PER CORE and GPU util %.
- pressure_skip=false -> gate observes (writes a marker) but NEVER skips a
- tick, so behavior is unchanged until the operator flips it true.
- (2) Classify dedup cooldown (seconds): an identical high-sev fingerprint
- inside this window is collapsed to a count-only update (no new LLM/DB row).
- (3) Max concurrent cron-fired actions (live Popen handles).
- (4) Quiescence backoff: when no new unsatisfied verdict + no new med/high
- digest in quiescence_window_min, widen the classify cadence (doubling)
- up to calm_max_tick_s. Resets to CLASSIFY_BATCH_S on any new notable signal.
- (5) Rate limiting for classify and refusal judge dispatches
- Units to watch for journal subscription. Operator 2026-05-21: consolidate
- from ALL GLOBAL sources -> default is now EMPTY = the whole journal
- (journalctl -f with no -u tails every unit). Was a 3-unit subset. The
- classifier samples the bounded buffer and low/noise is aggregated into
- log_digest, so broad coverage doesn't flood the model or the DB. Set
- ── agent-plane DB writer (Postgres+pgvector; legacy DB retired) ──────
- WS-A3: the legacy DB (:8000) is retired -> _db_post / _db_post_sync are no-op
- stubs. The daemon persists to Postgres+pgvector: _db_create mirrors rows via
- _pg_insert (parameterized), reads go through _db_read's pg_sql path, and the
- task_collector tick writes the canonical `kanban` + scratch + event rows on
- its 5-minute cadence so other agents (mios-agent-pipe, hermes) query one
- source of truth instead of polling N JSON files. (The legacy DB connection
- constants DB_URL/DB_USER/DB_PASS/DB_NS/DB_DB/_DB_AUTH were removed with the
- transports.)
- WS-9c cutover: mirror daemon writes to Postgres+pgvector via the shared
- mios-db --pg CLI (system-python, no psycopg). MIOS_DB_BACKEND: dual|postgres.
- ── inotify wrapper (stdlib ctypes; no pip deps for offline / Day-0) ──
- Phase A.2 of the AgentOS roadmap: replace the daemon's poll loops
- with kernel-event-driven mutations. Watches the /var/lib/mios/*
- scratchpads + state dirs; emits DB event rows (source=
- fs-watcher, kind=fs_change) on every change so other agents
- (agent-pipe critic, future DCI deliberation, ...) can subscribe
- via `SELECT FROM event WHERE source = 'fs-watcher' AND ts > <last>`
- instead of polling individual JSON files.
- Implementation: minimal ctypes wrapper around inotify_init1 +
- inotify_add_watch + raw read. No pip packages needed -- Day-0 bake
- carries no extra Python deps for this feature.
- /usr/include/sys/inotify.h flags + event mask bits.
- Watch every change that could carry agent-relevant state.
- Dirs the daemon (and other agents) write or expect mutations on.
- Sourced from mios.toml [fs_watcher].watch_dirs via the userenv.sh
- slot (MIOS_FS_WATCHER_DIRS, CSV). Falls back to the compiled-in
- defaults that match the mios.toml seed when env is unset.
- Map of mask-bit -> short op name for the DB event row.
- ── Shared state (handlers write here; flusher persists) ─────────────
- ── W0-T2 (1): host-pressure gate ────────────────────────────────────
- A ~5s-TTL cached read of the 1-min loadavg (per core) + a best-effort
- nvidia-smi GPU-util probe. The four cadence loops call this at the TOP
- of each tick; under pressure they SKIP the tick (no LLM call) and write
- a "deferred (host pressure)" marker -- so the always-on daemon stops
- adding fuel to a runaway instead of piling LLM/cron work onto a
- saturated box. Degrade-open: any probe error -> over_ceiling=False
- (proceed exactly as today). pressure_skip gates whether a hot signal
- actually causes a skip (default false = observe-only).
- ── W0-T2 (4): quiescence tracker ────────────────────────────────────
- Tracks the last time a NOTABLE signal occurred (a new med/high log
- digest OR a new unsatisfied verdict). When nothing notable lands within
- QUIESCENCE_WINDOW_MIN, the classify loop widens its cadence (doubling,
- capped at CALM_MAX_TICK_S) so an idle box isn't polled aggressively.
- Any new notable signal calls _mark_activity() which resets the cadence.
- ── Single shared /v1 client ─────────────────────────────────────────
- llama.cpp OpenAI /v1 (MiOS is /v1-only): the daemon-agent posts the OpenAI
- /chat/completions shape whether it runs on the iGPU Vulkan device or a CPU
- lane -- the server owns thread/offload config, so no num_gpu/num_thread knobs.
- FOREGROUND swarm turns pass a BIGGER model (AGENT_MODEL) for a heavy,
- VISIBLE, sustained CPU spike (operator 2026-05-26 "bigger CPU model");
- the always-on BACKGROUND loop omits `model` -> stays on the snappy MODEL.
- FOREGROUND swarm turns can target a DIFFERENT lane than the always-on
- background loop (operator 2026-05-26): the daemon's MODEL/ENDPOINT stay on
- the iGPU (the 2026-05-25 offload), but a swarm facet reply forces the CPU
- lane (AGENT_ENDPOINT=:11435) so the CPU node ACTUALLY + VISIBLY computes.
- ── Journal subscriber ───────────────────────────────────────────────
- Cap to avoid runaway memory
- ── Classify handler (was: mios-log-watcher) ─────────────────────────
- Log consolidation -> the DB (operator 2026-05-21: "logs should be
- compacted/compressed/consolidated and stored in global database(s)").
- Compress by SIGNAL: med/high severity -> one compact `log_digest` row
- (summary + tags + severity + count -- NOT raw lines); low/noise ->
- AGGREGATED into a periodic consolidated tally so the DB isn't flooded
- with a row every CLASSIFY_BATCH_S. Agents can query log_digest for a
- global, queryable log history (the state.json snapshot is latest-only).
- W0-T2 (2): per-(source,kind,summary-shingle) fingerprint dedup + cooldown.
- An identical high-severity classification recurring inside CLASSIFY_DEDUP_S
- is SUPPRESSED -- collapsed to a count-only state marker rather than a fresh
- LLM-grounded log_digest row + activity reset. This stops one stuck unit
- (the GPU-runaway pattern is the SAME line firing every batch) from flooding
- the DB and from defeating the quiescence backoff. Bounded LRU on the map.
- Bounded LRU: evict the oldest-touched entries when oversized.
- W0-T2 (2): dedup high-severity spam. An identical fingerprint inside
- the cooldown collapses to a count-only state marker -- no new LLM/DB
- row, and (crucially) no activity reset, so a single stuck unit can't
- keep the daemon perpetually "busy".
- low / noise: aggregate; flush ONE consolidated row per window.
- W0-T2 (4): adaptive cadence. Starts responsive (CLASSIFY_BATCH_S) and,
- when the box goes quiescent (no new med/high digest / unsatisfied
- verdict for QUIESCENCE_WINDOW_MIN), backs OFF exponentially toward
- CALM_MAX_TICK_S so an idle daemon isn't polling the model every batch.
- Interruptible sleep at the current (possibly widened) cadence.
- W0-T2 (4): recompute cadence for the NEXT cycle from quiescence.
- W0-T2 (1): host-pressure gate -- skip this tick (no LLM call) when
- load/GPU-util exceed the ceiling AND pressure_skip is enabled.
- Compose compact prompt
- journald MESSAGE can be a LIST (multi-line / byte-array fields) or
- bytes, not just str -- .strip() on a list crashed classify_loop
- ('list' object has no attribute 'strip', operator 2026-06-01) and
- KILLED the classify thread, blinding the daemon's load/oom watch.
- Coerce to a single string defensively.
- ── Refusal handler (was: mios-agent-nudger) ─────────────────────────
- Refusal/fabrication detection mode (SSOT [daemon].refusal_detect; env wins).
- "model" -> the micro-LLM judges EVERY hermes-agent response (is it a refusal,
- hedge, or fabrication instead of doing the work?); "off" -> detection
- disabled. There is NO English-phrase regex pre-filter deciding whether to even
- check (the deleted refusal-patterns.txt gate is gone) -- the judge is
- authoritative on every candidate. Degrade-open: an unreachable judge lane
- skips that turn's check, never falling back to a keyword list and never
- fabricating a refusal verdict. (operator NO-HARDCODE law)
- System prompt for the refusal judge. The model -- not a phrase list -- decides
- whether the assistant is refusing / hedging / fabricating instead of doing the
- work, in ANY language. A genuine attempt, a completed action, a normal answer,
- or a routine operational log line is NOT a refusal.
- Host-pressure gate -- when over ceiling AND pressure_skip is on, drop
- this tick's judge work rather than queue LLM calls onto a saturated
- box (last_index already advanced, so the batch is dropped not queued).
- degrade-open: judge lane down / unparseable -> skip this turn
- ── Cron handler (was: mios-cron-director) ──────────────────────────
- W0-T2 (3): cap concurrent cron-fired actions. Track live Popen handles
- (per gate-name + a global list) so the daemon NEVER re-fires a gate while
- its prior Popen is still alive, and never exceeds CRON_MAX_CONCURRENT
- in-flight actions total. A wedged action that never exits used to let the
- cron loop spawn a fresh process every min_interval_s -> fork-bomb-shaped
- runaway. _cron_inflight maps gate-name -> Popen; _reap drops finished ones.
- W0-T2 (1): host-pressure gate -- skip the whole cron evaluation tick
- (gate-eval LLM calls + any fires) when over ceiling AND pressure_skip.
- W0-T2 (3): concurrency cap. Reap finished handles first, then
- refuse to fire when (a) THIS gate's prior Popen is still
- alive, or (b) the global in-flight count is at the cap. The
- gate stays eligible next tick (we don't stamp _last_fire on a
- deferral) so it fires once capacity frees.
- Keep last 20 decisions
- Wait for next tick or stop
- ── Suggestions handler ──────────────────────────────────────────────
- Operator-flagged 2026-05-17: "OWUI doesn't show or generate any
- suggested chats on new chat windows" + "should have access to all
- local systems logs and can serve them; maybe this helps inform the
- suggestion/followups in OWUI chats".
- OWUI's blank-chat panel reads ui.prompt_suggestions (a static list
- in webui.db), not an LLM endpoint. Populate it here every N min
- from RECENT MiOS state -- classify_loop's summary, refusal_loop's
- alerts, recent operator chat language -- so the panel evolves with
- the operator's work. Pure LLM generation, no hardcoded English
- (operator directive: "no hardcoded answers" 2026-05-17).
- ── Launch verifier (operator directive 2026-05-17) ───────────────────
- "THIS is why we have a mios-deamon to checks logs and open apps to
- double check things were launched successfully!!!"
- Watches recent OWUI assistant messages for launch-success claims
- ("Steam GUI is now open", "X is now launched", "installation in
- progress", etc.). For each unverified claim:
- 1. Pull the app name + claim sentence from the message
- 2. Run mios-window-active --present "<app>"
- 3. If presented_to_operator==false AND process_alive==false,
- record a launch_failure to /var/lib/mios/daemon/launch_failures.json
- The agent's SOUL.md tells it to `cat` that file before retrying
- any launch operation -- closing the loop without prompt injection.
- Launch-claim detection mode (SSOT [daemon].launch_claim_detect; env wins).
- "model" -> the micro-LLM classifies whether an assistant message CLAIMS a
- launch and resolves the target generically; "off" -> verification disabled.
- No keyword/app-name list gates this decision (operator NO-HARDCODE law).
- System prompt for the launch-claim classifier. The model -- not a phrase or
- app-name list -- decides whether the assistant CLAIMED it launched/opened/
- started an app or installer that we should now verify on screen, and names
- the claimed target generically (any app/game/installer, any language).
- Structural (not keyword) sanity on the model-named target: strip quoting
- punctuation, bound the length, unicode-aware. An empty/oversized target
- is treated as "no usable claim", never back-filled from a list.
- Degrade-open: detector off or the classify lane unreachable -> no claims
- this tick (we never synthesise a claim from keywords).
- OWUI stores chats as JSON blobs; updated_at is epoch seconds.
- Pair each assistant message with the preceding user prompt.
- Degrade-open: lane unreachable -> skip the rest of this scan
- rather than fabricate claims from the remaining messages.
- Boot delay: let OWUI come up + mios-window-active be present
- Load existing failures so we keep history across ticks
- presented_to_operator ONLY: process_alive false-positives
- (mios-window-active's `pgrep -if <name>` self-matches the
- verifier's own cmdline), and the SOUL rule is "process alive
- is INSUFFICIENT -- success only when the window is presented".
- DB event: high-severity launch failure so
- other agents (pipe critic, hermes) can react.
- Cap to the most recent 50 entries
- Cap memory usage on the dedup set
- ── Task collector + nudger (operator directive 2026-05-18) ─────────
- "iGPU micro-llm agent is mios-daemon collects Linux logs, Journals,
- Agent(s) task(s), scratchpad(s), and success and failures and acts
- as a nudger/confirmation" + "DO WHATEVERS' NATIVE FOR OPENAI API
- STANDARDS AND PATTERNS FOR MODERN MULTIAGENTIC OS-NATIVE AI's".
- Every TASK_COLLECT_TICK_S the loop:
- 1. Aggregates state from the canonical shared mutable scratchpads:
- * /var/lib/mios/hermes/kanban.db          (active agent tasks)
- * /var/lib/mios/hermes/sessions/*.json    (recent tool calls)
- * /var/lib/mios/scratch/                  (shared agent scratch)
- * /var/lib/mios/ai/scratch/               (assistant-side scratch)
- * /var/lib/mios/daemon/launch_failures.json
- * classify_loop's recent summary in state.json
- 2. Sends the aggregate to the local mios-llm-light via the OpenAI
- /v1/chat/completions endpoint with response_format=json_object
- (the same structured-output shape any OpenAI-API-compatible
- backend uses).
- 3. Parses JSON {nudges: [{type, severity, summary, action}],
- digest: "..."}.
- 4. Writes /var/lib/mios/scratch/agent-nudges.md (operator-facing
- digest) + agent-nudges.json (structured for agent consumption).
- The agent reads these at start of each turn (SOUL.md rule)
- for ground-truth status without re-walking the logs itself.
- The Hermes CLI writes kanban.db under HERMES_HOME (operator-
- confirmed 2026-05-18: hermes config show -> Config:
- /var/lib/mios/hermes/.hermes/config.yaml). The stale path
- /var/lib/mios/hermes/kanban.db is from a pre-.hermes-subdir
- layout and is no longer written -- but kept readable to
- support legacy deployments.
- Discover the right table name (hermes has gone through a few)
- Pick the column shape gracefully
- ── Synchronous FIRE + VERIFY (operator 2026-05-25, 4A #2) ────────────
- "iGPU SHOULD FIRE MIOS OS CONTROL COMMANDS FOR AGENTS, that way the
- main agent/sub-agents just have to check for successful launch."
- The always-on daemon (the iGPU daemon-tier brain) FIRES the launch AND
- runs the Definition-of-Done success-check as ONE operation; the agent
- delegates the whole thing (the `launch_verified` verb -> mios-os-control
- -> POST /os_control here) and just reads `launched`. The fire goes
- THROUGH THE LAUNCHER BROKER -- never a direct subprocess: the broker
- runs as the operator's user systemd service, so only IT inherits the
- WSLg env (WAYLAND_DISPLAY / WSL_INTEROP) that actually surfaces a window
- on the operator's desktop. The broker is threaded, so this reentrant
- call (the daemon firing while the launch_verified verb is itself
- in-flight on the broker) does NOT deadlock.
- How long fire+verify polls for the window to surface (flatpak / WSLg
- cold-launches can take a while to first paint).
- PROSE-ARG GUARD (operator 2026-05-30): a #E ref can substitute an agent
- node's FULL answer ("Here are your installed games ... Wallpaper Engine has
- the highest rating ... Launching it now:") into the launch arg instead of a
- clean name -- the launcher then can't resolve it AND polls the full verify
- loop (~105s) for a window that can never appear. If the arg looks like prose
- (newline / many words), extract the SINGLE launch target via the micro-LLM.
- The in-session executor's verdict is AUTHORITATIVE for "a window appeared"
- (it runs on the real interactive desktop); trust it over the Linux-side
- probe, which false-reports no-window for Windows-host/Store windows.
- presented_to_operator ONLY -- process_alive false-positives via the
- verifier's pgrep self-match (see launch_verifier_loop); SOUL rule:
- "process alive is INSUFFICIENT, success only when window presented".
- The executor's in-session "presented" verdict ALSO counts as success.
- Boot delay: let the rest of the daemon initialize so the
- DB writer is warm before we start firing events.
- Best-effort create. If the parent dir is owned by another
- service (e.g. /var/lib/mios/ai owned by mios-hermes) and
- root's mkdir lands in a perms-conflict, skip silently --
- the dir will be created by its owner agent later, at which
- point we can re-add the watch on the next daemon restart.
- Pick the most informative op-name for the mask.
- Brief backoff so a persistent OS error doesn't spin.
- Boot delay -- let mios-daemon settle, sessions populate.
- Compose the user message: terse JSON dump of the aggregate.
- Atomic write of both the markdown digest + structured JSON
- WS-A3: sync into the CANONICAL pg kanban table (id/title/status/
- detail jsonb). Was a legacy kanban_shadow UPSERT -- dead on the
- retired :8000, and its pg mirror targeted a non-existent
- kanban_shadow table -> the daemon's task view never persisted.
- Parameterized upsert (id is the PK), degrade-open via _pg_run.
- Scratch row carrying the digest text (so other agents can
- see what the nudger concluded without re-parsing the .md).
- Per-tick event row -- audit trail of when the nudger ran.
- Boot delay so OWUI + llm-light warm before first generation
- W0-T2 (1): host-pressure gate -- skip this generation tick (the LLM
- call below) when over ceiling AND pressure_skip; still falls through
- to the interruptible sleep so the loop keeps its cadence.
- Interruptible sleep
- ── Main ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ── Satisfaction monitor (Phase E.1 -- daemon-side goal tracking) ───
- Operator directive 2026-05-18: "mios-daemon/agent should be
- monitoring successes and stopping work if ALL criteria is met and
- goals set are completed/tasks/user queries are satisfied".
- Polls the DB event table for kind=refine rows (each user query goes
- through agent-pipe's refine pass which writes one of these). For
- every refine that doesn't yet have a corresponding satisfaction
- verdict, AND-fold the post-refine tool_call.success values from
- the same session. Emit:
- event kind=user_query_satisfied   severity=info
- payload={refine_id, intended_outcome, tool_calls_checked,
- all_succeeded: true}
- event kind=user_query_unsatisfied severity=warn
- payload={refine_id, intended_outcome, tool_calls_checked,
- failed_tools: [...], stderr_preview: ...}
- agent-pipe + Hermes can SUBSCRIBE to these (poll the event table
- or pick up via the Phase A.2 inotify event bus) and halt-on-
- satisfied OR surface-failure-explicitly. The audit row also lets
- the operator query post-hoc: "show me all unsatisfied goals from
- the last day".
- Filter out refines that already have a satisfaction event
- referencing their id. The legacy backend doesn't have a JOIN; do it in
- a second query against the recent satisfaction events.
- WS-A3: this read is now LIVE in dual mode (see _db_read gate) -> bind
- refine_ts ($1, a DB-row value treated as tainted) out-of-band; the interval
- count is int-coerced inline.
- Pattern derived from the verb's most-likely-titled arg.
- URL -> netloc, then take the last path segment OR the bare name;
- mios-window-active accepts a comma-separated pattern list.
- Signal name -> check implementation. This registry is the SET of available
- checks (the capability), NOT the policy of which verb uses which -- that
- policy is SSOT in mios.toml [daemon.post_check] (_VERB_POST_CHECK).
- No tools after refine: can't AND-fold. For intent=chat this is
- EXPECTED (no tool dispatch needed) -> satisfied.
- For intent=agent/dispatch the daemon has NO basis to declare
- failure: under unify-on a verb runs INSIDE the sub-agent and
- leaves no tool_call row, and the daemon -- unlike the agent-pipe
- confirmation engine -- never sees the agent's delivered answer.
- Emitting "unsatisfied: no_tools_seen" here was a false-negative
- that, written 30s AFTER the orchestrator's authoritative inline
- verdict, OVERRODE it (newer ts wins) and made the NEXT turn's
- polish read a stale failure (operator 2026-05-22 confirmation-
- engine bug). The orchestrator's inline check (source=
- mios-agent-pipe) is authoritative for these turns; the daemon
- DEFERS by returning a "skipped" sentinel and writing no event.
- The daemon stays the cross-turn backstop ONLY for turns that DID
- record tool_call rows (the else-branch below).
- Per-verb check overrides bare tool_call.success when it
- ran -- the visible-outcome signal is more authoritative
- than the broker's exit code (which can be 0 even when
- the launch sandbox died after the broker collected it).
- No verb-specific check; fall back to bare success.
- W0-T2 (4): a fresh UNSATISFIED verdict is a notable signal -- reset the
- quiescence clock so the classify cadence drops back to responsive.
- ─── Directory indexer ────────────────────────────────────────────
- Walks the configured [daemon.index] roots on a cadence, upserts
- directory_entry rows into the DB. Agents query via the
- `directory_lookup` verb -- DB hit ~5ms vs the 60ms+ live
- mios-find / fs_search. Summaries extracted for text-shaped files
- so the agent can rank relevance without re-reading each file.
- Later layer wins on scalar keys; the roots LIST is REPLACED (not
- concatenated) -- the shared deep_merge overwrites a non-dict value,
- matching the former shallow update for [daemon.index]'s flat keys.
- Skip shebangs + obvious header noise; the next non-empty
- line is usually the real one-liner identifier.
- Depth check.
- Prune excluded dirs IN PLACE (os.walk respects the
- mutation of dirnames during top-down traversal).
- Field-by-field legacy-dialect with proper literal shapes.
- Count per-statement ERRs inside the 200-OK response.
- First statement is the USE prefix; data statements
- start at index 1.
- WS-A3: root_label + every per-entry value (filesystem PATHS and first-line
- file CONTENT -- attacker-influenceable) are BOUND as $n params, never
- f-string-spliced (the old _pgesc was not a binding). DELETE + batch INSERT
- run in ONE atomic statements-envelope so the root's index never half-updates.
- keep NULL inline (not a value) so the column default/NULL
- applies; drop the placeholder number back.
- pgvector mirror (R15) -- runs in dual + postgres modes.
- Legacy DB replace -- skipped once Postgres is primary (pg is then the
- source of truth); kept for the dual-mode transition window.
- Delete by root_label first.
- Deferred to the orchestrator's inline confirmation
- engine (no recorded tools to AND-fold). No event
- written; not a verdict.
- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- mios-daemon-agent :8644 -- the daemon's OpenAI-compatible /v1 face,
- now the CONSOLIDATED CPU reasoning lane.
- Operator 2026-05-18: "mios-daemon hosts a mios-daemon-agent ... keeps
- system logs in the loop for followups/redirections". Operator
- 2026-05-24: "mios-daemon-agent = mios-cpu/reasoner! CONSOLIDATE" -- so
- this one always-on CPU process IS both (a) the global journal/log
- monitor and (b) the council's CPU reasoning lane (the retired
- mios-reasoner-cpu merged in here). When agent-pipe fans a turn out to
- :8644, the daemon-agent REASONS on the CPU model (qwen3:1.7b @ the
- CPU lane :11435, num_gpu 0 -- same compute the old mios-reasoner-cpu
- used) via the proven think=False llm_chat() path, GROUNDED in the live
- global journal/log telemetry it already maintains, and bursts to 8c/16t
- for the foreground turn. agent-pipe's polish merges its answer with the
- dGPU primary's. (Was a telemetry-only context dump -- no inference --
- which polluted unrelated answers and forced fanout=false; reasoning +
- grounding fixes that, so the lane is now fanned out concurrently.)
- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Consolidated CPU-reasoner lane (operator 2026-05-24 "mios-daemon-agent =
- mios-cpu/reasoner! CONSOLIDATE"): when agent-pipe fans a turn out here, the
- daemon-agent now REASONS on the CPU model (not just a telemetry dump), and a
- foreground turn bursts to 8c/16t -- vs the background loop's light 4 threads.
- 400 (was 800): the foreground swarm reply runs the BIGGER qwen3.5:4b on CPU,
- so cap the length -- 400 tokens @ 16 threads is a clearly VISIBLE ~60-80s CPU
- burst without the ~120-150s a full 800-token 4B pass took (which, combined
- with deepen, pushed the swarm to 7.7min -- operator 2026-05-26).
- FOREGROUND swarm model -- decoupled from the background MODEL (operator
- 2026-05-26 "bigger CPU model"): the always-on background loop stays on the
- snappy MODEL (qwen3:1.7b) so the daemon is never sluggish, but a SWARM facet
- reply runs on this BIGGER CPU model (qwen3.5:4b ~4.7B) so the CPU node does a
- heavy, VISIBLE, sustained 8c/16t churn instead of a brief light blip. Must be
- a model present on the CPU lane (:11435). Empty -> fall back to MODEL.
- FOREGROUND swarm endpoint -- the CPU lane (:11435, num_gpu=0), so a
- swarm facet reply VISIBLY churns the CPU (operator 2026-05-26 "CPU is seeing no
- utilization") even though the daemon's background MODEL/ENDPOINT stay on the
- iGPU (the 2026-05-25 always-on offload). Both directives held: iGPU runs the
- always-on loop, CPU runs the heavy foreground swarm pass.
- NOTE (operator 2026-05-21): web/other tool use is NOT hardcoded here.
- Tools are GLOBAL -- every agent/sub-agent can call the whole surface
- (web_search, verbs, recipes) and is PRE-PROMPTED to use them via its
- Modelfile. So WHICH queries to run (multi-faceted or not) is the MODEL's
- decision, governed by the AI-driven CONFIRMATION ENGINE (the satisfaction /
- Definition-of-Done checker) -- never by hardcoded Python query-extraction or
- inline English prompts. The daemon-agent's automatic supplement therefore
- carries only its CORE DATA -- the consolidated GLOBAL journal/log telemetry
- it already collects (its job, not a tool-use decision). Model-driven web
- tool use runs through the shared agent tool-loop + confirmation engine.
- SYNCHRONOUS launch success-check (operator 2026-05-25 4A:
- "the daemon-agent ... runs the Definition-of-Done success
- check; the main agent/sub-agents just delegate and read the
- success signal"). The post-hoc launch_verifier_loop only
- catches false claims minutes later by scanning chats; this
- lets any agent ask IN-TURN "did app X actually launch?" and
- get the daemon's consolidated verdict (live window/process
- probe + the daemon's own recorded false-success history),
- so it can retry or report honestly instead of blind-claiming.
- The check is the same read-only mios-window-active --present
- probe the loop uses -- it never launches anything.
- presented_to_operator ONLY (process_alive false-positives via
- the verifier's pgrep self-match; SOUL: window-presented only).
- 4A #2: the daemon FIRES the OS-control launch (through the
- broker, in operator/WSLg context) AND runs the success-check,
- returning ONE verdict the agent reads. Body:
- {action:"launch", app:"<name>"}.
- Best-effort chmod: when STATE_DIR was created/owned by ANOTHER user (e.g. a
- root- or old-user-owned dir under this unit's User=mios-ai after the user
- consolidation), chmod EPERMs. That must NEVER crash the always-on daemon --
- mkdir already guaranteed the dir exists, and ownership is fixed by tmpfiles/
- chown, not here. (Writes still need ownership; that's the tmpfiles job.)
- Operator 2026-05-24: the daemon-agent runs always-on background work at
- ~2c/4t but must BURST to 8c/16t when it participates in a foreground AI
- pipeline (concurrent with the GPU/iGPU). So pin to UP TO 8 randomly-chosen
- cores (which cores varies per boot -> spreads wear); CPUQuota=800% in the
- drop-in (mios-daemon.service.d/20-cpu-limit.conf) allows all 8, while
- CPUWeight=20 + Nice=10 keep it LIGHT at baseline (the background loop uses
- ~2c; the 8 are there for the foreground burst) and make it YIELD to the
- GPU agents / interactive turns when contended. Best-effort: skipped where
- sched_setaffinity is unavailable or there are <2 cores; pins to all cores
- when the box has fewer than 8.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-dashboard-render-issue.sh
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-dashboard-render-issue.sh
- Composites the MiOS dashboard into /etc/issue.d/30-mios.issue so it
- appears on the console BEFORE the login prompt. Handles the
- headless-first-console case (operator boots a fresh image, lands on
- tty1 / ttyS0 / IPMI SoL with no GUI, and needs to see the system
- state immediately).
- Triggered by:
- - mios-dashboard-issue.service     (one-shot, after multi-user.target)
- - mios-dashboard-issue.timer       (every 5 minutes thereafter, so
- Quadlet-state changes propagate)
- Output is plain ASCII -- TERM=linux forces the dashboard's no-color
- path so the file is safe for kernel text VT, serial console, IPMI,
- and any other terminal that may not handle ANSI escape sequences
- cleanly.
- agetty reads /etc/issue and /etc/issue.d/* on each getty start, and
- `getty@.service` Restart=always ensures every login attempt re-reads
- the snippet, so refreshes from the timer always reach the next login.
- Fail safe: write a minimal banner instead of leaving a stale
- /etc/issue.d/30-mios.issue from a previous boot.
- Render in plain ASCII to a temp file, then atomic-rename so partial
- writes never reach getty. Invoked through explicit `env -i bash` to
- break the SHELLOPTS chain -- without it, mios-dashboard.sh inherits
- `nounset:pipefail` from this wrapper's exported SHELLOPTS and exits
- silently with rc=1 during one of its early `tput cols` / `((...))`
- paths when stdin is not a TTY (systemd context). With the clean env,
- the dashboard runs as if from a login shell.
- Render is best-effort: a getty without a banner is a cosmetic glitch,
- but a FAILED unit clutters every cockpit dashboard refresh and
- triggers needless restart-loops via the timer. So on render failure,
- we drop a minimal banner instead of exiting non-zero.
- `timeout` so a hung dashboard render (e.g. a service/port probe blocking during the
- transitional first-boot state, when mios-ai-firstboot saturates the VM) can never exceed
- the unit's TimeoutStartSec and land the service in a 'timeout'/killed FAILED state on a
- 5-min restart loop (observed: ExecMainStatus=15). On timeout we fall through to the
- minimal banner below -- the render is best-effort by design. -k 3: SIGKILL 3s after TERM
- so a child (fastfetch/probe) that ignores TERM still dies before the unit's own timeout.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-day0-reset
- mios-day0-reset
- Clear MiOS runtime + AI state back to a day-0 starting point.
- Operator-invoked: drops chat history, every tool_call/event/knowledge
- row, scratchpads, sessions, OWUI chats, SearXNG/crawl caches. KEEPS
- /etc, /usr, agent definitions, person/skill/app_install inventories,
- the ed25519 passport keypairs, MCP + A2A registries (operator config).
- Backend: pgvector is the SOLE agent datastore (the legacy :8000 DB is retired).
- pg runtime tables are TRUNCATEd through mios-db --pg; the table list is a
- trusted constant (config identifiers, never request data) so the names stay
- inline. OWUI chat history lives in webui.db (sqlite).
- Why a script: a chat-turn through Claude can't perform mass deletes
- (the auto-mode classifier blocks named-target destructive ops without
- explicit per-target authorization). This script bundles the canonical
- target set so a human operator can re-run it as needed without
- re-debating scope each time.
- Idempotent enough to re-run; not a "factory reset" -- the host stays
- fully provisioned. For a deeper reset (passport keys, agents, skills),
- extend the PG_DROP / KEEP lists below.
- Usage: sudo /usr/libexec/mios/mios-day0-reset
- ── pgvector is the SOLE agent store since the legacy->pgvector migration.
- Clear the runtime/AI tables in pg. KEEP the definitional/operator-curated
- tables (alias, app_install, resolves_to, run_template, skill) AND mios_rag
- (the docs-index RAG = baked SYSTEM knowledge, regenerated from /usr/share/doc
- -- leave it so "full AI systems knowledge" stays baked). TRUNCATE keeps
- schema + indexes; one statement so FK order never bites.
- PG_DROP is a trusted CONSTANT list (config identifiers, never request data),
- so the table NAMES stay inline in the SQL -- parameterization binds VALUES,
- not identifiers, and pg can't bind a table name out-of-band. Routed through
- mios-db --pg so creds + connection come from the SSOT [pgvector] section.
- Resolve the table names that actually exist (to_regclass returns NULL for a
- missing table) so a schema-drifted host still resets the rest. Degrade-open:
- any mios-db failure (DB down) leaves _pglist empty and we skip, never crash.
- Day-0 reset also resets dir OWNERSHIP that drifted (the agent-plane
- user consolidation left some dirs owned by the legacy `mios` user).
- Without this, mcp-init.sh + mios-daemon-state fail with EPERM after
- clearing because tmpfiles 'd' does not re-chown EXISTING dirs (only
- creates missing). Make every service-owned dir mios-ai:mios-ai 0750.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-db
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-db --pg '<sql>' [-f <file.sql>] [--json]
- [--owui '<sql>']
- [--embed '<text>'] [--embed-model <m>]
- Unified MiOS shared-state CLI -- one tool that fronts every
- local backend agents need to query.
- Operator directives 2026-05-18 stacked:
- * "make sure this is all OpenSource Alternatives /
- Local Endpoints / Self-Hosted Endpoints) and Open WebUI Native
- DB(s) for knowledge/memory/context/scratch/skills/functions/
- tools/etc-etc"
- * "unify all AI Surfaces!!"
- The three backends + which data lives where:
- --owui <sql>      Read/write Open WebUI's webui.db (SQLite).
- SOURCE OF TRUTH for: chat / message / memory /
- knowledge / file / tool / function / model /
- user / group / channel.
- --embed <text>    /v1/embeddings via the canonical
- MiOS embedding model (nomic-embed-text).
- Returns the float[] vector. SOURCE OF TRUTH
- for: embeddings. Switch model via --embed-model.
- --pg <sql>        PostgreSQL/pgvector at MIOS_PG_*. SOURCE OF TRUTH for:
- agent / session / tool_call / event /
- kanban / scratch / agent_metric.
- Cross-cutting state OWUI doesn't natively have.
- Env (with defaults). All envs source from the layered mios.toml chain
- via tools/lib/userenv.sh -- vendor (/usr/share/mios/mios.toml) <
- host (/etc/mios/mios.toml) < user (~/.config/mios/mios.toml). A shell
- `export` always wins (`:=` form). To change the defaults globally,
- edit [pgvector] / [ports] / paths in mios.toml -- DO NOT
- hardcode values here. See the SSOT directive in
- automation/34-render-quadlets.sh.
- MIOS_PG_HOST         localhost        [pgvector].host
- MIOS_PORT_PGVECTOR   8432             [ports].pgvector
- MIOS_PG_USER         mios             [pgvector].user
- MIOS_PG_PASS         mios             [pgvector].pass
- MIOS_PG_DB           mios             [pgvector].database
- MIOS_OWUI_DB         /var/lib/mios/open-webui/webui.db
- MIOS_LLM_URL         http://localhost:${MIOS_PORT_LLM_LIGHT:-11450}
- MIOS_EMBED_MODEL     nomic-embed-text [pgvector].embed_model
- Exits 0 on success, 1 on backend unreachable, 2 on missing binary.
- Source the SSOT-layered env first so MIOS_* envs reflect the operator's
- mios.toml overrides without callers having to source userenv.sh themselves.
- Canonical deployed paths mirror /etc/profile.d/mios-env.sh; silent no-op
- if the helper isn't present (e.g. a fresh host pre-image-rebuild). The
- script still works with raw env-var exports either way.
- shellcheck disable=SC1090
- WS-9 PostgreSQL + pgvector unified agent DB (--pg mode). SSOT [pgvector] /
- [ports].pgvector via userenv.sh; local-only defaults. Callers route through
- THIS tool so creds live in one SSOT place (no hardcoded root:root copies).
- ── MODE: --owui  (OWUI webui.db via sqlite3 over the bind-mount) ──
- Container-exec fallback: OWUI image ships python3 + sqlite.
- Pass SQL via stdin (sys.argv[1] = SQL); use a CURSOR for
- .description (Connection.execute returns a cursor but the
- description attr lives on the cursor, not the connection).
- ── MODE: --embed  (/v1/embeddings, OpenAI-compat) ──
- OpenAI-compat shape -- the canonical /v1 embeddings schema.
- Pass model + text as argv (NOT spliced into the -c source) so a model name
- or text containing a quote can't break out into the python program.
- ── MODE: --pg  (PostgreSQL + pgvector unified agent DB, WS-9) ──
- The unified agent DB (pgvector is the sole datastore). Creds from the
- SSOT [pgvector] section (above) -- no hardcoded values here.
- 1. local psql client (faster).
- 2. container-exec fallback: psql inside the mios-pgvector container.
- 3. pure-python TCP fallback (no psql binary AND no podman access -- e.g.
- the confined mios-ai service user running mios-daemon / dispatched
- verbs). Speaks the pg v3 wire protocol over loopback trust (pg_hba
- 127.0.0.1/32 trust). Offline, zero deps -- the universal path. (R15)
- ── MODE: --pg-json  (parameterized pgvector via the extended wire protocol) ──
- Reads a {"sql","params"} / {"statements":[...]} envelope on STDIN and binds the
- values OUT-OF-BAND (SQL-injection-safe). Only mios-pg-query can bind from an
- envelope (psql/podman exec take raw SQL), so this routes straight there with
- the SSOT-mapped connection env. (WS-A3 CLI SQL-safety -- the parameterized path
- the python memory tools call instead of f-string-splicing values into SQL.)
- ── No backend flag matched ──
- The legacy no-flag DB default is RETIRED -- cross-cutting agent state
- lives in PostgreSQL/pgvector now. Route explicitly so a bare invocation
- can't silently hit a dead backend; tell the caller which flag to use.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-directory-lookup
- Per-hit summary cap + a hard envelope cap so the --json output ALWAYS stays
- parseable under the dispatch broker's ~6 KB stdout truncation (a larger blob
- would be cut mid-string -> invalid JSON for the calling agent).
- pgvector is the unconditional path (the legacy DB is retired). A None return
- means the backend was unreachable -> degrade open to an empty result.
- Rank in-process: we pulled 3x the requested limit so the
- rank pass can prune.
- Bonus for filename containing the query as a whole word.
- Penalise deep paths slightly so top-of-tree wins ties.
- Hard envelope guard: drop lowest-ranked hits until under the cap so
- the agent always receives COMPLETE, parseable JSON (top hits kept).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-docgen
- markdown report -> Word
- markdown bullets -> PowerPoint deck (--- splits slides)
- CSV -> Excel workbook
- existing .docx -> PDF (LibreOffice headless)
- Format -> canonical file extension. Drives both routing and output naming.
- Pandoc owns the markup side; LibreOffice owns the office-binary side; the two
- overlap on docx/pptx/html (Pandoc preferred there for fidelity from markdown).
- Formats Pandoc can WRITE from markdown/markup source.
- Office-binary formats LibreOffice converts losslessly (its native domain).
- soffice --convert-to filter hints for ambiguous targets (e.g. csv->xlsx).
- -- config ------------------------------------------------------------------
- -- emit --------------------------------------------------------------------
- -- format resolution -------------------------------------------------------
- Accept an absolute path OR a PATH-resolvable name.
- -- LibreOffice headless conversion -----------------------------------------
- -- Pandoc conversion / authoring -------------------------------------------
- No LaTeX/pdf engine -> route PDF through LibreOffice instead.
- -- CSV -> XLSX (no pandoc path; LibreOffice native) ------------------------
- -- subcommands -------------------------------------------------------------
- Routing: CSV->xlsx and any office-binary source -> LibreOffice; markup
- source (md/txt/html) -> Pandoc; PDF from markup falls back to LibreOffice.
- Source content: inline --content TEXT (the agent-pipe VERB path -- agents
- pass text, and the launcher broker runs `bash -lc` with stdin CLOSED so a
- verb can't pipe; the dispatch shlex-quotes the arg so typical doc text is
- safe on argv), a --content-file PATH, or --stdin (the OWUI tool streams
- text here). Unifies the two docgen_build surfaces on TEXT semantics.
- Write the authored content to a temp source file, then convert.
- -- main --------------------------------------------------------------------
- Manual parse so an unknown/no subcommand prints help (exit 0).

- Print a unified index of every .md doc on the MiOS host so agents
- (Hermes, MiOS-Agent, future OpenCode, MCP clients) can DISCOVER
- what's available, then `cat` the specific file on demand. Per
- operator directive 2026-05-18: ".md files should ALL be accessible
- by all agents context windows/scratchpad (GLOBAL UNIFIED)".
- Doc surfaces scanned (all Day-0 image-immutable except scratch):
- /usr/share/mios/ai/           agent identities + system prompts
- /usr/share/mios/docs/         FHS architecture docs
- /usr/share/mios/hermes/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md
- /usr/share/mios/cookbooks/    operator workflows
- /usr/share/mios/prompts/      meta-prompts
- /etc/mios/system-prompts/     operator overrides (mutable)
- /var/lib/mios/scratch/        shared mutable scratchpad (agent notes)

- else the first H1 line, else the first 80 chars of the first
- non-blank line.

- wins; else first H1; else first non-blank line.
- 1. YAML frontmatter description: (handles single AND multi-line)
- 2. First H1
- 3. First non-blank, non-frontmatter, non-comment line

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-dotfiles
- the SSOT dotfiles (the theme surfaces + settings surfaces derived from
- mios.toml: btop, oh-my-posh, quickshell, fastfetch, VS Code colors, the live
- gitconfig, Windows Terminal, the Windows registry) to the operator's LIVE HOME by
- ORCHESTRATING usr/libexec/mios/mios-theme-render (the projection engine, which
- owns the surface registry, the per-platform apply.target map, timestamped RAW
- backups, json-/ini-merge, and the HOME-scope refusal backstop). This wrapper
- RENDERS NOTHING itself and NEVER writes: `status`/`diff` shell the engine's
- dry-run (`mios-theme-render diff`), `sync`/`apply` delegate every write + its
- backup to the engine (`mios-theme-render apply`). It only adds a friendly
- per-surface OK/skip/changed summary + a final tally on top of the engine's
- authoritative output. Degrade-open: a surface with no apply.target for THIS
- platform is a clean skip (the engine reports "no <os> HOME target -- skipping",
- rc unaffected), never a failure. Paired with mios-sync-theme (`--apply-home`
- chains into `sync`) + etc/profile.d/mios-verbs.sh (the `mios dotfiles` verb).
- Same repo/system root convention as mios-theme-render: MIOS_THEME_ROOT wins,
- else three dirs up from usr/libexec/mios/ (i.e. "/" in a deployed system, the
- worktree root in the repo). Propagated to the engine child so BOTH sides
- resolve the identical mios.toml overlay + repo-relative templates.
- Every per-surface engine line is "[mios-dotfiles-render] <diff|apply> <surface>: <rest>".
- (Surface names are [A-Za-z0-9_-]; the registry never emits a dotted surface.)
- Per-surface outcome classes (derived from the engine's own wording).
- Human labels per class, per mode. `change` reads differently for a dry-run
- (would-change) vs a real apply (applied); everything else is mode-neutral.
- Surface the engine's reason (e.g. "no windows HOME target").

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-dotfiles-render
- Repo/system root: default two dirs up from usr/libexec/mios/, overridable.
- Three-layer overlay (lowest first). Repo-relative vendor + absolute host/user.
- Layered SSOT loading + the canonical palette defaults come from the ONE shared
- resolver (the Python peer of tools/lib/userenv.sh) -- no local deep_merge/DEFAULTS copy.
- Values too generic to tokenize (used as plain colors everywhere, not as palette refs).
- A surface descriptor (ADR-0010). `kind` is the WRITE-SEMANTICS axis, orthogonal
- to `section` (the token source): absent kind => "template" so the 8 existing
- color/settings surfaces are byte-for-byte unchanged. `fixture` (merge kinds
- only) names the checked-in base + expected-merge pair the offline drift-gate
- diffs against; `policy` steers merge write-behavior (ini-merge, later).
- Always include [identity] section keys
- Try dotted path first (e.g. "identity.fullname" or "colors.bg")
- Try converting underscore to dots as a fallback (e.g., "identity_fullname" -> "identity.fullname")
- --- json-merge primitives (ADR-0010) ----------------------------------------
- A json-merge surface owns only a SUBTREE of a foreign JSON document (VS Code /
- Windows Terminal settings.json). The MiOS-owned subtree is spliced onto the
- foreign doc so every key MiOS does NOT emit is byte-preserved. Both the offline
- fixture.base (drift-gate) and the live settings.json (apply) are read as JSONC
- and must round-trip through a STRING-AWARE comment/trailing-comma strip that
- never mangles a `//` inside a string value (e.g. an `https://` URL). A base
- that will not parse is REFUSED (exit 2, write NOTHING) -- MiOS never corrupts
- an unreadable foreign file.
- JSONC trailing comma: drop a comma that (skipping whitespace)
- immediately precedes this closer. String-safe: we are not in_string.
- Array-merge-by-key (ADR-0010). By DEFAULT _json_deep_merge REPLACES a list
- wholesale at the owned pointer (index-merge is unsafe for most arrays). But a
- few foreign JSON docs keep a COLLECTION keyed by a stable field -- e.g. Windows
- Terminal's top-level `schemes` array, each element `{name, background, ...}`.
- Wholesale-replacing it would DELETE the operator's OTHER schemes. For the JSON
- pointers listed here ONLY, the two lists are merged BY KEY instead. The map is
- keyed by JSON pointer (e.g. "/schemes"), so every OTHER array -- and every
- current surface, NONE of which has a `/schemes` array (vscode-colors owns only
- objects) -- keeps the byte-identical wholesale-replace path. Extend this map to
- add a new keyed-array pointer; leave it be and nothing changes.
- --- ini-merge primitives (ADR-0010, AGY-58) ---------------------------------
- An ini-merge surface (git config) owns EXACTLY the keys its template emits
- (user.name/email, core.editor, init.defaultBranch, pull.rebase, alias.{co,br,
- ci,st}). Those owned keys are UPSERTED into a foreign gitconfig -- SEEDED if
- absent (append to the section block, or a fresh [section] at EOF), or REPLACED
- in place per the write policy if present -- while every line NOT in the owned
- set (credential.helper, user.signingkey, commit.gpgsign, [remote ...]) is byte-
- preserved. A git-config key is addressed by (section, subsection, key): git
- treats section + key names case-insensitively and the subsection case-
- sensitively, so the index lowercases section/key and keeps subsection verbatim.
- The rendered template is BOTH the ownership manifest (its (section,key) lines)
- AND the values; the un-rendered template recovers each line's @MIOS:token@ ->
- the mios.toml (section,key) that feeds it (for the operator_set policy test).
- blank line, #/; comment, or a line that is not a kv assignment (or one
- that precedes any section header): opaque, never owned.
- --- ssh-merge primitives (ADR-0010 / AGY-92) ---------------------------------
- --- kind dispatch (ADR-0010) ------------------------------------------------
- `derive_fn(surface, merged) -> committed-artifact bytes` is the uniform shape
- cmd_render writes and cmd_check byte-diffs (OFFLINE -- a merge surface's derive
- reads its checked-in fixture.base, NEVER a live foreign file).
- `live_apply_fn(surface, merged, current) -> bytes` is what cmd_apply writes to
- the operator's LIVE HOME (`current` = the live file's content, or None).
- Merge kinds require a fixture pair (no ungated merge surface). json-merge
- (JSON settings docs) + ini-merge (git config) splice a MiOS-owned subtree/key-
- set onto a foreign file, preserving every foreign key; registry / skip are
- declared valid by ADR-0010 but LAND LATER, so an unimplemented kind fails the
- same fail-loud exit-3 path as an unknown one.
- The surface registry is now SSOT-authored in mios.toml [dotfiles.registry.*]
- (ADR-0010) instead of a hardcoded literal, so the surface map itself is
- operator-editable via the Portal (ADR-0009) and can carry a per-platform
- live-HOME `apply` target, a `kind` (write-semantics), and a merge `fixture`.
- _load_surfaces() transcribes that namespace into a name -> _Surface(...) map;
- because an absent `kind` defaults to "template", the 8 color/settings surfaces
- render/check/capture byte-for-byte identically. A surface is projected + drift-
- gated once its .tmpl exists; add one by authoring its
- [dotfiles.registry.<name>] table then running `mios-theme-render capture
- <name>` (template surfaces) or authoring its fixture pair (merge surfaces).
- SETTINGS surface: `section` names the mios.toml section whose scalar
- keys project as @MIOS:<section>_<key>@ tokens (conf-formatted), the way
- btop-conf derives the WHOLE btop config from [btop].
- kind = WRITE-SEMANTICS axis (ADR-0010). Absent => template (byte-identity
- backstop). Unknown/unimplemented => exit 3, same posture as missing template.
- A merge kind MUST declare its drift-gate fixture pair (checked-in base +
- expected merge output) -- no ungated merge surface.
- COMPLETENESS floor (full-gate only): every *.tmpl on disk must be claimed by a
- [dotfiles.registry.*] surface. Otherwise dropping a surface's registry block would
- silently de-gate its artifact (the drift loop below only iterates REGISTERED
- surfaces) -- an orphaned template is a coverage hole. A named subset is an
- intentional narrowing, so the sweep runs only on the full gate.
- first differing line, for a legible message
- capture is TEMPLATE-ONLY: a merge surface's committed artifact is a
- deterministic merge output (fixture.expected), not a hex-tokenizable file.
- Self-verify: rendering the template must reproduce the artifact byte-for-byte.
- --- live-HOME apply/diff (ADR-0010) -----------------------------------------
- Additive verbs that render a surface and write it to the operator's LIVE HOME
- (per-platform [dotfiles.registry.<name>.apply.target]), NEVER touching the
- build-tree artifact the render/check drift-gate owns. Byte-fidelity + safety
- are paramount: the destination is opened newline='' (no CRLF translation, so
- the bytes match the render/check path exactly); an existing file -- even
- foreign/binary content -- is backed up RAW (shutil.copy2, mode+mtime) before
- any overwrite, never silently destroyed; and a target that resolves outside
- HOME, through a symlink, cross-drive, or with an unexpanded variable is
- REFUSED rather than written to a wrong path. A json-merge surface MERGES its
- owned subtree onto the live file (foreign keys preserved) instead of a whole-
- file overwrite; the same backup + HOME-scope refusals apply.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-enroll-secure-boot
- mios-enroll-secure-boot -- enroll the ublue/akmods Machine Owner Key (MOK) so
- the MOK-signed NVIDIA + ZFS kmods MiOS inherits from ucore-hci load under
- Secure Boot. Without this, a Secure-Boot system using the stable/lts NVIDIA or
- ZFS streams fails to load those modules (uCore documents the same mandatory
- step). Mirrors ublue's `ujust enroll-secure-boot-key`.
- Operator runs this ONCE: it imports the cert and prompts for a one-time
- password; at the next reboot the firmware's blue "MOK Manager" screen asks for
- that password to confirm enrollment. (R14 -- review-flagged Secure-Boot gap,
- 2026-06-06.) This is an operator action, not an agent verb.
- Candidate cert locations (ublue/akmods ship the .der under /etc/pki/akmods).
- Already enrolled? mokutil --list-enrolled would show it; skip if so.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-env-probe
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-env-probe [--brief|--full|--markdown|--json]
- Snapshot the agent's CURRENT environment as deterministic facts.
- Designed to be injected into a Hermes session's first turn via the
- pre_llm_call hook (see mios-hermes-init-hook), AND callable
- explicitly when an agent realises mid-conversation that it doesn't
- know what's around it.
- Operator directive 2026-05-15: "make sure the AI stack has an
- understanding of its environment when initialized -- MiOS AI's
- should have an understanding of the MiOS codebase/stack -- the
- Agents dispatched Globally Should be informed of the environment
- via an agent init/probe pass on first query".
- Modes:
- --brief      ~10-line summary (used as init context; cheap to inject)
- --full       all sections; longer
- --markdown   markdown formatting (default for --full)
- --json       machine-readable
- Guard set -u: a value with shell-metachars must not abort under set -u.
- ─── facts gathering ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
- _toml_get <section> <key> -- read mios.toml [section].key (vendor)
- WSL detection
- Hardware
- OS
- Services
- Models loaded on the /v1 lane
- App counts via mios-apps (cheap; just --names | wc -l per category)
- ─── render ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Windows-host facts ONLY when on WSL2 (best-effort; never blocks).
- Single-quoted PS expression so bash leaves the $vars alone; the
- PowerShell child receives literal $os / $cpu / $mem.
- Full Windows-host probe (computer info + GPU) when on WSL2.
- Single-quoted PS expression so bash leaves $vars alone.
- MiOS environment probe ($(date -Iseconds))
- # Identity
- # Linux host (the MiOS distro)
- # MiOS stack services
- # AI inference
- # Launchable inventory
- # Pointers (for any deeper question)
- Pass every value through the ENVIRONMENT (not source interpolation) so a
- quote/special char in a field -- or a bash boolean like $IS_WSL=true,
- which is NOT valid Python -- can't break the JSON. The heredoc is
- single-quoted so bash leaves the python untouched; python reads os.environ.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-env-snapshot
- ============================================================================
- usr/libexec/mios/mios-env-snapshot - 'MiOS' v0.3.0
- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Resolves the full layered mios.toml configuration in a clean environment and
- outputs all resolved MIOS_* environment variables sorted deterministically.
- ============================================================================
- Deterministic collation regardless of the caller's locale. The final `| sort`
- runs in THIS process's environment (outside the env -i), so without a pinned
- LC_ALL the baseline line order follows the host locale (C vs en_US.UTF-8 reorder
- ~454 lines) -> check_resolved_env_lossless drifts between the capture host and the
- CI runner. Pin C collation so the sorted snapshot is byte-stable everywhere.
- Pin HOME + the user-layer paths to a nonexistent location so ONLY the
- version-controlled vendor SSOT (+ in-tree mios.d fragments) resolves -- never a
- host-specific ~/.config/mios overlay. Then exclude the self-referential config-path
- meta-keys (HOME-derived, not SSOT) so the snapshot is byte-identical across hosts/CI.
- Without this the baseline bakes host-relative paths -> check_resolved_env_lossless
- fails "after restoration" on any runner whose $HOME differs from where it was captured.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-everything
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-everything <query> [-n <max>] [-ext <csv>]
- First-class wrapper around Voidtools Everything CLI (es.exe) for
- the entire MiOS agentic stack. Operator directive 2026-05-16:
- "WE HAVE EVERYTHING CLI STILL DOING NOTHING AS A TOOL FOR THE
- ENTIRE MIOS AGENTIC STACKS" -- previously the es.exe probe was
- siloed inside mios-find; promoting to its own helper so any
- agent (Hermes, sys-agent, opencode, micro-LLMs) can search the
- Windows NTFS index in <100 ms without going through mios-find.
- Returns matching paths (one per line) sorted by Everything's
- default relevance ranking. Empty stdout + exit 1 on no-match.
- Env-args-first path resolution (no hardcoded paths):
- 1. $EVERYTHING_CLI env (colon-separated probe list -- set by
- hermes-agent.service.d drop-in or /etc/mios/install.env)
- 2. mios.toml [paths].everything_cli  (operator-edited)
- 3. compiled-in /mnt/m/Programs/Everything/es.exe fallback
- ─── Parse args ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── Resolve es.exe path (env-args-first) ─────────────────────────
- Shared layered mios.toml resolver (vendor < host < user), path injected as argv[1].
- es.exe (Everything CLI) not installed. A PowerShell recursive fallback was
- tried (2026-06-09) but a non-indexed walk of C:\Windows/Program Files is too
- slow (times out) -- the NTFS index is the whole point. everything_search
- needs es.exe; meanwhile the agent uses fs_search / mios_find / app_search.
- ─── Build the es.exe invocation ──────────────────────────────────
- Extension filter via OR-of-wildcards (Everything's native syntax).
- es.exe normally returns in <100ms native, but a COLD WSL-interop spawn can be
- slower -- 8s ceiling so a cold first call isn't killed mid-spawn. stderr is
- CAPTURED (not discarded) so a connection failure is reported, not silenced.
- `|| true`: this script runs under `set -euo pipefail`, and a nonzero es.exe
- (e.g. exit 8 "IPC window not found" when es.exe is version-mismatched to the
- running Everything) would otherwise abort the WHOLE script here -- BEFORE the
- unreachable-vs-no-match JSON envelope below runs -- so the agent got a bare
- exit code instead of the structured error. stderr is captured separately into
- $_ES_ERR, so the IPC-detection grep + both envelopes still fire correctly.
- Distinguish "Everything UNREACHABLE" (es.exe can't find the IPC window --
- es.exe version mismatched to the running Everything, Everything not
- running, or an elevation/session split) from a genuine 0-result match, so
- agents + the operator get an ACTIONABLE signal instead of a silent "no
- match". Operator 2026-05-27: FS search was silently dead -- es.exe
- v1.1.0.30 vs Everything v1.4.x IPC mismatch returned "Error 8: IPC window
- not found" which the old code swallowed as "no match".
- Surface the SSOT-recommended ES release ([paths].everything_cli_version)
- so the actionable hint names WHICH es.exe to install (a stale es.exe vs
- the running Everything is the usual cause of this IPC error). Degrade-open:
- if the key is absent the hint just omits the version.
- Machine-mode JSON: array of {path, name, ext, drive} so the
- agent can filter/sort without re-parsing prose. Operator
- directive 2026-05-18 'shim machine-mode JSON sweep' (task #148).
- Pass RAW via env (RAW_LINES) -- heredoc + pipe stdin conflict
- made `printf '$RAW' | python3 - <<PYEOF` deliver the heredoc
- text to python's stdin, dropping the RAW data.
- Windows paths use backslash separator; posix os.path doesn't
- split on it. Split on both / and \ for basename extraction.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-find
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-find <query>
- Fast fuzzy lookup against the cached environment inventory. Use this
- as the FIRST step whenever the operator says "launch <app>" --
- returns a ready-to-execute launch command in <100 ms, without any
- Get-ChildItem -Recurse over the Windows drive.
- Output (single line on stdout when match is unambiguous):
- <launch-command>
- Output (multiple matches, top 5 to stderr + nothing to stdout):
- N matches for "<query>" (top 5):
- 1. [<category>] <name>  ->  <launch>
- ...
- Output (no match, exit 1):
- no match for "<query>" in inventory; try `mios-apps --filter <substr>`
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: "MiOS-Hermes should be given the
- opportunity to map out it's environment for faster follow-up
- questions like ex; 'launch this app for me' should be snappy
- because MiOS-Agent(s) initialize and understand the environment
- and where everything already is".
- Implementation: shells out to `mios-apps --json` which returns
- JSONL of every known launchable thing across Linux + Windows. The
- Windows side is pre-cached for 5 minutes inside mios-apps (via
- Get-StartApps), so mios-find inherits that speed.
- `set -u` only -- catches unset variables but tolerates non-zero
- exits from sub-commands. Fast-path A's `mios-everything -ext exe`
- CAN return non-zero on no-match, which under `set -e` aborted the
- whole script before fast-path B (the inventory python) ever ran --
- operator-flagged 2026-05-17: "open wallpaper engine for me" failed
- because mios-find silently exit-0'\''d with no output. Fall-through
- resolution is the design intent; errexit defeats it.
- --json flag flips emit mode. Operator directive 2026-05-18 (task
- #148): shims that the planner / polish-grounding consume should
- emit structured envelopes so the agent reads typed fields, not
- prose. The existing dual-emit paths (fast-path A es.exe / fast-
- path B inventory-rank) are preserved; this flag wraps their
- output post-hoc.
- If --json was passed, re-exec ourselves WITHOUT the flag, capture
- stdout+stderr+exit, then emit a structured envelope. Cleanest way
- to wrap the dual-emit fast-paths below without duplicating their
- logic.
- The fast-path A path prints '(found via mios-everything; ...'
- to stderr; the fast-path B path leaves stderr empty. Use that
- to attribute the source so polish knows where the launch came
- from.
- ─── Alias resolution: generic queries -> specific apps ───────────────
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: "open a browser to URL" returns
- mios-hermes-browser (headless agent CDP) instead of chromedev
- (visible operator browser) because "browser" is in the agent
- binary's name. Add a TOML-first alias table so operators can
- remap generic words ("browser", "web browser", "the browser") to
- their preferred concrete app. Read from mios.toml [mios-find.aliases].
- Shared layered mios.toml resolver (vendor < host < user), path injected as argv[1].
- Re-run mios-find with the alias target as the query (single-level;
- an alias value is a concrete app name, not another alias).
- ─── WS-D: App-type resolution ───────────────────────────────────────
- ─── Specific-before-role reduction ──────────────────────────────────
- Operator 2026-06-19 "open edge browser opened zen randomly": "<app> <role>"
- (e.g. "edge browser") -> the scorer can't substring-match the FULL query to
- "Microsoft Edge" (no "browser" in the name), so Edge fell to the Levenshtein
- tier where Zen (windows-browser, the default) tied + won. When the LAST word is
- a [desktop.apps] ROLE and the HEAD is a SPECIFIC (non-role) app, reduce the
- query to the head so the scorer resolves the NAMED app. A BARE role ("browser")
- is left alone -> the windows-browser default (Zen) still wins. SSOT = mios.toml
- roles; no hardcoded English app names.
- Shared layered mios.toml resolver (vendor < host < user), path injected as argv[1].
- Require a SUBSTANTIVE head (>=4 chars) so generic browser synonyms ("web") stay
- a bare-role ask (-> default browser), while a real app name ("edge"/"chrome"/
- "firefox") reduces to the specific app.
- ─── Fast path A: delegate to mios-everything ─────────────────────────
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: "WE HAVE EVERYTHING CLI STILL DOING
- NOTHING AS A TOOL FOR THE ENTIRE MIOS AGENTIC STACKS" -- promoted
- the es.exe probe + invocation out of this script into the
- first-class mios-everything helper. Any agent can now use
- mios-everything directly; mios-find just calls it as one of its
- resolution sources.
- `|| true`: mios-everything exits NON-ZERO when es.exe is dead/unreachable
- (the common case -- v1.1 es.exe vs v1.4 IPC mismatch). Without this, the
- command substitution fails under `set -e` and ABORTS mios-find before
- fast-path B (the mios-apps inventory) can resolve the app -- so EVERY
- lookup died on hosts with a degraded Everything. Tolerate it; fall through.
- ─── Fast path B: mios-apps inventory (Linux + Windows Start Menu + games) ─
- Shared layered mios.toml resolver (vendor < host < user), path injected as argv[1].
- ── Ranker SSOT: read the scoring weights / tier ordering / fuzzy bounds from
- mios.toml [mios-find.ranker] + [mios-find.category_priority] (three-layer
- override; first file that defines a key wins). A hand-rolled weight map baked
- in code is a hardcode -- these live in config. The documented defaults below
- equal the historical in-code values, so a missing/partial config degrades
- open to the exact prior behaviour rather than to any keyword gate.
- Merged layered read (vendor < host < user, highest wins) via the shared
- resolver -- replaces the hand-rolled MIOS_TOML/etc/usr layer loop.
- Tier name -> rank index (position in the SSOT ordering). A check whose tier
- name is absent from the configured list is disabled (returns None below).
- Use run() not check_output(): mios-apps exits NON-ZERO when ANY sub-scanner
- fails (e.g. Everything es.exe dead, or the Windows side unreachable) even
- though it still emits a perfectly good Linux/flatpak inventory on stdout.
- check_output discarded that stdout on the non-zero exit -> EVERY app
- resolution failed on hosts with a degraded scanner. Consume stdout
- regardless of returncode; only give up if stdout is genuinely empty.
- Bounded Levenshtein: returns cap+1 when distance exceeds cap, so the
- caller short-circuits without computing further. Iterative DP with a
- rolling row -- O(len(a) * len(b)) time, O(min) space.
- Score = (tier-rank, category-priority, length-tiebreak); LOWER wins.
- tier-rank is the candidate's position in the SSOT match ordering
- (TIERS); _r(name) yields that index, or None when the tier is disabled
- (absent from the configured ordering) -- so a check for a disabled tier
- is skipped entirely.
- Fuzzy tier: bounded Levenshtein on individual name tokens. Catches
- operator typos like "wreakfest" -> "wreckfest", "discrod" -> "discord",
- "wallpapr engine" -> "wallpaper engine". Bounds (min token length, max
- edit distance) come from the ranker SSOT so we don't match every short
- word; short queries stay too ambiguous to fuzzy-match.
- Proportional bound: allow at most a token-length fraction of
- edits (SSOT ratio), capped by the flat max -- so a short query
- can't match a different app at the flat cap ("forza"/"forge").
- Auto-resolve ambiguity by picking the highest-priority CATEGORY
- match at the best tier. The sort already orders by
- (tier, category-priority, length), so scored[0] is always the
- "best" by our rules. Print it. If there are >1 matches, also
- emit a brief "n other candidates" note to stderr for transparency
- -- but DO NOT bounce back to the operator demanding re-query
- (operator directive 2026-05-16: "should be snappy").
