## usr/libexec/mios/mios-firecrawl
- Gate ONLY on the Firecrawl API port this CLI actually talks to. Redis
- (6379) is the firecrawl pod's INTERNAL job queue -- reachable only by the
- firecrawl-api/worker containers inside the pod netns, never from this
- host-side CLI -- so probing it here ALWAYS failed and wrongly forced the
- healthy Firecrawl primary down to web_extract_fallback after deploy.
- Check if this is an async job
- A scrape job_id polls the SCRAPE-status endpoint (v1.0.0:
- GET /v1/scrape/{job_id}), NOT the crawl-status one -- a scrape job
- is not a crawl job. v1.0.0 may also return the scraped data
- directly (no crawl-style status=="completed"), so treat a payload
- that already carries data/markdown as complete.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-flatpak
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-flatpak <subcommand> [args...]
- Phase D.4 of the AgentOS roadmap: Linux-side package management
- surface for the MiOS agent stack. Singular `mios-flatpak` is
- the agent-facing JSON-envelope wrapper -- the existing
- `flatpaks-manage.sh` (alias `mios-flatpaks`) remains the
- operator-facing pretty-print version.
- Output is structured JSON by default. Pass --plain for the raw
- flatpak stdout for interactive use.
- SUBCOMMANDS
- search <query> [-n LIMIT]    Search the configured remotes.
- Returns {results:[{Application,
- Name, Description, Origin}]}.
- list  [--filter F]           Installed flatpaks.
- show  <id>                   Detailed flatpak info.
- install <id> [--system|--user]
- Install. Default scope follows
- MIOS_FLATPAK_DEFAULT_SCOPE env
- (default "system"). High-priv
- verb; tainted sessions refused.
- upgrade [<id>]               Update one flatpak, or -- with no arg
- / "all" / --all -- all of them.
- uninstall <id>               Uninstall.
- remotes                      List configured flatpak remotes.
- run <id>                     Launch a flatpak (forks detached).
- Same path mios-launch uses; the
- explicit verb is exposed for
- agents that prefer it over the
- semantic open_app launcher.
- help                         This message.
- Hardening:
- * Install/upgrade go through `flatpak install --noninteractive
- --assumeyes` so they can't prompt + hang the broker.
- * Output truncated to MIOS_FLATPAK_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES (default
- 256 KiB).
- * Auto-sudo when EUID != 0 for system-scope writes.
- ─── output capture + truncation ──────────────────────────────────
- EXPORT so _emit_envelope's python child sees them via os.environ (shell-local
- vars are invisible to the subprocess -> the long-standing empty-stdout bug
- that made list/search/show return "" despite flatpak returning data). 2026-06-10.
- ─── scope resolver ───────────────────────────────────────────────
- Use --columns so the column order is deterministic for parsing.
- Auto-sudo for system scope when not root.
- SSOT remote resolution: mios.toml [flatpak].prefer_beta=true
- routes to flathub-beta when that remote exposes the id, else
- falls back to default_remote (flathub). Operator binding
- 2026-05-19: "target betas for all flatpaks".
- No id, the literal keyword "all" (any case), or --all all mean
- "upgrade everything" -- the helper OWNS this contract so the
- agent-pipe dispatch template stays a clean `upgrade{id?}` (P3).
- Run flatpak in foreground (the broker captures stdout/stderr).
- For GUI apps the operator typically uses open_app -> mios-launch
- which forks detached; explicit run is for CLI flatpaks the
- agent invokes synchronously.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-flatpak-beta-migrate
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-flatpak-beta-migrate [--dry-run]
- For every installed flatpak whose origin is `flathub`, check whether
- `flathub-beta` exposes the same id. When it does, reinstall from
- beta (preserves user data under ~/.var/app/<id>/, only the runtime +
- code bytes get swapped). Operator binding 2026-05-19: "target betas
- for all flatpaks" -- this is the one-shot migration; future installs
- go through mios-flatpak[-install] which already prefers beta via
- mios.toml [flatpak].prefer_beta = true SSOT.
- SAFE: bears the same data-preservation guarantee as `flatpak update`
- (per-app state under ~/.var/app/<id> is untouched). Reinstall is the
- only way to flip the origin remote -- there's no `flatpak set-remote`
- command in mainline flatpak.
- Not on flathub stable -- nothing to migrate from.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-flatpak-icon-sanitize
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-flatpak-icon-sanitize
- Rename any ".svg" icon whose CONTENT is not actually SVG (e.g. a PNG
- mis-named .svg) out of the "*.svg" glob, so the WSLg compositor cannot
- crash on it.
- Why this exists (operator-hit 2026-06-06, MiOS-DEV / WSL 2.7.7.0):
- WSLg's weston (rdprail-shell) builds a RemoteApp app-list when the RDP
- peer (msrdc) connects, loading each app's icon. For a ".svg" file it
- calls librsvg; if the bytes are not XML/SVG (a PNG under a .svg name),
- rsvg returns NULL and weston NULL-derefs -> SIGSEGV. WSLGd respawns it
- >10x then gives up ("exited more than 10 times in 60 seconds"), so the
- wayland/X11 sockets refuse ALL clients (connect -> ECONNREFUSED) and
- every GUI launch is invisible. Root cause was the com.google.ChromeDev
- flatpak shipping a PNG at com.google.ChromeDev.svg.
- Runs at boot (root), BEFORE weston needs the app-list, via
- mios-wslg-permissions-fix.service. Idempotent + best-effort.
- -name '*.svg' matches both regular files and symlinks; head -c follows
- symlinks to read the real bytes. mv on a symlink renames the symlink
- itself (leaving the flatpak's actual deployed file untouched).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-flatpak-init
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-flatpak-init
- Apply MiOS's system-wide flatpak override policy at first boot.
- Operator directive 2026-05-15: "make sure agents can install new
- flatpaks ... be sure it's bootc immutable compatible and uses
- mutable/persistent userspace folders (var/home/mios/* where
- documents, pictures, videos, downloads, etc) at this mutable
- location(s) for flatpaks".
- WHAT IT DOES
- ────────────
- Writes a system-wide override (via `flatpak override --system`) that
- grants every installed flatpak read+write access to the operator's
- XDG user directories:
- xdg-documents  ($HOME/Documents)
- xdg-download   ($HOME/Downloads)
- xdg-pictures   ($HOME/Pictures)
- xdg-videos     ($HOME/Videos)
- xdg-music      ($HOME/Music)
- xdg-desktop    ($HOME/Desktop)
- xdg-public-share  ($HOME/Public)
- Plus the existing icon/theme grants (xdg-data/icons:ro, xdg-data/
- themes:ro) so apps inherit themes from the host.
- WHY OPERATOR-VISIBLE FILES, NOT SANDBOXED PRIVATE FOLDERS
- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Default flatpak sandboxes give apps access to nothing in $HOME except
- their own ~/.var/app/<id>/ tree. That's secure but useless when the
- operator wants Save File dialogs in epiphany / chrome / gedit /
- image-viewer to land in the same Documents/Pictures/Downloads they
- use from native apps. The MiOS contract is "the operator owns their
- data; flatpaks borrow it" -- not "every app has its own data island".
- WHERE OVERRIDES PERSIST
- ───────────────────────
- /var/lib/flatpak/overrides/global. /var is mutable on bootc, so the
- overrides survive image upgrades; operators can also edit them via
- `sudo flatpak override --system <flags>` after the fact (this script
- only WRITES the MiOS-managed overrides at first boot, doesn't
- overwrite operator-customised ones -- detected by a marker comment).
- IDEMPOTENT
- ──────────
- Re-runs check the existing override file for the MiOS marker; if
- present + the policy already applied, this is a no-op. If the
- operator removed the marker, this script LEAVES the override alone.
- Marker present + already applied -> skip the override-apply block
- (the WSLg .desktop bridge below still runs -- new flatpaks installed
- after firstboot need fresh symlinks even when the override is set).
- Read appearance from layered mios.toml [appearance]. Operator edits
- in /etc/mios/mios.toml override the vendor defaults in
- /usr/share/mios/mios.toml. Falls back to hard-coded defaults if the
- parser path is missing (defensive only -- mios.toml ships with
- [appearance] populated).
- _toml_get <key> <default>
- Apply each XDG dir + the existing icons/themes grants + theme env
- ADDITIVELY. `flatpak override --system --filesystem=X` only appends
- to the [Context]filesystems= line; existing entries are preserved.
- Same for --env=X -- each is its own [Environment] line, safe to
- re-apply on every boot. This is what fixes the "Nautilus rendered in
- default light Adwaita" drift seen 2026-05-15: bake-time set the
- theme env, but firstboot was re-applying a subset that didn't
- include GTK_THEME / XCURSOR_THEME / ADW_DEBUG_COLOR_SCHEME, so the
- global override drifted off them after the first boot.
- Explicitly REJECT /usr/share/{themes,icons} -- prior versions of
- this script tried to add those (commit 8f38451) but flatpak refuses
- with "Path /usr is reserved by Flatpak" on every app launch
- (operator-confirmed regression 2026-05-16). adw-gtk3-dark + Bibata
- theme/icons are available to flatpaks via the FLATHUB RUNTIME
- EXTENSIONS (org.gtk.Gtk3theme.adw-gtk3-dark already installed) +
- the xdg-data/themes mount -- no /usr access needed. nofilesystem
- negates any earlier add of these paths.
- Stamp the marker so the next run knows this is MiOS-managed (and
- any operator edit that REMOVES the marker will be honoured as
- "operator took ownership").
- Prepend the marker as a comment block at the top.
- ── Flatpak .desktop -> WSLg Start Menu bridge ─────────────────────────
- Operator directive 2026-05-15: "FIX windows host itself not showing
- WSL applications and flatpaks apps as native windows applications
- with Icons (Natively for WSL/Windows)".
- Root cause: WSLg's .desktop scanner only looks at
- /usr/share/applications/ (well-known XDG path). Flatpak exports its
- .desktop files to /var/lib/flatpak/exports/share/applications/ which
- WSLg never sees. Net effect: ChromeDev / Nautilus.Devel / Epiphany /
- Ptyxis / Codium / gedit / ExtensionManager / Flatseal are installed
- + launchable from the operator's session, but DO NOT show as Windows
- Start Menu entries.
- Fix: symlink each flatpak .desktop into /usr/share/applications/
- with a "_flatpak.desktop" suffix to avoid collision with same-named
- host packages. The icons are auto-found by WSLg via Icon= -> the
- /var/lib/flatpak/exports/share/icons/hicolor/ tree (WSLg already
- scans the standard XDG icon paths under /var/lib + /usr/share).
- Idempotent. Newly-installed flatpaks NOT automatically picked up by
- this one-shot service -- but mios-flatpak-install (operator's
- flatpak install wrapper) re-runs this script post-install, AND
- operators can `sudo systemctl start mios-flatpak-init.service`
- manually after a flatpak install to refresh.
- Skip the URL-handler companion files (they have main-app
- counterparts already + appear as confusing extras in Start Menu).
- Skip if symlink already correct.
- If a non-symlink file exists with the same name, leave it
- alone (host package owns that .desktop name).
- Kick the WSLg desktop scanner via systemd's path-units if any
- are watching the apps dir. systemd-tmpfiles / update-desktop-
- database are no-ops on bootc if absent.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-flatpak-install
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-flatpak-install <flatpak-id> [<flatpak-id> ...]
- Agent-friendly wrapper around `sudo flatpak install --system`. Lets
- Hermes (or any operator) install new flatpaks from flathub
- non-interactively, without dragging the agent through the standard
- install prompts ("This application is not signed by ... Continue?
- [y/n]").
- Operator directive 2026-05-15: "make sure agents can install new
- flatpaks ... and ALL works".
- WHY A WRAPPER (vs. just telling the agent "run sudo flatpak install ...")
- ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Three sharp edges the wrapper hides:
- 1. `flatpak install` is INTERACTIVE by default. Without --noninteractive,
- it stalls on the "OK to install? [Y/n]" prompt forever -- the agent
- sees a hung tool call.
- 2. `flatpak install <id>` ambiguously matches multiple remotes when the
- same id exists on flathub + flathub-beta + gnome-nightly; it prompts
- "Which one? [1-3]" -- another silent hang. Force the remote with
- `--from <remote>` (default: flathub).
- 3. After a fresh install, the new app inherits MiOS's system-wide
- override policy (XDG dirs etc.) automatically -- but the
- MiOS-managed override file at /var/lib/flatpak/overrides/global
- MUST exist first; if it doesn't (atypical install where mios-
- flatpak-init didn't run), this wrapper kicks it off so the new
- app comes up with the right grants from the very first launch.
- USAGE
- mios-flatpak-install org.gnome.gedit
- mios-flatpak-install org.gnome.Calendar org.gnome.Calculator
- MIOS_FLATPAK_REMOTE=flathub-beta mios-flatpak-install com.example.App
- Remote resolution priority (operator-binding 2026-05-19 "target
- betas for all flatpaks"):
- 1. Explicit MIOS_FLATPAK_REMOTE env override (per-call)
- 2. mios.toml [flatpak].prefer_beta = true: pick PER-APP -- if
- flathub-beta exposes the id, use beta; else fall back to the
- default_remote (stable flathub)
- 3. mios.toml [flatpak].default_remote
- 4. Hardcoded fallback: flathub
- Shared layered mios.toml resolver (vendor < host < user) via the mios-toml-get CLI.
- Probe whether flathub-beta has this id
- Legacy single REMOTE var retained for the log line; the actual
- install loop below resolves PER-ID via _resolve_remote_for.
- Make sure the override policy is in place before we install -- a
- new flatpak picks up overrides at first launch, so applying them
- AFTER the install would still work, but doing it first is cleaner
- (and prevents a transient "first launch with no XDG access" window
- when the operator clicks the new app immediately).
- Resolve to sudo if we're not already root.
- Default runtime branch used to disambiguate multi-branch refs (e.g. the
- Vulkan-layer extensions like MangoHud publish several //<branch>s). Under
- --noninteractive, `flatpak install <bare-id>` errors "Multiple refs match
- ... must specify one" instead of prompting -- so on that specific failure
- we retry once with //<branch> appended. Operator-overridable per call.
- Ambiguous-branch fallback: retry once with a default //<branch> appended
- (only if the id doesn't already carry one).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-flatpak-overrides-apply
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-flatpak-overrides-apply
- Apply the MiOS-managed global flatpak override (theming + portal +
- theme filesystem mounts) so every installed flatpak respects the
- operator's color-scheme + theme + cursor choices via xdg-portal-desktop.
- Idempotent: safe to run on every boot. Drops nothing operator-set
- (uses --reset to clear OUR override only and re-apply our keys).
- Why a script vs a tracked /var/lib/flatpak/overrides/global file:
- * `flatpak override` is the supported API; writing the file directly
- bypasses validation and is brittle across flatpak versions.
- * Operators expect to be able to add their own overrides via
- `flatpak override --system <appid> --env=...` -- those land in
- <appid> files, not in `global`, so we only own `global`.
- * The override survives flatpak upgrades AND OS upgrades cleanly.
- Called by mios-hermes-firstboot at first boot, and re-runnable by the
- operator (or agent) whenever they want to reset to MiOS defaults.
- Read appearance keys from layered mios.toml [appearance] (operator's
- /etc/mios overrides /usr/share/mios). This SSOT is the same one
- mios-flatpak-init reads; sourcing here ensures the firstboot --reset
- doesn't drop theme env that operators expect to be applied globally.
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: "should be the GLOBAL overrides so
- that newly installed apps/flatpaks take hold of the configurations
- as well".
- WSLg-stable render path (operator-flagged 2026-05-19: "ALL Windowed
- Linux applications have outdated and broken Windowing GLOBALLY").
- Without these, every flatpak GTK4 app misrenders because WSLg's
- compositor + dxgkrnl GPU passthrough don't honour modern GTK4 /
- libadwaita / Vulkan paths correctly.
- WSLg-aware override (operator trace 2026-05-30: every Linux flatpak
- "nothing launched"). WSLg's compositor exposes NO DRI3 GPU device, so
- GTK4's hardware GL renderers (ngl/gl/vulkan) fail to create a GL
- context -- "libEGL DRI3 error: Could not get DRI3 device" -- and the
- app DIES before mapping a window. The [graphics] SSOT is tuned for
- bare-metal GPUs (gsk_renderer="ngl"), which is correct THERE but fatal
- on WSLg. So: when running under WSLg, force the software render path
- regardless of the SSOT; on bare-metal (real DRM /dev/dri + DRI3) the
- SSOT hardware path is honoured untouched. This is detection logic, not
- a hardcoded per-deployment value -- the same vendor default works on
- both WSLg dev VMs and bare-metal MiOS deployments.
- --reset clears the global override file completely; then we re-create
- the MiOS-managed keys. This is safer than --unset of individual keys
- (which can fail silently if the key doesn't exist).
- Theme / icon / cursor reach into the sandbox.
- CORRECTION 2026-05-19 (operator trace): flatpak FLATLY REFUSES to
- bind-mount any host path under /usr ("F: Not sharing /usr/share/...:
- Path /usr is reserved by Flatpak"). The previous
- --filesystem=/usr/share/{themes,icons,fonts}:ro lines were DROPPED
- ENTIRELY at runtime -- NOT "a cosmetic warning" -- so flatpaks got
- ZERO host theme/icon/cursor access. Removed them. Correct reach is:
- * GTK3 theme      -> org.gtk.Gtk3theme.adw-gtk3-dark flatpak
- EXTENSION (installed from flathub; no /usr mount).
- * GTK4/libadwaita -> Adwaita built into org.gnome.Platform + portal
- color-scheme (GTK_USE_PORTAL=1 + ADW_DEBUG_*).
- * Cursor (Bibata) -> installed into ~/.local/share/icons (writable;
- /usr is RO on bootc) and reached via the
- xdg-data/icons:ro mount below + XCURSOR_PATH.
- Seeded by mios-cursor-ensure / firstboot.
- * Fonts           -> flatpak auto-shares host fonts (no mount needed).
- /dev/dxg was ALSO rejected ("unsupported type 0o20000") and is moot:
- we force software GL (LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE) + cairo + no Vulkan, so
- no flatpak needs the WSLg GPU paravirt device. Kept --device=all +
- /dev/dri (allowed) for the rare app that probes dri.
- Render-path env -- conditional includes so empty strings don't
- splat to "--env=FOO=" (which would clear the var). Booleans from
- TOML come through Python repr (True/False); normalise to "1"/"0".
- GTK_THEME is DELIBERATELY NOT set. It is a GTK3 theme name;
- setting it on a GTK4/libadwaita app (Nautilus, Epiphany, GNOME
- Settings) forces the OLD GTK3 adw-gtk3 chrome instead of native
- libadwaita -- operator trace 2026-05-19 "old windowing in
- Nautilus still". Mirrors /usr/lib/environment.d/50-mios.conf,
- which omits GTK_THEME for the same documented reason. GTK3-only
- flatpaks still get adw-gtk3-dark via the Gtk3theme extension +
- the mounted xdg-config/gtk-3.0 settings.ini; libadwaita apps get
- dark via ADW_DEBUG_COLOR_SCHEME below.
- --socket=x11 is REQUIRED with GDK_BACKEND=x11: WSLg provides Xwayland
- on DISPLAY=:0, but a flatpak only sees the X socket if it is shared
- in. Without it, x11-backend apps die with "Failed to open display"
- (operator trace 2026-05-19, Epiphany). Harmless on bare-metal Wayland
- -- apps still prefer wayland unless GDK_BACKEND forces x11.
- ─── Per-app overrides from mios.toml [flatpak.app_overrides] ────────
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: "EVERYTHING IS DICTATED AND
- UNDERSTOOD FROM THE mios.toml/html file(s)". Per-app env overrides
- (Epiphany GPU compositing, Chrome CDP port, etc.) live in mios.toml
- as nested tables under [flatpak.app_overrides."<app-id>"]. Iterate
- the table and emit one /var/lib/flatpak/overrides/<id> file per
- entry. Idempotent: each rewrite is full, no merge.
- Layered read: later file wins per key. /etc/mios overrides /usr/share/mios.
- Two SoT shapes are supported:
- 1. [flatpak.app_overrides."<id>"] = { KEY = VALUE, ... }   (legacy flat)
- 2. [[desktop.apps]] entry with overrides = { KEY = VALUE } (unified)
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: "toml/html packages sections are BOTH
- the installation references for MiOS builds and deployments globally
- -- AS WELL as AI agents references for defaults". The [[desktop.apps]]
- array is the unified SoT going forward; the flat [flatpak.app_overrides]
- table is kept for entries without app metadata.
- Shape 2: [[desktop.apps]] entries (preferred). Read FIRST so
- operator-overlay entries can shadow vendor app_overrides.
- Shape 1: [flatpak.app_overrides.*] (legacy / non-desktop apps).
- TOML bools/ints render as Python; flatpak override files
- are plain text so str() everything.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-flatpak-preflight
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-flatpak-preflight <app-id>
- Cheap probe to determine whether a flatpak app will successfully
- bootstrap its sandbox in the current runtime context BEFORE the
- operator-visible launch attempt. Runs `flatpak run --command=true
- <app-id>` (which boots the sandbox + execs `true` + exits) and
- captures stderr signatures known to indicate environmental
- breakage:
- * "/dev/dxg" + "unsupported type"  -> WSL GPU passthrough
- vs bubblewrap mismatch
- * "--env-fd: Not an open file descriptor"
- -> flatpak portal-helper
- got FDs not in this
- process namespace
- * "Connection: failed to receive credentials"
- -> session-bus SCM_CREDENTIALS
- handshake failed (broken
- user@<uid>.service /
- dbus-broker)
- * "Permission denied: '/'"          -> bwrap can't pivot_root
- (rare; usually fs.protected_*
- sysctls in WSL2)
- Output: JSON envelope on stdout, exit 0 on sandbox-ok, exit 1
- on sandbox-broken. Operators / agents call this BEFORE any
- flatpak open_app / open_url so they fail fast with a clear
- error instead of looping on a doomed launch.
- Operator directive 2026-05-18: agent shouldn't loop on
- failures; pre-flight gives the agent a synchronous yes/no
- answer before committing to the launch.
- Hard cap so a hung sandbox bootstrap can't block the agent.
- First probe. If it fails AND the failure pattern is one the heal
- verb knows how to fix (portal_helper_env_fd / user_bus_credentials
- / unknown_sandbox_error), invoke mios-wsl-flatpak-heal once and
- retry. Generic across any flatpak id -- no app-name knowledge in
- this script.
- Run heal as the operator user (the timer's natural
- context); falls back to a direct invocation if su
- isn't viable.
- Classify the failure when rc != 0. Operator-binding: structural
- tokens, NOT English narration. The agent reads `error_kind` to
- decide what to do (surface to operator with a remediation
- hint, switch to a non-flatpak target, etc.).
- Specialise: "runtime ... not installed" is a runtime-
- missing failure (the app is installed but its sandbox
- runtime isn't); plain "<app> not installed" is the
- app itself missing.
- Re-read stderr inside python so the JSON encoding is clean.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-forgejo-runner-firstboot.sh
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-forgejo-runner-firstboot.sh
- Run `forgejo-runner register` once so /srv/mios/forge-runner/.runner
- exists before mios-forgejo-runner.service starts the daemon. v7+ no
- longer auto-registers from FORGEJO_RUNNER_REGISTRATION_TOKEN env --
- the daemon subcommand strictly requires .runner on disk.
- Idempotent: if .runner already present, exit 0 immediately.
- shellcheck source=/dev/null
- The register call must reach the Forgejo instance, and crucially the
- .runner file it writes records the instance URL the *daemon* will
- later connect to. Both have to agree on a network:
- * bridge shapes (real OCI builds): forge is on mios.network, the
- daemon Quadlet is on mios.network, and FORGEJO_INSTANCE_URL is
- http://mios-forge:<port>/ -- so register must ALSO join that
- bridge or the `mios-forge` container-DNS name won't resolve.
- * WSL / dev-VM testbed: build-mios.ps1 drops forge AND the runner
- daemon to Network=host; FORGEJO_INSTANCE_URL is http://localhost:
- <port>/ -- so register runs --network host.
- forge is up by now (After=mios-forge.service), so inspect its live
- network and mirror it. This keeps register, the .runner URL, and the
- daemon all on one consistent network without hard-coding the shape.
- --user 0:0 so the in-container forgejo-runner can write
- /data/.runner. The host /srv/mios/forge-runner is root-owned
- (Law-6 exception alongside ceph + k3s), and the daemon Quadlet
- also runs User=0, so root-owned .runner is the consistent
- ownership across register + daemon. Without --user 0:0 the
- image's default uid 1000 hits "permission denied" on the
- .runner write.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-freeipa-enroll.sh
- 'MiOS' FreeIPA Zero-Touch Enrollment.
- Run by mios-freeipa-enroll.service (gated by:
- ConditionPathExists=/etc/mios/ipa-enroll.env       <- operator opt-in
- ConditionPathExists=!/etc/ipa/default.conf         <- not already enrolled
- ).
- Reads enrollment parameters from /etc/mios/ipa-enroll.env (sourced as
- shell). Required:
- MIOS_IPA_REALM        e.g. EXAMPLE.COM
- MIOS_IPA_DOMAIN       e.g. example.com
- MIOS_IPA_SERVER       e.g. ipa.example.com
- MIOS_IPA_PRINCIPAL    enrollment principal (e.g. admin)
- MIOS_IPA_PASSWORD     enrollment password (read at exec time only)
- Optional:
- MIOS_IPA_HOSTNAME     (defaults to current hostname)
- MIOS_IPA_NTP          (defaults to true)
- MIOS_IPA_AUTOMOUNT    (defaults to false)
- Service unit hardens UMask=0077 so the env file isn't world-readable
- during sourcing.
- shellcheck source=/usr/lib/mios/paths.sh
- shellcheck disable=SC1090

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-gpu-passthrough
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-gpu-passthrough
- Reconcile the AddDevice= drop-ins for every "background AI"
- Quadlet against the live CDI specs in /run/cdi/. Runs as the
- ExecStartPost of mios-cdi-detect.service so the moment iGPU
- specs land, AI containers get the right `--device` wiring on
- their next start.
- Operator directive 2026-05-17: "ALL background agents work on
- iGPUs detected in the environment!! Setup AMD iGPU and Intel
- iGPU capabilities in to ALL MiOS Deployment types!! Should be
- OCI GPU-PV for ALL Background AI Agents from the host".
- Vendor coverage:
- NVIDIA  -- /run/cdi/nvidia.yaml | nvidia-wsl.yaml | wsl2-nvidia.yaml
- -> AddDevice=nvidia.com/gpu=all
- AMD     -- /run/cdi/amd.json    (amd-ctk generated)
- -> AddDevice=amd.com/gpu=all
- Intel   -- /run/cdi/intel.yaml  (intel-cdi-specs-generator)
- -> AddDevice=intel.com/gpu=all
- AI Quadlet list (extend by editing MIOS_AI_QUADLETS below or
- overriding via /etc/mios/gpu-passthrough.conf):
- Operator directive 2026-05-17 (two-step clarification):
- first: "iGPU's are ONLY micro-llms"
- then:  "JUST ONLY USES Micro-llms in MiOS stack"
- Resolution: MiOS-stack consumers of the light lane only ask for
- small models (mios-daemon -> qwen3:0.6b-cpu,
- pipe refine/polish -> qwen2.5-coder:7b, prefilter -> small).
- The big-model tags on disk (qwen3-coder:30b, gpt-oss:20b) are
- parked for ad-hoc operator use; the backend's auto-scheduling lands
- the small MiOS-stack models on whichever device has room. With
- NVIDIA dGPU + AMD iGPU both registered as CDI devices, the backend
- spreads load across them; small models fit on the iGPU's WSL
- DXG path (no VRAM contention with the dGPU), bigger ad-hoc
- loads keep the dGPU free.
- Add a new Quadlet -> one line in the list; helper writes the
- correct drop-in on next boot. Per operator directive
- 2026-05-17: "make sure ALL is in code and can deploy Day-0 from
- clone on any machine" -- everything below ships in the image;
- fresh clone + bootc upgrade reproduces the wiring.
- Idempotent + non-destructive: if /run/cdi has no AMD or Intel
- spec, the corresponding drop-in is REMOVED so a stale spec from a
- prior host configuration doesn't break the container. The base
- Quadlet (with hardcoded NVIDIA AddDevice) keeps working unchanged
- on hosts without iGPUs.
- Exit codes:
- 0 = drop-ins reconciled (any change triggered systemctl
- daemon-reload + optional Quadlet service restart)
- 1 = systemd reload failed
- 2 = drop-in directory not writable
- Default list of background-AI Quadlets that should consume iGPU
- CDI specs when available. Each entry MUST correspond to a base
- Quadlet at /etc/containers/systemd/<name>.container OR
- /usr/share/containers/systemd/<name>.container.
- Install-robustness 2026-06-21: the FRONT-DOOR brain lanes + workers also
- hardcode AddDevice=nvidia.com/gpu=all, so on a non-NVIDIA host (AMD/Intel/
- CPU-only) podman hard-FAILS to start them ("CDI device nvidia.com/gpu=all
- not found") and the AI plane's primary lane dies. Reconcile them here too so
- the device line is authoritative-per-detected-hardware, not baked NVIDIA.
- Operator override: drop a one-liner here:
- MIOS_AI_QUADLETS=(mios-llm-light mios-open-webui mios-mycustom)
- or comment out an entry to skip wiring.
- shellcheck source=/dev/null
- --- 1. Detect which vendor specs are live ---------------------
- Match every spec layout mios-cdi-detect can emit:
- * <vendor>.yaml / .json  -- bare-metal vendor toolkit output
- * wsl2-<vendor>.yaml      -- WSL2 hand-rolled (/dev/dxg + WSL libs)
- * nvidia-wsl.yaml         -- legacy nvidia-ctk WSL output naming
- Snapshot for `mios-doctor` / `mios-system-status` downstream readers.
- --- 2. Build the AddDevice block content ----------------------
- /etc/containers/systemd/${quadlet}.container.d/${DROPIN_NAME}
- MiOS-managed iGPU CDI device wiring. Generated by
- mios-gpu-passthrough (called from mios-cdi-detect.service
- ExecStartPost). Do not edit by hand -- changes here are
- overwritten on every CDI re-detect. To OPT OUT for this
- Quadlet, remove the entry from MIOS_AI_QUADLETS in
- /etc/mios/gpu-passthrough.conf.
- CDI device names follow CNCF CDI convention vendor.com/class=id.
- Missing-spec lines are NOT emitted so podman doesn't fail to
- resolve them at container start.
- Install-robustness 2026-06-21: RESET the inherited AddDevice list first.
- The base Quadlets hardcode AddDevice=nvidia.com/gpu=all; a drop-in can only
- APPEND, so without this empty reset a non-NVIDIA host would STILL request the
- absent nvidia device and podman would hard-fail container start. The empty
- assignment clears the merged list (systemd list-reset semantics), then we
- re-add ONLY the device whose CDI spec is actually present -> the drop-in is the
- authoritative, hardware-adaptive source. No vendor present (CPU-only) -> the
- reset alone -> the container starts with NO GPU device (CPU mode) instead of
- dying on a missing nvidia spec. (Worst case if Quadlet ignores the reset: an
- NVIDIA host gets a benign duplicate nvidia line -- never a regression.)
- --- 3. Reconcile drop-ins for each AI Quadlet -----------------
- Install-robustness 2026-06-21: ALWAYS write the drop-in now -- it is the
- AUTHORITATIVE, hardware-adaptive device source (reset + the detected vendor,
- or just the reset on CPU-only). The old "delete when no iGPU" path left the
- base quadlet's hardcoded nvidia AddDevice in force, which hard-failed every
- non-NVIDIA host. (The base quadlet's static line stays as a no-CDI fallback
- but is overridden by this drop-in whenever the reconciler has run.)
- --- 4. systemd reload + optional restart ----------------------

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-gui
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-gui <app> [args...]
- Generic GUI launcher for ANY installed flatpak. Resolves <app> in this
- order:
- 1. Existing /usr/local/bin/<app> shim (chrome, nautilus, epiphany,
- codium, ptyxis, flatseal, extension-manager today; user-extensible).
- Shims exist when an app needs special flags (dark-mode, --remote-
- debugging-port, etc.) -- they layer on top of flatpak-launch.
- 2. Exact flatpak app ID match (e.g. mios-gui org.gnome.Calendar).
- 3. Fuzzy match against the LAST segment of every installed flatpak's
- app id, case-insensitive (e.g. mios-gui calendar -> org.gnome.Calendar
- auto-resolves; mios-gui chromedev -> com.google.ChromeDev). Any
- flatpak the operator installs later via `flatpak install` becomes
- reachable through mios-gui without code changes.
- 4. No match -> print the catalogue of installed flatpaks + exit 1.
- After spawning, mios-gui BOUNDED-POLLS the OS-control executor's read-only
- GET /windows for a NEW top-level window hwnd to appear (the same surface
- mios-autocenter / mios-window list read). It only prints an "Opened" success
- line if a window is CONFIRMED to have surfaced; otherwise it prints an honest
- "window NOT confirmed" line and exits 3 (unverified). This kills the
- false-positive where a detached spawn returned 0 but no window ever painted --
- common over a separate RDP session, where WSLg flatpak windows frequently do
- NOT surface (WSLg-over-RDP / VAIL session-scoping, a documented MiOS limit).
- A WSL-side process-alive check is only a weak supporting signal (a live
- process over RDP is NOT proof a window painted), never the success criterion.
- Degrade-open: no reachable executor / probe error -> honest "unconfirmed",
- never a hard crash and never a false success.
- ─── OS-control executor endpoint resolution (read-only window enumeration) ──
- Same resolver shape as mios-pc-control / mios-window / mios-autocenter:
- 1. MIOS_OSCONTROL_EXECUTOR env
- 2. [os_control].executor_endpoint in the layered mios.toml (/etc wins)
- 3. WSL2 NAT-gateway auto-discovery on :11437 (MIOS_OSCONTROL_PORT)
- The executor (mios-oscontrol-server.ps1) runs on the Windows desktop's
- WinSta0\Default, so its GET /windows is the ONLY surface that actually sees
- whether a window mapped on the operator's screen -- a WSL-side pgrep only
- proves a PROCESS is alive, which over a separate RDP session is NOT proof a
- window painted (WSLg-over-RDP VAIL session-scoping; documented MiOS limit).
- Returns "" when nothing is resolvable (degrade-open: caller treats the launch
- as UNCONFIRMED, never as a false success).
- Only return an endpoint that is actually UP (quick /health probe) so an
- unreachable/stale endpoint degrades to "" (-> unconfirmed) instead of
- making every confirm poll time out.
- Snapshot the CSV of currently-visible window hwnds from the executor.
- Read-only (GET /windows -- the same surface mios-autocenter / mios-window
- list already read). Prints "" on any error (degrade-open).
- Poll the executor for a window hwnd that was NOT present before the launch
- (i.e. a freshly-mapped window) within a bounded time. Prints "1" to stdout
- iff a new window surfaced; "" otherwise. Read-only; degrade-open (any error
- -> "", treated as unconfirmed). Bound is MIOS_LAUNCH_CONFIRM_SECS (default 12,
- covering the wsl.exe-session portal-bootstrap window in flatpak-launch).
- Shims first (they have flag-augmented launches)
- All other system flatpaks
- ─── Step 1: existing shim ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── Step 2: exact flatpak app id match ───────────────────────────────────
- ─── Step 3: fuzzy match on last app-id segment ───────────────────────────
- last . segment, lowercased
- ─── Step 4: host-RPM GUI fallback (gnome-software, gnome-system-monitor,
- gnome-disks, baobab, gnome-control-center, gnome-tweaks, ...) ──
- When no flatpak matches, look for a host-installed binary AND a
- corresponding .desktop file in /usr/share/applications/. The .desktop
- presence is the canonical "this is a GUI app" signal -- distinguishes
- `gnome-software` (GUI -> safe to launch via mios-host-launch) from
- things like `bash` (CLI -> would freeze). Operator directive
- 2026-05-15: agents kept hallucinating "headless environment" when
- they should have just been launching the host RPM through the same
- operator-session escape flatpak-launch uses.
- If a .desktop file exists directly matching the requested app name,
- extract the executable binary name from it.
- Fallback: check if the app name itself is a binary on PATH and has a matching desktop file.
- find any matching .desktop (case-insensitive on the Exec= line
- OR a bare $APP.desktop)
- ─── Snapshot windows BEFORE the launch (read-only) ─────────────────────────
- The honesty fix (operator 2026-06-14: `@ open epiphany` printed "Opened
- epiphany." but NO WINDOW appeared). The launchers DETACH and have, until now,
- claimed success ("fired"/"dispatched") purely because the spawn call returned
- 0 -- they never CONFIRMED a window actually surfaced. Over a separate RDP
- session WSLg flatpak windows frequently do NOT paint (WSLg-over-RDP / VAIL
- session-scoping, a documented MiOS limitation). So: capture the visible-window
- hwnd set NOW, fire the launch, then poll for a NEW hwnd to appear. Only claim
- success if a window is confirmed; otherwise say so honestly + exit non-zero so
- the caller (and the agent-pipe window-diff) never report a false success.
- Spawn (fires and forgets via flatpak-launch + systemd-run / wsl.exe session)
- ─── Confirm a window actually surfaced (bounded poll) ──────────────────────
- AUTHORITATIVE signal: a NEW top-level window hwnd appears on the operator's
- desktop (the executor's GET /windows sees WinSta0\Default). A WSL-side pgrep
- only proves a PROCESS is alive -- which, over RDP, is NOT proof a window
- painted -- so it is kept only as a weak supporting signal in the unconfirmed
- message, never as the success criterion.
- A new window mapped within the window -> genuine, visible success.
- ─── Unconfirmed: be HONEST, never claim "Opened" ───────────────────────────
- Either no executor was reachable to confirm (degrade-open) or no new window
- surfaced within the bound. Surface a weak process-alive signal for context,
- but the verdict is UNVERIFIED and the exit code is non-zero so the agent does
- NOT report success and instead tells the operator the truth (likely RDP/WSLg
- paint limitation -> check the desktop or use the browser frontend).
- Flatpak processes appear as `bwrap ... -- <binary> ...` where
- <binary> is the lowercased app shortname (epiphany for
- org.gnome.Epiphany); the uppercase app-id never appears in argv.
- Signal UNVERIFIED so the caller / agent-pipe window-diff does not report a
- false "Opened". Non-zero but distinct from a hard launch failure (rc>=1
- above): use 3 = "dispatched, window unconfirmed".

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-gui-launch
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-gui-launch <linux-gui-app> [args...]
- Operator directive 2026-05-17: agent failed to launch
- gnome-control-center because (a) it claimed "no display server"
- (false -- WSLg is up) and (b) gnome-control-center specifically
- refuses to start without XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=GNOME ("Running
- gnome-control-center is only supported under GNOME and Unity,
- exiting"). One canonical shim that handles every Linux GUI app
- launch under WSLg:
- * Ensures WAYLAND_DISPLAY + DISPLAY are set (inherited from
- WSLg if available; sensible default of wayland-0 / :0).
- * Sets XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=GNOME so gnome-* tools cooperate.
- * Sets XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland so wayland-aware apps prefer
- the native protocol over Xwayland fallback.
- * nohup + & + disown so the GUI app survives the agent's shell
- exit and doesn't block the broker call.
- * Routes stderr to a per-app log under /var/log/mios/gui/ for
- post-mortem if the window never appears.
- * Exits 0 immediately on dispatch; the GUI may take 1-3s to
- paint. Verify with `mios-window-active --present "<title>"`.
- Examples:
- mios-gui-launch gnome-control-center
- mios-gui-launch nautilus /home
- mios-gui-launch gedit
- mios-gui-launch flatpak run com.google.ChromeDev https://example.com
- Use this for ANY /usr/bin/<gui-app> launch from the agent. For
- Windows-side apps use mios-find / launch_app.
- ── Flatpak app-id / .desktop-id auto-dispatch ────────────────────────
- When called with a reverse-DNS-shaped name (com.foo.Bar /
- mobi.phosh.MobileSettings / org.gnome.Calls / etc.), the caller meant
- either a FLATPAK or a .desktop-id-installed RPM, not a bare PATH
- binary. Try BOTH before falling through to the "not found on PATH"
- error. Operator-flagged 2026-05-19: agent tried
- `mios-gui-launch mobi.phosh.MobileSettings` -> "not found on PATH",
- retried 4x, hit same_tool_failure_halt. Detection is purely
- structural: 2+ dots, alpha-leading segments.
- 1. Flatpak first (operator binding: Linux native first;
- flatpaks are the user-app surface).
- 2. .desktop file: look up /usr/share/applications/<id>.desktop
- + ~/.local/share/applications/<id>.desktop, extract Exec=,
- strip Desktop-Entry placeholders (%F %U %i %c %k), and exec.
- Exec= is a shell-tokenisable command line. Re-exec
- this same script with the FIRST token (binary) +
- the rest preserved + caller's args appended.
- shellcheck disable=SC2086
- Resolve the binary (allow absolute or PATH).
- Per-app log (no path traversal -- use basename only).
- WSLg env: prefer existing values (the user's session may have set
- specific values); fall back to known WSLg defaults.
- gnome-control-center + most Gtk-Adwaita apps gate on these.
- Some apps (Files / gedit / VSCode flatpak) read GTK theme from this.
- Dispatch -- detached, stdout+stderr to per-app log.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-handoff
- 1) Read the shared inter-agent context.
- 2) Frame the take-over message.
- 3) Dispatch through the existing A2A surface (carries contextId so
- the peer's scratchpad joins this thread).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-hardcode-lint
- Repo-relative path fragments that are exempt (data/snapshots/vendored docs where a
- date in text is legitimate content, not a code comment). Kept minimal + named.
- Exempt a value date: at the head of the literal, or quote-/joiner-led
- (slug/URL/version). Flag only a whitespace-led date -- prose/attribution.
- PS1 irm|iex parse needs the BOM (when present) at byte 0; a BOM in the head
- bytes but not at offset 0 is the Get-MiOS.ps1 stranding bug. Restrict to .ps1
- so a U+FEFF in a .py/.sh string is never misread as a file-BOM.
- A shebang, IF the file declares one, must be line 1. A sourced script with no
- shebang is fine (header comment first is correct for it).
- Check ports
- Check IPs
- Vendor-only, ROOT-RELATIVE read: this offline drift-gate scans a
- SOURCE tree (roots), so it must parse THIS root's vendor mios.toml,
- not the deployed /usr path -- a single explicit layer is the
- vendor-only view. (load_vendor() would read the fixed system path.)

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-hermes-browser
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-hermes-browser
- Launch the locally-installed ChromeDev flatpak (com.google.ChromeDev)
- with the Chrome DevTools Protocol port open on 127.0.0.1:9222 so
- Hermes-Agent's browser tool can attach to it (browser.cdp_url in
- /var/lib/mios/hermes/config.yaml is http://localhost:9222).
- Operator directive 2026-05-15: "should be using the locally installed
- ChromeDev flatpak install" -- NOT agent-browser's bundled Chromium
- download, NOT a separate Chromium RPM. Use the flatpak that's already
- on disk for `mios-gui chromedev`.
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: "can we have Hermes-Chrome open a
- non-headless window for browser control??" -- yes. Default flipped
- from HEADLESS=1 to HEADLESS=0 so the operator SEES the agent's
- browser activity (navigations, clicks, screenshots). Headless mode
- is still available for cron / scripted use by setting
- HERMES_BROWSER_HEADLESS=1 in the calling environment.
- Operator directive 2026-05-17: "fix CDP control". Browser_navigate
- from inside Hermes was hitting "All CDP discovery methods failed"
- because nothing was listening on :9222 and the agent had no way to
- bring it up. This script now supports an idempotent subcommand
- surface so the agent can ensure the port is up before any
- browser_* call:
- mios-hermes-browser ensure    # idempotent: noop if up, else launch in bg
- mios-hermes-browser status    # exit 0 if CDP responding, 1 otherwise
- mios-hermes-browser stop      # kill the ChromeDev process tree
- mios-hermes-browser start     # explicit foreground launch (the legacy path)
- mios-hermes-browser           # default = ensure (safest for the agent)
- `ensure` waits up to 8s for CDP to respond; SOUL.md tells the agent
- to call it before any browser_navigate / browser_screenshot / etc.
- Profile data lives under /var/lib/mios/hermes-browser/profile so the
- Hermes session is fully isolated from the operator's interactive
- Chrome session (separate cookies, separate signed-in accounts,
- separate extensions).
- Headless mode: AUTO-DETECT the display. Operator 2026-05-16 wanted a
- VISIBLE window to watch the agent browse on a desktop -- keep that when a
- display is actually reachable. But on a headless / WSL / remote host with
- no display (operator 2026-05-22: the visible default crash-looped 500+
- times -- "CDP did not come up", Chrome can't open a window without a
- display), fall back to headless so the CDP backend still comes up and the
- browse tool stays IN THE LOOP. Force either way with HERMES_BROWSER_HEADLESS.
- --- helpers -------------------------------------------------------
- Hit the CDP discovery endpoint with a short timeout. 200 = up.
- ChromeDev flatpak processes that bound 9222; scoped to our profile
- so we don't clobber the operator's interactive Chrome.
- --- subcommand dispatch -------------------------------------------
- Self-launch via `start` subcommand, backgrounded + detached.
- Legacy foreground launch path -- exec'd by `ensure` and also
- callable directly when operator wants to see the launch
- output live.
- --- foreground launch (start subcommand) --------------------------
- Strict mode for the actual launch. The dispatch above used -uo
- pipefail (no -e) so subcommand checks could fail gracefully.
- CDP needs to bind on a writable socket; flatpak sandbox redirects
- /tmp into a private mount, but 127.0.0.1:$CDP_PORT works because
- we don't enable --share=network=disabled.
- --filesystem=$PROFILE_DIR grants the flatpak sandbox write access to
- the dedicated profile path (it's outside the standard XDG locations
- the flatpak normally has). --filesystem=$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR keeps
- wayland/dbus sockets reachable for the headed-mode case.
- dbus-run-session: flatpak's portal helper insists on a session
- D-Bus bus even for headless invocations -- without one, the
- launcher dies with "Cannot autolaunch D-Bus without X11 $DISPLAY"
- before Chrome ever starts. dbus-run-session spins up a private
- transient bus for the duration of the flatpak run, which is enough
- to satisfy the portal init without needing a real desktop session.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-hermes-dashboard-auth-stub
- mios-hermes-dashboard-auth-stub
- Hermes-Agent - (build 2026.5.28) ships web_server.py with
- `from hermes_cli.dashboard_auth.routes import router`
- but the wheel does NOT include the dashboard_auth package. Result:
- hermes-dashboard.service crash-loops with ModuleNotFoundError.
- This shim plants a MINIMAL stub package so the import resolves:
- an empty APIRouter has zero Nous Portal OAuth routes to register --
- exactly the same effect as "auth disabled" but lets the dashboard
- SPA boot. MiOS does not use Nous Portal so an empty router is the
- right local-first answer; if upstream republishes 0.15.x with the
- real package included, the install will overwrite this stub and
- the shim becomes a no-op (idempotent: we only write files that
- don't already exist).
- Wired as ExecStartPre on hermes-agent.service so every restart
- (including post-pip-upgrade restarts) re-asserts the stub.
- Exit codes:
- 0 = stub already present / freshly applied / dashboard not vulnerable
- 2 = venv not found (hermes not installed; treat as no-op)
- If a routes.py already exists (real upstream fix OR this stub), nothing to do.
- Only stub when the broken import is actually present in the installed
- web_server.py -- if upstream removes the line in a future release we
- don't need (or want) a vestigial stub on disk.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-hermes-discord-reactions-patch
- New on_processing_start / on_processing_complete that replace the
- upstream single-emoji surface. _react_progression is the background
- task that adds emojis on a timer. _processing_tasks is a per-instance
- dict keyed by Discord message.id so concurrent runs don't stomp.
- Replaces the upstream on_processing_start / _complete pair so the
- operator sees a sequence of emojis on their message that reflect
- the agent's current phase (received -> thinking -> tools -> done).
- Operator directive 2026-05-18 "add more reactions ... to show it's
- thinking". Background task drives the progression so the gateway's
- main flow isn't blocked.
- Keyed per-message so concurrent in-flight runs don't stomp.
- Cancel progression task if still running.
- on_processing_complete must follow within ~50 lines for the
- adjacent-block assumption to hold.
- End of on_processing_complete: the next line at the SAME
- 4-space class-method indent (either `    async def ` or
- `    def `).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-hermes-firstboot
- MiOS -- mios-hermes-firstboot: generate /etc/mios/hermes/api.env if missing
- AND seed /var/lib/mios/hermes/config.yaml with the model selected in
- mios.toml [ai] + [ai.host_thresholds] auto-pick.
- The same key is read by both mios-hermes (gateway) and
- mios-open-webui (chat front-end) via EnvironmentFile= in their
- Quadlets. Idempotent: re-runs are no-ops once API_SERVER_KEY exists
- and the seeded config.yaml's MiOS-seeded sentinel + model match the
- resolved mios.toml [ai].model.
- Defined here (not just inside the seeded config.yaml) so unquoted
- heredocs that reference ${HERMES_HOME} in their commentary expand
- cleanly under `set -u`. Hermes-Agent 0.13.x reads
- ${HERMES_HOME}/config.yaml; the gateway service sets the same value
- via Environment= in mios-gateway-agent.service.
- ─── firstboot idempotency sentinel (AGY-38) ────────────────────────────────
- Once a full firstboot run has completed, skip the whole provision on every
- subsequent boot. The sentinel lives under /var/lib/mios (persists across
- bootc upgrades). To force a re-provision, delete it:
- rm -f /var/lib/mios/.hermes-firstboot.done && systemctl restart mios-hermes-firstboot
- ─── mios.toml layered overlay reader ───────────────────────────────────────
- Reads [section].key from ~/.config/mios/mios.toml -> /etc/mios/mios.toml
- -> /usr/share/mios/mios.toml, returning the FIRST non-empty match
- (operator overlay wins). Same arity + semantics as the bash resolver
- in /usr/libexec/mios/mios-dashboard.sh -- copied here so this script
- can run before mios-dashboard's helper is sourced.
- Drop-in over the shared layered resolver (usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py via the
- mios-toml-get shell CLI). Same signature/semantics as the retired awk scanner.
- Read an array-of-tables [[ai.catalog]] and emit id<TAB>label<TAB>ram_gb
- per row. Layered overlay: rows from the highest-precedence file that
- has ANY [[ai.catalog]] entries win wholesale (no merging across layers
- -- TOML AoT semantics don't merge, and operator editing the dropdown
- means they want their list, not the vendor's appended).
- ─── Resolve the model to seed ──────────────────────────────────────────────
- Start from [ai].model (the operator's chosen / vendor-default value).
- Then apply [ai.host_thresholds] auto-pick: if the host has enough RAM,
- roll up to mid_ram_model or big_ram_model. Auto-pick only runs when
- the operator hasn't overlaid [ai].model in /etc/mios/mios.toml or
- ~/.config/mios/mios.toml (operator override wins).
- Is [ai].model overlaid by an operator layer? (any non-vendor layer)
- Resolve tier model lookups from mios.toml [ai.host_thresholds].
- Detect actual GPU VRAM. Operator directive 2026-05-16 (mios.toml
- [ai.host_thresholds] comment, line ~651): "if detected GPU has more
- than 8GB of VRAM it deploys with medium sized models ... ALL AGENTS
- DEFAULTS TO CPU models -- across all hardware". So promotion is
- driven by VRAM, NOT system RAM. nvidia-smi (NVIDIA, incl. WSL2
- passthrough) and rocm-smi (AMD) are the canonical probes; if
- neither exists or returns 0, the host is CPU-only and we stay
- on small_ram_model.
- WSL2 ships nvidia-smi at /usr/lib/wsl/lib/nvidia-smi, which is NOT on the
- systemd unit PATH (/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin). So `command -v nvidia-smi`
- returned nothing under firstboot's systemd context and a 24 GB RTX 4090 was
- mis-detected as 0 GB -> small tier instead of mid (operator-confirmed
- 2026-06-21: "WHAT ARE YOU TALKING ABOUT CPU-ONLY"). Probe explicit
- locations (incl. the WSL path) so detection works regardless of PATH.
- install-robustness 2026-06-21.
- rocm-smi reports bytes; convert
- Auto-pick model tier based on GPU VRAM.
- Operators can still override via mios.html (sets [ai].model in
- /etc/mios/mios.toml, triggering the _overlaid=1 branch above).
- ─── Hermes role model (operator 2026-05-21) ────────────────────────────────
- "EVERY Agent and Sub-Agent should have an equivalent MiOS Modelfile for each
- role." Hermes (the general orchestrator) runs its role model
- mios-hermes:latest -- a Modelfile built FROM the auto-picked base with MiOS
- params; SOUL.md still drives behaviour at runtime. HERMES-SPECIFIC: the
- global [ai].model (10+ other consumers -- mios-micro-llm, mios-pc-vision,
- mios-doctor, ...) stays UNTOUCHED. Safe by construction: the tier-walk below
- validates this tag against Ollama's tags and falls back to the auto-picked
- base tier if mios-hermes wasn't built, and the base-model fallback_model
- chain backs it at runtime. Override with MIOS_HERMES_ROLE_MODEL=none to keep
- the bare auto-picked base, or =<tag> to pin a different role model.
- Backend endpoint for the generated config -- SSOT-derived from mios.toml
- [ai].backend (the mios-llm-light front; ollama :11434 retired). Default matches the
- vendor value so a missing/unreadable toml still yields a working endpoint
- (operator 2026-06-07: firstboot previously HARDCODED the port, so a stale REPL
- config survived the ollama->mios-llm-light migration; now it follows the SSOT).
- ── Agent-surface (orchestrator) endpoint + model for THIN clients ──────────────
- The interactive `hermes` CLI REPL must be a THIN client to the agent-pipe
- ORCHESTRATOR on :8640 (served model "MiOS-Agent"), exactly like the @/mios CLI
- and the Hermes DESKTOP app -- NOT a direct leaf granite native tool-loop on
- :11450. A leaf tool-loop fabricates (granite emits tool-call JSON it can't
- broker-execute -> "typed into chat" LIAR + same_tool_failure_halt). The
- orchestrator runs the loop SERVER-SIDE (refine -> route -> broker-exec +
- read-back verify -> polish), so a thin client never fabricates. Both values
- flow from the [ai] SSOT (operator "UNIFY THE MiOS AI PIPELINE" / "NO HARDCODES").
- Make sure the directory exists with the right ownership. tmpfiles.d
- should have done this already, but be defensive in case the .service
- fires before tmpfiles for some reason.
- Generate a 64-char hex key. openssl is in @core on Fedora CoreOS so
- this is always available; fall back to /dev/urandom if it isn't.
- Write the env file with secure perms BEFORE chowning to mios-hermes
- so the Quadlet's EnvironmentFile= read-as-root can succeed even if
- the per-uid mios-hermes login is denied (`/usr/sbin/nologin`).
- /etc/mios/hermes/api.env -- generated by mios-hermes-firstboot.service
- at $(date -Iseconds) on $(hostname).
- Rotate by deleting this file and restarting mios-hermes-firstboot.
- Hermes's "gateway run" mode bundles a messaging-platform router
- (Telegram / Discord / Slack) that enforces a USER ALLOWLIST on every
- request -- chat-completions included. Without an allowlist, the
- gateway DENIES all requests with the cryptic "No user allowlists
- configured. All unauthorized users will be denied" warning, then
- 401s the chat. MiOS isn't running messaging platforms (Workspace
- UI is the only frontend), so we opt out of the allowlist gate to
- let any caller with a valid API_SERVER_KEY through.
- Operator-flagged 2026-05-11: "all messages get Retry".
- Hermes Workspace consumes these via the SAME EnvironmentFile= mount.
- Systemd Quadlet Environment= directives do NOT expand \${API_SERVER_KEY}
- from sibling EnvironmentFile= contents, so we have to write the
- explicit duplicates here. The workspace falls back to a legacy HTML-
- scrape token flow when CLAUDE_DASHBOARD_TOKEN is unset, which fails
- against our minimal gateway image and triggers a client-side
- redirect to /error. Operator-flagged 2026-05-11.
- ─── /etc/mios/hermes/discord.env (Discord bot token, operator-managed) ─
- Empty stub seeded so that:
- * mios-gateway-agent.service's EnvironmentFile=- finds a readable file
- (no "file not found" warnings in the journal)
- * the operator has a known location to drop a token, with inline
- instructions on how to obtain one
- Discord toolset reads DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN from this file. If unset, the
- tool surfaces a clear "missing token" error to the agent on first
- call, which the agent then asks the operator about.
- /etc/mios/hermes/discord.env -- operator-managed.
- Drop a Discord bot token here for Hermes-Agent's `discord` toolset:
- DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=<your-bot-token>
- How to obtain a bot token (one-time):
- 1. https://discord.com/developers/applications -> New Application
- 2. Bot tab -> Reset Token -> copy the token (shown once)
- 3. OAuth2 -> URL Generator -> tick `bot` + `applications.commands`
- + the permissions your agent needs (Send Messages, Read Message
- History, Manage Threads, ...). Open the resulting URL and
- authorise the bot into your guild.
- 4. Paste the token below as DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=<token>, save, then:
- sudo systemctl restart mios-gateway-agent.service
- Permissions: 0640 root:mios-hermes (root edits, mios-hermes reads).
- ─── /usr/local/bin/chrome -- shim so mios-gui chrome / launch_app chrome ──
- routes through mios-chrome (CDP on :9222 + Wayland + persistent profile)
- instead of the bare flatpak-launch path the generic shim generator
- would produce. mios-gui detects this shim by the "MiOS shim for the"
- string in its first 3 lines. Idempotent: rewritten every boot so a
- stale generator-output gets superseded. Required for Hermes'
- browser_navigate / browser_snapshot / etc. to attach to the
- operator's actual visible Chrome instance (operator-flagged
- 2026-05-17).
- !/bin/sh
- /usr/local/bin/chrome -- MiOS shim for the com.google.ChromeDev flatpak.
- Routes through /usr/bin/mios-chrome which wraps the flatpak launch
- with --remote-debugging-port=9222 + Wayland args + persistent
- --user-data-dir so Hermes' browser_navigate connects to the SAME
- browser instance the operator drives (shared cookies, logged-in
- state). mios-gui detects this shim via the "MiOS shim for the"
- string in its first 3 lines and exec's it.
- ─── Reconcile MIOS_DISCORD_DEFAULT_* env from mios.toml [identity] ─────
- Operator sets [identity].discord_channel_default + .discord_guild_default
- in the layered mios.toml overlay (vendor < /etc < ~/.config). We sync
- those values into /etc/mios/hermes/discord.env so the running
- hermes-agent process has them in os.environ alongside DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN.
- The chat model is told about them via the seeded SOUL.md so it has
- the default channel as authoritative context when the operator says
- "send to discord" without naming a channel. Idempotent: the
- assignment line is REPLACED on every firstboot run if it drifts.
- Strip any existing line; append new (only when value non-empty).
- ─── /var/lib/mios/hermes/config.yaml (Hermes-Agent main config) ────────
- Hermes-Agent 0.13.x reads $HERMES_HOME/config.yaml. The direct host
- install (automation/72-hermes-agent.sh + mios-gateway-agent.service) sets
- HERMES_HOME=/var/lib/mios/hermes, so the agent's config lives at
- /var/lib/mios/hermes/config.yaml. NOTE: 0.13.x ignores the
- HERMES_CONFIG_PATH env var entirely -- HERMES_HOME is authoritative.
- SCHEMA -- load-bearing. Hermes-Agent 0.13.x resolves the inference
- provider via hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py::resolve_requested_provider:
- it reads config["model"], and ONLY honours a `provider:` key when
- `model` is a DICT. If `model` is a bare string the provider is
- unknown -> falls through to "auto" -> tries openrouter -> HTTP 401
- "Missing Authentication header" (no OPENROUTER_API_KEY).
- Operator-confirmed 2026-05-14. So `model` MUST be a mapping:
- model:
- provider: custom:<name>     # matches a custom_providers[].name
- default:  <ollama-model-id>
- base_url: ${_AI_BACKEND}/v1
- `provider: custom:local-llm` then resolves against the
- `custom_providers:` list entry named `local-llm`. The pre-0.13
- `backend:` block is genuinely unused by 0.13.x -- we drop it (the
- re-seed detection below treats a leftover `backend:` as stale).
- Architectural Law 5 (UNIFIED-AI-REDIRECTS): the agent loop stays
- fully local -- custom_providers[local-llm] points at the on-box
- Ollama OpenAI surface, no cloud calls.
- ─── Auto-recover Hermes-Agent venv if missing ───────────────────────
- automation/72-hermes-agent.sh installs Hermes-Agent directly onto
- the host (NOT a container) at /usr/lib/mios/agents/.venv. That
- script runs at OCI build time. But:
- * stale OCI images pre-2026-05 don't have it baked in
- * if the build-time install failed silently (network, PyPI hiccup),
- the venv won't be there post-install either
- In both cases mios-gateway-agent.service silently no-ops at boot via:
- ConditionPathExists=/usr/lib/mios/agents/.venv/bin/hermes
- and the operator gets a "Hermes won't work" surprise hours later.
- Detect the missing venv here and re-run the installer if we can find
- it. The installer is itself idempotent + safe to re-run -- worst case
- it re-pulls + re-installs the package. Operator-confirmed regression
- 2026-05-15: fresh MiOS install came up with hermes-agent inactive
- because the build never installed the venv.
- --no-block: firstboot must not WAIT on mios-gateway-agent settling
- (it has its own readiness deps + can deadlock against this very
- service in the early-boot ordering -- the ~23min hang, 2026-06-14).
- Ownership: mios-gateway-agent.service runs as the mios-hermes sysuser
- (uid 820). The pre-2026-05-14 mios-hermes CONTAINER ran with an
- in-container uid (10000) and bind-mounted this dir, leaving it
- orphan-owned 10000:10000 mode 0700 -- the direct-install service
- (uid 820) then cannot write its own state dir and chat completions
- die with "Permission denied: /var/lib/mios/hermes/cron". Force the
- whole tree to 820:820 on every run -- cheap, idempotent, and heals
- the container -> direct-install migration.
- Validate the resolved model against what the LIVE BACKEND actually serves.
- The [ai.host_thresholds] auto-pick can resolve to a model that was never
- baked or pulled on this host -- pointing Hermes at a missing model breaks
- chat just as hard as a stale schema.
- G5/G8: ollama (:11434) is RETIRED. The canonical front is mios-llm-light
- (the llama-swap proxy at $_AI_BACKEND, default :11450), which exposes the
- served set via the OpenAI-compat `GET /v1/models` ({"data":[{"id":...}]}).
- Probe THAT and key every model decision (primary validation + fallback
- chain) on the REAL served ids -- never on hardcoded qwen3* literals (the
- old `localhost:11434` probe + qwen3.5:4b/qwen3:1.7b literals were the
- stale-config root cause; 2026-06-14).
- Fallback policy still walks the TIER chain (small -> mid -> big), NOT
- whatever happens to be first in the served list. Operator directive
- 2026-05-16: never silently upgrade past the operator's tier choice. If
- the chosen tier is missing, prefer the SMALLER safer option first so the
- host stays responsive; only escalate if nothing smaller is available.
- Last-resort: any non-embed served id. Better than a 401 loop,
- but flag it loudly so the operator catches the gap.
- Build the fallback chain Hermes walks if the primary model emits invalid
- tool calls / empty bodies. Policy: never escalate ABOVE the resolved
- primary tier (the operator's tier ceiling is binding). Candidates are
- keyed on the REAL served set (no qwen3* literals): the resolved tier
- models (small -> mid) followed by the smallest served non-embed id as a
- universal safety net, so the chat NEVER silently fails over to an
- unreachable cloud provider. Emit only candidates the backend actually
- serves; skip duplicates of the primary.
- Trim trailing newline so heredoc doesn't get a blank line at the end
- Auxiliary + delegation model names -- pulled from the REAL served set
- (G5/G8: no qwen3* literals). The auxiliary lanes (compression, title-gen,
- triage, curator, mcp, web_extract, approval, skills_hub, session_search)
- and the delegate workers should run on a SMALL fast model: prefer the
- resolved small tier, then the smallest served non-embed id, finally the
- resolved primary (always valid). Both names are validated against
- $_served_ids when the backend is reachable; when it isn't (air-gapped
- firstboot) we trust the tier resolution. The big GPU model stays the
- primary; these keep auxiliary/delegate fan-out off the big lane.
- echo the first arg that is in the served set (or first arg if the
- backend is unreachable / served set unknown).
- nothing served matched -> fall back to the primary (guaranteed valid)
- Bump this in lockstep with the _config_version: NN literal in the seeded

- expand. No ${API_SERVER_KEY}-style values referenced here (those

- \$HERMES_HOME/config.yaml; HERMES_HOME=/var/lib/mios/hermes.
- AI chain: ollama (:11434, raw inference) -> Hermes-Agent (:8642/v1,
- OpenAI gateway + agent loop) -> Open WebUI (:3030). The gateway's own
- API key lives in /etc/mios/hermes/api.env (API_SERVER_KEY), loaded by
- mios-gateway-agent.service via EnvironmentFile=.
- Resolved values:
- [ai].model            -> ${_AI_MODEL_DEFAULT}
- validated vs Ollama   -> ${_AI_MODEL_RESOLVED}
- Primary model. MUST be a mapping (not a bare string) so
- resolve_requested_provider() sees the provider= key. provider=
- "custom:local-llm" resolves against the custom_providers entry
- below. Architectural Law 5: local Ollama only, no cloud calls.
- Hermes v0.15 PREFLIGHTS the runtime context window and REFUSES tool use
- under 64k ("Ollama runtime context is too small for Hermes tool use"),
- which silently failed EVERY agent:hermes swarm node (operator 2026-05-29).
- The gateway must REQUEST 64k from ollama on each call -- the model's own
- Modelfile num_ctx is not enough because the gateway sends its own
- options.num_ctx. Pin both: ollama_num_ctx (the per-request num_ctx the
- gateway passes through to ollama) + context_length (the window Hermes
- advertises to itself). 65536 matches mios-hermes.Modelfile PARAMETER
- num_ctx 65536 (9b @ 64k q8_0 KV ~10.6 GB, fits the 4090).
- Fallback chain (Hermes-Agent 0.13.x: model.fallback_model accepts
- a list of {provider, model} dicts and walks left-to-right when the
- primary returns invalid tool calls, empty bodies, or 3xx retries
- exceeded -- preserving conversation history across the swap).
- Walks DOWN the tier, never UP -- operator directive 2026-05-16:
- auto-selection must never escalate past the operator's chosen tier
- (e.g. a CPU-only host stuck with primary=4B should fall back to
- 1.7B / 0.6B safety nets, not climb to 30B and freeze).
- Auxiliary LLM services (context compression / summarization, memory
- flush, title + triage + curation, MCP reasoning, web-extract,
- approvals, skills-hub). 0.13.x does NOT inherit the main provider for
- these -- left unmapped it logs "No auxiliary LLM provider configured"
- and silently drops context-compression summaries. Map every one at
- the same on-box Ollama provider so the agent is fully self-contained.
- ALL auxiliary lanes need >= 64K context window or Hermes refuses
- to start chat completions ("Auxiliary <lane> model X has a context
- window of N tokens, which is below the minimum 64,000 required by
- Hermes Agent" -- operator-confirmed 2026-05-15 & re-confirmed
- 2026-05-17 when qwen3:1.7b @ 40,960 tokens was wired here and
- every delegate spawn 503'd). qwen3.5:4b @ 262,144 tokens is the
- safe default: small (~3GB), CPU-friendly, comfortably above the
- floor. Compression stays on the main model for context-fill
- events (infrequent).
- Vision-grounding lane for screenshot -> click-coordinate
- translation. Used by /usr/libexec/mios/mios-pc-vision (the
- PC-Control vision-grounded loop, Path B in the pc-control
- skill). qwen3-vl:4b has native 2D coordinate grounding;
- UI-TARS-1.5-7B is the upgrade-path candidate (PC-specific).
- Architecture: /usr/share/mios/docs/agents/PC-CONTROL-LOCAL.md.
- Web SEARCH -> the on-box SearXNG (mios-searxng, SEARXNG_URL). Web EXTRACT ->
- \`miosfetch\`, MiOS's OWN offline direct-fetch provider (stdlib urllib +
- readability HTML->text; plugins/web/miosfetch, deployed by 72-hermes-agent.sh

- -py v4 (firecrawl API v2, POST /v2/scrape) but MiOS self-hosts firecrawl

- operator-confirmed regression 2026-05-15: the same chat completion
- went from 163,742 prompt tokens to 13,017 prompt tokens (92% reduction)

- config.local.yaml (operator-overlay; vendor stays clean).

- Multi-agent delegation. Hermes 0.13.x's orchestrator can spawn child
- agents (delegate_task tool) -- typically used to fan out discrete
- subtasks (search this file, lint that path, write a test) in parallel
- while the main agent stays focused on the high-level plan.
- Architecture for this host (9950X3D 16-core / 40 GB RAM / RTX 4090
- 24 GB VRAM): the MAIN agent runs the big tool-calling model on the
- GPU (model.default = qwen3-coder:30b, MoE, ~19 GB), while DELEGATES
- and the AUXILIARY services (compression, title-gen, session_search,
- triage, curator, mcp, web_extract, approval, skills_hub) run on the
- small fast qwen3.5:4b model -- ollama keeps it warm alongside the
- big one (OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=4) and serves up to 4 concurrent
- requests per model (OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=4, set in ollama.container).
- Result: the orchestrator's children + auxiliary lanes actually run
- in parallel instead of serializing through one slot.
- subagent_auto_approve: true -- consistent with the operator's broad
- sudo grant for mios-hermes (10-mios-hermes); the agent is
- operator-authorized to act, including spawning its own children.
- Agent autonomy. Hermes's default approvals.mode = "manual" gates
- EVERY tool call behind a per-call operator OK -- which makes the
- whole stack we've built incoherent:
- * the operator-authorized broad sudo grant for mios-hermes
- (/etc/sudoers.d/10-mios-hermes) is wasted if every sudo call
- still pauses for click-to-approve,
- * delegation.subagent_auto_approve: true above is meaningless if
- the parent's tool calls (which is what spawns delegates) still
- need approval,
- * Open WebUI chat becomes a per-call clicking grind with no agent.
- auto = tool calls execute without per-call prompts. Destructive
- slash commands (/reset, /delete) still confirm, MCP reloads still
- confirm, cron-triggered runs are denied (the operator must launch
- cron jobs explicitly). To revoke autonomy: switch to "manual" here,
- or simply delete /etc/sudoers.d/10-mios-hermes (which then trips
- the build driver's privilege preflight too -- belt + suspenders).
- Tool-loop guardrails. The agent can loop forever on bad tool calls;
- hard_stop_enabled aborts after N consecutive same-kind failures so
- a stuck delegate doesn't burn the whole agent budget.
- Operator-flagged 2026-05-17: chats hitting 19-24 tool calls were
- below upstream's 5/8/5 thresholds (because each call was a
- DIFFERENT tool -- agent thrashing across browser/web_extract/
- skill_view rather than failing the same one repeatedly). The
- total-call cap (agent.max_turns: 20 above) handles thrashing
- across different tools; the per-failure thresholds below are now
- tightened so the agent backs off SOONER on a single tool that
- keeps erroring (web_extract returning "searxng is search-only"
- four times before the agent gives up was the original incident).
- Sessions: prune old sessions automatically. Keeps $HERMES_HOME clean
- without manual \`hermes session prune\` after every long-running build
- leaves a fat session file behind. retention_days=30 is a reasonable
- window; the operator can \`mios hermes wipe\` (TODO future verb) for
- a hard reset.
- Goals — configuration for /goal command continuations.
- Max continuation turns before Hermes auto-pauses the goal and
- asks the user to /goal resume.
- Agent: per-agent runtime tuning. reasoning_effort=xhigh is set
- Hard cap on tool-call iterations per chat. Upstream default is 90;
- operator-flagged 2026-05-17 had chats running 19-24 tool calls
- before giving up. For an OWUI conversational agent 100 is plenty
- (most asks resolve in 1-3 calls; multi-step in ~10). Sub-agents
- spawned via delegate_task still get their own 90-turn budget --
- this cap is for the OPERATOR-facing turn, not the children.
- MCP CLIENT (operator 2026-06-07: "Hermes should have access to all Global MiOS
- MCP surfaces"). Hermes consumes the global mios-mcp-server so its tool registry
- auto-extends with the COMPLETE MiOS surface -- all verbs + recipes + promoted
- skills (tools/list), every call routed through the launcher broker. Needs the
- \`mcp\` SDK in the venv (installed by automation/72-hermes-agent.sh). stdio = the
- MCP-canonical transport; the spawned relay forwards to the agent-pipe.

- [agents.hermes] is fanout=false/default=false (mios.toml) so the orchestrator never

- The `hermes` CLI runs as the operator (not the mios-hermes sysuser)

- ── Operator CLI key material (~/.hermes/.env) ──────────────────────
- config.yaml above seeds the PROVIDER half (custom:local-llm). But
- the bare interactive `hermes` CLI ALSO has a startup config-detection
- gate that trips with "no API keys or providers found -- run: hermes
- setup" when it sees no API_SERVER_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY in its
- environment (operator-confirmed 2026-06-14: `hermes` -> setup wizard
- despite a seeded config.yaml at /var/home/mios/.hermes/config.yaml).
- WHY the gateway service didn't hit this: mios-gateway-agent.service loads
- /etc/mios/hermes/api.env via EnvironmentFile=, so API_SERVER_KEY /
- OPENAI_API_KEY are in the SERVICE's os.environ. The interactive CLI
- runs as the operator and does NOT read /etc/mios/hermes/api.env --
- it auto-loads ~/.hermes/.env. Seed THAT with the SAME key material
- the service uses (single SSOT: the api.env this script generated
- above) so the CLI's "configured?" gate passes and it never drops
- into `hermes setup`.
- Architectural Law 5 (UNIFIED-AI-REDIRECTS) is preserved: the seeded
- config.yaml pins provider=custom:local-llm at ${_AI_BACKEND}/v1
- with api_key:"" (the local lane is keyless). This .env carries only
- the gateway's OWN key (so the CLI can also auth to the local :8642
- gateway) -- NO cloud provider, NO vendor URL is introduced.
- Re-seed if the current key isn't present (rotation/drift).
- ── Hermes persona / grounding (SOUL.md) ────────────────────────────────
- Hermes-Agent reloads $HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md fresh on EVERY message -- it
- is the live lever for the agent's persona AND its operating discipline.
- Stock Hermes ships an EMPTY SOUL.md (just a comment template), which
- left the local model ungrounded: it made up tool output, invented
- config flags, and claimed success on commands that errored or returned
- nothing (operator-confirmed 2026-05-14). MiOS ships a hardened SOUL.md
- at /usr/share/mios/ai/hermes-soul.md -- strong rules against
- fabricated output, full-shell-usage guidance, and pointers to the MiOS AI
- reference docs. Seed it for BOTH the gateway service (HERMES_HOME) and
- the operator's `hermes` CLI (~/.hermes), exactly like config.yaml.
- Re-seed when the target is missing OR still the stock template (no
- "MiOS-managed" marker) OR the source content has changed (so updates
- to /usr/share/mios/ai/hermes-soul.md propagate without a manual
- delete). An operator who wants their own persona just deletes the
- "MiOS-managed" marker line; MiOS then leaves the file alone forever.
- NOT MiOS-managed. Distinguish the Hermes BINARY's STOCK DEFAULT identity
- (the framework writes "You are Hermes Agent ... created by Nous Research"
- when SOUL.md is absent at first CLI launch) from a GENUINE operator-authored
- SOUL. The stock default left the operator's `hermes` CLI UNGROUNDED -- it
- answered "I am Hermes Agent by Nous Research" with no MiOS identity (operator
- 2026-06-16 "NOT GROUNDED IN MIOS / HAS NO IDEA WHO THEY ARE") because this
- gate treated it as operator-owned and never seeded the MiOS SOUL. SEED
- (replace) the vendor stock default; LEAVE a real operator SOUL alone. The
- signature matched is the vendor's OWN identity line, not a MiOS routing word.
- Compare ONLY the source body against the head of target -- our
- appended runtime-context block lives AFTER the SOUL_SRC bytes;
- cmp -n SRC_LEN matches when the body is current regardless of
- the appended context.
- Build a runtime-context block we append to SOUL.md so the model has
- operator-specific defaults (Discord channel/guild, etc.) as
- authoritative context without us having to wedge them into the
- vendor SOUL source. Empty values are simply omitted.

- ─── Seed Gateway Copies ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── Seed Operator/User CLI Copies ──────────────────────────────────────────
- Seed for all operator users (the configured user, mios, and root)
- Seed config.yaml
- Seed .env
- ${_u_env} -- MiOS-managed by mios-hermes-firstboot.
- Auto-loaded by the interactive \`hermes\` CLI so it never drops into the
- \`hermes setup\` wizard ("no API keys or providers found"). Mirrors the
- key material in /etc/mios/hermes/api.env (the gateway service's

- ${_u_cfg} (provider: custom:local-llm -> ${_AI_BACKEND}/v1).
- To take ownership: delete this "MiOS-managed" marker line and edit.
- Seed SOUL.md
- Seed skills
- Tell hermes to drop its in-process skills-prompt cache so the
- newly-seeded skills appear in the next chat turn's system prompt
- without a service restart. The cache key is mtime/size of every
- SKILL.md in $HERMES_HOME/skills, so touching a marker file in the
- skills dir invalidates the disk snapshot. The simpler hammer: if
- any skill was actually seeded above, restart the service.
- --no-block: don't wait on the restart settling (avoids the firstboot
- <-> hermes-agent start deadlock / ~23min hang, 2026-06-14).
- ─── Global flatpak override (theming + portal) ─────────────────────────
- Seed the GTK_USE_PORTAL=1 + xdg-config/data/themes/icons filesystem
- mounts so libadwaita / GTK4 flatpaks (Epiphany, Nautilus, Files,
- Calendar, Extensions Manager) pick up the operator's color-scheme
- (prefer-dark) and theme (adw-gtk3-dark) via xdg-portal-desktop. Without
- this, every flatpak boots with a generic white-mode GTK3 default.
- Operator-confirmed regression 2026-05-15: "epiphany has older GTK now"
- was because the global override was missing the xdg-data/themes mount.
- Idempotent + harmless if flatpak isn't installed (the helper exits 0).
- ─── Open WebUI: bootstrap first admin user if the user table is empty ──
- The OWUI Quadlet ships with ENABLE_SIGNUP=False (single-tenant lockdown)
- AND no built-in flow to seed the first admin. On a fresh install OR
- after an over-aggressive cache wipe (operator-confirmed regression
- 2026-05-15: my own mios-cache-clear deleted the user row alongside
- chats), there's no way for the operator to log in -- the signup form
