- ─── Open WebUI: enable built-in web search via local SearXNG ──────────
- OWUI's built-in web-search augmentation is OFF in upstream defaults.
- Operator directive 2026-05-15: should be ENABLED + pointed at the
- local SearXNG (mios-searxng on :8888) so chat turns can be augmented
- with retrieved web results without leaving the host. Idempotent.
- ─── Open WebUI: register MiOS docs as a Knowledge collection ──────────
- Walks /usr/share/mios/{ai,docs,cookbooks,hermes,prompts},
- /etc/mios/system-prompts, /CLAUDE.md, /AGENTS.md and registers each
- as an OWUI File row with path = absolute FHS path + a snapshot of
- content in file.data.content. Idempotent (sha256-keyed). Updates
- the MiOS-Agent model row's meta.knowledge to attach the collection
- so it becomes per-chat searchable context. Operator directive
- 2026-05-15: "OWUI's MiOS-Agent model have knowledge files (use
- exactly the current MiOS AI Files / Markdown files / Documentation
- / EVERYTHING ETC)".
- ─── Open WebUI: apply the MiOS AI system prompt ({{USER_LOCATION}}) ───
- E1 (operator 2026-06-22): recreate the "MiOS AI" model row with the
- location/time-aware system prompt ({{USER_LOCATION}} / {{CURRENT_TIMEZONE}} /
- {{CURRENT_DATE}}) on EVERY firstboot, so the OWUI-native location grounding
- survives a rebuild/reinstall (it was applied live-only and would otherwise be
- lost). Idempotent (the script upserts the model row). Runs after
- apply-knowledge so the model row exists for the prompt to attach to. Browser
- geolocation needs a SECURE CONTEXT (https://...ts.net or http://localhost:3030,
- NOT http://<LAN-IP>) -- documented in the script + the roadmap E1 note.
- ─── Auto-install MiOS-Agent OWUI Pipe ────────────────────────────────
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: "OWUIs MiOS-Agent is the model that
- users speak to ... should be using OWUIs emitter function". The
- pipe at /usr/share/mios/owui/pipes/mios_agent_pipe.py is the
- canonical user-facing entry. mios-owui-install-pipe (vendored at
- /usr/libexec/mios) idempotently registers/updates it in OWUIs
- functions table. Runs after mios-owui-apply-knowledge so the pipe
- inherits the knowledge bindings on first chat.
- Wait for OWUI's HTTP backend to be reachable. On a fresh boot OWUI
- Quadlet says "active" the moment podman launches the container, but
- the python uvicorn server inside takes ~5-15s to bind :8080. If
- install-pipe runs before then it gets connection-refused and the
- WHOLE firstboot script exits 7/NOTRUNNING (set -e + subprocess
- failure), which strands the SUBSEQUENT steps (install-tools,
- apply-suggestions, pre-warm, mios-daemon start) un-run. Wait up to
- 90s with 2s polls. Operator-flagged 2026-05-17 regression after the
- full reboot test.
- Each helper's failure is wrapped so a single misfire doesn't
- strand the rest of firstboot. The helpers are themselves
- idempotent; next firstboot run will pick up anything skipped.
- ─── Seed MiOS-specific default prompt suggestions ────────────────────
- Replaces upstream OWUI's generic chatbot cards with MiOS-relevant
- defaults (launch / find / system status / inventory apps / etc.).
- Idempotent: re-running with the same content is a no-op. Operator
- directive 2026-05-17: "suggested is not generated and relevant".
- ─── Install native MiOS verbs OWUI Tools class ──────────────────────
- Exposes launch_app / everything_search / mios_apps / mios_find as
- typed native tool_calls so the chat model invokes them with a
- proper JSON schema instead of going through `terminal: mios-<verb>`
- indirection. Idempotent (sha256 content compare). Operator
- directive 2026-05-17: "AI-stack native (Hermes tools???!!)".
- ─── Install the WS-4 computer-use OWUI Native tool (cu_* + docgen_*) ─────
- Registers the desktop-control + doc-gen surface as ONE OWUI Native tool.
- Idempotent (sha256 content compare); ships WRITE_ACTIONS_ENABLED=false so the
- agent can't drive desktop input until the operator opts in. Runs after
- install-tools so the OWUI functions/tools table exists.
- ─── Pre-warm model WEIGHTS only (NO chat completion, NO prompt) ──────
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: "the system prompt should run in the
- background upon installation/MiOS images deployments". CRITICAL
- clarification from operator: "MiOS-Agent Init has poisoned data and
- is opening apps/flatpaks during init--should be initializing and
- understanding its environment--user THEN dictates what it does".
- The previous "warmup" chat prompt was being INTERPRETED by hermes
- as a real request -- the agent then took unprompted actions
- (launched apps, ran tools, fabricated). Switched to /api/generate
- with prompt="" + num_predict=0: loads the model weights into VRAM,
- parses the SYSTEM prompt template, exits WITHOUT producing a single
- token of output OR receiving a real user message.
- Skip hermes warmup entirely -- it goes through the OpenAI-compat
- gateway which always runs a full chat turn. Only warm the bare
- Ollama models via /api/generate (load-only path).
- CPU pre-warm: mios-sys-agent IS the prompt refiner the
- mios-delegation-prefilter calls before forwarding to hermes.
- Operator architecture 2026-05-17: "the message should have
- NEVER BEEN SENT TO HERMES" if the refiner fails -- so the
- prefilter HARD-GATES on refine success. Cold-loading a 4 GB
- CPU model from disk takes 60-90s; if the FIRST chat after
- boot pays that, it times out and gets a 503 refiner_unavail
- back. Pre-warming with the SAME options (/api/chat + num_gpu=0
- + num_thread=8 + keep_alive=-1) the refiner uses guarantees
- the model is already resident in CPU memory + the right runner
- is bound when the first chat hits. ALL backgrounded -- firstboot
- doesn't block on it.
- GPU pre-warm: every model the chat path or fallback chain
- might land on, loaded into VRAM via /api/generate's load-only
- path (num_predict=0 short-circuits before token generation).
- Stays warm via keep_alive=-1; first chat skips the cold load.
- ─── Consolidated mios-daemon (replaces log-watcher + nudger + cron-director) ─
- Operator directive 2026-05-17: "ALL to be consolidated to one
- mios daemon/agent". The new mios-daemon.service holds a single
- qwen3:0.6b-cpu client + dispatches log-classify / refusal-detect /
- cron-gate handlers off a unified journal subscription. The three
- predecessor services are stopped + disabled here so we don't double-
- emit + double-load the micro-LLM. The mios_sidecar Filter has been
- updated to poll the unified /var/lib/mios/daemon/state.json
- (legacy paths still in SIBLING_AGENTS as a migration fallback).
- Start the consolidated daemon (idempotent -- systemctl restart on a
- running unit is a no-op when ExecStart hasn't changed).
- STATE dir must be owned by mios-ai (the daemon's User=) -- it writes
- state.json/launch_failures.json there. Creating it root:root (the old
- behaviour) crash-looped the mios-ai daemon on EVERY firstboot/rebuild
- ("PermissionError: '/var/lib/mios/daemon/state.json.tmp'", 315 restarts,
- operator 2026-06-01) -- contradicting the mios.conf tmpfiles decl. The
- /etc CONFIG dir stays root (daemon only READS it). chown -R repairs a dir
- that a prior root-run instance already created + any stale root-owned
- state files inside it (tmpfiles 'd' does NOT re-chown an existing dir).
- ─── Pin Windows-host tailscale IP for mios-windows helper ─────────────
- When the host is a WSL distro running inside Windows, the Tailscale CLI
- on the Windows side knows its own tailnet IP. mios-windows (the
- agent->Windows SSH helper) reads this IP from /etc/mios/windows-host
- instead of re-deriving it from `ip route` every call (which would just
- give the Hyper-V vSwitch gateway, not the Tailscale interface). We
- query the Windows tailscale.exe via wsl interop and write the file
- once on every firstboot. Idempotent.
- ─── Enable opt-in units per mios.toml [ttyd].enable + mining timer ───
- These are listed-but-not-installed-enabled by the bootc image (so
- operators on minimal hosts aren't paying for them), but mios.toml's
- vendor default opts in. Firstboot reads the toml SSOT and enables.
- Idempotent: systemctl enable on an already-enabled unit is a no-op.
- Read [identity].username from the SSOT mios.toml. The vendor
- ttyd unit ships `User=mios` as a convention placeholder, but
- on hosts where the operator chose a different username during
- install, the vendor value would target a non-existent account
- + ttyd would fail with "user does not exist". The drop-in
- below replaces single-value User=/Group= without modifying
- the vendor file. Read directly from toml so firstboot doesn't
- need EnvironmentFile= for userenv.sh.
- /etc/systemd/system/${_ttyd_unit}.service.d/10-mios-user.conf
- Render-time override of the vendor User=/Group=. Source of truth:
- [identity].username in /usr/share/mios/mios.toml (read by
- mios-hermes-firstboot through userenv.sh \$MIOS_USER).
- Skills miner: catalogs + mines tool-call patterns. Vendor default
- is enable -- the timer fires every [skills.mine_interval_minutes].
- Embedding backfill: off-hot-path vector backfiller.
- Starter-chip refresh: generates MiOS-aware revolving chips for
- OWUI's new-chat starter row, driven off recent operator state.
- Fires on a 10-min cadence (operator-tunable via the timer drop-in).
- Best-effort: tailscale.exe can fail transiently at firstboot
- time (just-booted Windows + tailscaled not yet responsive),
- and the WHOLE firstboot script would exit 1 because of set
- -euo pipefail. Wrap in a subshell with the strict flags
- locally relaxed so a probe failure doesn't kill firstboot.
- The cached file at /etc/mios/windows-host from any previous
- successful firstboot remains usable in the meantime.
- ── CephFS automount setup (Part 9 T-087) ──
- ── CephFS XDG and User Directories setup (Part 9 T-090, T-091) ──
- ── sentinel: firstboot reached completion -- gate re-runs on later boots (AGY-38)
- Degrade-open: the touch never hard-fails boot (|| true under set -e).
- Explicit exit 0 so the script's exit status doesn't depend on the
- last sub-block's truthiness under set -e (the Tailscale block
- always reaches here non-failing now, but a future maintainer
- adding a new tail block shouldn't have to think about set -e
- arithmetic).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-hermes-soul-sync
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-hermes-soul-sync
- Idempotent SOUL.md propagation. The hardened vendor SOUL.md lives at
- /usr/share/mios/ai/hermes-soul.md and is updated by code changes
- (commit/rebuild). The agent reads $HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md fresh on every
- message, but only after firstboot has SEEDED that path. Without this
- shim, SOUL.md updates between firstboot runs require a manual
- touch+restart on every operator host (operator-flagged 2026-05-17:
- WSLg rule didn't propagate after my deploy because cp preserved mtime).
- TWO classes of target, BOTH refreshed here:
- 1. The gateway SERVICE home ($HERMES_HOME, default /var/lib/mios/hermes,
- owned by mios-hermes) -- what hermes-agent.service reads.
- 2. INTERACTIVE operator homes (~/.hermes/SOUL.md). A human running the
- `hermes` CLI uses THEIR ~/.hermes, NOT the service home. firstboot
- seeds these ONCE, so a later SOUL update never reached the REPL --
- operator-flagged 2026-06-19: `hermes` kept truncating a stale 47K SOUL
- because only the service home was being refreshed. We now sync the
- interactive homes on every run too (root-only; writing another user's
- home needs privilege -- a no-op when run as the unprivileged service).
- Per target:
- * If target SOUL.md is absent -> seed it from source.
- * If target exists but lacks the 'MiOS-managed' marker -> leave it alone
- (the operator has taken ownership).
- * If the source body (BEFORE any appended runtime-context block) is
- byte-identical to the target body -> noop (preserves the operator's
- appended Discord/runtime context).
- * Otherwise -> rewrite the body from source, preserving the appended
- runtime-context block + ownership + permissions.
- Wired as ExecStartPre to hermes-agent.service via a drop-in so SOUL.md is
- always fresh when hermes boots. Also runnable from firstboot, the operator
- console, or an "update SOUL.md" automation.
- Exit codes:
- 0 = noop or successful sync (best-effort across homes)
- 1 = source missing (logged, non-fatal -- hermes still starts)
- Match the marker firstboot uses; preserve appended context across syncs.
- sync_one TARGET OWNER_USER OWNER_GROUP -- idempotent body-sync of $SRC onto
- one SOUL.md, preserving the operator's appended runtime-context block + the
- 'MiOS-managed' opt-out + ownership/permissions. Best-effort (never aborts).
- Operator-owned? Don't touch.
- Compare body-only. Target body = everything BEFORE the runtime-context
- marker; source is all body (firstboot appends runtime-context after copy).
- Drop the trailing blank line firstboot pads before the marker.
- Body differs -- preserve any appended runtime-context block, rewrite body.
- 1. Gateway SERVICE home (always).
- 2. INTERACTIVE operator homes -- only when privileged (writing another user's
- home needs root; a no-op for the unprivileged ExecStartPre). Sync every
- EXISTING ~/.hermes (we don't create one for users who never ran hermes).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-hermes-tail
- ─── Patterns the script extracts from hermes-agent journal ───────────
- Hermes-Agent 0.13.x logs format varies; these patterns are tuned to
- match the most visible activity markers. Add more as the hermes
- logging evolves (or as the operator wants surfaced).
- delegate_task spawning N subagents
- tool invocation lines (Hermes logs "Tool X invoked" or similar)
- subagent completion
- synthesis / final response generation
- empty-response retry loop (the operator's chronic frustration)
- max-retries exceeded (the give-up signal)
- invalid tool call (the chronic SOUL-violation signal)
- World-readable so mios-open-webui (the OWUI service user) can
- read it without group membership shenanigans.
- Atomic write: tmp + rename.
- Periodic flush even if no new events (so stale state ages out).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-host-launch
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-host-launch <binary> [args...]
- Operator-session escape + GUI-env injector for HOST-installed GUI
- RPMs (gnome-software, gnome-system-monitor, gnome-disks, baobab,
- gnome-control-center, ...). Mirrors the design of flatpak-launch
- but exec's the host binary directly instead of `flatpak run`.
- WHY THIS EXISTS
- ───────────────
- Operator directive 2026-05-15: agents kept failing to open
- gnome-software with messages like "we're likely in a headless
- environment" / "needs a graphical display" / "let me suggest dnf
- instead". WSLg DOES provide DISPLAY=:0 + WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0
- automatically, but ONLY in a real login session -- the moment a
- call comes in via Hermes-Agent's terminal tool (running as
- mios-hermes uid 820, no login session, no $HOME, no DBUS_SESSION_
- BUS_ADDRESS), GUI launches die with "Cannot autolaunch D-Bus
- without X11 $DISPLAY" and the agent then HALLUCINATES a
- "headless environment" diagnosis instead of fixing the env.
- This wrapper does what the agent should: re-exec into the
- operator's real session via systemd-run --uid=<operator>,
- carrying the right env. Identical operator-escape logic to
- flatpak-launch (intentional: same shape so future env additions
- only need to change one mental model).
- Resolve to absolute path so the operator-session re-exec doesn't
- get bitten by a $PATH difference under sudo / systemd-run.
- Step 0 ── Service-user re-exec.
- Identical pattern to flatpak-launch (see that file's header for the
- full rationale + ProtectSystem=strict caveat). When invoked under a
- service user (uid < 1000), re-exec via systemd-run into the
- operator's real session so DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY/DBUS work.
- Resolve operator UID -- only re-exec for SERVICE users (uid <
- operator's uid), not the operator themselves. Bug fix 2026-05-15:
- previous `id < 1000` test mis-fired for operator (uid 992).
- WSLg path: prefer mios-as-operator (broker socket -> wsl.exe --user)
- for service users only.
- Same as flatpak-launch: NOT --wait. GUI apps run for minutes
- to hours; --wait would block the caller (and time out OWUI).
- systemd-run returns instantly after the transient unit is
- registered; --collect cleans it up when the GUI exits.
- Step 1 ── WSL detection (namespace-stable via /proc/version).
- Step 2 ── XDG_RUNTIME_DIR.
- Step 3 ── Wayland / X11 / Pulse defaults (WSL).
- Step 4 ── D-Bus session bus.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-html
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-html [section]
- Open the MiOS configurator (`/usr/share/mios/configurator/mios.html`) in
- the operator's default browser. The configurator is the operator-facing
- UI for editing mios.toml — package selection, AI catalog, identity,
- locale, theme, network knobs, etc.
- Implementation: WSL hosts the file under /usr/share/mios/configurator/.
- Windows Explorer + browsers can reach it via the WSL UNC path
- (\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\usr\share\mios\configurator\mios.html).
- `mios-windows ps "Start-Process '<unc>'"` launches the file in the
- operator's default browser through their visible Windows session.
- Operator directive 2026-05-17: chat showed agent claiming mios.html
- was "not installed" + suggesting a fake `dnf install MiosGUI` package.
- This shim makes "open mios.html" / "open the configurator" /
- "customize MiOS" all resolve through a single helper that mios-find
- can route to. mios.toml [mios-find.aliases] maps "configurator" /
- "settings" / "mios.html" to this shim.
- Resolve the operator-visible Windows path. WSL distros are reachable
- via the \\wsl.localhost\<distro-name>\... UNC. WSL_DISTRO_NAME is set
- inside WSL; fall back to a generic prefix the operator can hand-edit
- if not present.
- Derive from /proc/version or /etc/wsl.conf if WSL_DISTRO_NAME is unset
- Append URL fragment for section deep-linking
- Dispatch via mios-windows ps so the launch happens in the operator's
- visible Windows session (through the launcher broker). Start-Process
- with a file:// or UNC path lets Windows pick the registered handler
- (default browser).
- Quote the UNC for PowerShell — single quotes preserve backslashes

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-ingest
- Embed-on-write (WS-0 durability + exposure): embed the L0+L1 text at ingest so
- the row is semantically RECALLABLE via the knowledge_emb_hnsw cosine index --
- the same path agent-pipe's _store_knowledge_task uses for chat Q+A. MUST match
- agent-pipe's model + endpoint EXACTLY (MIOS_VERB_EMBED_MODEL / _URL) so the
- 768-dim nomic-embed-text vectors are comparable under <=> cosine; a mismatch
- would make ingested rows un-rankable against chat-embedded queries.
- Cap the embed input (~1200 chars). nomic handles longer, but L0+L1 is already
- a compact tiered summary; capping keeps the light-lane call fast + bounded.
- OpenAI /v1 shape: {data:[{embedding:[...]}]}.
- The pg `knowledge` table is created by the schema-init step
- (usr/share/mios/postgres/schema-init.sql); no per-tool DDL needed.
- Embed-on-write: the tiered L0+L1 summary is what recall should match
- against, so embed that (NOT the raw L2 on disk). Best-effort -- a miss
- leaves emb NULL (row still stored + auditable, just not cosine-
- recallable). Capped inside _embed (EMBED_MAX_CHARS).
- idempotent upsert keyed on the source path. pg `knowledge` has no
- `src`/`source` columns, so the path lives in the `sources` jsonb
- array (preserving the old sources=[sp]) and we match it with the
- jsonb containment operator @>. session_id='ingest' marks provenance
- (was source='ingest'). ts defaults to now() at the column level.
- Atomic delete-then-insert upsert keyed on the source path. ALL
- file-derived values bind out-of-band ($1..$n); only the trusted
- table/column identifiers stay inline. The literal 'ingest'
- session_id is a fixed constant (not request data) so it stays
- inline. Add `emb` to the column list ONLY when the embed succeeded,
- binding the vector literal as a TEXT param cast with ::vector
- (matches mios_pg.build_insert). On a miss we omit the column so it
- defaults to NULL -- never fail the ingest.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-installer
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-installer <subcommand> [args...]
- Cross-platform package installer that fronts the three backends MiOS
- operators actually use:
- * winget   (Windows Package Manager) -- Windows-side apps + games
- via `mios-windows cmd "winget …"`
- * dnf      (Fedora RPM)              -- Linux CLI tools, system packages
- * flatpak  (Flathub)                 -- Linux GUI apps (mostly)
- Single entry point so agents and operators don't have to remember which
- package manager owns which app. Operator directive 2026-05-17:
- "mios-installer should be able to use windows CMD and Linux BASH for
- installing applications on their respective platforms".
- SUBCOMMANDS
- search <query> [--backend <name>]
- Search all three backends (or just one) and print combined results.
- Default: all available. --backend = winget | dnf | flatpak.
- install <id> [--backend <name>] [--no-confirm]
- Install by package ID. Auto-detects backend from the ID shape
- unless --backend is set:
- "Microsoft.PowerToys"   -> winget
- "org.mozilla.firefox"   -> flatpak (reverse-DNS = Flathub style)
- "vim", "htop"           -> dnf (single lowercase word)
- --no-confirm passes -y / --accept-package-agreements / --noninteractive.
- uninstall <id> [--backend <name>]
- Remove. Backend auto-detected the same way.
- info <id> [--backend <name>]
- Show package details (version, publisher, description, deps).
- list [--installed] [--backend <name>]
- List packages (default: installed=true).
- OUTPUT
- Default: human-readable tables. Pass `--json` (any subcommand) to
- emit one JSON object per result -- agent-friendly.
- EXIT CODES
- 0 success / found
- 1 not found / no match
- 2 backend not available
- 64 usage error
- ARCHITECTURAL NOTES
- * winget calls go through `mios-windows cmd "winget ..."` because
- winget.exe is a Windows binary; running it directly from WSL fails
- on AppExecutionAlias / current-directory issues. mios-windows cmd
- dispatches via the launcher broker so the operator's Windows
- session executes the command -- needed for UAC + Windows
- environment vars + Microsoft Store ToS prompts.
- * dnf is run via `sudo` -- mios-hermes has a broad sudo grant in
- /etc/sudoers.d/10-mios-hermes. Operators running this verb
- interactively get the same prompt as `sudo dnf install`.
- * flatpak install defaults to --user so the install lands per-user
- (no sudo). Use --system to install for all users.
- * On MiOS bootc, `dnf install` lands as a layered package via
- rpm-ostree's overlay; `bootc upgrade` preserves these layers.
- This is the operator-friendly default for "install a CLI tool".
- ─── helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- winget is on Windows side; we reach it via mios-windows cmd.
- Pick a default backend for a given package id shape.
- Reverse-DNS shape with dots + only-lowercase -> flatpak (Flathub
- convention: com.spotify.Client, org.mozilla.firefox, ...)
- Capital-letter publisher.product -> winget (Microsoft.PowerToys,
- 7zip.7zip, Notepad++.Notepad++)
- Single word -> dnf
- Fallback: dnf (most flexible package id shape)
- ─── search ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- winget search returns a multi-column table; pipe through column.
- --accept-source-agreements is implicit after first run.
- flatpak search emits TSV: Name | Description | Application ID | Version | Branch | Remotes
- ─── install ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── info ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── uninstall ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── list ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── arg parsing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Skip dispatch when sourced (lets tests `source mios-installer; _detect_backend foo`
- without hitting the usage+exit guard).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-keyring-autounlock
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-keyring-autounlock
- Dual-mode keyring unlock helper:
- 1. systemd ExecStart  (no args)            -> --daemonize (forks, exits 0)
- 2. D-Bus activation   (--foreground arg)   -> --foreground (stays attached,
- owns org.freedesktop.secrets
- AND org.freedesktop.impl.portal.Secret)
- Reads the unlock password from mios.toml [identity].default_password
- and pipes it to gnome-keyring-daemon. The daemon then unlocks (or
- creates) the login keyring + handles ALL bus interfaces for libsecret
- AND the secrets portal -- which is what flatpak apps using the
- modern xdg-desktop-portal Secret API need.
- Operator-flagged 2026-05-12:
- "keyring prompts when launching apps again"  (libsecret-direct path)
- "no Bibata cursor in Flatpaks"                (theme propagation)
- "we need credential saving"                   (portal Secret needs to work)
- Why both modes in one script:
- systemd starts us at WSL boot (proactive unlock so first app launch
- doesn't prompt). D-Bus may ALSO activate us on-demand if a portal
- Secret call beats the systemd unit (race). Same script handles
- both -- --replace ensures only one daemon ever owns the bus name.
- ─── mios.toml resolver ──────────────────────────────────────────────
- Drop-in over the shared layered resolver (usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py via the
- mios-toml-get shell CLI): vendor < host < user overlay, highest wins.
- Standard envs the daemon expects.
- Mode selection:
- $1 == "--foreground" : dbus activation context. Exec the daemon
- in --foreground so dbus sees us own the bus name. Stays attached
- for the lifetime of the daemon.
- otherwise            : systemd context. Use --daemonize so the
- service unit (Type=forking) sees a clean exit + forked bg pid.
- Replace any running daemon (--replace evicts the previous bus owner).
- --foreground keeps us in the dbus activation context.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-kg
- PKG store: PostgreSQL + pgvector via the shared mios-db --pg-json CLI (which
- binds params through mios-pg-query's extended protocol). The legacy BSL 1.1 store is
- retired -- ALL reads + writes go to pg. Natural-key model
- (resolves_to(phrase, app_id)) -- no record-id round-trips.
- Phase C.1 SSOT knobs from mios.toml [pkg].* (via userenv.sh slot
- map). Defaults match the mios.toml seed so a Day-0 deploy with
- no overrides still ingests sensibly.
- ─── bootstrap ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Upsert the person via DELETE + INSERT (cheaper than UPDATE for the
- singleton case + survives schema changes). Natural key = username; values
- are BOUND params.
- Ingest the inventory. Default source is `mios-apps --json`
- (NDJSON of {category, name, description, launch} objects).
- Operator can pass --source <path> or `-` for stdin so this
- CLI is a template -- any tool that emits the same NDJSON shape
- can re-bootstrap the graph (operator directive 2026-05-18:
- "tools/skills are global templates that can be self improved
- upon").
- Parse NDJSON. Aggregate by category so we keep the
- per-source cap.
- Extract app_id from "Display (com.foo.Bar)" suffix in description.
- Pull the parenthesised id from the description tail.
- Idempotent insert into pg app_install (natural key:
- short_name + source). All NDJSON-sourced fields are BOUND params
- -- an embedded apostrophe ("'MiOS' CDI spec ...") needs no escaping.
- ─── alias ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Resolve target: app:<short_name> or bare short_name.
- pg path (natural-key): phrase -> app_id via app_install.short_name.
- Resolve the target's app_id first so we can fail loudly when the
- operator names an app that isn't in the inventory.
- Upsert the alias + its resolves_to edge (delete-then-insert), atomically.
- pg JOIN replaces the legacy `->resolves_to->app_install` graph walk.
- LEFT JOIN so aliases with no edge still list (as "(unresolved)").
- Aggregate resolved targets per phrase into a JSON array of short_names.
- Constant SQL -- no external value.
- ─── lookup ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Exact first; fall back to contains. Run the queries in priority order and
- pick the first non-empty. pg JOINs replace the legacy
- `->resolves_to->app_install` graph walk (same shape the agent-pipe
- kg_lookup uses); each row aggregates its resolved apps into the `app` JSON
- array. `_app_obj` is a CONSTANT projection; `phrase` is a BOUND param ($1).
- Stage 1a: alias EXACT match.
- Stage 1b: alias CONTAINS match (fuzzy fallback).
- Stage 2: direct app_install lookup by short_name substring.
- ─── apps ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── who ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-knowledge-add
- Look up by exact name match. Pre-existing knowledge rows from
- mios-owui-apply-knowledge use a deterministic id; this helper
- uses a fresh uuid for separate collections to avoid colliding.
- Also append to knowledge.data.file_ids so OWUI's UI reflects it.
- --- optional: bind to a model row so the model RAGs over it ---
- Pre-existing model rows the operator might have on this host:
- Auto-include the pipe-derived id too if operator used the
- default. (mios-agent vs mios_agent.mios-agent both ship.)
- OWUI shape: list of {id, name, description} OR list of ids.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-knowledge-search
- ── pgvector knowledge fallback ──────────────────────────────────────
- When the OWUI admin api_key is unreachable (the agent user can't read it and
- granting it is a security-gated change), degrade-open to the LOCAL pgvector
- `knowledge` store (the same MiOS Q+A knowledge `recall` uses) so
- knowledge_search still returns relevant results instead of hard-failing. The
- OWUI-memory backend resumes automatically once a token is available.
- Ensure single quotes in query are escaped for the PL/pgSQL function call
- Independent relevance FLOOR for this degrade-open fallback. The pg
- `knowledge` table holds agent CHAT Q&A memories, NOT the curated doc
- corpus this verb claims to search, so an unrelated query can surface
- low-score off-topic rows (~0.51-0.53 observed) and present them as an
- answer. Gate on max(caller threshold, floor) so an unrelated query
- returns an honest empty result. Tunable via MIOS_KNOWLEDGE_FALLBACK_FLOOR.
- OWUI 0.9.6 returns {"items":[...], "total":N}; older returns a list.
- No match: return verbatim so the OWUI endpoint produces a
- clear "collection not found" error instead of silently using
- the wrong one.
- OWUI nests one level deep when querying multiple collections.
- OWUI admin key unreachable -> degrade-open to the pgvector knowledge
- store so knowledge_search still returns results (helpers above). The
- OWUI-memory backend takes over automatically once a token exists.
- No scope -> search across ALL collections (listed via the OWUI API,
- since the broker can't read webui.db). An empty list searches nothing.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-lan-status
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-lan-status [--enable]
- Inspect (and optionally enable) LAN-side accessibility of MiOS
- service ports. Operator-flagged 2026-05-17: "OWUI doesn't appear
- responsive remotely over LAN/Wifi" -- OWUI binds 0.0.0.0:3033
- inside the WSL2 distro, but Windows-side LAN traffic doesn't reach
- the WSL bridge without a netsh portproxy + Windows Firewall rule.
- The Setup-MiOSLanPortProxy.ps1 helper adds both, but it needs to
- run elevated on Windows.
- Usage:
- mios-lan-status            print state + the one-liner to enable
- mios-lan-status --enable   try to invoke the elevated PS1 helper
- (will UAC-prompt on the operator's screen)
- Exit codes:
- 0 = all ports reachable from the Windows host IP
- 1 = some ports listening locally but not LAN-forwarded
- 2 = listener missing (services not running)
- (port, name) pairs. Keep aligned with Setup-MiOSLanPortProxy.ps1.
- Find the Windows-routable host IP (skip wsl/loopback/docker bridges).
- In WSL2 the operator's Windows machine is reachable via
- the default gateway. /etc/resolv.conf nameserver is the
- WSL host's loopback-translated address; the Windows LAN
- IP is in `ip route get` toward an external addr.
- --- Local listener check ---------------------------------------
- --- One-liner the operator can paste --------------------------
- Translate /usr/libexec/mios path -> Windows form so the operator
- can paste it straight into an elevated terminal.
- --- Optional: try to invoke from here -----------------------------
- mios-windows ps runs the line through the operator-side broker;
- Start-Process -Verb RunAs will trigger UAC (operator must
- confirm on their screen).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-launch
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-launch <name> [args...]
- Universal launcher. Resolves <name> across every available
- environment in priority order:
- 1. Internal-service URL alias (cockpit, owui, hermes, prefilter,
- inference, searxng, forgejo) -> mios-open-url <url>
- 2. URL/IRI literal (http://, https://, file://) -> mios-open-url
- 3. Windows GUI app (notepad, explorer, calc, mspaint, snipping-
- tool, taskmgr, regedit, control, cmd, powershell, pwsh, OR a
- /mnt/c/.../*.exe path) -> mios-windows launch
- 4. MiOS shim (mios-doctor, mios-windows, mios-flatpak-install,
- mios-open-url, mios-skill-clone, mios-tool-clone, ...)
- -> exec the shim directly
- 5. Linux GUI (flatpak app id, fuzzy flatpak match, host RPM with a
- .desktop entry) -> mios-gui
- 6. Plain CLI on PATH -> exec
- If no resolution matches, list candidates from `mios-apps --filter`.
- Operator directive 2026-05-15: "MiOS-Agents should be aware of all
- systems; and be able to launch apps regardless of environment
- (including its own apps and using them too)". mios-apps is the
- discovery half; this is the launch half.
- Refuse empty query: previously a shlex-quoted '' from a kwarg
- mismatch upstream fell through to the games-cache substring scan
- and produced "ambiguous '' -- 10 matches" output that bubbled
- back to the operator as a misleading "doing something failed"
- DAG node. Fail fast instead so the caller sees the empty-arg bug.
- Operator-flagged 2026-05-18.
- ─── 0. mios.toml [mios-find.aliases] role -> concrete app ───────────
- Operator-binding SSOT: when the operator types a freedesktop role
- name ("files", "web", "terminal", "editor"), translate it to the
- concrete app id BEFORE the rest of the resolution chain runs.
- mios-find consults this same table; mios-launch was missing it,
- which is why launch_app("files") returned "no resolution for
- 'files'" even though [mios-find.aliases].files="nautilus" was set.
- Shared layered mios.toml resolver (vendor < host < user), path injected as argv[1].
- Normalised lookup key: lowercase, collapse whitespace to single
- hyphens. Lets "File Explorer", "file_explorer", "FILE-EXPLORER"
- match the same SSOT row.
- Strip "my " / "the " possessives so "my web browser" -> "web-browser"
- normalised, then drop word "browser" tail to hit role match.
- Also try the LAST word of multi-word input ("my web browser" -> "browser",
- "the file explorer" -> "explorer") so role-only names hit.
- Merged layered read (vendor < host < user, highest wins) via the shared resolver.
- ── Role-aware fallback: consult [[desktop.apps]] for the default app of a
- role. SPECIFIC-APP-BEFORE-ROLE (operator 2026-06-19 "open edge browser
- opened zen randomly"): when the input is "<specific> <role>" (e.g. "edge
- browser"), the LAST word is a role but the HEAD names a SPECIFIC app --
- resolve the head downstream (-> Microsoft Edge) instead of the role default
- (-> the operator's default browser, Zen). The role default fires ONLY for a
- BARE role ("browser", "my browser") whose head is empty or itself a role.
- SSOT = mios.toml; NO hardcoded English app-name mappings.
- "<specific> <role>" -> resolve the SPECIFIC head downstream, not the role.
- Bare role -> the operator's default app for that role.
- Preserve the user's ACTUAL term BEFORE the Linux freedesktop alias rewrites
- it. A Linux-role alias (step 0, e.g. calculator->gnome-calculator) must NOT
- poison the GENERATIVE resolvers below: on WSL the live mios-apps inventory +
- the Windows side know "Calculator", not the absent Linux app id. So the
- desc-chain (7) and the Windows fallback (7b) ALSO try this original term --
- generative detection from the live environment, no hardcoded app list
- (operator 2026-06-04: "no hardcodes for application detections").
- ─── WS-D: App-type resolution ───────────────────────────────────────
- ─── 1. Internal-service URL alias ───────────────────────────────────
- Ports from SSOT: install.env bridges mios.toml [ports] -> MIOS_PORT_*.
- Hardcoded literals here silently break when [ports] is renumbered (T-120/T-121).
- Guard set -u: a value with shell-metachars must not abort under set -u.
- ─── 2. URL / URI literal ────────────────────────────────────────────
- http / https / file / chrome / about -> open in the default browser
- via mios-open-url (the canonical opener). Any OTHER scheme (steam://,
- epicgames://, uplay://, ms-xbox-game://, vscode://, slack://, etc.)
- is delegated to mios-windows launch -- it already dispatches ANY URI
- through Windows Start-Process which invokes the registered protocol
- handler. Don't maintain a hardcoded list of game-launcher schemes
- here; mios-windows is the universal URI dispatcher.
- ─── 2b. PREFLIGHT: already running? -> raise to foreground + succeed ─
- Operator 2026-05-20 + 2026-05-29: launching an ALREADY-RUNNING app made the
- attempt "fail" (no NEW window) even though it's on-screen; the operator wants
- an already-open app FOCUSED + brought to the foreground (+centered) instead.
- RELIABLE + GENERATIVE detection (research 2026-05-29: flatpak apps are a
- first-class discovery surface keyed by reverse-DNS app-id via `flatpak ps`/
- `flatpak list`): query the RUNNING flatpak instances and fuzzy-match NAME to
- an app-id. The old mios-window-active probe was WSLg-unreliable here. Because
- flatpak instances are PER-USER and this preflight runs in the broker (root)
- context, query flatpak AS THE OPERATOR (same escape the close path uses).
- If a match is running, RAISE it -- `flatpak run <app-id>` on a single-instance
- GApplication activates/foregrounds the existing window -- and report
- already_running:true so the verify treats "no new window" as success.
- Bypass with MIOS_LAUNCH_NO_PREFLIGHT=1 (force a fresh instance).
- Raise the existing window to the foreground (single-instance activate),
- in the operator's WSLg session, then center it (best-effort).
- ─── 2c. PREFLIGHT (Windows): app already open? -> focus + succeed ────
- operator 2026-06-04: re-launching an ALREADY-RUNNING Windows app (Everything,
- Task Manager, a browser, ...) opens no NEW window, so the agent-pipe verify
- polled out + reported "not opened" though it's on-screen. The in-session
- executor (:11437) /windows enumerates the REAL desktop with app-name-bearing
- titles (native Windows windows carry their name, unlike WSLg), so match the
- request to an existing window, FOCUS it (mios-window focus -> executor
- /window/focus), and emit already_running:true -- the agent-pipe honours that
- as success (no duplicate launch, honest "already open"). Generative: the live
- window list is the SoT, no app-name table. Inert off-WSL / when no executor
- endpoint is set. Bypass with MIOS_LAUNCH_NO_PREFLIGHT=1. Window JSON passed by
- env (not stdin) so it can't collide with `python3 -`'s heredoc script.
- Read the executor endpoint from the layered toml. GUARD each file with
- `[ -r ]` + `|| true`: awk on a MISSING file exits 2 (even with 2>/dev/null
- the EXIT CODE survives), which under `set -e` aborts the whole launcher --
- and /etc/mios/mios.toml is an OPTIONAL overlay, absent until bootstrap (or
- the operator) writes it (operator 2026-06-07: a missing /etc overlay made
- EVERY launch exit 2 before reaching resolution).
- Skip browser tabs that merely MENTION the app in a page title (OWUI etc.)
- ─── 3. Windows GUI (GENERATIVE -- NO hardcoded app-name list) ───────
- operator 2026-05-29: "NO HARDCODES". A baked-in English allowlist of
- Windows builtins (notepad|calc|taskmgr|...) is exactly the anti-pattern.
- Route to the Windows side ONLY on GENERATIVE signals, then let WINDOWS
- (Start-Process resolving via the App Paths registry + System32 -- i.e. the
- REAL Windows install) resolve the concrete target:
- * a /mnt/c/...exe path                    -- an unambiguous Windows binary
- * an explicit "windows "/"win " qualifier -- the request named a Win app
- * a ".exe" suffix                         -- a Windows executable by name
- Everything ELSE falls through to LINUX-FIRST resolution below (operator
- preference). Names only Windows knows (Task Manager, regedit, ...) are still
- found generatively by the mios-apps desc-chain (step 7), which inventories
- windows-app / windows-gui entries from the LIVE environment -- no list here.
- Strip the qualifier/suffix; hand the bare name to Windows to resolve.
- ─── 3a. Browser (chromedev with CDP) ────────────────────────────────
- Hermes's browser_* tools all connect to a Chrome instance with
- --remote-debugging-port=9222. The bare `flatpak run com.google.
- ChromeDev` path leaves CDP unexposed -- mios-chrome wraps the
- flatpak launch with the right Wayland args + --remote-debugging-
- port=9222 + a persistent --user-data-dir so the operator AND Hermes
- drive the SAME browser instance (shared cookies, shared logged-in
- state). Dispatched through the launcher broker because the agent
- uid (mios-hermes) has NO WAYLAND_DISPLAY -- the broker runs in
- user@<uid>.service with the operator's full WSLg env so the window
- actually surfaces. Operator-flagged 2026-05-17: "make sure it
- opens the actual chromedev instance graphically for the user to
- watch".
- Fire-and-forget single-line dispatch; broker replies OK + detaches.
- ─── 3a. App-specific launcher override (SSOT-driven) ────────────────
- Some flatpak apps need a wrapper launcher (e.g. mios-chrome wraps
- com.google.ChromeDev with --remote-debugging-port=9222 so Hermes's
- browser_* tools can connect via CDP). Each [[desktop.apps]] entry
- can declare `launcher = "<shim>"`; when the resolved app id has one,
- we dispatch through it instead of bare `flatpak run`. NO hardcoded
- English mappings in this file -- the override list comes from
- mios.toml SSOT. Operator binding 2026-05-19.
- Shared layered mios.toml resolver (vendor < host < user), path injected as argv[1].
- ─── 3a2. WINDOWS executor FIRST ─────────────────────────────────────
- Operator binding 2026-06-17: "We want windows native apps to ALWAYS have precedence."
- Try Windows resolution BEFORE Linux flatpak/RPM/CLI. `mios-windows launch` posts
- to the OS-control executor which checks Start Menu/App Paths. If it resolves, it
- launches the real Windows app and exits 0. If not, it returns non-zero fast and
- we fall through to the Linux resolution below.
- ─── 3aa. Exact .exe lookup via Everything CLI ───────────────────────
- For launcher / client names that don't live in the Windows-GUI
- builtin allowlist (notepad/calc/etc.) but DO ship as a single
- canonical .exe on Windows -- steam.exe, discord.exe, spotify.exe,
- epicgameslauncher.exe, slack.exe, etc. -- query the live filesystem
- (via Everything CLI: mios-everything -ext exe <name>) and prefer an
- EXACT basename match. This is generative-of-environment: the path
- comes from the operator's actual install, not a hardcoded mapping.
- Operator directive 2026-05-18: "Detected hardcoded variable!!! NOT
- GENERATIVE OF THE ACTUAL ENVIRONMENT/OFFLINE FIRST" -- this step
- fixes the case where `launch steam` previously fell through to
- the MiOS shim `mios-steamcmd` instead of resolving the actual
- operator-installed Steam client.
- Only acts on UNAMBIGUOUS matches (exactly one path whose basename
- equals "<name>.exe" case-insensitively). Multiple matches +
- multiple drives = ambiguity -> fall through to games-cache, which
- has display-name priority + can prompt the operator.
- Query "<name>.exe" as a substring -- mios-everything's `-ext exe`
- filter relies on Everything's `ext:exe` colon-syntax which returns
- empty on some Everything CLI versions (operator-confirmed 2026-05-18
- on Everything 1.5+: `steam ext:exe` returned 0 hits while bare
- `steam.exe` returned the canonical C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\
- steam.exe path). Falling through to the bare substring is more
- portable + gives us all candidates whose path contains "<name>.exe"
- which the awk filter below narrows to basename-exact matches.
- Filter to paths whose basename (lowercased, sans .exe) == NAME.
- Drops noise like <name>.exe.old, STEAM.EXE-XXX.pf (Windows
- prefetch), etc. -- those have a trailing suffix that survives
- the .exe$ sub() and so don't match $n.
- Count non-empty lines (a path is just a non-empty string at
- this point; previous heuristic used `grep -c '/\|\\\\'` to
- require either a forward-slash or backslash anchor but the
- bash double-quoting + grep BRE-alternation collapsed
- silently to "0 matches" on real Windows-only-backslash paths,
- which is the operator-observed bug).
- ─── 3b. Windows games inventory (Steam/Epic/Xbox/Microsoft Store) ───
- mios-apps writes /var/lib/mios/agent-env/windows-games.cache with
- one line per detected installed game: "Display Name|launch-cmd".
- Resolves fuzzy substrings -- "beamng" matches "BeamNG.drive";
- "marvel" matches "Marvel Rivals". Single hit -> launch.
- Multiple hits -> list and exit so the model can disambiguate.
- All three shapes converge through mios-windows launch:
- * URI (steam://, epicgames://, etc.) -- Start-Process dispatch
- * /mnt/c/.../*.exe or *.lnk -- direct exec via interop
- * full `mios-windows launch ...` command line -- already shaped
- TD-1: eval-safe, input=internal games cache formatted commands (e.g. mios-windows launch ...), not agent-controlled
- ─── 4. MiOS shim ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── 5. WSL Windows-host: in-session executor with the CLEAN name FIRST ──────
- operator 2026-06-07: "open notepad" must open WINDOWS Notepad, not the wine
- wrapper. MUST run BEFORE the Plain-CLI section below: a same-named Linux/wine
- shim on PATH (there IS a `notepad` wine wrapper) would otherwise `exec` first and
- shadow the Windows app. The in-session executor (mios-oscontrol-server.ps1) does
- Windows-native resolution (Start Menu / App Paths) -- "notepad" -> Windows Notepad
- -- and returns FAST (fired:false, ~0s) for names with no Windows app, so Linux-only
- names fall straight through to the Plain-CLI + inventory sections. We hit /launch
- DIRECTLY (not full `mios-windows launch`) to skip its slow Start-Menu/Everything
- fallbacks, and pass the CLEAN original name (NOT the inventory's flaky windows-app
- AppX-GUID whose interop Start-Process can hang). Reachable over the WSL gateway
- with Tailscale OFF. Real Linux GUI flatpaks are already caught at section 4 above.
- ─── 5b. Linux GUI (delegate the shim/flatpak/host-RPM resolution to mios-gui) ─
- mios-gui already does all three steps with .desktop-presence as the
- host-RPM gating signal. Only call it if we have something it might
- actually handle.
- ─── 6. Plain CLI ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- operator 2026-06-14 ("everything is native"; flagged the wine launch a
- LIE): a Windows-only app name (notepad, mspaint, ...) resolves on PATH
- to a WINE wrapper -- e.g. /usr/sbin/notepad -> /usr/bin/wine64 -- when
- the in-session Windows executor (section 5b) is DOWN. exec'ing it opens
- the wine LOOK-ALIKE, not the native Windows app. Detect a wine-backed
- binary GENERATIVELY (the resolved real path is/lives-in wine; NO
- hardcoded app list) and, on WSL where the Windows-native interop
- fallback (7b) exists, SKIP it so the REAL Windows app launches via
- interop instead. A genuine Linux CLI (htop, jq, ...) is not wine and
- execs normally; Linux GUI flatpaks were already caught at section 5.
- do NOT exec; fall through to section 7b (mios-windows launch -> native interop)
- ─── 7. Description-fallback via mios-apps inventory ─────────────────
- Walk the full app inventory (mios-apps --json) and match against
- the description / display-name (not just the app-id short). This
- catches cases like "files" -> Nautilus.Devel (whose .desktop Name=
- is "Files" but app-id-last-segment is "Devel"). Rank candidates
- by category priority: linux-flatpak > linux-rpm-gui > linux-cli >
- windows-app > windows-gui (Linux-native wins over WSL-interop).
- The top match's `launch` field is exec'd via eval (the launch line
- is a verb call like `mios-gui devel` or `mios-windows ps "..."`).
- Returns one launch line per stdout line, ranked from best to
- worst. Caller iterates: try each in order, fall through to the
- next when one fails. Generalizes the browser fallback chain
- (already in mios-open-url) to ALL launches.
- Also match the user's ORIGINAL term (pre Linux-alias) so a role alias that
- points at an absent Linux app still resolves the real app from the LIVE
- inventory -- generative, Linux-first, no hardcoded app list.
- Category priority (lower = better). SSOT: mios.toml [os_control].
- launch_category_priority (a list; index = rank), /etc overlay winning over
- vendor. Default prefers NATIVE Windows apps over the wine wrapper on a Windows
- host -- operator 2026-06-07: "open notepad" must open Windows Notepad, not the
- wine notepad. Falls back to the built-in order if the toml is unreadable;
- unknown categories sort last (PRIORITY.get(cat, 9) below).
- Match quality: 0=exact name, 1=name substring, 2=description substring.
- Sort by (category_priority, match_quality) so Linux-native
- wins over Windows even on exact-name matches.
- De-duplicate launch lines while preserving order.
- Iterate the chain: try each launch line; on failure, fall
- through to the next. WSL flatpak portal env-fd bug for the
- primary linux-flatpak entry (e.g. Nautilus.Devel) cascades
- to the next fallback (rpm-gui or windows-app) without the
- operator having to retry. Same pattern as mios-open-url's
- browser chain.
- set-e-SAFE: run the candidate inside an `if` so a FAILING candidate
- (e.g. `mios-gui wine-notepad` exits 1) does NOT abort the whole script
- under `set -e` (operator 2026-05-29: "Open Notepad on Windows" died at
- try 1 + never tried the next candidate / the Windows fallback -- the
- bare `eval` tripped set -e). Now a miss just advances to the next
- candidate, and after all Linux candidates fail we reach the Windows
- generative fallback below.
- TD-1: Replace unsafe eval with shlex split to prevent command injection of agent-controlled input
- fall through to the Windows generative fallback below (don't exit yet)
- ─── 7b. Windows generative fallback ─────────────────────────────────────
- Handled at step 3a2.
- ─── No resolution -- show candidates ────────────────────────────────

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-launcher-daemon
- /run/mios-launcher/launcher.sock is the canonical path. Why not /tmp:
- hermes-agent.service has PrivateTmp=true -> the agent's terminal
- tool sees its own private /tmp namespace and can't reach a
- socket placed in the host's /tmp at all (operator-confirmed
- regression 2026-05-15: agent saw "PowerShell not at..." even
- after broker socket was bind-confirmed at /tmp because its
- PrivateTmp namespace had no such file). /run is NOT affected
- by PrivateTmp; both the operator's broker AND the agent's
- private-tmp shell see the same /run/mios-launcher/launcher.sock.
- /run/mios/ is created at boot by /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/
- mios-launcher.conf (mode 0755 root:root so all uids can
- traverse); the socket file itself carries mode 0666.
- Capture-mode (CAPTURE / CAPTURE_JSON) subprocess timeout. Raised from a
- hardcoded 45s + made env-configurable (WS-4) so slow SYNCHRONOUS verbs --
- docgen via LibreOffice cold-start (~60s), package installs -- aren't killed
- mid-run. A hung verb is still bounded. env MIOS_LAUNCHER_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_S
- (default 120). Fire-and-forget dispatch (the other protocol) is unaffected.
- Protocol:
- <command>             -> fire-and-forget; reply "OK\n"
- CAPTURE: <command>    -> run synchronously; capture stdout+stderr
- CONCATENATED as bytes (legacy form;
- kept for backward compat).
- CAPTURE_JSON: <command> -> run synchronously; reply with a
- single-line JSON object:
- {"stdout":"...","stderr":"...","exit_code":N}
- Lets the agent envelope split stdout
- from stderr cleanly -- English narrative
- from downstream tools (mios-find, mios-
- launch, ...) buckets into the stderr
- field instead of mixing with the
- tool_result.output structured data.
- CAPTURE removes the cross-user tempfile dance: broker runs the
- command in its own context, captures via subprocess.PIPE, sends
- the bytes back to the caller. No file in /tmp or /run/mios-
- launcher/ that another user has to write to. Operator-debug
- 2026-05-15 found that mios cross-user-write to a mios-hermes-
- owned mode 0666 file fails -- root cause unknown, fix unneeded
- via this protocol.
- Send as a single JSON line for unambiguous parsing.
- stderr concatenated after stdout (single capture stream).
- Override env per-dispatch:
- GDK_BACKEND=wayland: /etc/profile.d/mios-wslg.sh sets x11
- by default (operator-pinned for compat). Wayland is
- required for libadwaita dark theme rendering on flatpaks
- like Nautilus.Devel; without it, apps fall back to
- unthemed X11 even though GTK_THEME / ADW_DEBUG_COLOR_
- SCHEME are set in the operator's user@992 env (operator-
- confirmed regression 2026-05-15: "Nautilus has OLD GTK
- AGAIN").
- Per-dispatch log -- BEST-EFFORT, must NEVER block the launch. The
- daemon runs as the operator (uid 992) and CANNOT create under
- /var/log (root-owned); the old StateDirectory= assumption is gone, so
- os.makedirs("/var/log/mios-launcher") raised Permission denied and
- aborted the WHOLE dispatch -> no app ever launched (operator
- 2026-06-21 "open notepad" -> broker logged "dispatch: notepad.exe"
- then died "Permission denied: /var/log/mios-launcher"). Log to the
- operator-writable runtime dir, and fall back to DEVNULL on ANY error
- so the app still launches. install-robustness 2026-06-21.
- Cleanup stale socket; mode 0666 so cross-user connects work.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-locate
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-locate <query> [-n <max>] [-ext <csv>] [-path <subtree>] [-type f|d]
- Linux-side filesystem search shim -- the agentic peer to mios-everything
- (which is Windows-only via Voidtools Everything CLI). Operator directive
- 2026-05-18: "MiOS-Agent(s) can navigate, search, exec--all the same in
- the Linux Environments as well".
- Backend resolution (fastest first):
- 1. plocate (the modern locate; sub-100ms on indexed trees)
- 2. locate  (mlocate compat)
- 3. find    (universal POSIX fallback; slower but always present)
- Default search scope (when -path is not given) is the operator-facing
- Linux FHS surface: /usr /etc /var/lib /opt /home /root /var/log
- /var/lib/mios /usr/share/mios. Skips /proc /sys /run /dev /tmp
- /mnt /var/cache /var/tmp by default to avoid noise + WSL DrvFs.
- Returns one absolute path per line on stdout. Exit 0 with match(es);
- exit 1 on no-match. English narratives go to stderr (suppressed by
- the OWUI dispatch via 2>/dev/null) so tool_result.output stays clean.
- --json flag (task #148): emit a structured envelope so the agent
- reads typed fields. Re-exec ourselves without the flag, capture
- stdout+stderr+exit, then wrap.
- Rebuild the non-json args list. PATHS array becomes -path args.
- Default search scope. Operator-tunable later via mios.toml [paths].locate_roots.
- Filter the path list to those that actually exist (skip silently).
- ─── Backend selection ────────────────────────────────────────────────
- plocate / locate query the whole indexed FS; we filter by path-prefix
- in awk afterward. find walks the tree directly.
- Stdin: one path per line from the upstream backend (plocate / locate
- / find). Apply: path-prefix include, ext filter, type filter, query
- substring (case-insensitive). Then head -n MAX.
- NB: must use `python3 -c "<script>"` and NOT `python3 - <<PYEOF`.
- The heredoc-as-script form redirects python's stdin to the
- heredoc content, so the piped upstream output never reaches
- sys.stdin (operator-debug 2026-05-18 -- queries returned
- "no match" because the find output was lost to the heredoc).
- Drain the rest of stdin so the upstream backend (plocate/locate/find)
- finishes writing instead of getting SIGPIPE -> exit 141 under
- `set -o pipefail` (the bug that made fs_search return 141 + no output).
- Try plocate first.
- Try locate (mlocate).
- Find fallback. Universal but slower. Run across the EXISTING_PATHS
- with prune for noise dirs. -iname matches case-insensitively on
- basename. Type filter applied here for efficiency.
- Pipe find output through the same filter for consistent ext/limit semantics.
- `|| true`: find exits non-zero when ANY root is unreadable (e.g. /root for the
- non-root broker user) EVEN AFTER printing matches from readable roots -- under
- `set -e` + `pipefail` that killed the script before the results were emitted
- (fs_search returned empty as mios-ai while working as root). The empty-check
- below still reports a genuine no-match. operator 2026-06-10.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-login-account
- Resolution order (degrade-open, so a stale display name never appears):
- 1. pgvector `person` singleton (the operator account) -- the intended DB source.
- 2. pgvector `account` real user row (kind=user, excluding ephemeral
- mios-cli-* session rows) -- the account control plane.
- 3. the live primary human system account (lowest uid in [1000,65000) with a
- real login shell) -- what the OS actually provisioned.
- 4. the vendor default `user`.
- The operator DISPLAY name ([user].name / MIOS_USER) is DELIBERATELY never
- consulted: it is a display label, not a login account, and must not land in a
- credential slot. Full DB<->OS account control is WS-ACCT (T-150..T-153).
- Usage:  mios-login-account          -> the login account NAME
- mios-login-account password -> the advertised login password
- Advertised login password = the fresh-seed convention (initial password
- equals the account name), which the dashboard shows as a first-boot HINT.
- We deliberately do NOT read any stored secret: passwords live hashed
- (account.password_hash, WS-ACCT), never plaintext, and a dashboard must
- never materialize a credential. Once an operator personalizes their
- password they already know it, so the hint is only meaningful on a fresh
- vendor seed -- where it correctly reads "<name>/<name>".

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-mcp-server
- Streamable-HTTP session id. The relay is stateless (it just dispatches
- verbs), but the MCP spec lets a server assign a session at initialize, and
- strict clients (Hermes treats a missing/empty Mcp-Session-Id as a FATAL
- session fault and abandons the connection -- issue #13383) require a
- non-empty value. One id per server process is sufficient.
- Version negotiation (MCP lifecycle): this relay is version-agnostic -- it only
- lists verbs + dispatches, using no revision-specific features -- so it HONORS the
- client's requested protocolVersion when present (liberal-in: an older client
- agrees on its own revision and is never forced to abort) and otherwise advertises
- the declared current revision (strict-out).
- tools.listChanged=True: the background refresher pushes
- notifications/tools/list_changed over the standalone SSE channel when the
- catalog recovers (SSOT floor / degraded set -> full surface), so clients that
- honor it (Hermes) re-list mid-session instead of staying degraded for life.
- resources.listChanged stays False (no resource watcher yet).
- Last-good tools/list cache. tools/list proxies agent-pipe /v1/verbs (/v1/tools);
- when agent-pipe is momentarily down (a restart), an UNCACHED relay returns 0 tools
- -> a fresh Hermes/OpenCode session registers NO MiOS tools and stays toolless for
- its ENTIRE life (MCP tools load only at session start, no mid-session reload). That
- is exactly the recurring "desktop app can't launch/type" failure (operator
- 2026-06-15). Caching the catalog (mem + disk) lets the relay ride out the blip.
- Must live under the unit's ReadWritePaths (mios-mcp.service: ProtectSystem=strict
- + ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/mios/mcp) -- /var/lib/mios/agent-env is sandbox-blocked.
- Resilience tunables. A background thread keeps the catalog warm (mem+disk) every
- _REFRESH_INTERVAL_S, INDEPENDENT of when a client connects -- so a client that
- handshakes moments after an agent-pipe restart still receives the full last-good
- set instead of the empty/partial catalog agent-pipe serves mid-warmup. The
- per-request tools/list fetch uses a SHORT timeout so a hung/slow agent-pipe can
- never stall the client's handshake; the warm cache covers the gap.
- Open standalone-SSE connections (the GET /mcp channel). Each holds a private
- threading.Event; the background refresher SETS every event on catalog recovery,
- and each connection's own do_GET loop wakes, writes notifications/tools/list_changed,
- and resumes keepalive. All socket writes happen in the owning handler thread -- the
- refresher only signals -- so there are no cross-thread writes to one socket. This is
- how an ALREADY-CONNECTED client (Hermes honors tools/list_changed, auto-re-lists
- mid-session) recovers the full catalog after connecting during an outage, with no
- app restart.
- /v1/tools is the UNIFIED capability feed: every verb + every OS recipe +
- every promoted skill. It is served in OpenAI function-tool shape
- ({type:function, function:{name,description,parameters}}); MCP tools/list
- REQUIRES {name, description, inputSchema}. Convert here so strict MCP
- clients (Hermes, Claude Desktop, Cursor) parse the full surface -- without
- this the tools arrive nameless and unusable. A row already in MCP shape
- (top-level `name`) passes through untouched.
- SHORT timeout: a hung/slow agent-pipe must never stall the client's
- handshake -- the warm cache (kept fresh by the background refresher)
- covers the gap.
- agent-pipe momentarily down/slow. Returning 0 tools would leave a fresh
- session PERMANENTLY toolless (MCP tools load once at session start, no
- mid-session reload). Serve the last-good warm cache across the blip.
- Cold cache AND agent-pipe down: build the verb+recipe FLOOR straight from
- mios.toml so a client is NEVER handed zero tools (it would be toolless for
- its whole life -- the recurring "can't launch/type" failure).
- agent-pipe can answer 200 with an EMPTY/partial catalog for a few seconds after
- a restart (verb catalog still loading). The catalog only grows in normal use, so
- an empty or >50%-shrunk live feed => warmup, not a real removal: serve the
- last-good cache instead. (A genuine large reduction lands via a rebuild, which
- restarts this server and re-seeds the cache.) Closes the restart toolless window.
- Route by name prefix -- the SAME mangling the unified /v1/tools feed
- applies. mios_skill__<name> executes via the skill runner; a
- mios_recipe__<name> wraps the opaque os_recipe verb; a bare name is a
- plain verb. All three land on the launcher-broker path eventually, but
- via the correct endpoint/envelope. Discover at /v1/tools, execute here.
- MCP wraps tool results as content blocks. We surface the JSON
- envelope as a single text block; modern clients (Claude Desktop,
- Cursor) parse JSON-shaped text content automatically.
- /v1/resources is the COMPLETE read-only surface: every verb (script),
- every recipe, and EVERY skill (promoted AND not), as MCP Resources --
- the progressive-disclosure half of the catalog. Browse here; fetch via
- resources/read. The curated CALLABLE half is tools/list. (operator
- 2026-06-04 "port all skills/tools/recipes/scripts to MCP")
- MCP resource-not-found is -32002.
- Notifications carry no id and expect no response.
- ── Streamable-HTTP transport (MCP spec §transports) ─────────────────────────
- A stdio server cannot be a standalone daemon -- with no client on stdin it
- reads EOF and exits. This transport lets mios-mcp.service actually SERVE the
- verb relay as a persistent service. Bound to 127.0.0.1 ONLY: tools/call
- dispatches MiOS verbs, so unauthenticated tailnet exposure is deliberately
- withheld until an auth gate ships (operator no-live-launch rule).
- POST a JSON-RPC request -> application/json response (with an Mcp-Session-Id
- assigned at initialize); GET /mcp -> an idle keepalive SSE stream so strict
- clients that open the server->client channel during the handshake don't hang;
- GET /health for liveness. Stdlib only (offline-safe).
- Assign a session id on initialize so strict clients get a non-empty
- Mcp-Session-Id (the relay itself is stateless).
- Streamable-HTTP standalone SSE stream (server->client). This tools-only
- relay emits no server-initiated messages, but strict clients (Hermes's
- streamable_http client) OPEN this stream during the handshake and HANG
- then abandon if it 405s -- so hold an idle, keepalive'd event stream
- open instead of refusing it. Per-connection thread (ThreadingHTTPServer
- + daemon_threads), reaped when the client disconnects.
- Register so the refresher can wake this connection to push
- notifications/tools/list_changed; otherwise emit a keepalive every 15s.
- Transport select: HTTP (persistent daemon, via the service) vs stdio
- (a client spawns us as a subprocess and talks over our stdin/stdout).
- Warm the catalog (disk last-good, else mios.toml SSOT floor) BEFORE
- serving, then keep it warm in the background -- so tools/list is never
- empty/partial regardless of how soon a client connects after a restart.
- Line-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-md

- (MIT, ~1 KB) -- zero CDN, zero telemetry, runs entirely in the
- browser.
- OWUI already renders markdown emitted by the agent inline; this
- shim covers the OTHER direction: a dedicated window where the
- operator types / pastes markdown and sees rendered markup live.

- markdown to markup text". OWUI-side: polish pass now emits bare
- markdown (no ```markdown fence) so chat renders properly. THIS
- shim is the standalone surface for ad-hoc editing.

- directly from WSL; the ?text= query carries the markdown payload.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-model-router
- Compute nodes. cpu = orchestrator host (always up, CPU-only); light(dGPU)+igpu =
- fast worker nodes; heavy(SGLang) is usually down (VRAM) -> simply never healthy.
- logical model -> (mode, ordered lane names). failover = preference order;
- roundrobin = rotate per request so concurrent children spread across nodes.
- NOTE (2026-06-08 measured): the tool-laden requests Hermes sends (~17K tokens of
- 113 MCP tools) are ONLY fast on the dGPU (4090, 2.2s); CPU/iGPU are ~100 tok/s ->
- 169-180s+ and time out. So with a single fast GPU, delegated children must PREFER
- the dGPU and SERIALIZE there (2s each, prefix-cached) rather than scatter across
- slow nodes (180s each). True cross-node parallelism needs per-child tool-surface
- reduction (AIOS Context Manager) so children are small enough for the slow lanes —
- a follow-up. Until then fanout is failover(light-first), not roundrobin.
- GAMING MODE: when ON, the front door (mios-orchestrator / default) must NOT touch
- the RTX 4090 (a chat turn would stutter the game). The CPU node never touches it
- (and the iGPU is a separate GPU), so route there instead — slow (~169s on the tool
- surface) but contention-free. dGPU(light) stays only as an absolute last resort if
- both are down. Toggle via POST /gaming {"on":true|false} (off by default); from
- Windows: curl 127.0.0.1:11442/gaming -d '{"on":true}'. Wire it to your game launcher.
- Gaming mode reroutes the front door + delegated children off the dGPU
- (see GAMING_FRONT note). mios-cpu/mios-heavy keep their explicit routes.
