## usr/libexec/mios/mios-open-url
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-open-url <url> [<browser-override>]
- Open a URL in the MiOS-defined default browser. Operator directive
- 2026-05-16: "WRONG BROWSER!!!! NOT THE GLOBALLY DEFINED LINUX
- DEFAULTS FROM THE USER SPECIFIED mios.toml/html" -- this used to
- hardcode chromedev as the default, which routed URLs through the
- operator's Windows-side default browser via WSL interop instead
- of the MiOS-defined Linux default.
- Resolution order for the default browser (high precedence first):
- 1. <browser-override>  if passed as $2 (operator-tunable per-call)
- 2. mios.toml [[desktop.apps]] entry with role="browser" + default=true
- 3. mios.toml [mios-find.aliases].web
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: "Should be understood from the
- source that defines all global settings(mios.toml/html)" -- NO
- compiled fallback to a specific app name. If mios.toml defines
- no default browser, this script ERRORS so the operator knows to
- pick one via mios.html. Silent-default-to-some-name is a bug.
- The URL is passed through to mios-gui <resolved-default> "$URL"
- which dispatches via flatpak-launch into the operator's WSLg
- session. Window appears on the operator's desktop, NOT in the
- headless Hermes-Agent CDP browser.
- ── Native launch args (from the open_url verb schema) + back-compat positional
- <url> [<browser-override>]. mode/private/reuse drive tab-vs-window: the URL is
- opened as a TAB in the ALREADY-RUNNING browser by default (reuse the instance),
- never a new window. NO-HARDCODE: the per-browser flags come from mios.toml. ──
- Effective disposition: private overrides; reuse=false forces a fresh instance.
- A literal "default" / "operator default" / "system" / "none" is NOT a browser
- id -- it means "use the mios.toml-defined Linux default chain". Treating it as
- an app id made mios-gui try to launch a bogus flatpak
- "org.fedoraproject.Platform.CL.default" -> bwrap execvp /bin/sh failure
- (operator 2026-05-27). Normalise these sentinels to empty so the resolved
- Linux-native browser chain is used (Linux apps are always the first default).
- Quick sanity: warn (not error) if it doesn't look like a URL.
- ─── Resolve the browser FALLBACK CHAIN from mios.toml ──────────────
- SSOT: mios.toml [[desktop.apps]] entries with role="browser". The
- default=true entry leads; the rest follow in declaration order.
- Caller iterates the chain on launch failure -- when Epiphany hits
- the WSLg portal env-fd error (operator-flagged trace 2026-05-18),
- the next browser (ChromeDev, then Windows-side host) gets a shot.
- MiOS is Linux-native first. Browser chain reads [[desktop.apps]]
- role=browser in declaration order (defaults first). Windows-side
- fallback (cmd.exe /c start) is the LAST resort -- appended only
- at the tail by mios-open-url's runtime loop, NOT prepended.
- Operator binding: "always prefer Linux native apps first."
- Pass 1: defaults first (preserve declaration order)
- Pass 2: non-defaults
- mios-find.aliases.web as tail fallback (legacy operator config)
- Resolve the native tab/window flag(s) for a browser target + mode from the SSOT
- [browser.*] map. Empty when unknown (degrade-open: the running instance opens a
- tab by default when the binary is invoked with the URL). NO-HARDCODE.
- Additional role="browser" entries form the fallback chain
- in declaration order.
- would propagate python json-parse failures as exit-1.
- Iterate the fallback chain. First browser that lands a presented
- window wins. Each attempt: launch -> wait -> verify presented.
- Heal-on-failure once after the FIRST flatpak failure (covers the
- stale portal env-fd / dbus credentials case); subsequent chain
- entries get their own launch attempt without re-healing.
- Native disposition flag (tab reuses the running instance; SSOT [browser.*]).
- ─── Already running CDP browser shortcut ───
- Try local CDP port first if responding
- cmd.exe start delegates to the Windows default browser's protocol
- handler, which reuses the running instance -> opens a TAB already.
- shellcheck disable=SC2086  # $_FLAG deliberately word-splits into flag tokens
- shellcheck disable=SC2086
- Poll the window verifier up to ~15s with progressive delays.
- WSLg flatpak cold-launches register a Win32 window via the
- weston RDP rail AFTER bwrap unpack + GTK4 init + Wayland surface
- bind + RDP frame -- empirically 5-12s on first launch (faster on
- warm). A single immediate check (the prior implementation)
- caught only fast launches; slow ones reported "no-window" while
- the window actually rendered seconds later. Operator-flagged
- 2026-05-19: "in the end it DID actually open it in ChromeDev"
- despite mios-open-url declaring EXHAUSTED chain.
- PID-PROBE verification (operator 2026-05-30: "just probe PIDs for verifying
- success"). WSLg windows are NOT enumerable here (no wmctrl/xdotool), so the
- mios-window-active check above false-fails even when the browser opened. So
- confirm the flatpak's PROCESS is RUNNING instead -- a live instance means the
- app launched on the WSLg desktop. Linux is the DEFAULT; fall through to the
- next browser / Windows last-resort only when NOTHING is running.
- PID probe against the GLOBAL process table. The flatpak runs as the
- operator (uid != agent uid), so neither `flatpak ps` (per-user) nor
- `mios-as-operator flatpak ps` (a fire-and-forget LAUNCHER that returns
- NO stdout -- it dispatches detached) can see it. But /proc is global,
- so pgrep finds the operator's process from any agent context. Match
- the full app-id (present in the bwrap'd flatpak app path) then the
- trailing segment / binary name as a looser fallback. Backoff loop
- because GTK4 apps take a moment to fork the real process in.
- If the browser was already running, and we opened a tab, we don't expect a new window to open.
- So if the process is still alive and mios-gui succeeded (rc=0) or returned unconfirmed (rc=3),
- we treat it as success immediately.
- First-failure heal: when launch_rc != 0 (sandbox bootstrap
- broke), restart the user-side portal stack ONCE before
- continuing the chain. Subsequent attempts on different
- browsers don't re-heal (one heal per turn).
- Re-try the SAME browser one more time after heal before
- moving down the chain (give the heal a chance on the
- operator's preferred default).
- shellcheck disable=SC2086
- Chain exhausted with no winner.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-os-control
- Window-placement fallbacks. These are the LAST resort only -- the
- real values live in mios.toml [os_control] (SSOT). Kept here purely so
- `window-defaults` still answers on a host whose TOML predates the
- section; they are not authoritative and never override TOML.
- A verb is any [verbs.<name>] dict carrying a description -- mirrors
- agent-pipe _load_verb_catalog (which also keys on the metadata
- block) so this export and the dispatcher never disagree.
- OpenAI requires `items` for array params; default to
- string items unless the verb declares otherwise.
- Standard OpenAI tools array.
- Only the scalar window keys belong here; ignore any nested tables.
- A zero-arg verb (ai, dash, help, ...) legitimately has no sig and
- no params. Only a verb that HAS params but NO sig is a problem:
- without the sig, required-arg detection silently treats every
- param as optional.
- Required params (from sig) must each have a params entry.
- Reconstruct multi-word app names whether the dispatcher quoted {app}
- (arrives as one token) or not (arrives split).
- exit 0 only when the launch is CONFIRMED; 1 otherwise.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-os-recipe
- WSL is a Linux env that can dispatch to Windows -- we treat it as
- both, picking the template per-recipe (operator may run a
- Linux-only recipe inside WSL fine; a Windows-only recipe inside
- WSL is also fine since explorer.exe / powershell.exe are PATH-
- accessible via WSL interop). Default to whichever the recipe
- declares; this function returns the PREFERRED template family.
- Windows cmd quoting: wrap in double-quotes + escape embedded ".
- Substitute every {key} with a shell-quoted value; refuse if any
- placeholder lacks a binding (prevents the recipe from running
- with a literal "{path}" in the command).
- Recipe catalog keys are HYPHENATED ([recipes.disk-usage]) but the agent's
- projected tool-names + the mios_recipe__<n> -> os_recipe(name=<n>) translation
- use UNDERSCORES (mios_recipe__disk_usage). Without this normalization every
- recipe the agent calls fails as "unknown recipe" (all 18 silently broken).
- Strip any kwarg not declared (defense in depth -- the agent
- shouldn't be able to splice a phantom {key} that exists in the
- template but not in `args`).
- Resolve target OS: explicit --os flag > detected default. Recipe
- must declare a template for the chosen OS.
- If recipe doesn't have a template for the chosen OS but DOES
- have one for the other, surface a clear message.
- WSL path conversion: when the recipe declares wsl_paths AND the
- windows template was chosen, convert each named arg.
- Execute. Linux: bash -c. Windows-from-WSL: binfmt_misc handles the
- .exe exec when the full path is given. Recipe templates name
- /mnt/c/Windows/... binaries directly because the MiOS distro sets
- `appendWindowsPath=false` in /etc/wsl.conf -- bare names don't
- resolve via PATH lookup. Operator-confirmed 2026-05-19.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-oscap-gate
- Structural severity ordering (XCCDF severity vocabulary). Not operator config.
- Rule id -> severity (fallback when a rule-result omits its own @severity).
- Unknown threshold -> strictest meaningful gate (fail-safe, never silently
- widen). "any" must be requested explicitly.
- The count is the gate verdict; total is context for the log.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-oscontrol-health
- WSL gateway + the WSL-interop powershell.exe path) and emits typed JSON status so the
- agent can report "control plane offline" instead of a silent exit -1 when a Windows
- control/recipe action returns no data.
- Research 2026-06-15 (ai-os-control-patterns) quick win: the in-session Windows executor
- can be DOWN (operator must start it / log in); without this verb the agent gets a bare
- exit -1 and can't explain it. Read-only, no side effects.
- Guard set -u: a value with shell-metachars must not abort under set -u.
- WSL2 NAT: the default gateway is the Windows host that runs the in-session executor.
- appendWindowsPath=false keeps bare powershell.exe OFF the VM PATH, so probe via the
- FULL interop path (the recipes use it too); fall back to PATH if present.
- Escape the reason for JSON (only quotes/backslashes appear here).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-owui-apply-knowledge
- Knowledge collection identity. The id is a stable v5-uuid derived from
- a fixed MiOS namespace + name so every host that runs this helper
- generates the same id (lets operators move their webui.db between
- hosts without losing the link).
- Per-file collection ids (`file-{file_id}`) are what OWUI keys its
- vector chunks under. We derive each file's id deterministically too,
- so re-runs reuse the same chunk collection (no re-vectoring noise on
- every apply).
- Curated corpus. Anything not on disk is silently skipped. Add new
- entries here when new authoritative docs ship.
- The agent's own canonical surface (prose docs)
- Versioned data surface (machine-readable manifests; ALSO useful
- as RAG so the agent can introspect its own /v1 surface).
- Day-0 / day-n operator docs
- Cookbooks (worked examples)
- Hermes skills (the agent's own playbook)
- Role prompts (host overrides for engineer / reviewer / troubleshoot)
- Architectural laws + agent guidance at repo root
- The SSOT
- Schema sanity -- log any unexpected absence so operator can
- tell whether OWUI got upgraded out from under us.
- Per-file knowledge_file table layout differs slightly across
- OWUI 0.9.x patch versions; introspect at runtime.
- Ensure knowledge row exists.
- Upsert files.
- Link file <-> knowledge if not already linked.
- Refresh knowledge.data.file_ids.
- Attach knowledge ID to MiOS-Agent model row's meta.knowledge.
- Schema: meta.knowledge is a list of {type, id, name, ...} dicts.
- remove any pre-existing entry with our id (prevents
- duplicates if the helper runs after operator-side edits)
- Post-commit: verify vector_db actually has chunks for the
- collection. The day-0 wipe (mios-cache-clear --all) drops
- chroma.sqlite3 contents but the knowledge_file links here
- see hash-unchanged and skip the vector-clear branch, so
- vectors stay missing + knowledge_search returns 0 hits.
- Detect-and-heal: count chroma rows; if zero but file
- content is present, force re-add of every file via OWUI's
- /api/v1/knowledge/{kid}/file/add (the only endpoint that
- actually triggers chunk + embed).
- Re-open the operator-side webui.db to enumerate file_ids and
- mint a request token. Read-only handle so we don't race the
- main mutation path above.

- Toggles in the chat input bar (web search / image gen / code interpreter)

- Chat.svelte's defaultFeatureIds.includes(...) gate).

- defaults, leave everything alone (per MiOS-managed marker
- convention).

- (observed live: "table user has no column named api_key").

- [identity].email. If so, RECONCILE its login password to the SSOT
- (non-destructive UPDATE) on every run -- the same lock-step model as
- usr/libexec/mios/forge-firstboot.sh, so ONE operator password backs
- OWUI / Forge / Portal / Cockpit / RDP alike. An operator who wants a

- UI (which a reboot would otherwise silently revert).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-owui-install-pipe
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-owui-install-pipe
- Install the MiOS-Agent OWUI Pipe Function into the running OWUI.
- Auto-generates an admin API key (stashed in webui.db's api_key
- table) if none exists, then POSTs the pipe to the functions API.
- Idempotent: re-running updates the function content if changed.
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: "OWUI's MiOS-Agent is the 'model'
- that users speak to" / "OWUI should emit all global agents
- printing/answers/etc". This script makes the vendored pipe at
- /usr/share/mios/owui/pipes/mios_agent_pipe.py available in OWUIs
- model dropdown without the operator having to paste it manually.
- User-facing display name shown in OWUI's model dropdown + chat
- header. Operator preference 2026-05-18: shorter, more consumer-
- y ("MiOS AI" not "MiOS-Agent"). The PIPE_ID below stays
- "mios_agent" for backwards compatibility (the id is the stable
- row key in webui.db's function table; renaming it would orphan
- existing chats that reference the old model id).
- Sidecar filter id, retained ONLY so the disable block below can
- target the row in webui.db when a previous install enabled it.
- agent-pipe is the canonical orchestrator now; it surfaces its own
- SSE status events and the sidecar's hermes-tail polling + post-
- call response-replacement was actively destructive on chat turns.
- ─── Find / generate an admin API key (MIOS_OWUI_TOKEN env wins -- e.g. a
- JWT from /auths/signin, used when OWUI's api-key auth is disabled) ──
- Find an admin user
- Check for existing API key
- Generate new API key + insert (OWUI's format: sk-<32 hex chars>)
- ─── Build the pipe payload ───────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── POST to OWUI's functions API ────────────────────────────────────
- Send the payload via a TEMP FILE (-d @file), NOT an inline arg: the pipe
- source is large enough to blow ARG_MAX as a curl command-line argument
- ("curl: Argument list too long" -- operator-flagged 2026-05-21 after the
- UserValves persona fields grew the pipe). printf is a shell builtin, so
- writing the file does not hit the exec arg limit.
- Already exists; try update
- ─── Bind a Model entry that uses the pipe ────────────────────────────
- OWUI distinguishes "Functions" (which include Pipes) from "Models".
- A Pipe registered in Functions is callable but doesn't auto-appear
- as a chat model unless a Model entry binds to it via base_model_id.
- This block creates that Model entry so "MiOS-Agent" shows up in the
- chat dropdown + actually routes through our pipe.
- Materialise the SSOT-driven system prompt to a tempfile FIRST so both
- the create-model payload + the post-install sqlite sync can read the
- same bytes (no risk of the two python invocations rendering different
- strings if the operator edits mios.toml between them).
- Shared layered mios.toml resolver (vendor < host < user), path injected as argv[1].
- SSOT: rendered upstream by the bash-level mktemp + python loader, so
- both this payload + the post-install sqlite sync see the SAME bytes.
- OWUI native tool features ENABLED BY DEFAULT on the USER-FACING
- pipe model (operator 2026-05-22: "OWUI tools can't be used if the
- actual OWUI tools aren't enabled by default"). Without these the
- web_search / code / image features sit behind a per-chat toggle,
- so the agent's tool_calls + the daemon-agent fan-out can't reach
- them. Mirrors mios-owui-apply-system-prompt's DEFAULT_FEATURE_IDS.
- web_search DISABLED 2026-05-24 (operator "disable OWUI web search for
- mios-agent"): OWUI's BUILT-IN web search auto-fired every message and
- injected its OWN, often EMPTY-content sources that COMPETED WITH and
- POLLUTED the MiOS pipeline's own web-research loop (search -> extract ->
- crawl, fed to every agent). The PIPELINE owns web research now; OWUI
- must not run a second, worse one. Capability off + not in the auto-fire
- set. (Re-enable by setting web_search True + adding it back below.)
- defaultFeatureIds: native OWUI feature toggles ON by default in a fresh
- chat. EMPTY now -- web_search was the only one and is disabled (above);
- image_generation + code_interpreter were dropped 2026-05-22 after they
- auto-fired destructively (code_interpreter ran os.listdir('/mnt/uploads')
- on an anime-schedule query; image_generation errored on a greeting).
- Native tool surface -- the model SEES these in its tool_calls list.
- Operator 2026-05-22: ALL registered tools active by default (the
- force-sync block below is authoritative and re-derives this from the
- `tool` table dynamically, so this literal is just the fresh-install
- seed). Each entry must match a tool row id in OWUI's `tool` table.
- NO hardcoded suggestion_prompts: mios-daemon.suggestions_loop
- populates the blank-chat panel dynamically every 20 min from
- recent state + chat language (operator directive 2026-05-17:
- "no hardcoded answers or anything hardcoded for english").
- The system prompt OWUI prepends to every chat. Edit in
- the OWUI admin UI (Settings -> Models -> MiOS-Agent) or
- re-run this installer.
- Sampling defaults tuned for the refine -> hermes -> polish
- chain. Low temperature: agent should be predictable about
- which canonical verb to call, not "creative". top_p left
- at OWUI default. Hermes internally overrides these on its
- delegate spawns -- this is just the outer chat-completion
- default.
- Stop tokens: hermes occasionally emits these as text inside
- delegate-spawn tool args; cut them so they don't leak into
- the polished answer.
- OWUI streams tokens incrementally; no need to override.
- OWUI returns 401 (not 409) for "model id already registered"
- -- detail body "Uh-oh! This model id is already registered."
- Treat all three as "exists -- need to update".
- ─── Register the anti-meta Filter Function (post-hoc scrubber) ───────
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: research-driven approach -- replace
- rigid "DO NOT say X" SOUL.md text-blocks with an OWUI Filter that
- strips meta-speak from the stream. The filter reads the same shared
- refusal-patterns.txt the nudger + prefilter use; one source of truth.
- ─── Register the SWARM toggle Filters (operator 2026-05-22 "AI SWARM") ──
- Three chat-bar toggle-filters (toggle=True chips): Council / Delegate /
- Force-tool. Each inlet injects body.mios_flags.<flag>, which the MiOS
- Agent Pipe (:8640) reads per-request to force the swarm behaviour. Same
- create-or-update-on-409 pattern + admin TOKEN as the anti-meta filter.
- OWUI's functions/create API ignores is_active / is_global in the payload --
- new functions always land inactive. Force-enable + globalize the swarm
- toggle-filters in webui.db so they render as chat-bar toggles. toggle=True
- in each filter keeps them defaulting OFF, so global is safe (no auto-fire).
- ─── MiOS Agents Sidecar Filter -- RETIRED ────────────────────────
- agent-pipe is the canonical orchestrator now and emits its own
- SSE status events (📡 prompt / 🧭 route / 📋 plan / 💬 chat / ...).
- The sidecar tailed /var/lib/mios/hermes-tail/latest.json and would
- surface stale Hermes events as if current on every chat -- and its
- post-call response sometimes REPLACED the legitimate polished
- reply ("launch steam" succeeded internally but the operator saw
- "I cannot launch Steam" because the sidecar's post-emit overwrote
- the agent-pipe reply). Forcing it disabled here is the safety net;
- the install path no longer creates+enables it.
- A previous run may have installed + enabled the sidecar; force-
- disable both flags in webui.db so a re-run leaves the row in the
- correct disabled state.
- ─── Rename any stale duplicate model rows ──────────────────────
- OWUI's pipe-function registration creates an auto-managed model
- row under `<function_id>.<model_id>` (e.g. mios_agent.mios-agent)
- alongside our explicit `mios-agent` model row. Both surface in
- the model dropdown. When we rename one (PIPE_NAME / MODEL_NAME
- above), we must rename the auto-managed twin OR the operator
- sees both "MiOS-Agent" (old auto-row) AND "MiOS AI" (new
- explicit row) in the dropdown.
- Force-sync params.system on BOTH the explicit + twin model rows.
- OWUI auto-creates the twin row on first pipe registration with no
- params.system, then never refreshes it -- result was the OLD
- baked-in English prompt persisting on the twin even after the
- SSOT prompt in mios.toml was updated. Operator-flagged
- 2026-05-19.
- OWUI native tool features the USER-FACING model must have ON by
- default (operator 2026-05-22: "OWUI tools can't be used if they
- aren't enabled by default"). OWUI never refreshes meta after first
- create, so force-sync capabilities + defaultFeatureIds + toolIds onto
- BOTH rows here (mirrors the create payload + apply-system-prompt).
- web_search DISABLED 2026-05-24 (operator "disable OWUI web search for
- mios-agent"): OWUI's built-in web search competed with + polluted the MiOS
- pipeline web-research (empty-content sources). The PIPELINE owns web
- research; OWUI must not run its own. Auto-fire set is EMPTY now
- (image_generation + code_interpreter were already pulled 2026-05-22 after
- auto-firing destructively on non-matching queries).
- ALL registered tools active by default (operator 2026-05-22, reversing
- the earlier MiOS-authored-only restriction). The third-party tools
- (openui by thesysdev/vishxrad, sub_agent by skyzi000) are re-attached.
- HISTORY the operator accepted: openui once FABRICATED a fake "interactive
- OpenUI visualization" on a "send to Discord" turn (claimed success while
- nothing happened). If that recurs, narrow this query back to MiOS-authored
- tools. Query stays dynamic: every row in the `tool` table auto-attaches,
- so a newly-installed tool needs no code edit here. Empty result (tools
- not yet installed at firstboot ordering) -> rows keep existing toolIds.
- AUTHORITATIVE set (not a merge): replace toolIds with the full
- `tool`-table set computed above, so the live rows always converge on
- exactly the installed tools (no drift from manual UI edits).
- ─── Force WEBUI_NAME into config.data.webui.name ────────────────
- OWUI seeds the browser-tab title + top-left banner from
- WEBUI_NAME env at first boot, but persists it into
- config.data.webui.name where it then OVERRIDES the env on
- subsequent boots. If the operator-visible banner still shows
- the old name despite the Quadlet update, this is the DB row
- we need to force.
- OWUI stores the banner / browser-title under different keys
- depending on version; set all three so the right one lands.
- ─── Memory feature ON by default for every user ─────────────────
- OWUI's memory feature is per-user via settings.ui.memory = true.
- Operator confirmed they want it ON by default for the MiOS-Agent
- experience (without it, the agent forgets context between turns
- at the OWUI layer). Walk every user row, ensure memory: true.
- Idempotent: already-true users are left alone.

- search is THE first call for any Windows-launch ambiguity: it

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-passport
- ─── SSOT env knobs ───────────────────────────────────────────────
- pgvector store via the pure-python mios-pg-query wire client (the legacy
- BSL 1.1 store is retired). Loopback trust -- no auth/psql/podman; works for the
- confined mios-ai service user. Same client mios-rag / mios-db --pg use.
- ─── pgvector helper (mios-pg-query, pure-python pg wire client) ──────
- ─── canonical-JSON op_hash (same algorithm as agent-pipe) ────────
- ─── key material ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
- DB fallback (pgvector agent_keypair). The PEM is multi-line; select it
- with newlines folded to a sentinel so mios-pg-query's one-row-per-line
- output stays parseable, then restore them before parsing.
- ─── signing + verification ────────────────────────────────────────
- ─── provisioning ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Determine the new kid. v1 on first provision; on --force we
- increment past the existing kid.
- Write atomically. Private key 0600; public key world-readable
- so any agent can verify without ACL coordination.
- Register in pgvector (agent_keypair). Retire any prior live row first.
- psql -At columns, in SELECT order; pad short rows (trailing NULLs).
- pg renders booleans as 't'/'f' in -At output.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-powershell
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-powershell <script>
- First-class Windows-side PowerShell execution surface for the
- MiOS agent stack. The analogue of bash -c on the Windows side --
- the agent passes a PowerShell script and gets stdout + stderr +
- exit code back through the broker.
- Mirrors Anthropic's bash_* tool schema shape but for the Windows
- subsystem, closing the gap the operator flagged 2026-05-18:
- `powershell_run` belongs as a first-class verb so agents that
- need to call Windows-side cmdlets (Get-Process, Get-Service,
- Get-WmiObject, Get-AppxPackage, registry reads, COM, ...) don't
- fall back to fragile pc_type+pc_key paths.
- SECURITY: this verb is in [security].firewall_high_privilege_verbs
- -- any tool_call in a tainted session refuses dispatch. Standalone
- `mios-powershell` (operator running it directly) is unaffected.
- Usage:
- mios-powershell '<script>'            # script via argv
- mios-powershell -c '<script>'         # explicit -c form
- echo '<script>' | mios-powershell -   # stdin
- Flags:
- --timeout N    seconds (default 30)
- --work-dir P   working directory passed to powershell.exe
- (default: PWD on the WSL side)
- --json         wrap stdout/stderr/exit_code in a JSON envelope
- (matches the agent-pipe CAPTURE_JSON shape so
- external integrators get a stable response)
- Resolution: tries pwsh.exe first (PowerShell 7+, modern surface),
- falls back to Windows-builtin powershell.exe (PowerShell 5.1).
- Both invoked with -NoProfile -NonInteractive so script behaviour
- is deterministic + the agent's call doesn't pick up the operator's
- $PROFILE side effects.
- Hardening caps (SSOT-overridable). Defaults match agent-pipe's
- CAPTURE_JSON stdout truncation so the broker's response shape
- stays stable.
- Parse leading flags. Positional script can come as bare arg, -c
- <script>, '-' meaning stdin, or --shell for an interactive
- PowerShell session (used by mios-ttyd-powershell.service).
- Interactive shell mode -- exec pwsh.exe with no -NonInteractive
- and no script body, inheriting the controlling terminal. ttyd's
- pty layer + WSL interop give the agent a full Win32 PowerShell
- session that survives client reconnects (ttyd buffers stdout).
- Hardening: script size cap. A pathological multi-MB script would
- slow the broker, trip podman socket buffers, and balloon the
- tool_call args column.
- Resolve a PowerShell binary the agent's PATH can reach. The
- Windows-side binaries live under /mnt/c/Windows/System32/ +
- /mnt/c/Program Files/PowerShell/7/. We probe pwsh.exe first
- (modern) then powershell.exe (5.1 ships everywhere).
- Last-chance fallback: hope it's on PATH (interop scenarios where
- /mnt/c paths aren't visible but `pwsh.exe` / `powershell.exe`
- resolve via WSL interop registration).
- Stage script in a temp file. PowerShell's -EncodedCommand path
- avoids quote-mangling but adds base64 overhead; passing a file
- via -File is cleaner + lets large scripts work without hitting
- the argv length limit.
- UTF-8-no-BOM output + exit-code propagation (research 2026-06-15 AI-shell
- doctrine): PS5.1 redirection defaults to UTF-8-WITH-BOM (the EF BB BF prefix
- corrupts JSON the agent parses), and a PS script's exit derives from its LAST
- statement -- a failing tail native exe still reports 0, so the agent declares
- success on failure. Pin no-BOM stdout encoding (best-effort) + propagate the
- real native exit via $LASTEXITCODE. Explicit `exit N` in $SCRIPT still wins.
- Determine where the script file is from PowerShell's perspective.
- /tmp on WSL is reachable from Windows as \\wsl.localhost\<distro>\tmp
- but invoking that path can be slow + flaky; mounting /tmp under
- /mnt/wsl/.../tmp is the modern path. Easiest: stage the file under
- /mnt/c/Users/Public/Documents/mios-ps/ which Windows reads natively.
- Fallback to the WSL UNC if the public dir isn't writable.
- If elevation is requested but we have no Windows-side staging path, fail early.
- Build the powershell.exe argv. -NoProfile makes invocation
- deterministic; -NonInteractive prevents prompts from hanging.
- Stdin path: PowerShell reads the script from stdin via -Command -.
- Optional working dir: prepended as `Set-Location` in the script.
- Simpler than passing via -WorkingDirectory which not all PS
- versions support.
- Resolve native Windows path for Start-Process to execute correctly on host
- Escape paths for PowerShell Start-Process string arguments
- Encode the elevated command to Base64 (UTF-16LE) to avoid nested quote mangling
- Strip trailing CRLF so the consumer doesn't see literal \r in
- every line (Windows PowerShell defaults to crlf line endings).
- Hardening: truncate per stream to the output cap so a runaway
- script (`Get-EventLog -Newest 10000000`) can't fill the agent's
- context window. The marker line lets the agent see explicit
- truncation rather than silently mis-counting.

- context (interactive or scripted, rootless or not, Termius / ttyd / cron).
- Containers run ROOTFUL; a non-root `podman ps` sees nothing. This reads the
- root-written, WORLD-READABLE snapshot (/var/lib/mios/podman-ps.json, refreshed
- by mios-podman-ps.timer -- the same SSOT the dashboard, the container_status
- verb, and the interactive `podman ps` augmentation use) so containers are
- universally visible WITHOUT granting rootful-socket control. Falls back to a

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-rag
- OpenAI /v1/embeddings (mios-llm-light serves nomic-embed-text; MiOS is /v1-only)
- Paragraph-aware chunking with overlap capped at CHUNK_CHARS.
- pgvector store. Brute-force cosine is fine for the docs-sized corpus; an
- HNSW index is added best-effort.
- PARAMETERIZED: source (filesystem path) + content (file text)
- are BOUND, never spliced -> no quote/backslash/encoding edge
- case can break or inject the SQL.
- transient embed 500 (mios-llm-light loading) or a bad chunk --
- skip it and keep going so one failure can't abort the run.
- pgvector cosine: distance is emb <=> qv ; similarity = 1 - distance. The
- vector is BOUND as $1 (reused); LIMIT stays inline (int-coerced -> safe).
- Flatten newlines/tabs in content so mios-pg-query's tab-separated,
- one-row-per-line output stays parseable.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-rechunk
- Creates a zstd-compressed block-level delta bundle
- Compress new block with zstd
- Write manifest
- SEC-03: Sign the manifest if key is provided (simulate SHA-256 chain signing)
- We just do a mock signature for the chain
- Create tar

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-remember
- P1 AIOS Memory Manager: embed agent-memory facts ON WRITE so they're
- semantically RECALLABLE (the self-edit tier was write-only -> inert: nothing
- embedded the rows, so the HNSW recall never surfaced them). Embed via the live
- dGPU /v1 lane; degrade-open -- the row still writes without emb on any miss.
- WS-A2 embedding-version hygiene: stamp the embedding identity alongside every
- stored vector so a model/dim change is detectable + re-embeddable (matches the
- agent-pipe EMB_VERSION). Bump MIOS_EMB_VERSION when the model/dims change.
- Strip leading conversational filler so the STORED fact is clean
- ("Please remember this fact: I prefer X" -> "I prefer X"); the refine
- extraction sometimes keeps the "this fact:" prefix (Claude 2026-06-15).
- Upsert by (key, scope): DELETE then INSERT in ONE atomic batch
- (BEGIN/COMMIT). All values are BOUND params ($1..$n) -- TABLE is a
- trusted config identifier, never request data.
- WS-A2: stamp the embedding identity (model + version) too.
- LIMIT stays inline (int-coerced -> not injectable); scope is bound.
- A bare UPDATE returns rc 0 even when it matches ZERO rows, so the
- old code reported ok/updated:1 for a key that doesn't exist. Confirm
- the key exists first (same proven json_agg SELECT path as `list`) and
- report the real match status so a no-op update is never a phantom
- success.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-restart
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-restart <service-or-quadlet>
- Smart restart for any MiOS-managed service. Knows the difference between:
- * a podman Quadlet (lives at /etc/containers/systemd/<name>.container,
- systemd unit name is <name>.service) -- restart MUST go through
- `systemctl restart <name>.service`. `podman restart <name>` desyncs
- systemd's view and the unit gets ExecStop'd ~1 minute later
- (operator-confirmed regression 2026-05-15: podman restart killed
- mios-open-webui repeatedly).
- * a regular systemd service (hermes-agent, sshd, etc.) -- normal
- `systemctl restart`.
- * a hermes-agent gateway "soft restart" -- restart the service AND
- drop the in-process skills-prompt cache so newly-edited SOUL.md /
- SKILL.md takes effect on the very next chat.
- Accepts either short name (open-webui, hermes, llm-light) or full unit
- name (mios-open-webui.service). Doesn't accept ambiguous matches.
- Map short names to full unit names. Lowercase + alias-expand.
- Pass through with .service appended if absent.
- Privilege check.
- Hermes-specific PRE-restart: rsync vendor skill set from
- /usr/share/mios/hermes/skills/ into HERMES_HOME/skills so newly
- vendored skills appear without requiring a full mios-hermes-firstboot
- re-run. firstboot owns the initial seed; this re-syncs on demand for
- the operator's `mios-restart hermes` flow. Idempotent (rsync skips
- unchanged files). Operator directive 2026-05-15: skill staleness
- bit us when pc-control + windows-control + mios-environment were
- added vendor-side but never appeared in HERMES_HOME because
- firstboot only runs once.
- Try every plausible HERMES_HOME -- the service one is canonical
- but operator CLI homes also benefit. Owner per-target.
- rsync if available; cp -a fallback. -u keeps newer dest
- files (operator's local edits) untouched.
- SOUL.md follows the SAME pattern: vendor edit at
- /usr/share/mios/ai/hermes-soul.md, gateway-side firstboot stamps
- to $HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md once, operator-CLI ~/.hermes/SOUL.md once.
- Between firstboots, edits don't propagate -- and operator's CLI
- gets a stale prompt with old refusal-fix language. Mirror the
- skills behaviour: re-sync if the MiOS-managed marker is still
- present (operator took ownership iff they removed it).
- If existing file doesn't carry the MiOS-managed marker,
- operator has taken ownership -- leave it alone.
- Bounded readiness poll instead of a fixed `sleep 2` + single is-active: a
- slow-starting unit (a container Quadlet, the SGLang heavy lane, OWUI) is still
- 'activating' 2 s in, so the old code reported a transient/incorrect state.
- Poll every 1 s up to 30 s (well under TimeoutStartSec), break on a TERMINAL
- state, and report elapsed time so the result is honest.
- Hermes-specific POST-restart: drop the in-process skills-prompt cache
- so SOUL.md / SKILL.md edits take effect immediately on the very next
- chat (without a second restart).
- Quadlet-aware tail of the unit's recent journal so the operator/agent
- sees immediate evidence the unit actually came up (vs hung in
- 'activating' or restart-loop).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-sandbox-exec
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-sandbox-exec [opts] -- <command> [args...]
- P4.4 (agent-code sandbox): run AGENT-GENERATED code/commands inside a
- userspace sandbox. Full gVisor (userspace kernel) needs runsc + kernel
- features WSL2 lacks; bubblewrap (bwrap) gives a REAL namespace+FS sandbox
- that works HERE -- no privileged container, no kernel module. This is the
- "Execution Sandbox" the Hermes v2026.5.28 brief calls for, deliverable now.
- PROGRESSIVE ENFORCEMENT (mirrors the brief's eBPF observe->baseline->enforce):
- --level enforce  (default) read-only /, writable WORKSPACE only, NO network
- egress (--unshare-net), unshare pid/ipc/uts, die-with-parent,
- no-new-privs, + cgroup MemoryMax/CPUQuota via systemd-run.
- --level baseline same FS isolation but network ALLOWED (for fetches).
- --level observe  run normally (no FS jail) but log the command -- for
- migrating an existing flow before tightening it.
- OPTS
- --workspace DIR   the ONE writable dir (default: $PWD). bind rw; rest ro.
- --level L         enforce|baseline|observe (default enforce)
- --net             allow network even at enforce level (opt-in egress)
- --mem  N          MemoryMax (default 2G)   --cpu PCT  CPUQuota (default 200%)
- --timeout SEC     hard wall-clock kill (default 120)
- EXIT: the command's exit code, or 126 if the sandbox itself can't start.
- Offline: no network unless --net; no cloud; pure local namespaces.
- Fully leak-proof: the whole body is wrapped so a non-writable log (e.g. when
- run by a user other than mios-ai) NEVER spills an error to stdout/stderr.
- observe: no jail, just run + log (migration aid).
- Hardened bwrap profile: read-only system, writable workspace + /tmp only.
- no-new-privs: block setuid escalation from inside the sandbox.
- network: enforce => unshare (no egress) unless --net; baseline => keep net.
- Resource caps via a transient systemd scope when a user manager is up;
- else fall back to ulimit (address-space) inside the shell.
- No user systemd bus (common under WSL service ctx) -> bwrap + timeout
- only; resource caps degrade to the wall-clock timeout.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-scheduled-research
- Autonomous turns must NOT trigger the WIDE research fan-out (operator
- 2026-06-01 autonomous-wedge fix). A scheduled research prompt is a research
- turn -> the agent-pipe would otherwise fan out with include_research=True and
- cold-load every 2-4GB replica across all lanes; fired on a timer with no human
- watching, that periodically thundering-herds the backend and wedges the VM. We tag
- the request metadata.mios_autonomous=true so the pipe takes the BOUNDED path
- (narrow council, no research-replica fan-out). SSOT: MIOS_SCHED_BOUNDED.
- Honored by the agent-pipe (_council_research / fan-out gate): an
- autonomous turn stays narrow no matter the research intent.
- Discord hard-caps at 2000 chars; leave room for the header.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-screenshot
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-screenshot [output-path] [--open] [--clipboard]
- Capture a screenshot of the operator's primary Windows monitor and
- save it to a PNG. Sensible defaults: filename like
- `MiOS-YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS.png` under the operator's Windows Pictures/
- Screenshots folder (the same place Win+PrtScr writes to).
- Implementation: thin wrapper around `mios-pc-control screenshot
- <path>`, which dispatches mios-pc-control.ps1 on the Windows side via
- the launcher broker. The PS helper uses System.Drawing.Bitmap +
- CopyFromScreen, which works in any operator-session PowerShell
- (no fancy desktop / no AppExecutionAlias / no UAC needed).
- Operator directive 2026-05-17: chat showed agent flailing for 6 min
- trying `screencapture.exe` (macOS tool), `Invoke-Screenshot` (not a
- real cmdlet), and dozens of broken PowerShell pipelines. Concluded
- "Windows screenshot tools aren't available in this WSL environment".
- WRONG -- mios-pc-control screenshot has worked since day one. This
- shim makes the surface obvious: ANY "screenshot" intent maps to
- `mios-screenshot` (via the mios-find alias) and gets one tool call.
- OPTIONS
- <output-path>   Optional explicit path. Linux-style (/mnt/c/...)
- or Windows-style (C:\Users\...). Default:
- /mnt/c/Users/<operator>/Pictures/Screenshots/
- MiOS-YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS.png
- --open          After capture, open the PNG in the operator'\''s
- default image viewer (via mios-open-url).
- --clipboard     After capture, also copy the image bytes to the
- Windows clipboard so the operator can paste into
- Discord/email/etc.
- OUTPUT
- Prints the absolute path (Linux style) to the captured PNG on
- stdout. Prints capture dimensions to stderr.
- --window: focus the matched window first so it's on top + visible,
- then capture the full primary monitor. Operator-flagged 2026-05-17:
- "take screenshot of notepad" -> agent went down a 6-min flail. The
- fix is to make a window-targeted capture a 1-call verb. mios-window
- focus handles the un-minimize + foreground; the resulting capture
- shows the target window front-and-center.
- Give the WM a tick to bring it to top
- Default output path: operator's Windows Pictures/Screenshots folder
- WSL operator name = the windows username (mios.toml [identity].windows_user
- is the canonical source; fall back to $USER if unreadable).
- Translate Linux path -> Windows path for mios-pc-control (which
- dispatches to PowerShell on the Windows side).
- Linux-side path -- save under the venv user but mios-pc-control
- needs a Windows-reachable path. Reject + tell operator.
- Capture. mios-pc-control screenshot prints its own success/dimensions line.
- Verify the file landed
- mios-pc-control might have buffered output; give it a moment
- Optional: copy to clipboard via Set-Clipboard -Path (Windows)
- Optional: open in operator's default image viewer
- Print the path on stdout (single line; agents parse this)

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-show-image
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-show-image <query> [--position left|right|center|top|bottom] [--engine images|videos]
- Operator directive 2026-05-17: "should just open the image directly
- in a browser window then!! (localhost browser on windows or Local
- MiOS linux browser(s)(if multiple present))". The agent was running
- 13 tool calls trying to download + save + screenshot images, hitting
- WSL filesystem read-only errors, when the operator's actual ask was:
- search -> open URL in browser. Done.
- Flow:
- 1. SearXNG image search via the local mios-searxng service
- (NO cloud APIs, NO file downloads, NO image saves)
- 2. Pick the top result's img_src
- 3. Open that URL via mios-open-url (resolves the MiOS-defined
- default browser per mios.toml -- could be Windows-side Chrome
- or a Linux flatpak; operator's choice)
- 4. (optional) After 1.2s, mios-window move "<title-pattern>" to
- the requested screen-half via mios-window
- Exit codes:
- 0 = found + opened (+ optional position applied)
- 1 = searxng returned no images
- 2 = searxng unreachable / parse failure
- 3 = mios-open-url failed
- Env-overridable:
- MIOS_SEARXNG_URL   probe-list, comma-separated. Defaults:
- "http://127.0.0.1:8888,http://mios-searxng:8888,
- http://mios-searxng:8080,http://localhost:8888"
- MIOS_IMAGE_TIMEOUT seconds per searxng call (default 8)
- --- 1. SearXNG image search -------------------------------------
- Parse JSON, surface the first usable image URL. Prefers
- img_src (full-res) over thumbnail_src; falls back to url.
- --- 2. Open in default browser ----------------------------------
- --- 3. Optional positioning -------------------------------------
- Browser takes a moment to render the window. mios-window-active
- --present waits for the window to actually surface before
- mios-window can target it.
- Pull the browser window by host title (image hostname or "image")
- Fallback: try by short title fragments most browsers use

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-skill-clone
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-skill-clone <name> [--as <new-name>] [--force]
- Fork a system-shipped skill into the agent's writable skills
- directory so the agent can edit it (the immutable /usr tree won't
- accept writes). The Hermes skill resolver loads the local copy at
- $HERMES_HOME/skills/<name>/ FIRST, so:
- * Same-name clone -> the agent's edited version overrides the
- vendor skill on every load.
- * Renamed clone (--as <new-name>) -> a sibling skill that both
- the original and the fork show up in `skill_view`.
- Operator directive 2026-05-15: "make sure these skills are clone-
- able and modifiable by the agents themselves too! that way Hermes
- is properly improving skills and tools for things iteratively".
- This is the workflow:
- mios-skill-clone parallel-fanout              # fork in place
- $EDITOR ~/.hermes/skills/parallel-fanout/SKILL.md
- # next prompt loads the edited version automatically
- mios-skill-clone windows-control --as windows-power
- # original windows-control still loaded; new windows-power skill
- # ships alongside it
- Layout under each skill dir:
- SKILL.md             (mandatory)
- any other support files (templates, sample configs, ...)
- The clone copies the whole directory tree, not just SKILL.md.
- Resolve the agent's writable skills dir.
- Priority:
- 1. $HERMES_HOME env (set by hermes-agent.service when the agent
- is the caller -- the most authoritative signal)
- 2. /var/lib/mios/hermes (the gateway service user's actual home;
- mios-hermes's passwd entry says /var/empty, but the unit and
- `hermes` CLI both treat /var/lib/mios/hermes as $HERMES_HOME --
- operator-confirmed convention)
- 3. $HOME/.hermes (operator running the helper from their own shell)
- Stamp a clone marker into the SKILL.md so the next reader can tell
- it's a fork. Inserted after the YAML frontmatter (or at top if no
- frontmatter).
- has frontmatter: insert after the closing --- on line N

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-skills
- ─── SSOT env knobs ───────────────────────────────────────────────
- Postgres/pgvector is the sole backend (the legacy :8000 DB retired). All SQL is
- bound out-of-band via the shared mios-db --pg-json CLI: a JSON envelope on
- STDIN ({"sql": "... $1 ...", "params": [...]}) bound over the pg v3 extended
- protocol. No request data is ever spliced into SQL text; table/column names
- are trusted config identifiers and stay inline. INTEGER values (LIMIT,
- interval counts) stay inline via int()-coercion (text->int inference is
- unreliable); only strings/text/vectors are bound.
- Strip the /v1 suffix when calling /skills/* (which lives at the
- service root, not under /v1).
- Phase C.2 mining knobs (all SSOT-routed -- see mios.toml [skills]).
- P2 outcome-driven promotion gate (operator 2026-06-01): in addition to the
- support/confidence threshold, only auto-promote a skill whose RECENT runs
- actually succeeded. Degrade-open: a skill with fewer than MIN_SUCCESS_SAMPLES
- recorded invocations (incl. brand-new mined skills with NO history) is treated
- as passing -> the gate never blocks a skill purely for lack of data.
- ── T-049 (GAP-3): hard pass^k skill-promotion gate ───────────────
- Promoting a skill MUTATES the runnable surface every agent in the stack shares,
- so the DGM/tau-bench lesson applies: a candidate must PROVE reliability, not
- merely have passed once. When the gate is ON, `promote` REPLAYS the skill
- through the same /skills/run firewall+taint+audit chokepoint PASS_AND_K_COUNT
- times (a DGM-class self-rewrite, run with --dgm, uses the stricter
- PASS_AND_K_DGM_COUNT) and flips status ONLY IF EVERY replay succeeds; ONE
- failure vetoes. pass^k is tau-bench's worst-case reliability metric ("ALL k
- repeats must succeed"). DEFAULT-OFF -> promote behaves exactly as before, so an
- env with no reachable agent-pipe is unaffected (degrade-open, byte-identical
- without the mios.toml [reliability] edit). When ON the gate is FAIL-CLOSED: an
- unreachable/erroring replay counts as a failed replay (a promotion must be
- PROVEN, not assumed). All knobs SSOT-routed through mios.toml [reliability] via
- userenv.sh (MIOS_RELIABILITY_*); the numeric defaults mirror those TOML values.
- ─── miner: sequence extraction over tool_call ────────────────────
- Bucket session-less rows into time-windowed groups of 10 min so
- they still contribute to mining (rare path; agents that don't
- tag sessions still produce useful sequences).
- Postgres returns timestamps as ISO strings.
- Count N-grams across sessions; track which sessions contributed.
- Find the row run that produced this ngram to lift
- the concrete arg values as defaults.
- Filter by support + subsume shorter ngrams that always appear
- as a prefix of a longer one (avoid mining 1-grams when a 4-gram
- always wraps them).
- P2 outcome gate: AND-fold the skill's recent success rate into the
- auto-promote decision. Degrade-open -- a freshly-mined skill has no
- invocation history (it isn't persisted yet), so _skill_success_rate
- returns (1.0, 0) and the gate is a no-op; it only ever DEMOTES a
- re-mined skill name whose recorded runs have been failing.
- First occurrence of a verb's arg becomes the param;
- later occurrences re-use the same param name so a
- repeating verb chain like focus_window -> pc_type ->
- pc_key -> focus_window gets two "focus_window_title"
- params unified.
- WINDOW_HOURS is an int knob -> inline; the skill id binds as a text
- param ($1) cast to match the skill column type.
- support/confidence are numeric knobs -> inline (int/float coercion);
- name/description/body/source/status are external values -> bound ($1..$5).
- ─── list / show / promote / retire / delete ──────────────────────
- Plain-tabular for grep/awk.
- 422 (and any 4xx that carries a JSON body) IS the run-result envelope.
- T-049 (GAP-3) HARD pass^k gate: when enabled, a promotion must PROVE
- reliability by replaying the skill k times through the live /skills/run
- chokepoint -- ALL must succeed or the promotion is vetoed. A DGM-class
- self-rewrite (--dgm) uses the stricter DGM count. Default-OFF -> the gate is
- skipped entirely and promote behaves exactly as it always did.
- ─── run: dispatch a skill via agent-pipe ─────────────────────────
- ─── import: load JSON template skills from disk ──────────────────
- stdin: one skill JSON per line (NDJSON) or a single JSON
- object/array.
- Atomic-write: stage to .new, rename. Avoids partial reads
- by Hermes mid-write.
- USER/SYSTEM/AI separation: chgrp to mios-ai + chmod 0640 so
- every AI agent in the bucket group reads without world-ro.
- Best-effort -- fails silently when the group doesn't exist
- (a deployment that doesn't enroll mios-ai yet).
- ─── argparse wiring ──────────────────────────────────────────────
- T-049 pass^k gate replay inputs (used only when the gate is enabled):

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-smart-resize
- Math scaling logic
- Save metadata to PNG text chunk
- Output PNG to stdout

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-sriov-init
- 'MiOS' Universal SR-IOV initialization.
- Run by mios-sriov-init.service early in boot (After=network-pre.target).
- Reads operator config from /etc/mios/sriov.conf, configures the requested
- number of Virtual Functions on every listed PF (Physical Function).
- Config format -- one PF per line:
- <pci_addr>  <num_vfs>
- Example /etc/mios/sriov.conf:
- 0000:01:00.0  4
- 0000:01:00.1  4
- When the config file is absent OR no PFs support SR-IOV, this is a
- no-op. Re-running is safe: it writes the same num_vfs and ignores
- "device or resource busy" if VFs are already configured.
- shellcheck source=/usr/lib/mios/paths.sh
- Setting numvfs requires zero first if non-zero (kernel requirement)

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-ssh-dev-cmd
- The MiOS dev container (code-server) ships no sshd of its own, so the path
- into it is: SSH to the host, then `podman exec` into the container. EVERY
- field is resolved from the RUNNING system -- nothing is hard-coded, so the
- line stays correct on a fresh install, after a podman re-init, or when the
- container is renamed:
- port      -- the admin sshd's effective Port (`sshd -T`, needs privilege,
- so we try `sudo -n` and degrade to the [ports].ssh SSOT).
- container -- the running container whose code-server invocation carries
- --bind-addr (the browser IDE). Found live; no name literal.
- workdir   -- that container's bind-mount destination (the folder
- code-server serves) so the shell lands on the MiOS tree.
- user      -- the account that OWNS that tree (so it runs the rootless
- container and can podman-exec) -- read live from the mount
- source, NOT the operator's display identity (which may not be
- a real login account).
- Usage:
- mios-ssh-dev-cmd          -> the full `ssh -t ... "podman exec ..."` line
- mios-ssh-dev-cmd port     -> just the effective sshd port (for status cells)
- Must be sourced/run in a context that can see the rootful containers (the
- login-shell podman connection). With no code-server container running we
- degrade to a plain host SSH so the caller's row never disappears.
- SSH user = the owner of the served tree (so it runs the rootless container).
- When that can't be read (no container / stat fails), fall back to the SAME
- DB-driven login account the dashboard uses (mios-login-account), NOT MIOS_USER
- / [user].name -- that is the operator's DISPLAY name and would
- drift this command away from the dashboard's `login <user>` line. Resolve the
- helper next to this script, then the deployed path.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-steamcmd
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-steamcmd <subcommand> [args...]
- Native MiOS wrapper around Valve's SteamCMD (the official command-line
- Steam client) + the steam:// URI protocol handler. Operators (and
- agents) get one verb for any Steam-side install / update / info /
- status operation without having to remember which path to call.
- TWO install routes -- pick by your situation:
- uri     - Operator-owned game, Steam client running.
- Dispatches `steam://install/<appid>` to the Steam GUI.
- Steam pops the install dialog; operator confirms.
- Works for ANY game the operator owns. No credentials
- needed in MiOS -- Steam already knows the user.
- cmd     - Headless / scripted install via SteamCMD.
- Works for: free apps, anonymous-installable content
- (dedicated servers like CSGO srcds, Valheim server,
- etc.). For owned single-player games SteamCMD requires
- the operator's Steam username + Steam Guard 2FA at
- first install -- run `mios-steamcmd login <user>` once.
- Auto-bootstrap: if SteamCMD isn't installed, this shim runs
- `mios-installer install Valve.SteamCMD --backend winget --no-confirm`
- the first time you ask for the `cmd` route. ~3 MB install, takes
- 10-20 s on first run.
- SUBCOMMANDS
- install <appid> [--route uri|cmd] [--dir <path>] [--user <steam-user>]
- Default route auto-picks: `uri` (operator-friendly) unless
- --user is set, then `cmd`. Override with --route.
- uninstall <appid> [--route uri|cmd]
- update    <appid> [--route cmd] [--validate]
- SteamCMD `app_update <appid> validate` -- updates + verifies
- file integrity. Anonymous login by default.
- validate  <appid>
- Same as update --validate but without re-downloading missing
- files; just verifies hashes.
- status    <appid>
- SteamCMD `app_status <appid>` -- prints install status,
- buildid, size, last-updated.
- info      <appid>
- SteamCMD `app_info_print <appid>` -- full appinfo blob
- (name, depots, branches, install scripts).
- login     <steam-user>
- Interactive SteamCMD login. Opens the operator's Steam Guard
- prompt on Windows. SteamCMD caches credentials so subsequent
- cmd-route operations don't re-prompt.
- list
- Print known installed apps from Steam's libraryfolders.vdf.
- search    <query>
- Search the Steam store (no SteamCMD needed; uses store API).
- path
- Print the resolved SteamCMD .exe path (Windows-side).
- Operator directive 2026-05-17: "make a steamCMD a native tool for
- handling steam CMD commands GLOBALLY". This shim is that surface.
- ─── helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Resolve steamcmd.exe on the Windows side. winget installs to a
- versioned dir under Microsoft/WinGet/Packages/. Cache the resolved
- path in /var/lib/mios/steamcmd.path so repeated calls are O(1).
- Probe known locations + winget --info
- invalidate cache + re-probe
- Run steamcmd with the given +commands and quit. $* should be the
- entire `+cmd arg +cmd arg ...` string. SteamCMD's exit code is
- returned; output goes to stdout.
- Quote-safe dispatch via mios-windows ps. The args MUST be on the
- SteamCMD command line, separated by spaces, each starting with `+`.
- ─── subcommand handlers ─────────────────────────────────────────────
- Default install dir: C:\SteamCMDLibrary\<appid>
- Read Steam's libraryfolders.vdf (Windows side) to find all install paths.
- Parse each library root + enumerate appmanifest_*.acf
- Use Steam store search API (no auth, no rate limit on light use).
- cc=US, l=english -- can be parameterized later.
- Source guard
- --user implies cmd; otherwise default to uri (Steam GUI)

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-stresstest
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-stresstest -- end-to-end direct-chat stress test of the
- MiOS agent-pipe (/v1/chat/completions). Bounded, load-aware, completes every
- turn (never orphans). Operator/dev tool -- NOT an agent verb (no chat turn can
- launch a stress run). Runs the harness with python3 (httpx = an agent-pipe dep).
- Examples:
- mios-stresstest --count 40 --concurrency 8 --load-ceiling 42 --verbose
- mios-stresstest --endpoint http://localhost:8640/v1 --count 100 --concurrency 16
- Exits 0 if the verdict PASSes (error-rate + p95 within thresholds), else 1.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-suggestion-refresh
- Suggestion generation needs a MORE capable model than the micro
- refiner -- a 1.7b produced repetitive, id-leaking chips ("Open
- directory lookup", operator 2026-05-20). qwen2.5-coder:7b is
- non-thinking + instruction-capable + warm on the dGPU lane; this is a
- periodic BACKGROUND task so its latency doesn't touch chat turns.
- Vast out-of-the-box set (operator 2026-05-20: "a vast set of defaults
- out of the box" covering MiOS functionality, that also iterates per
- use-case). Tunable via env.
- [verbs]+[recipes] across vendor + /etc (etc wins) via the shared resolver.
- De-dupe, keep order, cap so the prompt stays bounded.
- pg `kanban.status` is todo|doing|done|blocked (+ tolerate a legacy
- 'completed'); exclude the finished states. Ordered by ts (the shadow's
- synced_at has no pg equivalent).
- llama.cpp OpenAI /v1 (MiOS is /v1-only): qwen3 (incl. 1.7b) otherwise dumps
- the JSON into message.reasoning with EMPTY content (operator test 2026-05-20),
- so disable the thinking channel to emit the chips JSON straight to
- message.content. max_tokens has room for ~28 chips of JSON.
- OpenAI /v1 shape {"choices":[{"message":{"content"}}]}.
- qwen3-family reasoning models sometimes burn the entire token
- budget in the `reasoning` field with empty `content` (operator-
- observed on a cold-restart probe). Fall back to reasoning when
- content is empty -- the chip extractor below strips <think>
- tags + code fences so either field's payload works.
- Strip qwen3 <think> tails + code fences.
- Extract JSON object substring
- De-dupe case-insensitively, preserve order -- small models repeat
- (operator test 2026-05-20 saw "Query system state" x3 in one batch).
- Shuffle so a different slice of the real capability library leads
- each refresh -> the set genuinely rotates/iterates over time
- (variety sourced from real capabilities, never a hardcoded pool).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-summarize
- qwen3 thinking off so the summary isn't polluted (llama.cpp honors this;
- the </think> strip below is the robust fallback if it isn't applied).
- Cap the body fed to the model (the small model's context is limited);
- L2 keeps the (separately-capped) raw text.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-swarm-pack-firstboot
- mios-swarm-pack-firstboot
- SWARM Phase-2 (operator 2026-06-12): arm the dGPU/CPU small-model SERVER pack so
- 3-4 single-model llama-server instances run CONCURRENTLY (the mios-llm-worker@
- template). Reads the SSOT, ENFORCES Sigma(vram_mb) <= vram_budget_mb so it can
- NEVER oversubscribe the shared 4090 (the documented OOM-cascade), writes a
- per-worker /run/mios/swarm/<name>.env, and starts the armed workers.
- OPERATOR-GATED (Phase-3): does NOTHING unless [dispatch].gpu_profile == "swarm".
- Default "orchestrator" => inert (the single SGLang heavy lane keeps running).
- Idempotent + degrade-open: any parse error or oversubscription => arm NOTHING +
- log, never wedge boot.
- SSOT (mios.toml, layered /usr/share <- /etc <- ~/.config):
- [dispatch].gpu_profile      "orchestrator" | "swarm"
- [dispatch].vram_budget_mb   the agent-lane VRAM ceiling (e.g. 11000)
- [nodes.<name>] with serve=true + gguf=<file under /usr/share/mios/llamacpp/models>
- + endpoint (port is parsed from it) + ngl/ctx/vram_mb
- Emit the arming plan as shell-evalable lines, or "PROFILE_OFF" / "REFUSE ...".
- Shared layered mios.toml resolver (vendor < host < user), path injected as argv[1].
- Layered read: vendor < /etc < ~/.config (highest wins) via the shared resolver.
- parse :PORT from the endpoint, else explicit port
- Hard oversubscription guard.

- vendor/host/user overlay tools/lib/userenv.sh already resolves for shell
- consumers. This is the CSS/QML-facing sibling of the existing
- /etc/mios/install.env bridge: one command, one regenerated artifact, so a
- palette edit in mios.toml reaches the Portal, the Configurator, the
- Quickshell panel, and (via automation/67-bake-surfer.sh /
- automation/65-bake-hyprland.sh at build time) the browser shell and
- compositor borders, without hand-editing hex codes in five different files.
- usr/share/mios/branding/mios-app-shell.css, tools/lib/userenv.sh,
- usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/mios-theme.conf, usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-sync-theme.service
- Usage: mios-sync-theme               # regenerate from the resolved TOML layers
- mios-sync-theme --check       # print what would be written, don't write
- mios-sync-theme --apply-home  # regenerate AND push the dotfile surfaces
- # to the operator's LIVE HOME (via
- # mios-dotfiles sync -- backup-safe,
- # HOME-scoped). Combine with --check for a
- # dry-run (mios-dotfiles diff).
- Same layering as userenv.sh: /usr/share/mios/mios.toml (vendor, lowest)
- < /etc/mios/mios.toml (host) < ~/.config/mios/mios.toml (user, highest).
- Lenient flag parse (backward-compatible: the sole caller, the systemd unit,
- passes no args; unrecognized args are ignored just as the old single-$1 test
- ignored $2+). --apply-home is additive and off by default.
- Palette from the shared resolver (single source; SSOT over the canonical defaults).
- [theme] acrylic/opacity/scrollbar_state are the operator's standing
- "frameless / borderless / 50% acrylic" directive (mios.toml [theme],
- originally a Windows Terminal setting) -- carried here so the web/QML
- surfaces can honor the SAME frosted-glass intent instead of inventing a
- separate opacity value.
- Project every OTHER committed theme surface (btop, oh-my-posh, quickshell,
- fastfetch, the app-shell CSS, the terminal OSC fallbacks) from the SAME palette
- SSOT, so this single command is the GLOBAL runtime theme refresh. The surface
- registry + templates live in mios-theme-render; --check mirrors ours (diff, no
- write). A projection error warns but never aborts the bridge write above.
- Optional: also push the projected dotfile surfaces to the operator's LIVE HOME
- via the mios-dotfiles verb backend (the SAME engine apply path), so the one
- global theme refresh can ALSO land the dotfiles in $HOME. Off by default:
- without --apply-home, sync-theme only refreshes the build-tree artifacts
- (unchanged behavior). --check + --apply-home = a HOME dry-run (no writes).
- Regenerate the MiOS XDG icon theme (SVGs for all branded surfaces) whenever

- above), so it always uses the freshly resolved palette.

- Refresh the GTK icon cache so apps pick up the new SVGs immediately

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-sync-to-root
- repo) DIRECTLY onto the deployed MiOS system root so agent edits go LIVE without a
- GitHub round-trip. GATED to MUTABLE MiOS-DEV roots only -- an immutable bootc/ostree
- root (read-only /usr) is REFUSED (use `bootc upgrade` / `mios-deploy`). Syncs ONLY
- git-visible files (tracked + new, minus .gitignore), never deletes by default, never
- touches untracked system dirs (/home, /var runtime, /proc...). Agent-triggerable via
- the `sync_to_root` verb / the sync-to-root skill.
- /usr/bin/mios-deploy, /etc/mios/install.env, mios.toml [verbs.sync_to_root]
- WHY (timeless): the war-room develops MiOS on a writable ext4 REPLICA because WSL
- /mnt/c (drvfs) is not container-writable; the deployed dev root and the replica only
- converged via git push->pull, which is slow/error-prone. This closes the last mile
- with a DIRECT, gated, git-visible-only sync. On an immutable production image the OS
- tree is read-only by design, so this MUST refuse there -- image changes ship via bootc.
- Usage: mios-sync-to-root [apply|check|dry-run]   (default: apply)
- check | dry-run  -- show what WOULD change, touch nothing (rsync --dry-run)
- apply            -- perform the sync
- Env (all SSOT / degrade-open; nothing hardcoded that lives in mios.toml):
- MIOS_FRONTIER_WORKSPACE / MIOS_A2O_WORK  -- the replica repo (SRC). Auto-detected
- if unset (first dir with a .git below).
- MIOS_SYNC_ROOT_DEST      -- target root (default /). Must be a MiOS root.
- MIOS_SYNC_ROOT_PRUNE=1   -- ALSO delete files removed from SRC (off by default; the
- safe default never removes anything from the live root).
- --- resolve the replica (SRC) from SSOT, else auto-detect a repo checkout ---
- --- target must be an actual MiOS root (prevents syncing onto a wrong / -- e.g. the
- code-server container's own image, whose os-release is NOT MiOS) ---
- --- MUTABILITY GATE: only mutable MiOS-DEV roots (immutable bootc is read-only) ---
- Per verify-root.sh: an immutable production image is ostree-booted with a read-only
- /usr. The definitive operational test is whether we can write the OS tree at DEST.
- --- build the git-visible fileset: tracked + new untracked, honoring .gitignore
- (so build artifacts output/, *.qcow2/iso/vhdx, node_modules, .venv are excluded).
- NUL-delimited to survive spaces/newlines in paths. ---
- --- sync (rsync, NUL file list, NEVER --delete unless PRUNE explicitly set) ---
- Deletion is intentionally NOT the default: a stray SRC state could otherwise
- remove live files. PRUNE only prunes files git no longer tracks, still scoped
- to the git-visible set via --delete-missing-args semantics of --files-from.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-sync-toml
- derived copies (curated root <checkout>/mios.toml + the bootstrap repo's mios.toml) so
- they can never hand-drift. The toml sibling of mios-sync-theme: one command, and a
- [ports]/[colors] edit in the canonical SSOT reaches both repo copies verbatim -- which
- is exactly what keeps drift-gate 22 (bootstrap [ports] parity) and gate 48 (root subset)
- green by construction. Owned sections ([autounattend], [smoke_tests], [mios_app], and the
- gate-48 ignored_prefixes) and the derived copies' own [ports.lan_firewall] sub-table are
- NEVER touched. Source of truth: usr/share/mios/mios.toml.
- usr/lib/mios/mios_toml.py, usr/libexec/mios/mios-sync-theme, automation/98-drift-checks.sh,
- usr/lib/systemd/system/mios-sync-theme.service
- Usage: mios-sync-toml            # regenerate the projected sections in both derived copies
- mios-sync-toml --check    # report drift, write nothing, exit 1 if any copy is stale
- Same layering doctrine as mios-sync-theme: the canonical VENDOR copy
- (usr/share/mios/mios.toml) is the source; the two committed derived copies are pure
- projections of its PROJECTED sections. The Portal still writes only the user layer.
- Sections that are PURE PROJECTIONS from canonical -- safe to regenerate verbatim into the
- derived copies. Verified (superset, no key drops, scalar-value parity): [ports] (35 canonical
- scalars; the derived copies' [ports.lan_firewall] sub-table is preserved) and [colors]
- (28 keys, identical sets). Extend this list only after confirming canonical ⊇ derived for the
- section, so a projection can never DROP a key a consumer reads.
- Trim the trailing comment/blank run (the next section's header comment).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-sys-env
- ── pgvector store (FOSS-pure replacement for the retired legacy agent DB).
- The singleton lives in the shared `sys_env` table (schema-init.sql): one row
- id='current', the whole envelope under the `data` jsonb column. Reached via
- the pure-python mios-pg-query client -- the same pattern mios-rag uses. ─────
- Fixed singleton key (was the legacy record id `sys_env:current`).
- Per-category cap so a huge host can't bloat the stored row.
- Per-category sample size for the COMPACT `get` envelope (the agent-facing
- read). The dispatch broker truncates a verb's stdout at ~6 KB, which would
- corrupt a larger JSON mid-string; the full inventory lives in the DB row +
- `get --full`, while agents read counts + a small sample (and use app_search /
- mios_apps to resolve a specific app). Keeps the read parseable + lean.
- Categories mirror mios-env-probe's launchable inventory (kept in sync with
- mios-apps' own category set; passed straight through, no semantic hardcode).
- Do NOT swallow silently: a timed-out env-probe returns None, which
- empties the entire `env` envelope (identity / host HW / services) --
- the most valuable part of sys_env. Surface it loudly so an empty env
- is never mistaken for "no data available".
- The env-probe is the slow leg (~24 s on a busy box -- seven sequential
- service/HW probes), so give it a generous, env-tunable budget instead of
- the 20 s _run_json default. A too-short timeout silently empties `env`
- (host='', env_sections=[]) even on a successful refresh.
- Single ATOMIC upsert of the fixed singleton key. ON CONFLICT (vs
- DELETE+INSERT) is race-safe when the refresh timer and an agent's
- sys_env_refresh fire concurrently -- last-write-wins, O(1), one row, no
- history bloat. The envelope is json.dumps'd into a jsonb literal; quotes
- are doubled ('' ) so app names/paths can't break out (no injection).
- The whole envelope is stored under the `data` jsonb column of the
- singleton row; unwrap it back to a top-level dict (env/apps/host/...)
- so _compact / cmd_get see the same shape the database row had.
- Row missing (e.g. first boot, before the timer/refresh ran): live
- fallback so a READ is never empty. NOT persisted -- get stays read-only;
- sys_env_refresh / the timer own the write.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-system-status
- WSL2 GPU passthrough installs nvidia-smi to /usr/lib/wsl/lib --
- that directory isn't on the default user PATH so shutil.which()
- alone misses it. Operator-flagged 2026-05-17: broker-side probe
- returned gpu=[] even though nvidia-smi works for root.
- MiOS-specific health roll-up. is-active returns the state string
- (active / inactive / failed) for each unit, one per line.
- Windows HOST OS -- best-effort; null (with no fabrication) when WSL
- interop / the launcher broker is unreachable.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-sysview
- Rootless fallback: a hardened / non-root caller can't see the ROOTFUL
- containers (the dashboard hits the same wall -- /run/podman is 0700
- root:root). mios-podman-ps.service writes a root `podman ps -a --format
- json` snapshot for exactly this; read it so container_status is never
- blind. Same SSOT the portal consumes.
- Every MiOS container is a systemd Quadlet. A bare `podman restart` desyncs
- the managing <name>.service (systemd still owns the OLD container object;
- its next action can kill or duplicate the one podman just restarted). If
- this name is Quadlet-managed, delegate to mios-restart (systemctl restart +
- readiness poll); only an unmanaged ad-hoc container falls back to podman.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-text-edit
- Hardening: read + write size caps. Operator override via env so
- legitimate large-doc edits still work but the default refuses
- pathological inputs that would balloon agent context.
- Path hardening: WRITE-class operations refuse these prefixes so
- a confused agent can't overwrite system files. Operator override
- via env (CSV of forbidden write prefixes). READS are unrestricted
- -- they only contribute to taint, not damage.
- Windows-side: the OS dirs + Program Files are out of bounds.
- Resolve symlinks. If the path doesn't exist yet (create case),
- realpath returns the would-be path with intermediate symlinks
- resolved -- still useful for the prefix check.
- Check standard and case-insensitive
- If on Windows, translate WSL /mnt/c/ prefixes in the blocklist to Windows C:\ paths
- Resilience: surface Everything-suggested matches so the
- planner can retry with the real path instead of giving up.
- Hardening: enforce a max read size BEFORE pulling the file
- into memory -- agents asking to view /var/log/giant.log
- should fail fast rather than OOM the process.
- Skip hidden dirs in-place so the walk doesn't recurse.
- File path.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-tool-clone
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-tool-clone <name> [--as <new-name>] [--force]
- Fork a system-shipped MiOS shim into the operator-writable
- /usr/local/bin/ so the agent can edit it (the immutable /usr tree
- rejects writes; /usr/local is mutable on bootc).
- After the clone, /usr/local/bin/<name> wins over /usr/libexec/mios/
- <name> on PATH (because /usr/local/bin precedes /usr/libexec/mios
- in the standard /etc/profile chain). Same-name clones thus override
- the vendor shim transparently.
- Operator directive 2026-05-15: "make sure these skills are clone-
- able and modifiable by the agents themselves too! that way Hermes
- is properly improving skills and tools for things iteratively".
- mios-tool-clone mios-windows                  # fork in place
- $EDITOR /usr/local/bin/mios-windows
- # next mios-windows call uses the local copy
- mios-tool-clone mios-windows --as mios-windows-experimental
- # original mios-windows still active; experimental ships alongside
- Authoring brand-new tools (no existing source to clone) goes through
- `write_file /usr/libexec/mios/<name>` + chmod + symlink, per the
- self-improvement section of SOUL.md. mios-tool-clone is for
- augmenting existing shims.
- /usr/local/bin is root-owned on most installs; sudo via NOPASSWD if
- the caller isn't root.
- Stamp a clone marker as a comment in the second line so future readers
- can tell at a glance it's a fork. Carefully preserve the shebang.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-ttyd-expose
- mios-ttyd-expose -- securely publish the loopback ttyd terminal to the TAILNET
- for mobile access (#82). Official pattern (researched 2026-05-30): ttyd stays
- on 127.0.0.1; `tailscale serve` is the tailnet-ONLY HTTPS reverse proxy in
- front (auto-provisioned TLS cert; NOT `tailscale funnel`, which is public).
- The basic-auth credential is the SSOT [identity] login (username /
- default_password, vendor default mios/mios) that mios-ttyd-launch inherits --
- NOT a random per-host secret (operator 2026-05-30: "all usernames/passwords
- match the mios.toml user selection"). Idempotent. `mios-ttyd-expose off`
- revokes the tailnet exposure.
- Gated/opt-in: this OPENS a shell to the tailnet, so it is NOT run by default.
- Enable per-deploy via SSOT [ttyd].tailnet_expose=true -> firstboot calls this,
- or the operator runs it directly.
- Section-aware layered mios.toml reader (/etc overrides /usr).
- Day-0 gate: the boot oneshot (mios-ttyd-expose.service) runs with --auto and
- ONLY proceeds when the operator opted in via SSOT [ttyd].tailnet_expose=true
- (default false -> fresh installs keep the terminal loopback-only). A manual
- `mios-ttyd-expose` (no arg) always exposes -- an explicit operator action.
- Restart ttyd-bash so it re-reads the [identity] credential (mios-ttyd-launch
- inherits it), then REFUSE to expose unless ttyd actually requires auth (401)
- -- never publish an open shell to the tailnet.
- Publish tailnet-only HTTPS in front of loopback ttyd (persists via --bg).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-ttyd-launch
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-ttyd-launch <bash|powershell>
- Builds the ttyd argv from the MIOS_TTYD_* env (sourced via
- /etc/mios/userenv.sh, which the systemd unit EnvironmentFile=s)
- and execs ttyd. Splitting the assembly out of the .service file
- keeps the unit declarative + lets the operator override pieces
- via mios.toml [ttyd] without editing the unit.
- Load environment configurations explicitly
- Guard set -u: a value with shell-metachars must not abort under set -u.
- Variant arg picks WHICH ttyd instance to start:
- bash       -> port MIOS_PORT_TTYD_BASH (default 7681), runs
- MIOS_TTYD_BASH_SHELL or /bin/bash.
- powershell -> port MIOS_PORT_TTYD_POWERSHELL (default 7682),
- runs MIOS_TTYD_POWERSHELL_SHELL or
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-powershell --shell.
- Common knobs (both variants):
- MIOS_TTYD_BIND               default 127.0.0.1
- MIOS_TTYD_REQUIRE_AUTH       default true; refuses exposed bind
- without auth creds.
- MIOS_TTYD_AUTH_USER / _PASS  basic-auth credentials.
- MIOS_TTYD_SSL_CERT / _KEY    optional TLS termination.
- MIOS_TTYD_WRITABLE           default true.
- MIOS_TTYD_MAX_CLIENTS        default 0 (ttyd default).
- Section-aware, layered mios.toml reader (/etc overrides /usr). Used to inherit
- the global MiOS login credential from [identity] (operator 2026-05-30: "all
- usernames/passwords match the mios.toml user selection, default mios/mios").
- Resolve port + shell defaults.
- SSOT credential inheritance (operator 2026-05-30: "all usernames/passwords
- match the mios.toml user selection, default mios/mios"). Per-instance auth
- ([ttyd].auth_user/_pass -> MIOS_TTYD_AUTH_*) OVERRIDES; otherwise inherit the
- global MiOS login from [identity] (username / default_password), same as the
- Portal / Cockpit / Forge logins (server.py _pcfg pattern). Vendor default
- mios/mios. No per-host random secret -- the credential is the operator's one
- user selection everywhere. See [[mios_mobile_access]].
- Safety: refuse to bind beyond loopback without credentials. ttyd
- itself happily exposes an unauthenticated shell; this guard is
- the difference between a casual local convenience and a remote
- code execution surface.
- Window title in the browser tab.
- Pin the xterm font size so the portal's inline embed renders a deterministic
- ~80x20 grid in its fixed pixel box (operator: "80x20 everywhere"). SSOT:
- [ttyd].font_size -> MIOS_TTYD_FONT_SIZE.
- Final argv: ttyd <flags> <shell-cmd> [shell-args]
- Split SHELL_CMD on whitespace so "mios-powershell --shell" becomes
- argv[0]=mios-powershell + argv[1]=--shell.
- shellcheck disable=SC2206
