## usr/libexec/mios/mios-web-extract
- Boilerplate containers stripped WITH their contents (never the article body).
- Main-content containers: when a page marks its <article>/<main>, extract ONLY
- that subtree so site chrome (header menus, section lists, promos, newsletters)
- is dropped -- the readability win for news pages (operator 2026-05-24: the AP
- page came back full of menu/section nav instead of the actual stories).
- stdlib html.unescape resolves ALL named + numeric entities (decimal AND
- hex, e.g. &#x27;) correctly -- the old hand-rolled map missed hex entities,
- so apostrophes/quotes leaked as "&#x27;" into the extracted text.
- Prefer the largest <article>/<main> subtree (the real content) when the
- page marks it; fall back to the whole stripped page when it doesn't, or
- when the marked region is too thin to be the body.
- Be HONEST -- never fabricate page content. The caller surfaces this
- so the agent says it couldn't read the page instead of inventing.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-web-search
- SSOT endpoints (env rendered from mios.toml); localhost fallbacks = the
- vendor container publish ports.
- Query-EXPANSION model. Operator 2026-05-24 ("did NOT do multiple passes /
- differing queries"): the old default (qwen3:0.6b-cpu on the retired micro lane)
- was loaded NOWHERE -- cold -- so every expansion blew the 6 s budget and SILENTLY fell
- back to a single query, killing the whole fan-out. Default instead to the
- model the mios-daemon pins ALWAYS-WARM on the CPU lane (qwen3:1.7b @ :11435,
- keep_alive=-1): expansion is then sub-second, never cold-fails, and is more
- capable than the weak 0.6b. Override via MIOS_WEB_EXPAND_MODEL / _ENDPOINT.
- Native /api/chat lives at the base (strip a trailing /v1 like agent-pipe).
- Reciprocal Rank Fusion constant (the standard 60 from the RRF paper).
- publishedDate passthrough (operator 2026-05-25): SearXNG NEWS
- engines set this on dated stories -- lets the caller PREFER real
- articles over bare homepages and cite recency. Empty on general web.
- Topical anchor: a multi-word but OFF-TOPIC invented sub-query ("what is 2026
- minus 1978" from a flights ask) passes the degenerate word-count filter yet
- fetches junk (age calculators), which RRF then surfaces. Require >=1 shared
- CONTENT token with the ORIGINAL query. Structural -- a classic function-word +
- generic-qualifier screen + trailing-s plural fold, NOT a topic deny-list. The
- stopword list is SSOT-sourced (mios.toml [search].anchor_stopwords), not baked
- in code. Pure numbers are excluded (a bare year is too weak an anchor).
- Unicode-aware word tokenizer (replaces the Latin-only [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{2,},
- which tokenized CJK/accented text to ZERO -> every non-Latin expansion was
- dropped as "degenerate"/"off-anchor"). CJK/Kana/Hangul are written WITHOUT
- spaces and are information-dense, so each ideograph is its own token (else a
- whole spaceless sentence reads as ONE token and trips the word-count gates);
- every other script keeps whole word-runs of unicode letters+digits (so "café",
- "Zürich", "naïve" survive intact). `re.UNICODE` is implicit for str patterns.
- ASCII noise floor: the old regex required >=3 chars, dropping tiny Latin
- fragments ("us"); keep that for ASCII but NEVER length-gate non-Latin
- (a single CJK char carries real meaning).
- Date-aware (operator 2026-05-26 "use env detect for current values for all
- AI functions"): the live system year, so time-sensitive sub-queries anchor
- to NOW (2026 this year, 2027 next) instead of a stale year. Never hardcoded.
- Recency-aware year-anchor (operator 2026-06-12): when the CALLER already passes
- a time_range / news category, SearXNG date-filters server-side, so appending a
- bare year is redundant AND magnets "2026 - Wikipedia" year-overview pages. In
- that case steer the micro toward 'latest'/concrete-event terms instead.
- llama.cpp OpenAI /v1 (MiOS is /v1-only): the expander posts the OpenAI
- /chat/completions shape + response_format json_object. qwen3 via llama.cpp
- /v1 strands the answer in <think> and returns EMPTY content -> 0 sub-queries
- (silent single-query fallback), so disable thinking to land the JSON in content.
- De-silenced (operator 2026-05-24: a SILENT cold-micro fallback to one
- query is exactly what hid the dead fan-out). Log to stderr so a broken
- expansion is visible in the journal; still fall back so search runs.
- Drop DEGENERATE expansions before they hit SearXNG: a bare single word or
- stopword fragment ("last" from "last minute", "set" from "set up", "best",
- "many") makes the metasearch return a DICTIONARY / unrelated page (Merriam-
- Webster, Last.fm, a card game) that then pollutes the RRF-fused results
- (operator 2026-05-26: "last"->dictionary, "set"->card game). Language-
- agnostic -- word-count + length only, NO keyword/topic list. The ORIGINAL
- query is ALWAYS kept (it is the caller's real, vetted facet); only the
- model-invented alternatives are screened. Tunable knobs.
- The ORIGINAL is normally the lead facet (the caller's vetted query). BUT a LONG,
- instruction-like query ("research and report on all of today's global trending")
- searched VERBATIM returns junk -- the word "research" matches the Research Wikipedia
- page (operator 2026-06-12) -- while the micro-LLM's reformulated facets are clean.
- So when the original is long (an instruction, not a search TERM) AND we got
- reformulations, lead with the reformulations instead of the raw instruction.
- Script-neutral word-count gate (unicode tokenizer, NO keyword/topic list);
- degrade-open (return below falls back to [query] if every reformulation gets
- screened out).
- Token count over unicode word-runs so HYPHENATED / underscored slugs
- ("cheapest-flights-toronto-to-tokyo" -> 5 tokens) count as multi-word
- and pass, a CJK phrase counts per-ideograph (not zero), while a bare
- "last" / "set" (1 token) is dropped.
- OFF-TOPIC drop: a multi-word invented sub-query that shares NO content
- token with the original has drifted (the "2026 minus 1978" case); skip
- it so the fan-out stays on-topic. Skipped when the anchor is too thin.
- RRF: each result earns 1/(RRF_K + rank) per query list it appears in;
- appearing high across MULTIPLE phrasings wins. Dedupe by URL.
- Offline / SearXNG down: be HONEST -- never fabricate. The caller
- surfaces this so the model says it couldn't reach the web instead
- of inventing an answer.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-webtools-firstboot.sh
- (crawl4ai-slim FastAPI engine and Mendable firecrawl API/worker stack). Runs as
- a prerequisite service before the web-tools containers are started by Quadlet.
- WS-DEPLOY: each image build is INDEPENDENT (one failure never aborts the other),
- RETRIED with backoff (a transient network blip under install-time contention no
- longer leaves an image unbuilt so the consumer Quadlet can't start), and VERIFIED
- to exist after the build. Exits non-zero if any needed image is still missing so
- the .service's Restart=on-failure re-attempts instead of leaving webtools down.
- NOTE: intentionally NOT `set -e` -- a failed crawl4ai build must not skip the
- firecrawl build. Errors are handled explicitly per image and aggregated into $_rc.
- ─── firstboot idempotency sentinel ────────────────────────────────
- Once both webtools images are built + verified, skip re-running on every boot.
- The sentinel lives under /var/lib/mios (persists across bootc upgrades). It is
- written ONLY on a fully-successful run (_rc==0) below, so a partial/failed
- build still retries. Delete it to force a rebuild:
- rm -f /var/lib/mios/.webtools-firstboot.done && systemctl restart mios-webtools-firstboot
- need_build <image> <containerfile> -> echoes 1 if a (re)build is needed, else 0.
- Rebuild when the image is absent OR the Containerfile is newer than the image.
- build_image_retry <image> <containerfile> <context> -> 0 on success (image
- present + verified), 1 after exhausting retries. Backoff: 10s, 20s.
- maybe_build <image> <containerfile> <context> <label> -> respects need_build,
- never aborts the caller; returns the build result (0 ok / 1 failed / 0 skipped).
- 1. crawl4ai-slim FastAPI engine
- 2. firecrawl API/worker stack (independent -- runs even if crawl4ai failed)
- sentinel: all images built + verified -- gate re-runs on later boots.
- Degrade-open: the touch never changes the exit status.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-win-scan
- The Windows system drive as mounted in WSL. Honour a non-default mount
- (wsl.conf `root=`), falling back to the drvfs default.
- Dedup by name (Store packages ship several versions with the same AUMID;
- a game may also have both a store entry and a Start-Menu shortcut). First
- source wins -- sources are ordered store/game-authoritative before the
- generic Start-Menu sweep.
- ── Steam ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ── Epic ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- ── GOG ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Prefer the largest .exe (the game, not an updater/redistributable).
- ── Store / UWP / Game Pass ────────────────────────────────────────
- <Name>_<version>_<arch>__<PublisherHash>  ->  <Name>_<PublisherHash>
- Namespace-agnostic parse (AppxManifest uses several xmlns).
- Skip obvious non-user frameworks/runtimes/DLC-trackers early.
- Fallback name: the Identity Name's last dotted segment, spaced.
- ── Start Menu shortcuts ───────────────────────────────────────────
- Skip uninstallers / docs / update shims -- not launch targets.
- Launch by the .lnk's WINDOWS path: the real-host executor
- Start-Process'es it, resolving whatever the shortcut points at
- (exe / UWP / URI).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-window
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-window <subcommand> [args...]
- Title-pattern-driven wrapper around mios-pc-control's window-* verbs.
- Lets agents + operators say "center Notepad" or "move Discord to
- (100,100)" instead of having to first call window-list, parse hwnds,
- then dispatch a second verb with the numeric handle.
- SUBCOMMANDS
- list
- Print all visible top-level windows (delegates to
- `mios-pc-control window-list`).
- center  <title-pattern>
- focus   <title-pattern>
- move    <title-pattern> <x> <y>
- resize  <title-pattern> <w> <h>
- minimize <title-pattern>
- maximize <title-pattern>
- restore <title-pattern>
- Each resolves the pattern to a window handle (case-insensitive
- substring match against MainWindowTitle from window-list) and
- forwards to `mios-pc-control window-<verb> <hwnd> [args...]`.
- Ambiguous matches: takes the first match and lists alternatives
- to stderr.
- Operator directive 2026-05-17: "make sure window moving is active/
- functional and can launch things centered by default and that it can
- be told to move the windows". Launch-time centering is in mios-windows
- launch (URI + .exe branches). Post-launch move/center/focus/resize
- now flow through this single ergonomic shim.
- ─── helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
- Parse mios-pc-control window-list output (column-aligned). The window list
- is passed via the MIOS_WL env var, NOT a pipe: `python3 - <<HEREDOC` reads
- its PROGRAM from stdin, so a pipe on the same fd would be shadowed by the
- heredoc and sys.stdin would arrive empty (every lookup then "no match").
- Same env-var-carries-the-data idiom mios-everything uses for RAW_LINES.
- Header / divider / blank
- 7 columns: hwnd pid x y w h title (title may contain spaces)
- Print primary hwnd to stdout; alternatives to stderr
- ─── show/restore/minimize/maximize via ShowWindow ───────────────────
- mios-pc-control doesn't have these natively, so we shell out to
- PowerShell directly. SW_NORMAL=1, SW_MINIMIZE=6, SW_MAXIMIZE=3,
- SW_RESTORE=9.
- Source guard: lets tests `source mios-window; _resolve_hwnd discord`
- without firing the dispatch + usage exit.
- Directory this script lives in -- so the half-screen region actuator can find
- its sibling pure-geometry helper (mios_window_region.py) whether invoked by
- absolute path, PATH lookup, or symlink.
- [os_control].region_snap_halves gate. The half-screen snap regions
- (left-half / right-half / top-half / bottom-half) are ADDITIVE region names;
- degrade-open -> enabled when the key is ABSENT so they work without a
- mios.toml edit. Set false to restrict to the historical region vocabulary
- (the new names then behave exactly like any other unknown subcommand).
- Shared layered mios.toml resolver (vendor < host < user), path injected as argv[1].
- Degrade-open: absent key -> enabled (exit 0); honor the highest layer that sets it.
- ─── Cross-desktop executor routing (operator 2026-05-29 OS-control train) ───
- focus/close/move/center failed with "no window title matches" because this
- tool enumerates + acts LOCALLY in the WSL session, which is BLIND to the
- operator's actual windows (WSLg flatpaks + Windows-host apps both appear as
- top-level windows on the WINDOWS desktop, not the WSL X11 session). The
- Windows-side executor (mios-oscontrol-server.ps1 @ [os_control].executor_
- endpoint) SEES them all + has /window/<op> endpoints. When that endpoint is
- configured, route the window OP there (the same surface _enumerate_windows
- already reads). Falls through to the local mios-pc-control path when no
- executor is set (bare-metal Linux desktop). Semantic positions (left/right/
- top/...) map to the executor's center/move; 'center' has a direct endpoint.
- WSL2 local auto-discovery (operator 2026-06-07): no env/toml endpoint, but the
- in-session executor listens on :11437, reachable over the WSL NAT gateway with
- Tailscale OFF. WITHOUT this, _OSC_EP stays empty -> the executor routing below is
- SKIPPED -> window ops fall to the BLIND local enumeration -> "no window title
- matches" (the close_window failure the operator hit on "close spotify": the
- executor SEES the window via case-insensitive -like, the local WSL path does not).
- Same resolver shape as mios-windows / mios-pc-control. Fixes close/focus/move/
- minimize/maximize/restore all at once.
- Executor health-gate -- mirror mios-pc-control's guard (its python L141-145
- probes "<exec_ep>/health" with a 3s timeout and clears the endpoint on any
- failure). mios-window historically LACKED this: on a default WSL dev VM the
- auto-discovery above sets _OSC_EP=http://<gw>:11437 even though no executor
- is listening there, so every window op POSTed to a dead socket and the branch
- ended in `exit $?` (curl's timeout rc) -- the working LOCAL mios-pc-control
- window-* fallback (the case block below) was dead code. Probing /health and
- clearing _OSC_EP on failure makes a down/absent executor fall through to the
- local path, while a real, reachable executor (federation / bare-metal-with-
- server) still wins. Fixes focus/move/position/resize/close/window_state at once.
- Parse title and optional monitor
- flatpak instances are PER-USER. The agent dispatches window ops through
- the launcher broker, which runs as ROOT -- so a bare `flatpak ps` here
- sees NONE of the operator's running apps (operator 2026-05-29 train:
- the flatpak-kill close fired fine when run directly as the operator but
- the broker/root path saw no instance + fell through). Run flatpak AS the
- operator: directly when we already are them, else switch user (runuser
- when root, sudo otherwise) WITH the operator's XDG_RUNTIME_DIR so flatpak
- finds the per-user instance registry under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/.flatpak/.
- WSLg/flatpak windows are hosted on the Windows side by msrdc
- (the RAIL/RDP client); a Windows-side WM_CLOSE does NOT
- propagate into the Linux app -- the executor returns ok:true
- but the window stays open (operator 2026-05-29 OS-control
- train: close_window matched gedit, ok:true, window-diff 18->18,
- never closed). MiOS GUI apps are flatpaks, so close them from
- the WSL side via `flatpak kill <app-id>` (reliable + offline).
- Map the title needle to a RUNNING flatpak instance (substring
- either direction vs the app-id last segment OR full id). Fall
- through to the executor WM_CLOSE for NATIVE Windows apps
- (notepad, taskmgr, ...) which DO honour it.
- Pass through --json if present so agents get structured output.
- TD-1: eval-safe, input=internal integers and layout bounds, not agent-controlled
- Half-screen snap regions. The rectangle is derived LIVE from the
- monitor work area (queried via `mios-pc-control screen-layout`) by the
- sibling pure-geometry helper -- no pixel constants (Law 7). window-move
- + window-resize route through mios-pc-control, so this works whether an
- OS-control executor is present or not.
- Graceful close via WM_CLOSE -- the same as the operator
- clicking the X. NOT a kill; apps with unsaved state get to
- prompt. Operator-flagged 2026-05-17: agent ran
- `pkill -f hermes-agent` thinking "close the crew" meant
- "close the agent crew" and self-terminated. window-close on
- the matched window is the correct verb every time.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-window-active
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-window-active <name-pattern>
- Reports whether the named app's window is actually PRESENTED to
- the operator -- not just whether the process is alive. Operator
- directive 2026-05-16: "if MiOS Agents detect the launched
- process(es) as alive or present -- MiOS Agents should understand
- that simply having the application live isn't enough and that it
- needs to present the active window to the user(s)".
- A process can be alive but its window:
- * never created (MainWindowHandle == 0)
- * minimized to the taskbar (IsIconic == true)
- * hidden (IsWindowVisible false)
- * sized off-screen
- Any of these means the operator does NOT see the app, even
- though `pgrep` / `Get-Process` would say "running".
- Output: ONE-LINE JSON to stdout. Single source of truth -- agents
- parse this instead of running their own ad-hoc Get-Process check.
- {
- "query": "epiphany",
- "process_alive": true,
- "process_id": 12345,
- "process_name": "epiphany",
- "window_handle": 1248892,
- "window_title": "Welcome to Web - Epiphany",
- "window_visible": true,
- "window_minimized": false,
- "window_foreground": true,
- "window_rect": {"x": 720, "y": 232, "w": 1280, "h": 720},
- "on_screen": true,
- "presented_to_operator": true,
- "summary": "presented"
- }
- `presented_to_operator` is the bottom-line bool the agent should
- trust: TRUE iff process_alive AND window_handle != 0 AND
- window_visible AND NOT window_minimized AND window rect is
- on-screen with positive area.
- `summary` is one of:
- presented        -- visible + not minimized + on-screen (success)
- not-running      -- process_alive false
- no-window        -- process alive but MainWindowHandle == 0 (still spawning OR pure CLI)
- minimized        -- process + window exist but iconic
- hidden           -- process + window exist but IsWindowVisible false
- off-screen       -- window rect outside every monitor work area
- Works for both Windows apps and WSLg-hosted Linux apps -- WSLg
- wraps each Linux Wayland surface in a Win32 top-level owned by
- msrdc.exe / mstsc.exe, so the Win32 API sees them identically.
- Multi-pattern support: caller may pass a comma-separated list of
- patterns ("epiphany,web,gnome web"). We try each in order against
- both process name AND window title. First match wins.
- Operator-flagged 2026-05-16: Win32 windows hosted by WSLg msrdc.exe
- show the LINUX-app display name in MainWindowTitle (e.g., Epiphanys
- .desktop Name= is "Web", not "Epiphany"), so a single-pattern
- "epiphany" search misses the window.
- Build the PowerShell pattern list as a quoted comma-joined string.
- First pattern is the canonical query (for output JSON + pgrep).
- Stringify the --present flag for embedding in the PowerShell literal.
- ─── Linux-side pre-check: pgrep across all patterns ──────────────────
- WSLg-hosted Linux flatpaks (Epiphany, Nautilus, Ptyxis, etc.) are
- wrapped in msrdc.exe on the Windows side -- the Win32 Get-Process
- loop sees "msrdc.exe", not "epiphany". So a Win32-only check reports
- "not-running" even when the Linux process IS alive. Run pgrep
- (against ANY of the patterns) first; if the Linux process exists,
- surface process_alive=true in the JSON even if no Win32 window is
- found yet.
- pgrep -f matches FULL cmdlines, so it SELF-MATCHES this verifier
- (its own argv contains the search pattern) -> a false process_alive
- for an app that isn't running. Drop any matched pid whose cmdline
- mentions mios-window-active (the verifier's own process tree).
- PowerShell snippet -- the query is embedded as a single-quoted
- literal so it survives broker dispatch (no env var inheritance
- needed).
- Word-boundary regex match instead of bare substring.
- Substring matching gave false positives: e.g. pattern
- "web" hit "WebUI" in an unrelated browser's title bar,
- causing the launch verifier to report "presented" for
- Epiphany when Epiphany never actually opened (the verifier
- latched onto the operator's Zen window with title
- "MiOS Agent (Open WebUI) - Zen Twilight"). Word-boundary
- \b<pat>\b requires non-word chars on both sides, so "web"
- matches "open web" or "the web" but NOT "WebUI".
- If pgrep on the Linux side found the process, report that fact
- so the caller can distinguish "process exists but no Win32 window
- yet" from "process not even running".
- --present mode: actuate before re-measuring. FORCEFUL foreground
- (operator 2026-05-26 "Xbox-mode focus didn't work" -- a fullscreen
- Game Pass game stayed window_foreground:false after a plain
- SetForegroundWindow because Windows blocks foreground changes from a
- background caller, only flashing the taskbar). Bypass the foreground
- lock the standard way: tap Alt, AttachThreadInput to the current
- foreground window's thread, THEN SetForegroundWindow, and toggle
- TOPMOST to force z-order. SW_RESTORE=9 / SW_SHOWNORMAL=1 un-minimise
- first. Works for normal + borderless-fullscreen windows (true
- EXCLUSIVE-fullscreen can still resist -- a hard Windows limit).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-windows
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-windows <subcommand> [args...]
- Reach the Windows host from inside this WSL2 distro. The agent uses
- this when it needs to launch a Windows app, run a PowerShell command,
- or otherwise touch the host the WSL VM lives inside.
- TWO BACKENDS, ONE FRONTEND
- ──────────────────────────
- WSL interop (default; no setup, no SSH, no Tailscale required):
- /init -- the program PID 1 inside this WSL2 distro -- transparently
- exec's any /mnt/c/.../*.exe directly on the Windows host, with
- stdout/stderr piped back into the Linux side. Works for every
- GUI app + any non-elevated cmd.exe / powershell.exe one-liner.
- Tailscale SSH (subcommand: `ssh-ps`; opt-in for remote / elevated):
- For commands that need to run AS the host's interactive operator
- account (not the SYSTEM-context interop spawns), or that need to
- reach a different machine on the tailnet, the legacy Tailscale-SSH
- path is preserved. Requires Tailscale SSH enabled host-side
- (`tailscale set --ssh`); see /etc/mios/windows-host (pinned
- tailnet IP) and the [identity] block in mios.toml.
- OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-05-15
- ─────────────────────────────
- "didn't create a skill or tool to use--should be able to ssh in to
- the hosts' shell environment via loopback (or similar)". The "or
- similar" turned out to be plain WSL interop -- no SSH needed for
- the common case (launching notepad, running ipconfig, querying a
- service status). The Tailscale-SSH path stays for the cases where
- interop's SYSTEM-spawned context isn't what's wanted.
- SUBCOMMANDS
- launch <app>      Launch a Windows GUI app by short name (notepad,
- explorer, calc, mspaint, snipping-tool, taskmgr,
- regedit, control, cmd, powershell, pwsh) or by
- full /mnt/c/.../*.exe path. Detached; returns
- immediately.
- ps "<cmd>"        Run a Windows PowerShell command via interop.
- Output captured + returned. Default PowerShell
- 5.1 (System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0). Override
- via MIOS_WINDOWS_PWSH=<absolute path> for pwsh 7.
- cmd "<cmd>"       Run a Windows cmd.exe command via interop.
- ssh-ps [-e] "<cmd>"   Run a PowerShell command via Tailscale SSH
- (preserves the legacy logic for elevated /
- remote-tailnet cases). -e wraps in a
- SYSTEM-level Task Scheduler trigger
- (placeholder; not yet wired).
- list              Print known short-name -> .exe mappings.
- help              Print this help.
- GENERATIVE Windows-app name resolution -- NO hardcoded short-name->exe table
- (operator "NO HARDCODES"; research 2026-05-29). The canonical exe-name->path
- map on Windows is the App Paths registry: HKCU/HKLM \SOFTWARE\Microsoft\
- Windows\CurrentVersion\App Paths\<name>.exe whose (Default) value is the
- fully-qualified path (per-user installs under HKCU, all-users under HKLM, so
- scan BOTH). Resolve a bare name straight from the live registry via reg.exe;
- returns a WSL path on stdout, or non-zero if not registered (caller then
- tries System32 / mios-find). This covers notepad/calc/mspaint/regedit/... and
- every operator-installed app that registers App Paths -- without a baked list.
- GENERATIVE Start-Menu .lnk resolution (research 2026-05-29 open-Q1: App Paths
- is INSTALLER-OPTIONAL + incomplete, and the Everything index is install-gated,
- so a name in neither would fail). The Start Menu is the canonical, always-
- present app catalog on Windows: scan both the all-users (%ProgramData%) and
- per-user (%APPDATA%) Programs trees for a .lnk whose name matches, pick the
- shortest (closest) match, and return its WSL path -- Start-Process opens a
- .lnk directly (covers Store/UWP shortcuts too, which have no plain exe path).
- Everything-INDEPENDENT (pure filesystem scan); the fallback before mios-find.
- GENERATIVE UWP/Store app resolution (operator 2026-06-04 "no hardcodes for
- application detections"). UWP built-ins (Calculator, Settings, Photos, Camera,
- Clock, ...) register NO App Paths exe and NO Start-Menu .lnk -- they live ONLY
- in the AppsFolder, enumerable via Get-StartApps (Name + AppID). Fuzzy-match the
- requested name to a Start app and echo `shell:appsFolder\<AppID>` (the exact
- form the launch dispatch + the in-session executor already open via explorer's
- appsFolder handler). No baked app list -- the LIVE Get-StartApps catalog is the
- source of truth, so this resolves ANY installed UWP app, not a fixed set.
- Match SPACE/PUNCTUATION/CASE-insensitively: agents routinely mangle a
- display name ("Character Map" -> "CharacterMap", "Task Manager" ->
- "TaskManager"), so normalise BOTH the query and each candidate to
- alphanumerics-lowercase before substring-matching. >=2 chars guards the
- empty/degenerate query from matching everything (operator 2026-06-04).
- Resolve the Windows OS-control executor endpoint from SSOT: the
- in /etc (host overlay wins) then /usr mios.toml. Echoes the trimmed URL (no
- trailing slash) or nothing. No hardcoded host/port (operator binding).
- WSL2 local auto-discovery (operator 2026-06-07): no env override + no
- configured endpoint, but the in-session executor (mios-oscontrol-server.ps1)
- listens on :11437. Reach it over the WSL NAT default-route gateway (the
- Windows host) so VISIBLE launches work WITHOUT Tailscale -- otherwise the
- WSL-interop fallback lands in a Session-0 window station (no visible window).
- The caller curls /launch, so an unreachable gateway simply falls back to the
- legacy route -- no regression, and it self-heals once the host firewall
- admits the WSL subnet. Same resolver shape as mios-pc-control.
- Launch a Windows GUI app THROUGH the in-session executor (operator 2026-05-29:
- the canonical fix). A Windows process spawned via WSL interop / the launcher
- broker lands in a NON-INTERACTIVE window station -- simple Win32 apps may still
- surface, but multi-process Electron apps (Discord, Slack, Teams, VS Code)
- spawn their processes there and their window NEVER reaches the operator's
- visible desktop (proven live: Discord -> 6 procs, MainWindowHandle=0, ZERO
- top-level windows). The executor (:11437) runs as a scheduled task INSIDE the
- operator's interactive session, so its Start-Process shows the window on the
- real desktop + verifies it + centers it. Returns 0 on a confirmed launch (so
- the caller exits), non-zero to fall through to the legacy broker route.
- Fast reachability pre-check: a configured-but-unreachable executor (e.g. the
- auto-resolved WSL-gateway endpoint before the host firewall admits the WSL
- subnet) must fall back to the legacy interop path in ~2s, NOT stall the whole
- launch on the 45s POST timeout below (operator 2026-06-07).
- Extract clean token: e.g. WindowsCalculator, SpotifyMusic
- `verify` = the human title hint (MIOS_LAUNCH_TITLE_HINT, e.g. "Forza
- Horizon 6") so the executor matches the WINDOW by title, not by a steam://
- URI / shell:appsFolder string that never appears in a window title
- (operator 2026-05-30). Falls back to `app` when no hint is set.
- launched:true (window confirmed present) OR fired:true (process started --
- the executor's in-session Start-Process succeeded; honest about windowless
- apps via launched). Either means we used the correct in-session path.
- Arm the executor-based auto-center (operator 2026-05-29: "launches are ALWAYS
- centered"). The in-PowerShell center loop relies on the launched process's
- MainWindowHandle, which is 0 for Store apps (the stub process doesn't own the
- window) -> notepad et al. open top-left. mios-autocenter instead snapshots the
- window hwnds BEFORE the launch + centers the LARGEST NEW window afterward via
- the Windows executor -- robust for Store/native/WSLg alike. No-op without an
- executor endpoint. Same mechanism flatpak-launch uses for Linux GUIs.
- ─── Tailscale SSH path (legacy; preserved verbatim from prior version) ──
- Resolve Windows tailscale IP. Single-tenant dev VM contract: there's
- exactly one Windows host on the tailnet that this distro runs inside.
- IP is stored once in /etc/mios/windows-host (created by
- mios-hermes-firstboot if Tailscale is detected).
- Resolve operator username -- the agent's identity for the SSH session.
- GENERATIVE: enumerate the live Windows App Paths registry (the real
- exe-name -> path map) instead of a hardcoded short-name table.
- Stdin mode: `mios-windows launch -` reads the path from
- stdin. Sidesteps bash paren-parsing on paths like
- C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steam.exe where the unquoted
- `(x86)` triggers a subshell-syntax error before the script
- is even invoked. Operator-confirmed regression 2026-05-16:
- agent emitted `mios-windows launch C:\Program Files
- (x86)\Steam\steam.exe` without quoting -- bash errored
- "syntax error near unexpected token `('".
- URI passthrough: `mios-windows launch uplay://launch/16732/0`
- (or steam://, epic://, http://, etc.) re-dispatches to the
- ps subcommand with Start-Process -- Windows registers
- protocol handlers per scheme. Without this, the existence
- check below rejects URIs as "unknown app" and the agent
- spirals into refusal. Operator-confirmed regression
- 2026-05-16: agent saw `mios-find "the crew motorfest"`
- return `mios-windows ps "Start-Process uplay://..."` but
- then called `mios-windows launch uplay://...` (wrong
- subcommand) and got "unknown app", concluding the URL was
- invalid. Now both subcommands accept URIs.
- ─── URI / UWP launches: center+focus the resulting window ───
- Direct .exe launches center via Start-Process -PassThru +
- MainWindowHandle polling on $p (the launched process). URI
- launches (steam://, com.epicgames.launcher://, http://, ...) and
- UWP shell:appsFolder\ launches DON'T return the game's process
- -- they return the protocol handler (steam.exe, explorer.exe).
- Without explicit post-launch window discovery, these never get
- centered. Operator directive 2026-05-17: "launching apps should
- launch centered too!! MiOS Agents must have launch param/args
- tools for launching applications(should always launch centered
- and focused)".
- Strategy for URI/UWP: snapshot the current top-level window
- handles, run Start-Process, poll for new top-level windows for
- up to MIOS_LAUNCH_CENTER_TIMEOUT seconds (default 15), then
- center+focus the first new window matching MIOS_LAUNCH_TITLE_HINT
- (case-insensitive substring) -- or the first new window if no
- hint. mios-find sets the hint to the app name from the
- inventory so multi-window protocol handlers (Steam launches
- both the storefront AND the game) center the right one.
- $1 = Start-Process invocation, e.g. "Start-Process 'steam://...'"
- OR "Start-Process -FilePath explorer.exe -ArgumentList 'shell:appsFolder\\...'"
- $2 = title hint (may be empty)
- PowerShell here-doc: snapshot -> launch -> poll new windows.
- Single-line for the broker's "CAPTURE: <cmdline>\n" wire.
- UNIFIED window source (operator 2026-06-22 "unify MiOS systems"): center+detect
- the launched window via the SAME EnumWindows + IsWindowVisible enumeration the
- window_list verb (mios-pc-control.ps1) uses -- NOT Get-Process MainWindowHandle,
- which is 0 for Electron / child-process windows (Spotify, Steam) so the old code
- reported "[no new window]" + skipped centering on apps that DID open. Full C#
- class (-TypeDefinition) so the EnumWindowsProc delegate is a normal nested type.
- Un-minimize if needed (SW_RESTORE = 9, SW_SHOW = 5), then center + focus.
- In-session executor FIRST: Start-Process invokes the protocol
- handler for steam:// / epic:// / uplay:// etc. natively + shows
- the window on the operator's desktop. The old broker/WSL-interop
- `ps` path fails "powershell.exe: Invalid argument" (the broker
- CWD isn't Windows-translatable) AND lands in a non-interactive
- window station (operator 2026-05-30: "play a game" -> steam:// ->
- Invalid argument). Fall back to the ps path only with no executor.
- UWP / Microsoft Store / Xbox / Game Pass apps. AppIDs come
- in two shapes:
- 1. shell:appsFolder\<PackageFamilyName>!<Entry>
- -- canonical full URI (what mios-apps writes to the
- windows-games cache for UWP entries)
- 2. <PackageFamilyName>!<Entry>
- -- bare AppID as Get-StartApps returns
- (e.g. "Microsoft.Limitless_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App")
- Both dispatch via explorer's shell:appsFolder URI handler
- -- the standard Windows mechanism to launch a UWP package
- by its package-family-name. Operator-flagged 2026-05-17:
- "Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 ... launching it directly
- hasn'\''t been working" because the .exe doesn'\''t exist
- at a predictable filesystem path for UWP packages.
- UWP / Store / Xbox apps. In-session executor first (it launches
- shell: URIs via explorer.exe + shows the window on the desktop);
- the broker/interop ps path is the fallback (Start-Process can't
- grok shell: URIs, so explorer.exe is the handler there too).
- Auto-heal dropped backslashes (e.g. shell:appsFolderSpotifyAB... -> shell:appsFolder\SpotifyAB...)
- Bare AppID (PackageFamilyName!Entry) from Get-StartApps --
- prepend shell:appsFolder\ then launch via the in-session
- executor first (explorer.exe handler), broker ps as fallback.
- Translate Windows-style paths (C:\... or D:\...) to WSL paths
- before the existence check. Operator-confirmed regression
- 2026-05-16: mios-find returns Windows-style paths (intended
- for Start-Process on the Windows side) -- mios-windows
- launch was rejecting them with "unknown app" because the
- bash `[ -e <C:\...> ]` test cant resolve a literal backslash
- path from WSL. wslpath -u handles the translation.
- UWP/Store built-in (Calculator, Notepad, Settings, Photos, ...) -- no exe,
- no .lnk; resolved generatively via Get-StartApps -> AppID. Launch
- the shell:appsFolder URI via the in-session executor (explorer
- handler) first, broker ps as the fallback. Tried BEFORE the
- System32 fallback so Windows 11 UWP AppX apps (Notepad/Calc) use shell:appsFolder.
- Last-resort: ask mios-find. Operator-confirmed regression
- 2026-05-16 night: agent called `mios-windows launch beamng`
- (just the name) and got "unknown app", then FABRICATED a
- nonexistent "mios-windows install" subcommand to suggest.
- If mios-find returns ONE runnable line, exec it -- this
- is the canonical chain anyway (mios-find -> launch), now
- done implicitly so the helper is forgiving.
- The mios-find line is a raw `mios-windows ps` INTEROP command
- (Start-Process in a NON-INTERACTIVE station -> the window opens
- where the operator never sees it -> "nothing launched" for Store
- games / URIs; operator 2026-05-30 Wreckfest: fired:true but
- presented_to_operator:false). Extract the launch TARGET (first
- single-quoted token: a shell:appsFolder URI, a protocol:// URI,
- or a path) and RE-LAUNCH it through THIS script's executor-first
- path so it lands on the REAL interactive desktop. Fall back to
- the interop line only if nothing usable extracts.
- ALWAYS-CENTER: snapshot windows + center the new one post-launch via
- the executor (operator 2026-05-29 "launches are ALWAYS centered").
- ── PRIMARY: in-session executor launch ───────────────────────
- Fire through the Windows executor (:11437), which runs in the
- operator's INTERACTIVE desktop session, so the window appears on the
- real screen + is verified + centered. The broker/interop route below
- leaves multi-process Electron apps (Discord/Slack/Teams) WINDOWLESS --
- their window is created in a non-interactive station the operator never
- sees (operator 2026-05-29: "discord NEVER OPENED" -- proven: executor
- /launch shows it, broker cmd/start does not). Falls through to the

- ── Service-user broker route (fallback) ──────────────────────
- Operator-confirmed regression 2026-05-16: agent ran
- `mios-windows launch ...` -> process succeeded, returned PID,
- but operator saw NOTHING on screen. Cause: direct setsid+nohup
- from mios-hermes (uid 820) launches the .exe in the WSL
- SERVICE session, not the operator's interactive Windows
- session. The window opens in session-0 (invisible) instead
- of session-1 (operator's desktop).
- Fix: route through the operator-side launcher broker. The
- broker runs as the operator (uid 992) inside their WSLg
- session; Start-Process there pops the window in the
- operator's interactive desktop where it's actually visible.
- Translate /mnt/c/... back to C:\... for Start-Process
- Build the PowerShell Start-Process call + auto-center post-launch.
- Operator directive 2026-05-16: "MiOS apps STILL don't center launch
- and don't self center". Default Win32 placement is top-left or
- last-position; centering here means every launched window appears
- in the middle of the operator's primary monitor working area.
- -PassThru returns the Process object so we can read MainWindowHandle.
- Win11 DWMWA_WINDOW_CORNER_PREFERENCE = 33; DWMCSP_ROUND = 2.
- PowerShell path resolution order (operator directive 2026-05-16:
- environment args first):
- 1. $WINDOWS_POWERSHELL env (set by hermes-agent.service.d drop-in)
- 2. mios.toml [paths].powershell_exe
- 3. canonical default
- Shared layered mios.toml resolver (vendor < host < user); lib dir via env.
- FIRE-AND-FORGET dispatch, NOT a CAPTURE (operator 2026-05-29 "MULTIPLE
- FAILURES": "open notepad" returned exit -1 "capture timeout >45s" though the
- window opened). A GUI launch is long-running -- the CAPTURE protocol made the
- broker WAIT for the whole PowerShell (Start-Process + the 5s center loop) and
- the agent-pipe's 45s capture wrapped THAT, so a slow/Store-app launch tripped
- the timeout + reported a false failure. The broker's plain dispatch Popens the
- command in a NEW session (detached) + returns "OK" instantly; the agent-pipe
- verifies via the window-diff / global pgrep. Mirrors the flatpak-launch detach.
- Operator-flagged 2026-05-18 (round 2): Start-Process still
- produced no window. Root cause: mios-launcher.service runs
- under user@992.service (systemd user manager = session c2
- `manager-early`), NOT the operator's interactive desktop
- session c11 (`user`). When PowerShell.exe is exec'd via
- WSL interop from c2, its Start-Process inherits the user-
- manager session context -- new process has no window
- station/desktop, MainWindowHandle stays 0.
- Bulletproof Win32-from-WSL pattern: cmd.exe /c start "" ...
- `start` uses ShellExecute, which goes through HKEY_CURRENT_
- USER associations + uses the interactive shell's window
- station regardless of the launching session. cmd.exe runs
- via the WSL interop bridge and attaches to session 1 (the
- operator's interactive). Resulting process surfaces on the
- operator's desktop.
- PowerShell is still used for the post-launch place/center
- step -- that's pure Win32 API (MoveWindow / SetForeground
- Window) on an existing hwnd, not a process spawn, so the
- session-context issue doesn't apply.
- cmd.exe /c start "" "<target>" [args...] is the canonical
- session-1 spawn for any Windows program from WSL.
- Operator directive 2026-05-18: "MiOS-Agent(s) MUST also KNOW
- window launch params/args to be able to launch and move
- precisely!!!". Three env-driven knobs the caller can set BEFORE
- invoking mios-windows launch:
- MIOS_LAUNCH_POSITION   left|right|top|bottom|center|none
- (default: center; "none" leaves WHERE the
- OS placed the window)
- MIOS_LAUNCH_SIZE       <W>x<H>  (e.g. 1280x720; default: keep
- the size Start-Process gave the window)
- MIOS_LAUNCH_PLACE      <X>,<Y>  (absolute top-left, takes
- precedence over MIOS_LAUNCH_POSITION)
- Operator directive 2026-05-18: "always default launched perfectly
- centered as a 16:10 window centered at the screens current
- resolutions bounds--centered and sized centered and ratioed at the
- golden ratio + centered per 3x3 screen grid". Default position is
- now "default": 16:10 window sized at W = screen_W / phi, centered
- on the primary monitor's WorkingArea.
- Compute the placement PowerShell snippet from those knobs.
- NOTE: place_block uses $wh for window-HEIGHT to avoid colliding
- with $h which is the hwnd in the post-launch script below.
- Size override (parse "WxH"); applied before position so position
- uses the NEW geometry.
- Absolute placement override.
- Otherwise apply named position relative to PrimaryScreen WorkingArea.
- 16:10 window sized at W = screen_W / golden_ratio,
- H = W * 10/16, centered both axes. The PowerShell-side
- [Math]::Round + integer cast keeps the numbers clean.
- Don't exceed working area
- explicit values already in place for "_explicit")
- 1. Spawn via cmd.exe /c start "" -- session-1 attach via WSL
- interop + ShellExecute. The "" empty title slot is required
- so `start` doesn't treat the next arg as a window title.
- 2. Post-launch FOCUS (always) + optional placement (if not as-is).
- Operator-flagged 2026-05-18: open_app(name="notepad") with
- position="as-is" (the new typed-tool default) succeeded -- but
- notepad opened BEHIND Windows Xbox Fullscreen Experience and
- was never brought to the foreground because the placement
- script was gated on `position != "none"` and skipped focus too.
- Fix: split focus from placement. ALWAYS bring the new window to
- the foreground (works around XFSE / Game Bar / any active full-
- screen overlay); only call MoveWindow when position changes.
- Bulletproof Win32 focus pattern: AttachThreadInput (attach our
- thread to the target's; SetForegroundWindow always succeeds
- once attached) + ShowWindow SW_RESTORE (handles minimized) +
- BringWindowToTop + SetForegroundWindow + a SendKeys nudge to
- grant the foreground-window permission Windows otherwise
- restricts.
- Move only when position changes geometry. "as-is" and "none"
- leave the window where the OS put it; "default" applies the
- golden-16:10 centered geometry (the new MiOS global default).
- place_block already uses $wh for window-height (clean
- naming -- no $h shadowing of the hwnd variable).
- ── optional move (only when position changed) ──
- ── optional focus (skipped for background / as-is) ──
- Last-resort fallback if PowerShell is unreachable.
- Operator should never hit this path on a healthy MiOS;
- window will almost certainly be invisible. Logged so
- post-mortem can identify the missing-PWSH cause.
- Service-user routing: mios-hermes (uid 820) cannot exec
- /mnt/c/.../powershell.exe directly because of the WSL
- metadata-perm wall. Route through the operator-side
- launcher broker's CAPTURE protocol -- broker runs the
- PS command in its own (operator) context, captures
- stdout+stderr via subprocess.PIPE, sends bytes back to
- us inline. No tempfile; no cross-user write.
- Read until EOF (broker closes after capture done).
- Same CAPTURE route for service users (no tempfile dance).
- Backwards-compat: if the first arg looks like a PowerShell
- command (starts with a verb like Get-/Set-/New-/Restart-),
- treat the whole call as the legacy "ssh-ps <cmd>" form to
- keep operator muscle memory working.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-winget
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-winget <subcommand> [args...]
- Phase D.4 of the AgentOS roadmap: Windows-side package
- management surface for the MiOS agent stack. Wraps winget.exe
- (Windows Package Manager) through WSL interop so MiOS agents
- can search / install / upgrade / uninstall Windows apps via
- the same dispatch path they use for Linux-side verbs.
- Output is structured JSON by default (broker + agent-pipe
- tool_call rows stay parsable). Pass --plain for the raw winget
- stdout for interactive use.
- SUBCOMMANDS
- search <query> [-n LIMIT]    Search the winget catalog.
- Returns {results:[{Name, Id,
- Version, Source}]}.
- list  [--filter F]           Installed packages on this host.
- show  <id>                   Detailed package info.
- install <id> [--silent]      Install (DEFAULT silent --no-banner
- so no interactive prompts hang the
- broker). High-privilege verb;
- tainted sessions refused.
- upgrade [<id>]               Upgrade one package, or -- with no
- arg / "all" / --all -- every installed
- package with an update available.
- uninstall <id>               Uninstall.
- sources                      List configured winget sources.
- help                         This message.
- Resolution: looks for winget.exe at
- /mnt/c/Users/<operator>/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WindowsApps/winget.exe
- (per-user install location), then PATH (WSL interop registration).
- Returns a JSON error envelope when winget.exe is unreachable
- rather than crashing -- callers parse {ok:false,error:...}.
- Hardening:
- * Output truncated to MIOS_WINGET_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES (default 256 KiB)
- so pathological winget output (huge `list` on a large host)
- can't fill the agent's context window.
- * --silent + --disable-interactivity flags forced on install/
- upgrade/uninstall so prompts can't hang.
- * Install/upgrade/uninstall write a structured outcome envelope
- {ok, verb, id, exit_code, stdout, stderr}.
- ─── locate winget.exe ────────────────────────────────────────────
- 1) Per-user install location (most common). Resolution
- order: MIOS_USER env -> USER (when != root) -> mios.toml
- [identity].username -> scan /mnt/c/Users/ for any user
- who has the WindowsApps dir. Root sessions (sudo, services)
- don't have MIOS_USER + USER=root won't hit a Windows
- profile, so the scan is the resilient path.
- Scan /mnt/c/Users/ as a last resort. Skips Default / Public
- which never have user winget installs.
- 2) System-wide (rare but possible on managed hosts).
- 3) PATH (WSL interop registration -- works when winget.exe is
- registered as a Windows interop binary).
- ─── output capture + truncation helper ───────────────────────────
- Strip CRLF (Windows defaults) so JSON-encoded blobs don't
- carry literal \r in every line.
- Cap per stream.
- EXPORT so _emit_envelope's python child sees them via os.environ (shell-local
- vars are invisible to the subprocess -> empty-stdout bug for list/show/etc.). 2026-06-10.
- Parse winget's column output into structured results.
- winget headers: Name  Id  Version  Match  Source.
- Find the header row (first line containing "Name" and "Id").
- Column starts -- find each header position.
- winget appends "<additional entries truncated due to
- result limit>" as the last line when -n caps the
- output. Skip any line whose first non-space char is
- `<` -- those are winget chrome, not real packages.
- No id, the literal keyword "all" (any case), or --all all mean
- "upgrade everything" -- the helper OWNS this contract so the
- agent-pipe dispatch template stays a clean `upgrade{id?}` (P3).

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-wsl-flatpak-export-sync.sh
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-wsl-flatpak-export-sync.sh
- Mirror flatpak's `.desktop` + icon exports into the system XDG dirs so
- WSL2's Start Menu app sync can see them. Operator-flagged
- "no icons match and all apps aren't populating in windows NATIVELY".
- Why WSL2 needs this: the wsl.exe distro launcher scans .desktop files
- under /usr/share/applications/ (and ~/.local/share/applications/) and
- auto-creates Windows Start Menu .lnk shortcuts under
- %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\<distro>\. Flatpak
- installs every .desktop under /var/lib/flatpak/exports/share/, which
- wsl.exe does NOT scan. Symlinking the exports into /usr/share/ on
- each boot is the cheapest way to surface flatpak apps to Windows.
- What this script does:
- 1. Symlink every /var/lib/flatpak/exports/share/applications/*.desktop
- into /usr/share/applications/  (skip duplicates).
- 2. Symlink the entire flatpak icons hicolor tree into
- /usr/share/icons/hicolor/ at the SIZE+CATEGORY level, so apps
- whose .desktop says `Icon=org.gnome.Epiphany` resolve to the
- flatpak-shipped PNG/SVG.
- 3. Refresh icon caches (gtk-update-icon-cache + update-desktop-database)
- so the symlinks register immediately.
- Idempotent: re-runs are no-ops if every link already points at the
- right target. Run as ExecStart of mios-wsl-flatpak-export-sync.service
- (boot + flatpak-install path-changed trigger).
- 1. Mirror .desktop files. Use symlinks so a flatpak uninstall removes
- the dangling link on the next sync (we GC stale links below).
- Skip if a NATIVE non-symlink already provides this app (don't shadow
- an RPM-installed .desktop with the flatpak one; flatpak ships the
- alternative app under .Devel or .ChromeDev suffix anyway).
- 2. Mirror icons. hicolor is the canonical icon theme that every
- .desktop's Icon= resolves through. flatpak exports its icons under
- /var/lib/flatpak/exports/share/icons/hicolor/<size>/apps/, matching
- the standard XDG layout.
- `find -L` follows symlinks: flatpak's hicolor/scalable/apps/*.svg
- entries are symlinks into /var/lib/flatpak/app/<id>/current/...
- which `-type f` (no -L) rejects. With -L, find resolves them and
- the -type f predicate matches the target regular file.
- 3. GC stale symlinks (flatpak uninstall left behind).
- 4. Refresh caches so the desktop databases see the new entries.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-wsl-flatpak-heal
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-wsl-flatpak-heal
- Pre-emptively ensure the user-side flatpak portal stack is alive
- so the next flatpak launch doesn't die at sandbox-credential
- bootstrap. WSL2g sessions consistently let flatpak-portal idle
- out (~10-18min observed) without dbus auto-activation re-firing
- it; the result is `Connection: failed to receive credentials`
- from any flatpak the operator/agent invokes.
- Operator-flagged 2026-05-18: every flatpak (epiphany, nautilus,
- gnome-software, ...) failed identically because flatpak-portal
- was inactive even though every OTHER portal service (dbus-broker,
- xdg-desktop-portal*, xdg-document-portal) was active.
- This script is the heal helper. It:
- 1. Checks the user-bus + portal services we know flatpak needs.
- 2. Starts any that are inactive.
- 3. Pings flatpak-portal via dbus to confirm responsiveness.
- Run by:
- * mios-wsl-flatpak-heal.timer (user-side, every 5 min)
- * any operator/agent before a flatpak launch they need to land
- Idempotent: starting an already-active service is a no-op.
- Services we manage. xdg-document-portal + flatpak-portal are
- what bubblewrap sandboxes actually need; the others are present
- for completeness but rarely the failure point.
- Verify flatpak-portal responds to a dbus ping. The portal accepts
- Introspect on its well-known path which is the cheapest probe
- that proves the activation chain works end-to-end.
- Emit JSON envelope so agents can consume the result + decide.
- Non-zero exit when the portal still doesn't respond after all
- heals -- caller surfaces "flatpak portal not reachable" rather
- than attempting a doomed launch.

## usr/libexec/mios/mios-wslg-env-import
- /usr/libexec/mios/mios-wslg-env-import
- Push the WSLg display environment into the systemd --user manager AND the D-Bus
- activation environment, so that --user services and flatpak's transient --user
- scopes (flatpak runs GUI apps in an `app-flatpak-*.scope` under the user
- manager) INHERIT DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY and can reach the WSLg compositor.
- WHY (microsoft/WSL#12436, verified on MiOS 2026-06-06): WSLg injects
- DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY/XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/PULSE_SERVER only into *login shells*
- (via /etc/profile.d). The `systemd --user` manager starts before any of that and
- never receives them, so anything it activates -- including every flatpak GUI --
- launches with no display and dies with:
- (app:N): Gtk-WARNING **: Failed to open display
- The canonical fix is exactly what an interactive GNOME/KDE session does after the
- compositor comes up: import the values into the user manager and the dbus
- activation env. On WSLg the values are stable, so set them explicitly (so this
- works even when our own env wasn't pre-populated).
- Inert off-WSL (the unit is ConditionVirtualization=wsl gated).
- set-environment is deterministic (doesn't depend on this process's own env being
- populated, unlike `import-environment VAR`).
- Mirror into the D-Bus activation environment so dbus-activated services (the
- xdg-desktop-portal stack flatpak GUIs need) also get the display.

## usr/libexec/mios/selinux-init
- 'MiOS' SELinux init -- load custom MiOS SELinux modules at first boot.
- Run by mios-selinux-init.service (gated by sentinel
- /var/lib/mios/.selinux-init-done so it only fires once per deploy).
- Modules ship as compiled .pp policy modules in
- /usr/share/selinux/packages/mios/. They're built but NOT loaded at
- image-build time -- composefs verity would seal a stale state. Loading
- happens on the booted host where the running policy can absorb the
- modules cleanly.
- After loading, persistent booleans + fcontexts are applied via semanage.
- shellcheck source=/usr/lib/mios/paths.sh
- Sentinel guard (also enforced by service unit ConditionPathExists)
- SELinux must be available
- Detect mode (enforcing/permissive/disabled). On disabled, skip module loads.
- Load every .pp under the module dir (compiled policy module package)
- Apply persistent booleans declared by the policy package

## usr/libexec/mios/system-env.sh
- /usr/bin/mios-env -- print the resolved MIOS_* environment surface.
- Documented in INDEX.md sec 4 as the canonical CLI for inspecting the
- layered environment overlay (legacy env-style files /etc/mios/env.d/*.env ->
- /etc/mios/env.d/*.env -> /etc/mios/install.env -> ~/.env.mios ->
- ~/.config/mios/env). Wraps /etc/profile.d/mios-env.sh + the
- tools/lib/userenv.sh TOML resolver and reports the consolidated values
- the running session would actually see.
- Usage:
- mios-env                  # all MIOS_* vars, sorted (KEY=VALUE)
- mios-env <NAME>           # one var, value only (suitable for $(...) capture)
- mios-env --json           # machine-readable JSON
- mios-env --unset          # POSIX 'unset' lines (for re-evaluating in a parent shell)
- mios-env --explain        # show which layer supplied each value
- mios-env --help
- Architectural Law 5: MIOS_AI_ENDPOINT / MIOS_AI_MODEL / MIOS_AI_KEY
- resolved here are the canonical values for every OpenAI-API-shaped
- client on the system.
- Canonical layer paths (mirrors mios-env.sh). The mios.toml overlay
- is loaded LAST via _load_toml_layers below so TOML overrides every
- legacy env-style file. mios.toml is THE singular SSOT.
- /etc/mios/env.d/*.env (alphabetical)
- shellcheck disable=SC1090
- Also fold in the TOML resolver (tools/lib/userenv.sh) which deep-merges
- /usr/share/mios/mios.toml -> /etc/mios/mios.toml -> ~/.config/mios/mios.toml.
- That library exports a richer set of typed MIOS_* slots derived from the
- unified mios.toml schema.
- shellcheck disable=SC1090
- Print all currently-set MIOS_* variables sorted by name.
- JSON-escape the value: backslash, double-quote, control chars.
- For each MIOS_* variable, identify the highest layer that set it.
- Parse KEY=... lines from this layer (env-file format).
- Emit 'unset' lines for every MIOS_* var. Useful for callers that
- want to clear and re-source the resolver in their own shell.
- Only echo the value (no name=); suitable for $(mios-env MIOS_AI_ENDPOINT).

## usr/libexec/mios/system-sync-env.sh
- /usr/bin/mios-sync-env -- regenerate /etc/mios/install.env from the
- layered mios.toml dotfile.
- Why both files exist:
- mios.toml    user-edited source of truth (layered overlay:
- ~/.config/mios/mios.toml > /etc/mios/mios.toml >
- /usr/share/mios/mios.toml). Owned by the operator.
- install.env  derived; env-var format consumed by shell scripts,
- systemd EnvironmentFile= directives, and first-boot
- services that can't easily parse TOML on their own.
- Owned by the system; regenerated from mios.toml.
- This CLI is the bridge: edit mios.toml (via /usr/share/mios/
- configurator/mios.html or your editor of choice), then run
- 'mios-sync-env' to refresh install.env. Idempotent.
- SECRETS ARE NEVER WRITTEN HERE. The operator password hash lives in
- /etc/shadow (baked via `chpasswd -e` in automation/11-user.sh) and in
- /etc/mios/secrets.env (0600); Forge admin password + GitHub token also
- live in secrets.env. install.env carries ONLY non-secret tunables.
- Rationale: install.env is read by THREE parsers with incompatible
- quoting rules -- systemd EnvironmentFile= (no $-expansion, strips outer
- quotes), bash `.`-source (word-splits + set -u expands $6), and podman
- --env-file (does NOT strip quotes). The only serialization safe under
- all three is BARE `KEY=value` with no shell-metachar/whitespace values.
- A `$`-bearing secret (the sha512 hash `$6$salt$digest`) cannot be
- represented safely here at all -- so it is evicted, not quoted.
- Output: /etc/mios/install.env, mode 0640, owned root:root. Requires
- sudo because /etc/mios/ is system config (FHS).
- Usage:
- mios-sync-env              # regenerate from current mios.toml
- mios-sync-env --dry-run    # print to stdout without writing
- mios-sync-env --show-source # print the resolved layered TOML
- source first, then the generated env
- Source the layered TOML resolver. Lives at /usr/lib/mios/userenv.sh
- (installed by automation/59-tools.sh) and exports MIOS_* vars derived
- from the deep-merged mios.toml overlay.
- shellcheck disable=SC1090
- emit KEY VALUE -- write ONE bare `KEY=value` line, the only form safe
- under all three consumers of install.env (see header): systemd
- EnvironmentFile=, bash `.`-source, and podman --env-file. Reject values
- that cannot be represented bare -- whitespace (bash word-splits),
- double/single quote, `$`, backtick, `#` (mis-parse/expand). Such values
- do not belong in a tri-parser flat env file (secrets -> secrets.env;
- free-text/multi-line -> read from mios.toml directly). install-robustness.
- Render the new install.env. Order matches what wsl-firstboot,
- forge-firstboot, and the llm-light prep step expect.
- /etc/mios/install.env -- DERIVED from mios.toml by mios-sync-env.
- Edit mios.toml (or use /usr/share/mios/configurator/mios.html), then
- run 'sudo mios-sync-env' to refresh this file. Manual edits here are
- overwritten on the next sync. This file holds ONLY non-secret tunables
- as bare KEY=value lines. Secrets (MIOS_USER_PASSWORD_HASH,
- in /etc/shadow and /etc/mios/secrets.env (0600).
- Generated: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
- Source layers (highest precedence first):
- Identity
- Global default password. Every MiOS service (Hermes Workspace,
- Forge admin, etc.) reads this as its default login credential
- unless the operator overrides per-service. Vendor default is
- "mios"; override in /etc/mios/mios.toml [identity].default_password.
- AI surface (Architectural Law 5: UNIFIED-AI-REDIRECTS). The resolver
- (userenv.sh) populates these from the layered mios.toml; prefer the
- resolved value, emit a fallback ONLY for the few keys shell/systemd
- consumers always expect. Fallback defaults track the live SSOT:
- endpoint -> [ai].endpoint  = http://localhost:8640/v1 (AGENT-PIPE ORCHESTRATOR
- - the UNIFIED entrypoint, model "MiOS-Agent";.
- Hermes :8642 is now a LEAF the pipe calls, NOT the client surface.)
- model -> [ai].model = granite4.1:8b (fleet; the earlier
- qwen3.5:2b was a dropped model -> a stale/unservable default)
- Inference backend the agents forward to (mios-llm-light front; the
- :11434 lane retired G5). Derived from the resolver's MIOS_HERMES_BACKEND_URL
- ([ai].hermes_backend_url, e.g. http://localhost:11450/v1) so MIOS_AI_BACKEND
- follows the SSOT instead of a hardcoded port. Strip a trailing /v1 so
- consumers that append their own path get a clean host:port base.
- llama.cpp light lane ([llamacpp] -> MIOS_LLAMACPP_*). All resolver-
- populated; emit only the values the resolver actually produced (no
- hardcoded literals). BAKE_MODELS feeds 73-model-prep.sh + the
- mios-ai-firstboot online GGUF retry.
- Part 10: Converged-Resource Architecture (MIOS_CONV_*)
- Anti-fabricated-execution guard ([verity].antifab_enable -> the agent-pipe
- routing layer, which reads MIOS_ANTIFAB_ENABLE from this EnvironmentFile).
- Resolver-populated; emit only what resolved so an unset SSOT key leaves the
- Python default (guard ON) intact -- degrade-open.
- Per-section grounding thresholds ([verity].antifab_min_entities / .ground_min
- -> the FAB-02 citation guard). Resolver-populated; emit only what resolved so
- an unset key leaves the Python degrade-open default intact.
- Frontier / A2O war-room roles (mios.toml [frontier] -> MIOS_A2O_* that the
- mios-agents container's mios-a2o harness reads). Resolver-populated; emit only
- what resolved (empty effort-flag templates stay unset = degrade-open).
- Heavy GPU lanes (gated/off-by-default; resolver-populated served names +
- ports). Endpoints assembled from the lane ports so the value tracks the
- SSOT rather than a hardcoded literal; emit only when the port resolved.
- Resolved service ports (SSOT [ports].*). Emitted as NUMERIC vars so
- EnvironmentFile= consumers (agent-pipe, hermes) AND ${MIOS_PORT_*}
- templates in mios.toml endpoint URLs can resolve -- systemd and Python
- do NOT expand ${...} from sibling env lines, so the ports must exist as
- their own vars. Without this the agent-pipe read a LITERAL
- "${MIOS_PORT_HERMES_WORKER}" worker port -> httpx InvalidURL -> :8640 500.
- (the greenboot AI-plane health check, datastore probes) read the datastore
- port from the SSOT instead of a hardcoded :5432 literal.
- install-robustness.
- ttyd parameters
- Image
- Forge admin (non-secret half)
- Secrets are intentionally ABSENT here (R2). MIOS_USER_PASSWORD_HASH,
- /etc/shadow (baked) and /etc/mios/secrets.env (0600). The password
- hash is a `$6$salt$digest` string -- unrepresentable in a bare
- tri-parser env file -- so it was the root of the `$6: unbound
- variable` service cascade; evicting it (not quoting it) is the fix.
- Force a clean 0 return so a trailing false `&& emit` never makes
- `generate_env > "$TMP"` fail under set -e and brick the env bridge.
- Write atomically (mktemp + rename) so a concurrent reader never
- sees a half-written file.
- R4 self-test: assert the serialization can never crash a consumer.
- Runs on the TMP before the atomic swap. Non-fatal (a warned imperfect
- file beats no env at all -- see the generate_env brick history), but
- loud; the hard gate is drift-check "install-env-safe" in automation/38.

## usr/libexec/mios/user-setup.sh
- 'MiOS' init-user-space -- initializes XDG user configuration for MiOS.
- Seeds the single unified ~/.config/mios/mios.toml from the vendor template,
- plus the empty $XDG_DATA / $XDG_CACHE / $XDG_STATE directories.
- If legacy split files (env.toml / images.toml / build.toml / flatpaks.list)
- exist, their values are migrated into mios.toml on first run.
- Migrate legacy split files into a single mios.toml body. Returns the merged
- TOML on stdout; emits the vendor template if no legacy data is found.
- Trailing `|| true` because grep returns 1 on no-match, which under
- set -e + pipefail aborts the calling assignment.

## usr/libexec/mios/verify-root.sh
- 'MiOS' verify-root -- early-boot composefs/ostree integrity check.
- Run by mios-verify-root.service before basic.target and greenboot. Lives
- in a heavily-locked-down systemd sandbox (ProtectSystem=strict, read-only
- /usr+/etc, no network, no writable state). Failure here makes greenboot
- rollback the deployment.
- What it checks (each independently; any single failure is fatal):
- 1. /run/ostree-booted exists       (we're on an ostree/bootc rootfs)
- 2. /usr/lib/os-release exists      (basic /usr layout intact)
- 3. composefs verity state          (where exposed by kernel + ostree)
- 4. /usr is read-only               (composefs/erofs mount character)
- shellcheck source=/usr/lib/mios/paths.sh
- 1. ostree-booted marker
- 2. /usr/lib/os-release present and parseable
- 3. /usr is read-only (composefs/erofs/overlayfs mount)
- 4. composefs verity probe (best-effort -- fsverity may be absent on WSL2)
- 5. ostree commit metadata sanity (best-effort -- ostree CLI present?)

## usr/libexec/mios/wsl-early
- MiOS -- wsl-early: WSL2 pre-sysinit fixups.
- Runs as PID 1's child with full root caps BEFORE basic.target and BEFORE
- any service that creates a mount namespace. Fixes two WSL2-specific gaps
- that cause cascading failures across cockpit and rootless podman:
- 1. Root mount propagation -- WSL2's /init mounts / private, which makes
- systemd's per-unit `mount(NULL, "/", NULL, MS_REC|MS_SLAVE, NULL)`
- return EOPNOTSUPP. That's the actual cause of `cockpit.service:
- Failed to set up mount namespacing: Operation not supported` and
- every "status=226/NAMESPACE" failure on WSL. Marking root rshared
- lets every subsequent unit's PrivateTmp/ProtectSystem/etc. clone
- a private mount namespace cleanly.
- 2. /dev/net/tun and /dev/fuse -- the WSL2 kernel builds tun + fuse
- in-tree, but systemd-udevd is condition-gated off (ConditionPathIs
- ReadWrite=/sys fails because /sys is RO under WSL2's /init), so
- nothing auto-creates the char device nodes. Without /dev/net/tun
- slirp4netns can't open its tap fd; without /dev/fuse fuse-overlayfs
- reports "cannot mount: No such file or directory" and rootless
- podman storage init fails entirely. We mknod them by hand here.
- Why this script and not tmpfiles.d:
- * `c!` lines in tmpfiles.d would work in theory, but tmpfiles is run
- after some early namespace-using units have already failed, and
- because tmpfiles itself uses sandboxing on some unit paths, mknod
- can return EPERM under the same propagation lock that bites cockpit.
- Doing it from a no-sandbox oneshot before basic.target avoids both.
- Hard gate: only on WSL.
- 1. Make / rshared so per-unit mount namespaces can MS_SLAVE-propagate.
- Idempotent: a second --make-rshared on an already-shared mount is a no-op.
- 2. Ensure /dev/net/tun (c 10:200) and /dev/fuse (c 10:229) exist.
- Both are kernel-builtin on the microsoft-standard-WSL2 kernel; the
- nodes only need to be present in /dev for slirp4netns and
- fuse-overlayfs to open them.

## usr/libexec/mios/wsl-firstboot
- MiOS -- wsl-firstboot: minimal WSL-specific first-boot bridge.
- Everything that can be declared at IMAGE BUILD TIME has been moved
- out of this script per the "native Fedora user creation at overlay
- time" principle:
- * /etc/passwd, /etc/group, /etc/shadow              -> automation/11-user.sh
- + /usr/lib/sysusers.d/10-mios.conf
- * /etc/subuid, /etc/subgid                          -> automation/11-user.sh
- * /var/home/mios + skel copy + ownership            -> /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/mios-user.conf
- * /var/lib/systemd/linger/mios marker               -> /usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/mios-user.conf
- What's left here is the genuinely WSL-runtime-bound work that has
- no native Fedora declarative equivalent:
- * /etc/hostname  -- comes from install.env which is only readable
- at boot, not at the cross-platform build phase
- * loginctl-shaped warnings if the marker didn't materialize
- (defensive; tmpfiles.d should already have
- handled it but logind being condition-gated
- off on WSL means we can't verify via varlink)
- Runs once (guarded by ConditionPathExists=!/var/lib/mios/.wsl-firstboot-done).
- Safe to re-run: all operations are idempotent.
- shellcheck source=/usr/lib/mios/paths.sh
- logger may fail if journald isn't up yet -- never fatal
- ── Load identity from install.env (written at bootstrap time) ──
- shellcheck disable=SC1091
- ── Hostname ──
- hostnamectl requires logind which is condition-gated off on WSL,
- so write /etc/hostname directly. The kernel call is best-effort.
- ── Defensive verification (no-op when overlay-time setup worked) ──
- tmpfiles.d/mios-user.conf and automation/11-user.sh should have
- already handled all of these. The blocks below are defensive logging
- only -- they never repair, just warn so a broken image is loud rather
- than quietly degraded.
- ── Mark done ──

## usr/libexec/mios/wsl-init
- MiOS -- wsl-init: WSL2 runtime bridge (runs every boot).
- ── /etc/wsl.conf drift guard ──
- WSL2 reads /etc/wsl.conf only at instance startup, so we can't repair it
- during the same boot it broke. But if a user (or a misbehaving service)
- edits /etc/wsl.conf into an unparseable state, this restores it from the
- canonical reference at /usr/lib/wsl.conf so the NEXT `wsl --shutdown` +
- relaunch comes up clean. Intentionally cmp-strict: drift in either
- direction means re-sync, not merge.
- Ensure /var/lib/mios runtime dirs exist
- Expose /mnt/wslg socket for GUI apps if WSLg is present
- ── Podman/WSL2 subnet conflict repair ───────────────────────────────────────
- Podman rootful creates a bridge (podman0) on 10.88.0.0/16 by default.
- WSL2 assigns eth0 addresses from the same range, so once Podman adds its
- route the eth0 prefix route is shadowed and all WSL2 host networking breaks,
- taking Cockpit (9090) and localhost forwarding down with it.
- containers.conf.d/99-mios-network.conf moves NEW default networks to
- 172.28.0.0/16, but any previously-created "podman" network still carries
- the old CIDR.  This block repairs both problems at boot time.
- Only relevant in a WSL2 environment
- Find any Podman rootful network whose subnet starts on the same /8+/16
- Recreate the default network on the safe range from containers.conf.d

## usr/libexec/mios/wsl-theme-bridge.sh
- /usr/libexec/mios/wsl-theme-bridge.sh
- Bridges the Windows AppsUseLightTheme registry value to GNOME's
- org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme + gtk-theme keys, so GTK /
- Adwaita / libadwaita apps inside MiOS-DEV (WSLg) follow the host's
- light/dark setting automatically.
- Why a poll loop:
- Windows does not expose a registry-change notification across the
- WSL2 boundary. WSLg's compositor reads the host theme for its own
- chrome but does not propagate it to guest dbus/gsettings -- guest
- apps query org.freedesktop.appearance via xdg-desktop-portal-gtk,
- which reads gsettings, which reads dconf, which has no signal source
- for the Windows side. A 15s poll is cheap (one cmd.exe registry read
- per tick) and gsettings only writes when the value actually changes,
- so dconf doesn't churn.
- Why a user service rather than system:
- gsettings writes per-user; the bus is /run/user/$UID/bus. Running as
- the user via mios-wsl-theme-bridge.service (user instance) avoids any
- need to su or fiddle with DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS plumbing.
- WSL-only by ConditionVirtualization in the unit; this script also
- bails if /mnt/wslg is absent (defense in depth for unusual WSL flavors
- without WSLg).
- We need cmd.exe (preferred -- no PATH lookup quirks) or reg.exe to
- query the registry. Both come from the WSL interop layer.
- gsettings is the write surface. If absent (gsettings-desktop-schemas
- missing), exit cleanly -- the schema gap is what really needs fixing.
- gtk-theme is a legacy fallback for apps that don't honor
- color-scheme yet (older GTK3, some Electron). adw-gtk3-theme ships
- both variants; if not installed, the set is a no-op-with-warning.
